**Exodus 6:18**

And sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. And the years of Kohath's life were one hundred thirty years.

**Exodus 6:19**

And sons of Merari: Mahali and Mushi. These are the houses of Levi according to their kinships.

**Exodus 6:20**

And Amram took Jochebed, daughter of his father's brother, as wife to himself, and she bore to him Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister. And the years of Amram's life were one hundred thirty-two years.

**Exodus 6:21**

And sons of Izhar: Core and Nepheg and Zichri.

**Exodus 6:22**

And sons of Uzziel: Elzaphan and Setri.

**Exodus 6:23**

And Aaron took Elizabeth daughter of Amminadab, sister of Nahshon, as wife to himself, and she bore to him Nadab and Abiud and Eleazar and Ithamar.

**Exodus 6:24**

And sons of Core: Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph. These are the generations of Core.

**Exodus 6:25**

And Eleazar son of Aaron took for himself as wife one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore to him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their generations.

**Exodus 6:26**

This is Aaron and Moses, to whom God told them to bring out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt with their forces.

**Exodus 6:27**

These are the ones speaking to Pharaoh king of Egypt and bringing out the sons of Israel from Egypt: this Aaron and Moses.

**Exodus 6:28**

Now it happened on the day the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,

**Exodus 6:29**

that the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the Lord. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak to you."

**Exodus 6:30**

And Moses said before the Lord, "Look, I am weak-voiced, and how will Pharaoh listen to me?"

#### Chapter 7

**Exodus 7:1**

And the Lord said to Moses, saying, "See, I have given you as god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet."

**Exodus 7:2**

You shall speak to him all that I command you, and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh so that he may send out the sons of Israel from his land.

**Exodus 7:3**

But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and I will multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 7:4**

And Pharaoh will not listen to you, and I will lay my hand upon Egypt, and with my power I will bring out my people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt with great vengeance.

**Exodus 7:5**

And all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, stretching out my hand upon Egypt, when I bring out the sons of Israel from their midst.

**Exodus 7:6**

And Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord commanded them; so they did.

**Exodus 7:7**

Now Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron his brother was eighty-three years old, when he spoke to Pharaoh.

**Exodus 7:8**

And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, saying,

**Exodus 7:9**

And if Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, Give us a sign or a wonder, then you shall say to Aaron your brother, Take the staff and throw it on the ground before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it will become a dragon.

**Exodus 7:10**

And Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and his servants, and they did so, just as the Lord had commanded them. And Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a dragon.

**Exodus 7:11**

Then Pharaoh called together the wise men of Egypt and the sorcerers, and the enchanters of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries.

**Exodus 7:12**

And each one threw down his staff, and they became dragons, but Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.

**Exodus 7:13**

And Pharaoh's heart grew strong, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken to them.

**Exodus 7:14**

And the Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart has become heavy, so that he will not send out the people."

**Exodus 7:15**

Go to Pharaoh in the morning. Look, he is going out to the water, and you shall stand to meet him on the bank of the river, and you shall take in your hand the staff that was turned into a snake.

**Exodus 7:16**

And you shall say to him, The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, Send out my people so that they may serve me in the wilderness, and look, until now you have not listened.

**Exodus 7:17**

These things says the Lord: By this you shall know that I am the Lord. Look, I strike with the staff in my hand upon the water in the river, and it will turn into blood.

**Exodus 7:18**

And the fish in the river will die, and the river will stink, and the Egyptians will not be able to drink water from the river.

**Exodus 7:19**

And the Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron your brother, Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers and their canals and their marshes and every standing water of theirs, and it will become blood. And there will be blood in all the land of Egypt, both in the woods and in the stones.

**Exodus 7:20**

And Moses and Aaron did so, just as the Lord commanded them, and lifting up his staff, he struck the water in the river before Pharaoh and before his servants, and all the water in the river turned into blood.

**Exodus 7:21**

And the fish in the river died, and the river stank, and the Egyptians were not able to drink water from the river, and the blood was in all the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 7:22**

And the enchanters of the Egyptians did likewise with their sorceries, and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.

**Exodus 7:23**

And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his mind even on this.

**Exodus 7:24**

And all the Egyptians dug around the river so that they might drink water, for they were not able to drink water from the river.

**Exodus 7:25**

And seven days were fulfilled after the Lord struck the river.

**Exodus 7:26**

And the Lord said to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, These things says the Lord: Send out my people so that they may serve me.

**Exodus 7:27**

But if you do not want to send them out, look, I strike all your borders with frogs.

**Exodus 7:28**

And the river will teem with frogs, and they will come up and enter into your houses and into the inner rooms of your bedchambers and upon your beds and into the houses of your servants and your people and into your dough and your ovens.

**Exodus 7:29**

And upon you and upon your servants and upon your people the frogs will come up.

#### Chapter 8

**Exodus 8:1**

And the Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron your brother, Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers and over the canals and over the marshes, and bring up the frogs.

**Exodus 8:2**

And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt and brought up the frogs, and the frog came up and covered the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 8:3**

And the enchanters of the Egyptians did likewise with their sorceries, and they brought up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 8:4**

And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said, Pray concerning me to the Lord, and let him take away the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send out the people, and they will sacrifice to the Lord.

**Exodus 8:5**

And Moses said to Pharaoh, Set for me when I should pray concerning you and concerning your servants and concerning your people, to wipe out the frogs from you and from your people and from your houses; only in the river will they be left.

**Exodus 8:6**

And he said, Tomorrow. Then he said, As you have spoken, so that you may know that there is no other besides the Lord.

**Exodus 8:7**

And the frogs will be taken away from you and from your houses and from the courtyards and from your servants and from your people; only in the river will they be left.

**Exodus 8:8**

And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to the Lord concerning the appointed matter of the frogs, as Pharaoh had set it.

**Exodus 8:9**

And the Lord did just as Moses said, and the frogs died out of the houses and out of the courtyards and out of the fields.

**Exodus 8:10**

And they gathered them in heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.

**Exodus 8:11**

And Pharaoh, seeing that there had come relief, made his heart heavy, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken.

**Exodus 8:12**

And the Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron, Stretch out your hand with your staff and strike the dust of the earth, and there will be gnats both on human beings and on the four-footed animals and in all the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 8:13**

So Aaron stretched out his hand with the staff and struck the dust of the earth, and the gnats came on human beings and on the four-footed animals, and in all the dust of the earth there were gnats in all the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 8:14**

And the enchanters did likewise with their sorceries, trying to bring out the gnat, and they were not able, and the gnats were on the human beings and on the four-footed animals.

**Exodus 8:15**

Then the enchanters said to Pharaoh, This is the finger of God. And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken.

**Exodus 8:16**

And the Lord said to Moses, Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and look, he goes out to the water, and you shall say to him, These things says the Lord: Send out my people so that they may serve me in the wilderness.

**Exodus 8:17**

But if you do not want to send out my people, look, I send upon you and upon your servants and upon your people and upon your houses the dog-fly, and the houses of the Egyptians will be filled with the dog-fly, and even the land on which they are.

**Exodus 8:18**

And I will distinguish wondrously on that day the land of Goshen, on which my people dwell, where the dog-fly will not be there, so that you may know that I am the Lord, the Lord of all the earth.

**Exodus 8:19**

And I will put a distinction between my people and between your people. Tomorrow this sign will be upon the land.

**Exodus 8:20**

And the Lord did so, and the dog-fly came in abundance into the houses of Pharaoh and into the houses of his servants and into all the land of Egypt, and the land was ruined by the dog-fly.

**Exodus 8:21**

Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, saying, Go, sacrifice to your God in the land.

**Exodus 8:22**

And Moses said, It cannot happen this way, for we shall sacrifice to the Lord our God the abominations of the Egyptians; for if we sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians before them, we shall be stoned.

**Exodus 8:23**

We will go a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to the Lord our God, just as he said to us.

**Exodus 8:24**

And Pharaoh said, I send you out, and sacrifice to the Lord your God in the wilderness, only do not cut it too far to go. Pray then concerning me to the Lord.

**Exodus 8:25**

And Moses said, Look, I am going out from you, and I will pray to God, and the dog-fly will depart from you and from your servants and your people tomorrow. Only do not add again, Pharaoh, to deceive by not sending out the people to sacrifice to the Lord.

**Exodus 8:26**

And Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.

**Exodus 8:27**

And the Lord did just as Moses said, and he removed the dog-fly from Pharaoh and his servants and his people, and not one was left.

**Exodus 8:28**

And Pharaoh made his heart heavy also at this time, and he did not want to send out the people.

#### Chapter 9

**Exodus 9:1**

And the Lord said to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, These things says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send out my people so that they may serve me.

**Exodus 9:2**

If, however, you do not want to send out my people, but still hold them back,

**Exodus 9:3**

look, the hand of the Lord will come upon your livestock in the fields, both on the horses and on the beasts of burden and the camels and oxen and sheep, a very great death.

**Exodus 9:4**

And I will make a wondrous distinction at that time between the livestock of the Egyptians and the livestock of the sons of Israel; not one thing from all that belongs to the sons of Israel shall die.

**Exodus 9:5**

And God set a limit, saying, Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing on the land.

**Exodus 9:6**

And the Lord did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of the Egyptians died, but from the livestock of the sons of Israel not one died.

**Exodus 9:7**

And Pharaoh, seeing that not one had died from all the livestock of the sons of Israel, made Pharaoh's heart heavy, and he did not send out the people.

**Exodus 9:8**

And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, saying, Take for yourselves full handfuls of furnace soot, and let Moses scatter it into the sky before Pharaoh and before his servants.

**Exodus 9:9**

And let it become dust over all the land of Egypt, and it will be on the human beings and on the four-footed animals sores with blisters boiling up in all the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 9:10**

So they took the furnace soot before Pharaoh, and Moses scattered it into the sky, and it became sores with blisters boiling up on the human beings and on the four-footed animals.

**Exodus 9:11**

And the sorcerers were not able to stand before Moses because of the sores, for the sores came on the sorcerers and in all the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 9:12**

And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded.

**Exodus 9:13**

And the Lord said to Moses, Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, These things says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send out my people so that they may serve me.

**Exodus 9:14**

For at this present time I send all my blows into your heart and into the heart of your servants and your people, so that you may know that there is no other like me in all the earth.

**Exodus 9:15**

For now, sending out my hand, I will strike you and your people with death, and you will be wiped off from the earth.

**Exodus 9:16**

And because of this you have been preserved, so that I may display in you my strength and so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth.

**Exodus 9:17**

Do you still set yourself against my people so as not to send them out?

**Exodus 9:18**

Look, tomorrow at this hour I will rain a very great hail, such as has not happened in Egypt from the day it was created until this day.

**Exodus 9:19**

Now then hasten to gather your livestock and all that is yours in the field, for all the human beings and the livestock, as many as may be found in the field and not come into a house, when the hail falls upon them, will die.

**Exodus 9:20**

The one fearing the word of the Lord among Pharaoh's servants gathered his livestock into the houses.

**Exodus 9:21**

But whoever did not attend in his mind to the word of the Lord left the livestock in the fields.

**Exodus 9:22**

And the Lord said to Moses, Stretch out your hand to the sky, and there will be hail on all the land of Egypt, both on the human beings and on the livestock and on every plant on the land.

**Exodus 9:23**

And Moses stretched out his hand to the sky, and the Lord gave voices and hail, and the fire ran along on the ground, and the Lord rained hail upon all the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 9:24**

And there was hail, and the fire flaming in the hail, and the hail was very, very great, such as had not happened in Egypt from the time a nation came to be upon it.

**Exodus 9:25**

And the hail struck in all the land of Egypt, from human being to livestock, and the hail struck every plant in the field, and the hail shattered all the trees in the field.

**Exodus 9:26**

Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, there was no hail.

**Exodus 9:27**

And Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron and said to them, I have sinned this time. The Lord is righteous, but I and my people are ungodly.

**Exodus 9:28**

Pray then concerning me to the Lord, and let there cease from becoming voices of God and hail and fire, and I will send you out, and you shall no longer remain.

**Exodus 9:29**

And Moses said to him, As soon as I go out from the city, I will spread out my hands to the Lord, and the voices will cease, and the hail and the rain will be no more, so that you may know that the earth belongs to the Lord.

**Exodus 9:30**

But you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear the Lord.

**Exodus 9:31**

And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was standing, and the flax was seeding.

**Exodus 9:32**

But the wheat and the rye were not struck, for they were late.

**Exodus 9:33**

And Moses went out from Pharaoh, outside the city, and spread out his hands to the Lord, and the voices ceased and the hail and the rain no longer fell on the earth.

**Exodus 9:34**

And Pharaoh, seeing that the rain and the hail and the voices had ceased, added to sin, and he made heavy his heart and the heart of his servants.

**Exodus 9:35**

And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not send out the sons of Israel, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses.

#### Chapter 10

**Exodus 10:1**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, so that these signs may come in turn upon them,"

**Exodus 10:2**

"so that you may tell your children and your children's children how I mocked the Egyptians and the signs I performed among them, and you will know that I am the Lord."

**Exodus 10:3**

Then Moses and Aaron went in before Pharaoh and said to him, "These things says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Send my people away, so that they may serve me."

**Exodus 10:4**

"But if you refuse to send my people away, behold, at this hour tomorrow I am bringing a great swarm of locusts upon all your borders."

**Exodus 10:5**

"They will cover the face of the earth, and you will not be able to see the earth. They will eat every remainder of the land left behind, what the hail left for you, and they will eat every tree growing for you on the land."

**Exodus 10:6**

"Your houses will be filled, and the houses of your servants, and all the houses in all the land of the Egyptians, with things your fathers never saw, nor their forefathers, from the day they came to be on the earth until this day." Then Moses turned away and went out from Pharaoh.

**Exodus 10:7**

And Pharaoh's servants said to him, "How long will this be a snare to us? Send the men away, so that they may serve their God. Do you need to learn that Egypt is ruined?"

**Exodus 10:8**

And they brought Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, "Go, serve the Lord your God. But who exactly are the ones going?"

**Exodus 10:9**

And Moses said, "We will go with young and old, with our sons and daughters, with our sheep and cattle, for we have a feast of the Lord our God."

**Exodus 10:10**

And he said to them, "So be it: may the Lord be with you, just as I send you out, you and your baggage. See, evil lies ahead of you."

**Exodus 10:11**

"Not so. Let the men go and serve God, for this is what you yourselves seek." And they drove them out from Pharaoh's presence.

**Exodus 10:12**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, and let the locust come up on the land and eat every plant of the land and every fruit of the trees that the hail left."

**Exodus 10:13**

And Moses lifted up the rod toward heaven, and the Lord brought a south wind upon the land all that day and all that night. Morning came, and the south wind brought in the locust.

**Exodus 10:14**

And it came up over all the land of Egypt, and it settled over all the borders of Egypt in very great abundance. Before it no locust like it had come to be, and after it none will be so.

**Exodus 10:15**

And it covered the face of the earth, and the land was ruined. And it ate every plant of the earth and every fruit of the trees left by the hail. No green thing was left on the trees or in any plant of the field in all the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 10:16**

Then Pharaoh hurried to call Moses and Aaron, saying, "I have sinned before the Lord your God and against you."

**Exodus 10:17**

"Forgive, then, my sin just this once, and pray to the Lord your God, and let him take this death away from me."

**Exodus 10:18**

And Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to God.

**Exodus 10:19**

And the Lord changed the wind to a strong wind from the sea, and it took up the locust and cast it into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left in all the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 10:20**

And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not send away the sons of Israel.

**Exodus 10:21**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand to heaven, and let darkness come over the land of Egypt, darkness that can be felt."

**Exodus 10:22**

And Moses stretched out his hand to heaven, and there came darkness, gloom, storm-cloud over all the land of Egypt for three days.

**Exodus 10:23**

No one saw his brother for three days, and no one rose from his bed for three days. But all the sons of Israel had light in every place where they lived.

**Exodus 10:24**

Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, saying, "Go, serve the Lord your God. Only leave the sheep and cattle behind, and let your baggage go along with you."

**Exodus 10:25**

And Moses said, "But you too will give us whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, and we will offer them to the Lord our God."

**Exodus 10:26**

"Our livestock too will go with us, and we will not leave behind a hoof, for from them we will take what we need to serve the Lord our God. But we do not know with what we will serve the Lord our God until we come there."

**Exodus 10:27**

But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was not willing to send them away.

**Exodus 10:28**

And Pharaoh said, "Go away from me. Watch yourself. Do not see my face again, for on the day you appear before me, you will die."

**Exodus 10:29**

And Moses said, "You have spoken. I will no longer appear before your face."

#### Chapter 11

**Exodus 11:1**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Yet one plague I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt, and after that he will send you out from here. Whenever he sends you out, he will surely drive you out with a complete expulsion."

**Exodus 11:2**

"Speak secretly into the ears of the people, and let each man ask from his neighbor, and each woman from her neighbor, silver and gold vessels and clothing."

**Exodus 11:3**

And the Lord gave his people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent to them. And Moses the man became exceedingly great in the sight of the Egyptians and before Pharaoh and before all his servants.

**Exodus 11:4**

And Moses said, "These things says the Lord: About midnight I enter into the midst of Egypt,"

**Exodus 11:5**

"and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from Pharaoh's firstborn who sits on the throne to the firstborn of the female servant by the mill, and to the firstborn of every beast."

**Exodus 11:6**

"And there will be a great cry through all the land of Egypt, such as has never happened and will never be added again."

**Exodus 11:7**

"But among all the sons of Israel not a dog will snarl with its tongue, from man to beast, so that you may know how marvelously the Lord will distinguish between the Egyptians and Israel."

**Exodus 11:8**

"And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow to me, saying, Go out, you and all the people whom you lead, and after that I will go out." Then Moses went out from Pharaoh with anger.

**Exodus 11:9**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that I may greatly multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt."

**Exodus 11:10**

And Moses and Aaron did all these signs and wonders in the land of Egypt before Pharaoh. But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was not willing to send the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

#### Chapter 12

**Exodus 12:1**

Then the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

**Exodus 12:2**

"This month will be for you the beginning of months; it is first for you among the months of the year."

**Exodus 12:3**

"Speak to the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, saying, On the tenth day of this month let each take for themselves an animal from the flock according to ancestral houses, each an animal from the flock for the household."

**Exodus 12:4**

"But if those in the house are too few for an animal from the flock, he shall take along his neighbor nearest to him according to the number of persons. Each according to what is enough for him shall be counted toward the animal from the flock."

**Exodus 12:5**

"The animal from the flock shall be for you unblemished, male, a year old. You shall take it from the lambs and from the kids."

**Exodus 12:6**

"And it shall be kept by you until the fourteenth day of this month, and the whole multitude of the assembly of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening."

**Exodus 12:7**

"And they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel in the houses where they eat it."

**Exodus 12:8**

"And they shall eat the flesh on this night, roasted by fire, and unleavened bread. With bitter herbs they shall eat it."

**Exodus 12:9**

"You shall not eat any of it raw or boiled in water, but only roasted by fire, the head with the feet and the inner parts."

**Exodus 12:10**

"You shall not leave any of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone from it. But what remains of it until morning you shall burn with fire."

**Exodus 12:11**

"And thus you shall eat it: your waists girded, your sandals on your feet, your staffs in your hands, and you shall eat it in haste. It is Passover to the Lord."

**Exodus 12:12**

"And I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast, and on all the gods of the Egyptians I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord."

**Exodus 12:13**

"And the blood will be for you as a sign on the houses where you are, and I will see the blood and shelter you, and there shall not be among you a blow of destruction when I strike in the land of Egypt."

**Exodus 12:14**

"And this day will be for you a memorial, and you shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout your generations. As an age-lasting ordinance you shall celebrate it."

**Exodus 12:15**

"Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and from the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses. Everyone who eats leavened food, that person shall be destroyed from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day."

**Exodus 12:16**

"And the first day shall be called holy, and the seventh day shall be a holy assembly for you. No work of service shall you do on them, except what will be made for every person; that alone may be done for you."

**Exodus 12:17**

"And you shall keep this command, for on this very day I will bring your hosts out of the land of Egypt, and you shall keep this day throughout your generations as an age-lasting ordinance."

**Exodus 12:18**

"Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread until evening of the twenty-first day of the month."

**Exodus 12:19**

"For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses. Everyone who eats leavened food, that person shall be destroyed from the assembly of Israel, among both the newcomer and the native-born of the land."

**Exodus 12:20**

"You shall eat nothing leavened. In every dwelling of yours you shall eat unleavened bread."

**Exodus 12:21**

Then Moses called all the elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, "Go and take for yourselves an animal from the flock according to your families, and sacrifice the Passover."

**Exodus 12:22**

"And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, and after dipping it in some of the blood by the door, you shall touch the lintel and both doorposts with some of the blood by the door. But none of you shall go out from the door of his house until morning."

**Exodus 12:23**

"And the Lord will pass by to strike the Egyptians, and he will see the blood on the lintel and on both doorposts, and the Lord will pass by the door and will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike."

**Exodus 12:24**

"And you shall keep this word as an ordinance for you and for your sons forever."

**Exodus 12:25**

"And when you enter the land that the Lord will give you, just as he spoke, you shall keep this service."

**Exodus 12:26**

"And it shall be that when your sons say to you, What is this service?"

**Exodus 12:27**

"you shall say to them, This Passover is a sacrifice to the Lord, who sheltered the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when he struck the Egyptians but rescued our houses." And the people bowed low and worshiped.

**Exodus 12:28**

And the sons of Israel went away and did just as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.

**Exodus 12:29**

And it happened at midnight that the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from Pharaoh's firstborn sitting on the throne to the firstborn of the captive woman in the pit, and every firstborn of beast.

**Exodus 12:30**

And Pharaoh rose by night, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry in all the land of Egypt, for there was no house in which there was not one dead.

**Exodus 12:31**

And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron by night and said to them, "Rise up and go out from my people, both you and the sons of Israel. Go and serve the Lord your God, just as you say."

**Exodus 12:32**

"Take your sheep and your cattle and go. But bless me too."

**Exodus 12:33**

And the Egyptians pressed the people in haste to drive them out of the land, for they said, "We are all dying."

**Exodus 12:34**

And the people took the dough before it was leavened, their kneaded batches wrapped in their garments on their shoulders.

**Exodus 12:35**

And the sons of Israel did just as Moses instructed them, and they asked from the Egyptians silver and gold vessels and clothing.

**Exodus 12:36**

And the Lord gave his people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, and they lent to them, and they plundered the Egyptians.

**Exodus 12:37**

Then the sons of Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides the baggage.

**Exodus 12:38**

And a great mixed company went up with them, and sheep and cattle and very much livestock.

**Exodus 12:39**

And they baked the dough they had brought out from Egypt into unleavened cakes, for it had not been leavened, because the Egyptians had driven them out and they were not able to delay, nor had they prepared provisions for themselves for the journey.

**Exodus 12:40**

Now the dwelling of the sons of Israel, during which they had dwelt in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, was four hundred and thirty years.

**Exodus 12:41**

And it happened after the four hundred and thirty years that all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 12:42**

It is a night-watch kept for the Lord, so as to bring them out from the land of Egypt. This same night is a watch kept for the Lord for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.

**Exodus 12:43**

Then the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, "This is the law of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it."

**Exodus 12:44**

"And every household slave or one bought with silver, you shall circumcise him, and then he shall eat of it."

**Exodus 12:45**

"A settler or a hired worker shall not eat of it."

**Exodus 12:46**

"In one house it shall be eaten, and you shall not carry any of the flesh out from the house, and you shall not break a bone from it."

**Exodus 12:47**

"The whole assembly of the sons of Israel shall keep it."

**Exodus 12:48**

"And if any newcomer comes to you to keep Passover to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male of him, and then he shall come near to keep it, and he shall be like the native-born of the land. No uncircumcised person shall eat of it."

**Exodus 12:49**

"One law shall be for the native-born and for the newcomer who comes among you."

**Exodus 12:50**

And the sons of Israel did just as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron for them; so they did.

**Exodus 12:51**

And it happened on that day that the Lord brought the sons of Israel out from the land of Egypt with their hosts.

#### Chapter 13

**Exodus 13:1**

Then the Lord said to Moses, saying,

**Exodus 13:2**

"Set apart to me every firstborn, first issue, opening every womb among the sons of Israel, from man to beast. It is mine."

**Exodus 13:3**

Then Moses said to the people, "Remember this day on which you came out from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out from there, and leaven shall not be eaten."

**Exodus 13:4**

"For on this day you are going out, in the month of new grain."

**Exodus 13:5**

"And it shall be that when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites and Hittites and Hivites and Girgashites and Amorites and Perizzites and Jebusites, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you shall perform this service in this month."

**Exodus 13:6**

"For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the Lord."

**Exodus 13:7**

"For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. No leavened thing shall be seen among you, nor shall leaven be with you in all your borders."

**Exodus 13:8**

"And you shall tell your son on that day, saying, Because of this the Lord my God dealt with me when I was going out from Egypt."

**Exodus 13:9**

"And it shall be for you as a sign on your hand and as a memorial before your eyes, so that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth, for with a mighty hand the Lord God brought you out from Egypt."

**Exodus 13:10**

"And you shall keep this law at the appointed times, from days to days."

**Exodus 13:11**

"And it shall be that when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, just as he swore to your fathers, and gives it to you,"

**Exodus 13:12**

"you shall set apart to the Lord every opener of the womb, the males. Every opener of the womb from the herds or among your livestock, as many as come to you, the males you shall consecrate to the Lord."

**Exodus 13:13**

"Every opener of the womb of a donkey you shall exchange for a sheep, and if you do not exchange it, you shall redeem it. Every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem."

**Exodus 13:14**

"And if your son asks you after this, saying, What is this? you shall say to him, With a mighty hand the Lord brought us out from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery."

**Exodus 13:15**

"And when Pharaoh hardened himself against sending us away, he killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of humans to the firstborn of beasts. Because of this I sacrifice to the Lord every opener of the womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I will redeem."

**Exodus 13:16**

"And it shall be as a sign on your hand and fixed before your eyes, for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out from Egypt."

**Exodus 13:17**

And when Pharaoh sent the people away, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, because it was near. For God said, "Lest perhaps the people change their mind when they see war and turn back to Egypt."

**Exodus 13:18**

So God led the people around by the road to the wilderness, to the Red Sea. And in the fifth generation the sons of Israel went up out from the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 13:19**

And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had solemnly bound the sons of Israel by oath, saying, God will surely visit you, and you shall carry my bones up from here with you.

**Exodus 13:20**

Then the sons of Israel set out from Succoth and camped at Etham by the wilderness.

**Exodus 13:21**

And God led them, by day in a pillar of cloud to show them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire.

**Exodus 13:22**

The pillar of cloud by day did not fail, nor the pillar of fire by night, before all the people.

#### Chapter 14

**Exodus 14:1**

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

**Exodus 14:2**

"Speak to the sons of Israel, and after turning back let them camp opposite the village, between Migdol and the sea. Opposite Baalzephon, before them, you shall camp by the sea."

**Exodus 14:3**

"And Pharaoh will say to his people, These sons of Israel are wandering in the land, for the wilderness has shut them in."

**Exodus 14:4**

"And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will pursue after them, and I will be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his army, and all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord." And they did so.

**Exodus 14:5**

And it was reported to the king of the Egyptians that the people had fled, and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people, and they said, "Why have we done this, sending away the sons of Israel so that they need not serve us?"

**Exodus 14:6**

So Pharaoh yoked his chariots, and he gathered all his people with himself.

**Exodus 14:7**

And taking six hundred chosen chariots and all the cavalry of the Egyptians, he took commanders over all of them.

**Exodus 14:8**

And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt and of his servants, and he pursued after the sons of Israel. But the sons of Israel were going out with uplifted hand.

**Exodus 14:9**

And the Egyptians pursued after them and found them encamped by the sea, all Pharaoh's cavalry and chariots and horsemen and army, opposite the village, opposite Baalzephon.

**Exodus 14:10**

And Pharaoh drew near, and the sons of Israel lifted up their eyes and saw: the Egyptians had camped behind them. And they feared greatly, and the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord.

**Exodus 14:11**

And they said to Moses, "Was it because there were no tombs in the land of Egypt that you brought us out to die in the wilderness? Why have you done this to us, bringing us out from Egypt?"

**Exodus 14:12**

"Was this not the word we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, Leave us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians? For it would be better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in this wilderness."

**Exodus 14:13**

Then Moses said to the people, "Take courage. Stand and see the salvation from God that he will accomplish for us today. For in the way you have seen the Egyptians today, you shall never again see them through all time."

**Exodus 14:14**

"The Lord will fight for you, and you will be still."

**Exodus 14:15**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to me? Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them break camp."

**Exodus 14:16**

"And you, lift up your rod and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it, and let the sons of Israel enter into the midst of the sea on dry ground."

**Exodus 14:17**

"And behold, I am hardening the heart of Pharaoh and of all the Egyptians, and they will go in after them, and I will be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his army and in his chariots and horses."

**Exodus 14:18**

"And all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord when I am glorified in Pharaoh and in his chariots and horses."

**Exodus 14:19**

Then the angel of God who went before the camp of the sons of Israel moved and went behind them, and the pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them.

**Exodus 14:20**

And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and there it stood. And there came darkness and gloom, and the night passed, and they did not come near one another through all the night.

**Exodus 14:21**

Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the Lord drew back the sea by a violent south wind all night, and he made the sea dry, and the water was split.

**Exodus 14:22**

And the sons of Israel entered into the midst of the sea on dry ground, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.

**Exodus 14:23**

Then the Egyptians pursued and went in after them into the midst of the sea, all Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and riders.

**Exodus 14:24**

And in the morning watch the Lord looked upon the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and cloud, and he threw the camp of the Egyptians into confusion.

**Exodus 14:25**

And he bound the axles of their chariots and made them drive with difficulty. And the Egyptians said, "Let us flee from before Israel, for the Lord fights for them against the Egyptians."

**Exodus 14:26**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the water return and cover the Egyptians, both the chariots and the riders."

**Exodus 14:27**

And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the water returned toward day to its place. And the Egyptians fled down into the water, and the Lord shook the Egyptians off into the midst of the sea.

**Exodus 14:28**

And the water returned and covered the chariots and the riders and all Pharaoh's force, those who had gone in after them into the sea. Not even one of them was left.

**Exodus 14:29**

But the sons of Israel traveled through dry ground in the midst of the sea, and the water was a wall for them on the right and on the left.

**Exodus 14:30**

Thus the Lord rescued Israel on that day from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians lying dead by the shore of the sea.

**Exodus 14:31**

And Israel saw the great hand, the things the Lord had done against the Egyptians, and the people feared the Lord, and they believed God and Moses his attendant.

#### Chapter 15

**Exodus 15:1**

Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to God and said, "Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been glorified gloriously; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea."

**Exodus 15:2**

"He became for me a helper and a shelter for salvation. This is my God, and I will glorify him, God of my father, and I will exalt him."

**Exodus 15:3**

"The Lord shattering wars; the Lord is his name."

**Exodus 15:4**

"Pharaoh's chariots and his force he threw into the sea; chosen mounted officers he sank in the Red Sea."

**Exodus 15:5**

"The deep covered them; they went down into the depth like a stone."

**Exodus 15:6**

"Your right hand, O Lord, has been glorified in strength; your right hand, O Lord, shattered enemies."

**Exodus 15:7**

"And in the abundance of your glory you crushed the adversaries; you sent out your wrath, and it devoured them like stubble."

**Exodus 15:8**

"And by the breath of your wrath the water stood apart; the waters congealed like a wall; the waves congealed in the midst of the sea."

**Exodus 15:9**

"The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide spoil, I will fill my soul, I will kill with my sword, my hand will rule."

**Exodus 15:10**

"You sent out your wind, the sea covered them; they sank like lead in mighty water."

**Exodus 15:11**

"Who is like you among gods, O Lord? Who is like you, glorified among holy ones, wondrous in glories, doing wonders?"

**Exodus 15:12**

"You stretched out your right hand; earth swallowed them."

**Exodus 15:13**

"You guided in your righteousness this people whom you redeemed; by your strength you led them onward to your holy resting-place."

**Exodus 15:14**

"Nations heard and grew angry; pangs seized those dwelling among the Philistines."

**Exodus 15:15**

"Then the chiefs of Edom hastened; the rulers of the Moabites, trembling took hold of them; all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away."

**Exodus 15:16**

"Let fear and trembling fall upon them; by the greatness of your arm let them turn to stone, until your people pass over, O Lord, until this people passes over, whom you acquired."

**Exodus 15:17**

"Bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, in your prepared dwelling-place, which you prepared, O Lord, the sanctuary, O Lord, which your hands made ready."

**Exodus 15:18**

"The Lord reigns forever and beyond."

**Exodus 15:19**

For Pharaoh's horse went in with chariots and riders into the sea, and the Lord brought the water of the sea upon them. But the sons of Israel traveled on dry ground through the midst of the sea.

**Exodus 15:20**

Then Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the timbrel in her hand, and all the women went out after her with timbrels and dances.

**Exodus 15:21**

And Miriam led them, saying, "Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been glorified gloriously; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea."

**Exodus 15:22**

Then Moses moved the sons of Israel away from the Red Sea and led them into the wilderness of Shur. And they went three days in the wilderness and found no water to drink.

**Exodus 15:23**

And they came to Marah, and they were not able to drink from Marah, for it was bitter. Because of this the name of that place was called Bitterness.

**Exodus 15:24**

And the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What will we drink?"

**Exodus 15:25**

Then Moses cried out to the Lord, and the Lord showed him a piece of wood, and he cast it into the water, and the water was sweetened. There he set for him ordinances and judgments, and there he tested him.

**Exodus 15:26**

And he said, "If in hearing you hear the voice of the Lord your God and do the things pleasing before him and give ear to his commands and keep all his ordinances, every sickness that I brought upon the Egyptians I will not bring upon you, for I am the Lord who heals you."

**Exodus 15:27**

And they came to Elim, and there were there twelve springs of water and seventy trunks of palm trees, and they camped there by the waters.

#### Chapter 16

**Exodus 16:1**

And they set out from Elim, and the whole assembly of the sons of Israel came into the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had come out from the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 16:2**

And the whole assembly of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron,

**Exodus 16:3**

and the sons of Israel said to them, "If only we had died, struck by the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pots of meat and ate bread to fullness. But you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger."

**Exodus 16:4**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Behold, I am raining bread for you from heaven, and the people will go out and gather what is needed for the day, day by day, so that I may test them whether they will walk in my law or not."

**Exodus 16:5**

"And it shall be on the sixth day that they will prepare what they bring in, and it will be double what they gather, day by day."

**Exodus 16:6**

And Moses and Aaron said to the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, "At evening you will know that the Lord has brought you out from the land of Egypt,"

**Exodus 16:7**

"and in the morning you will see the glory of the Lord, because he has heard your grumbling against God. And what are we, that you grumble against us?"

**Exodus 16:8**

And Moses said, "This will be when the Lord gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread in the morning to fullness, because the Lord has heard your grumbling that you grumble against us. And what are we? Your grumbling is not against us but against God."

**Exodus 16:9**

Then Moses said to Aaron, "Tell the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, Come near before God, for he has heard your grumbling."

**Exodus 16:10**

And when Aaron spoke to the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, they turned toward the wilderness, and the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud.

**Exodus 16:11**

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

**Exodus 16:12**

"I have heard the grumbling of the sons of Israel. Speak to them, saying, Toward evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread, and you shall know that I am the Lord your God."

**Exodus 16:13**

And it happened at evening that quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning, as the dew was settling around the camp,

**Exodus 16:14**

behold, over the face of the wilderness was a fine thing, like coriander seed, white like frost upon the earth.

**Exodus 16:15**

And when the sons of Israel saw it, they said one to another, "What is this?" for they did not know what it was. Then Moses said to them, "This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat."

**Exodus 16:16**

"This is the word the Lord has commanded: Gather from it, each for those assigned to him, a gomor per head, according to the number of your persons. Each with those in your tent shall gather it."

**Exodus 16:17**

And the sons of Israel did so, and some gathered much and some little.

**Exodus 16:18**

And when they measured it by the gomor, the one who had much had nothing left over, and the one who had little had no lack. Each gathered according to those assigned to him.

**Exodus 16:19**

Then Moses said to them, "Let no one leave any of it until morning."

**Exodus 16:20**

But they did not listen to Moses, and some left from it until morning, and it bred worms and stank, and Moses was embittered against them.

**Exodus 16:21**

And they gathered it morning by morning, each according to what was needed for him. But when the sun grew hot, it melted.

**Exodus 16:22**

And it happened on the sixth day that they gathered what was needed double, two gomors for one person. Then all the rulers of the assembly came in and reported it to Moses.

**Exodus 16:23**

And Moses said to them, "This is the word the Lord spoke: Tomorrow is Sabbath, a holy rest to the Lord. Whatever you will bake, bake, and whatever you will boil, boil, and all that is left over leave stored up until morning."

**Exodus 16:24**

And they left some of it until morning, just as Moses commanded them, and it did not stink, nor did a worm appear in it.

**Exodus 16:25**

Then Moses said, "Eat it today, for today is Sabbath to the Lord. Today it will not be found in the field."

**Exodus 16:26**

"For six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day is Sabbath, because it will not be on that day."

**Exodus 16:27**

And it happened on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, and they found none.

**Exodus 16:28**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to listen to my commands and my law?"

**Exodus 16:29**

"See, for the Lord has given you this day as the Sabbath. Because of this he has given you on the sixth day bread for two days. Let each stay in his houses. Let no one go out from his place on the seventh day."

**Exodus 16:30**

And the people Sabbathed on the seventh day.

**Exodus 16:31**

And the sons of Israel called its name Man. It was like white coriander seed, and its taste was like a cake in honey.

**Exodus 16:32**

Then Moses said, "This is the word the Lord commanded: Fill the gomor with Man for storage throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread that you ate in the wilderness when the Lord brought you out from the land of Egypt."

**Exodus 16:33**

And Moses said to Aaron, "Take one golden jar and put into it a full gomor of Man, and you shall place it before God for preservation throughout your generations,"

**Exodus 16:34**

just as the Lord commanded Moses, and Aaron placed it before the testimony for preservation.

**Exodus 16:35**

And the sons of Israel ate Man forty years, until they came into an inhabited land. They ate Man until they came to the region of Phoenicia.

**Exodus 16:36**

Now the gomor was the tenth part of three measures.

#### Chapter 17

**Exodus 17:1**

And the whole assembly of the sons of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin, by their encampments, according to the word of the Lord, and they camped in Rephidim. But there was no water for the people to drink.

**Exodus 17:2**

And the people reviled Moses, saying, "Give us water, so that we may drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you revile me, and why do you test the Lord?"

**Exodus 17:3**

And there the people thirsted for water, and there the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "Why is this? Have you brought us up out from Egypt to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?"

**Exodus 17:4**

Then Moses cried out to the Lord, saying, "What shall I do with this people? A little more and they will stone me."

**Exodus 17:5**

And the Lord said to Moses, "Go on ahead of this people, and take with yourself some of the elders of the people. And the rod with which you struck the river, take in your hand and go."

**Exodus 17:6**

"Look, I am standing before you there on the rock in Horeb, and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out from it, and my people will drink." And Moses did so before the sons of Israel.

**Exodus 17:7**

And he called the name of that place Testing and Reviling, because of the reviling of the sons of Israel and because of their testing the Lord, saying, "Is the Lord among us or not?"

**Exodus 17:8**

Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.

**Exodus 17:9**

And Moses said to Joshua, "Choose for yourself strong men and go out and draw up in battle array against Amalek tomorrow. And look, I will stand on the top of the hill, and the rod of God will be in my hand."

**Exodus 17:10**

And Joshua did just as Moses told him, and he went out and drew up in battle array against Amalek. And Moses and Aaron and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

**Exodus 17:11**

And it happened that whenever Moses lifted up his hands, Israel prevailed, and whenever he let down his hands, Amalek prevailed.

**Exodus 17:12**

But Moses' hands were heavy, and taking a stone they put it under him, and he sat on it. And Aaron and Hur were supporting his hands, one from this side and one from that side, and Moses' hands became supported until the setting of the sun.

**Exodus 17:13**

And Joshua routed Amalek and all his people with the slaughter of the sword.

**Exodus 17:14**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Write this as a memorial in a book, and put it into the ears of Joshua, for in wiping out I will wipe out the memorial of Amalek from under heaven."

**Exodus 17:15**

And Moses built an altar to the Lord and called its name, "The Lord is my refuge,"

**Exodus 17:16**

for with hidden hand the Lord wages war against Amalek from generation to generation.

#### Chapter 18

**Exodus 18:1**

And Jethro, priest of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses, heard all that the Lord had done for Israel, his own people, for the Lord had brought Israel out from Egypt.

**Exodus 18:2**

And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took Zipporah, the wife of Moses, after her sending away.

**Exodus 18:3**

and her two sons. The name of one was Gershom, saying, "I was a resident alien in a foreign land,"

**Exodus 18:4**

and the name of the second was Eliezer, saying, "For the God of my father is my helper, and he rescued me from the hand of Pharaoh."

**Exodus 18:5**

And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, and his sons and wife, came out to Moses into the wilderness where he had camped at the mountain of God.

**Exodus 18:6**

And word was reported to Moses, saying, "Look, your father-in-law Jethro is coming to you, and your wife and your two sons with him."

**Exodus 18:7**

Then Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down to him and kissed him, and they greeted one another and brought him into the tent.

**Exodus 18:8**

And Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the Lord had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, and all the hardship that had come upon them on the way, and that the Lord had rescued them from the hand of Pharaoh and from the hand of the Egyptians.

**Exodus 18:9**

And Jethro was amazed at all the good things that the Lord had done for them, that he had rescued them from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharaoh.

**Exodus 18:10**

And Jethro said, "Blessed be the Lord, because he has rescued his people from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharaoh."

**Exodus 18:11**

"Now I know that the Lord is great above all the gods, because in this matter they acted arrogantly against them."

**Exodus 18:12**

And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took whole burnt offerings and sacrifices to God. And Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses before God.

**Exodus 18:13**

And it happened on the next day that Moses sat to judge the people, and all the people stood by Moses from morning until evening.

**Exodus 18:14**

And when Jethro saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he said, "What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone while all the people stand by you from morning until evening?"

**Exodus 18:15**

And Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to seek judgment from God."

**Exodus 18:16**

"For whenever they have a dispute and come to me, I decide each one and instruct them in the ordinances of God and his law."

**Exodus 18:17**

Then the father-in-law of Moses said to him, "This thing that you are doing is not right."

**Exodus 18:18**

"With ruin you will wear away, with unbearable exhaustion, both you and all this people that is with you. This thing is too heavy for you. You will not be able to do it alone."

**Exodus 18:19**

"Now then, listen to me, and I will advise you, and God will be with you. Be for the people in the things toward God, and you shall bring their words to God."

**Exodus 18:20**

"And you shall testify to them the ordinances of God and his law, and you shall make known to them the ways in which they shall walk and the works that they shall do."

**Exodus 18:21**

"And you, select for yourself from all the people able men, God-fearing men, righteous men, hating arrogance, and you shall appoint them over them as commanders of thousands and hundreds and fifties and tens."

**Exodus 18:22**

"And they shall judge the people at every hour. The over-large matter they shall bring to you, but the small cases they shall judge themselves, and they shall lighten the load from you and help you."

**Exodus 18:23**

"If you do this thing, God will strengthen you, and you will be able to stand, and all this people will come to its own place with peace."

**Exodus 18:24**

And Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he said to him.

**Exodus 18:25**

And Moses chose able men from all Israel and made them over the people as commanders of thousands and hundreds and fifties and tens.

**Exodus 18:26**

And they judged the people at every hour. Every over-large matter they brought to Moses, but every light matter they judged themselves.

**Exodus 18:27**

Then Moses sent away his father-in-law, and he went to his own land.

#### Chapter 19

**Exodus 19:1**

And in the third month of the departure of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, on this day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.

**Exodus 19:2**

And they set out from Rephidim and came into the wilderness of Sinai, and Israel camped there opposite the mountain.

**Exodus 19:3**

And Moses went up to the mountain of God, and God called to him from the mountain, saying, "These things you shall say to the house of Jacob, and you shall announce to the sons of Israel:"

**Exodus 19:4**

"You yourselves have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and I took you up as on the wings of eagles, and I brought you near to myself."

**Exodus 19:5**

"And now, if in hearing you hear my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be to me a people of special possession from among all the nations, for the whole earth is mine."

**Exodus 19:6**

"And you shall be to me a royal priesthood and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the sons of Israel."

**Exodus 19:7**

Then Moses came and called the elders of the people and set before them all these words that God had commanded him.

**Exodus 19:8**

And all the people answered with one accord and said, "All that God has spoken, we will do and we will hear." And Moses carried the words of the people up to God.

**Exodus 19:9**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "Look, I am coming to you in a pillar of cloud, so that the people may hear me speaking with you and may trust you forever." And Moses reported the words of the people to the Lord.

**Exodus 19:10**

And the Lord said to Moses, "Go down and solemnly warn the people, and purify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments,"

**Exodus 19:11**

"and let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day the Lord will come down upon Mount Sinai before all the people."

**Exodus 19:12**

"And you shall mark off the people all around, saying, Take heed for yourselves not to go up on the mountain or touch any part of it. Everyone who touches the mountain shall surely die."

**Exodus 19:13**

"No hand shall touch him, for he shall certainly be stoned with stones or shot through with a missile. Whether beast or man, he shall not live. When the voices and the trumpets and the cloud depart from the mountain, they may come up on the mountain."

**Exodus 19:14**

Then Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified them, and they washed their garments.

**Exodus 19:15**

And he said to the people, "Be ready for three days. Do not come near a woman."

**Exodus 19:16**

And it happened on the third day, when morning came, that there were voices and lightnings and a gloomy cloud on Mount Sinai. The sound of the trumpet rang out loudly, and all the people in the camp were terrified.

**Exodus 19:17**

And Moses brought the people out from the camp to meet God, and they stood beneath the mountain.

**Exodus 19:18**

And Mount Sinai smoked all over because God had come down upon it in fire, and the smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and all the people were exceedingly astonished.

**Exodus 19:19**

And the sounds of the trumpet kept advancing, growing much stronger. Moses was speaking, and God answered him with a voice.

**Exodus 19:20**

And the Lord came down on Mount Sinai, on the top of the mountain, and the Lord called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.

**Exodus 19:21**

And God said to Moses, saying, "Go down and solemnly warn the people lest they draw near to God to gaze, and a multitude from among them fall."

**Exodus 19:22**

"And let the priests who draw near to the Lord God sanctify themselves, lest the Lord break out against some of them."

**Exodus 19:23**

And Moses said to God, "The people will not be able to come up to Mount Sinai, for you yourself solemnly warned us, saying, Mark off the mountain and sanctify it."

**Exodus 19:24**

And the Lord said to him, "Go, go down, and then come up, you and Aaron with you. But let not the priests and the people force their way to come up to God, lest the Lord destroy some of them."

**Exodus 19:25**

Then Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

#### Chapter 20

**Exodus 20:1**

And the Lord spoke all these words, saying,

**Exodus 20:2**

"I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery."

**Exodus 20:3**

"No other gods shall be yours besides me."

**Exodus 20:4**

"You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor any likeness of whatever is in heaven above and whatever is in the earth below and whatever is in the waters beneath the earth."

**Exodus 20:5**

"You shall not bow down to them, nor indeed serve them, for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying fathers' sins upon children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,"

**Exodus 20:6**

"and showing mercy into thousands for those who love me and keep my commandments."

**Exodus 20:7**

"You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will certainly not clear the one who takes his name in vain."

**Exodus 20:8**

"Remember the day of the Sabbaths, to keep it holy."

**Exodus 20:9**

"For six days you shall work and do all your works,"

**Exodus 20:10**

"but the seventh day is Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall do no work, you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, your ox and your pack animal and every beast of yours and the newcomer staying among you."

**Exodus 20:11**

"For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them, and he rested on the seventh day. Therefore the Lord blessed the seventh day and sanctified it."

**Exodus 20:12**

"Honor your father and your mother, so that it may go well for you and so that you may become long-lived on the good land that the Lord your God is giving you."

**Exodus 20:13**

"You shall not commit adultery."

**Exodus 20:14**

"You shall not steal."

**Exodus 20:15**

"You shall not murder."

**Exodus 20:16**

"You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor, false testimony."

**Exodus 20:17**

"You shall not desire your neighbor's wife. You shall not desire your neighbor's house, nor his field, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his pack animal, nor any beast of his, nor whatever belongs to your neighbor."

**Exodus 20:18**

And all the people were seeing the voice and the torches and the sound of the trumpet and the mountain smoking. And all the people were afraid and stood far off,

**Exodus 20:19**

and they said to Moses, "You speak to us, and let not God speak to us, lest we die."

**Exodus 20:20**

And Moses said to them, "Take courage, for God has come for the sake of testing you, so that his fear may be among you, so that you may not sin."

**Exodus 20:21**

And the people stood far off, but Moses entered into the gloom where God was.

**Exodus 20:22**

Then the Lord said to Moses, "These things you shall say to the house of Jacob, and you shall announce to the sons of Israel: You yourselves have seen that from heaven I have spoken to you."

**Exodus 20:23**

"You shall not make for yourselves gods of silver, and gods of gold you shall not make for yourselves."

**Exodus 20:24**

"You shall make me an altar of earth, and upon it you shall sacrifice your whole burnt offerings and your offerings of salvation, your sheep and your calves. In every place where I cause my name to be called, I will come to you and bless you."

**Exodus 20:25**

"But if you make me an altar of stones, you shall not build them cut, for you have laid your tool upon them, and they have been defiled."

**Exodus 20:26**

"And you shall not go up by steps to my altar, so that you do not uncover your indecency upon it."

#### Chapter 21

**Exodus 21:1**

And these are the ordinances that you shall set before them.

**Exodus 21:2**

If you buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve you, and in the seventh year he shall go out free for nothing.

**Exodus 21:3**

If he comes in alone, he shall also go out alone. But if his wife comes in with him, his wife shall also go out with him.

**Exodus 21:4**

But if his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and the children shall belong to his master, and he alone shall go out.

**Exodus 21:5**

But if the servant answers and says, "I have loved my master and my wife and my children. I will not run away free,"

**Exodus 21:6**

then his master shall bring him to the judgment-seat of God. Then he shall bring him to the door, to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.

**Exodus 21:7**

If someone sells his own daughter as a household servant, she shall not go out as the female servants go out.

**Exodus 21:8**

If she does not please her master, to whom she had been promised, he shall let her be redeemed. He has no authority to sell her to a foreign nation, because he has broken faith with her.

**Exodus 21:9**

But if he promises her to his son, he shall treat her according to the right of daughters.

**Exodus 21:10**

But if he takes another woman for himself, he shall not deprive her of what is needed, or of clothing, or of her companionship.

**Exodus 21:11**

But if he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out free, without money.

**Exodus 21:12**

If someone strikes a person and he dies, let him certainly be put to death.

**Exodus 21:13**

But if he did not do it willingly, and God delivered him into his hands, I will give you a place where the killer may flee.

**Exodus 21:14**

But if someone attacks his neighbor to kill him with deceit, and he flees to my altar, you shall take him from there to put him to death.

**Exodus 21:15**

Whoever strikes his father or his mother, let him certainly be put to death.

**Exodus 21:16**

Whoever reviles his father or his mother shall surely die.

**Exodus 21:17**

Whoever steals one of the sons of Israel, and after overpowering him sells him, and he is found in his hand, let him certainly be put to death.

**Exodus 21:18**

If two men revile each other and one strikes his neighbor with a stone or with his fist and he does not die but is laid in bed,

**Exodus 21:19**

if the man rises and walks about outside on his staff, the one who struck him shall be clear. Yet he shall pay for his idleness and for his healing.

**Exodus 21:20**

If someone strikes his male servant or his female servant with a rod and the servant dies under his hands, let justice be exacted.

**Exodus 21:21**

But if the servant lives a day or two, he shall not be avenged, for he is his money.

**Exodus 21:22**

If two men fight and strike a pregnant woman, and her child comes out not yet formed, he shall pay a penalty according as the woman's husband lays upon him. He shall pay with assessment.

**Exodus 21:23**

But if it is formed, he shall give life for life,

**Exodus 21:24**

eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

**Exodus 21:25**

burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.

**Exodus 21:26**

If someone strikes the eye of his servant or the eye of his female servant and blinds it, he shall send them out free for their eye.

**Exodus 21:27**

And if he knocks out the tooth of his servant or the tooth of his female servant, he shall send them out free for their tooth.

**Exodus 21:28**

If a bull gores a man or a woman and they die, the bull shall be stoned with stones, and its flesh shall not be eaten. But the bull's owner shall be clear.

**Exodus 21:29**

But if the bull has been a gorer since yesterday and the third day, and they have testified to its owner and he has not confined it, and it kills a man or a woman, the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall also die.

**Exodus 21:30**

But if a ransom is laid upon him, he shall give a ransom for his life, whatever they lay upon him.

**Exodus 21:31**

If it gores a son or a daughter, they shall do to him according to this ordinance.

**Exodus 21:32**

But if the bull gores a male servant or a female servant, he shall give thirty silver didrachms to their master, and the bull shall be stoned.

**Exodus 21:33**

If someone opens a pit or quarries a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls in there,

**Exodus 21:34**

the owner of the pit shall make compensation. He shall give silver to their owner, and the dead animal shall be his.

**Exodus 21:35**

If one person's bull gores the bull of his neighbor and it dies, they shall sell the living bull and divide its silver, and they shall divide the dead one.

**Exodus 21:36**

But if it is known that the bull has been a gorer since yesterday and the third day, and testimony had been made to its owner, and he did not confine it, he shall repay bull for bull, and the dead one shall be his.

**Exodus 21:37**

If someone steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall repay five oxen for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.

#### Chapter 22

**Exodus 22:1**

If the thief is found in the breach and is struck and dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.

**Exodus 22:2**

But if the sun rises on him, there is guilt. He shall die in return. But if he has nothing, let him be sold for what was stolen.

**Exodus 22:3**

If the stolen thing is found alive in his hand, whether donkey or sheep, he shall repay them double.

**Exodus 22:4**

If someone lets a field or vineyard be grazed and lets his beast graze another field, he shall repay from his own field according to its produce. But if it grazes the whole field, he shall repay the best of his own field and the best of his vineyard.

**Exodus 22:5**

If fire goes out and finds thorns and sets aflame a threshing floor or sheaves or a field, the one who kindled the fire shall make repayment.

**Exodus 22:6**

If someone gives his neighbor silver or goods to keep, and it is stolen from the man's house, if the thief is found, he shall repay double.

**Exodus 22:7**

But if the thief is not found, the master of the house shall come before God and swear that he has surely not acted wickedly against any part of his neighbor's deposit.

**Exodus 22:8**

In every matter of wrongdoing, concerning an ox and a beast of burden and a sheep and a garment and every alleged loss, whatever it may be, the judgment of both shall come before God, and the one convicted through God shall repay double to his neighbor.

**Exodus 22:9**

If someone gives his neighbor a beast of burden or an ox or a sheep or any livestock to keep, and it is injured or dies or is taken captive, and no one knows,

**Exodus 22:10**

an oath of God shall be between both of them, that he surely has not acted wickedly against any part of his neighbor's deposit. So its owner shall accept it, and he shall not repay.

**Exodus 22:11**

But if it is stolen from him, he shall repay its owner.

**Exodus 22:12**

But if it becomes beast-torn, he shall bring it as evidence of the prey, and he shall not repay.

**Exodus 22:13**

If someone borrows from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies or is taken captive, and its owner is not with it, he shall repay.

**Exodus 22:14**

But if the owner is with it, he shall not repay. But if it is hired, it shall stand for its hire.

**Exodus 22:15**

If someone entices an unbetrothed virgin and lies with her, he shall surely pay the bride-price and take her as wife for himself.

**Exodus 22:16**

But if her father utterly refuses and does not wish to give her to him as wife, he shall pay silver to her father according to the bride-price of virgins.

**Exodus 22:17**

You shall not preserve sorcerers alive.

**Exodus 22:18**

Everyone who lies with an animal, you shall certainly put them to death.

**Exodus 22:19**

The one sacrificing to gods shall be destroyed by death, except to the Lord alone.

**Exodus 22:20**

You shall not mistreat a newcomer, nor oppress him, for you were newcomers in the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 22:21**

You shall mistreat no widow or orphan.

**Exodus 22:22**

But if by evil-treatment you mistreat them, and crying out they cry to me, I will surely hear their voice.

**Exodus 22:23**

And I will become angry with wrath and kill you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows and your children orphans.

**Exodus 22:24**

If you lend silver to your poor brother beside you, you shall not press him hard, nor lay interest upon him.

**Exodus 22:25**

If you take your neighbor's garment as a pledge, you shall give it back to him before sunset.

**Exodus 22:26**

For this alone is his covering; this is the garment of his nakedness. In what shall he sleep? So if he cries out to me, I will hear him, for I am merciful.

**Exodus 22:27**

You shall not revile gods, and you shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.

**Exodus 22:28**

You shall not delay the firstfruits of your threshing floor and your winepress. You shall give me the firstborn of your sons.

**Exodus 22:29**

So you shall do with your ox and your sheep and your beast of burden. Seven days it shall be under its mother, and on the eighth day you shall give it to me.

**Exodus 22:30**

And you shall be holy men to me, and you shall not eat flesh torn by beasts; you shall throw it to the dog.

#### Chapter 23

**Exodus 23:1**

You shall not accept a vain report. You shall not join with the unjust to become an unjust witness.

**Exodus 23:2**

You shall not be with the many for evil. You shall not side with a crowd to turn aside with the many so as to bend justice.

**Exodus 23:3**

And you shall not spare a poor man in judgment.

**Exodus 23:4**

If you meet your enemy's ox or his beast of burden wandering, you shall surely turn it back and return it to him.

**Exodus 23:5**

If you see your enemy's beast of burden fallen under its load, you shall not pass it by, but you shall help raise it with him.

**Exodus 23:6**

You shall not pervert the judgment of a poor man in his case.

**Exodus 23:7**

Keep far from every unjust word. You shall not kill the innocent and the righteous, and you shall not justify the ungodly for gifts.

**Exodus 23:8**

You shall not take gifts, for gifts blind the eyes of those who see and destroy just words.

**Exodus 23:9**

You shall not oppress a newcomer, for you know the soul of the newcomer, because you were newcomers in the land of Egypt.

**Exodus 23:10**

Six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce.

**Exodus 23:11**

But in the seventh you shall make a release and let it rest, and the poor of your nation shall eat, and what they leave the wild beasts shall eat. So you shall do with your vineyard and your oliveyard.

**Exodus 23:12**

Six days you shall do your works, but on the seventh day there shall be rest, so that your ox and your beast of burden may rest, and the son of your female servant and the newcomer may be refreshed.

**Exodus 23:13**

Guard all that I have said to you, and you shall not mention the name of other gods, nor shall it be heard from your mouth.

**Exodus 23:14**

Three times of the year celebrate a feast to me.

**Exodus 23:15**

Keep the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, just as I commanded you, at the time of the month of new grain, for in it you came out from Egypt. You shall not appear before me empty.

**Exodus 23:16**

And you shall keep the feast of harvest of the first produce of your labors, whatever you sow in your field, and the feast of completion at the going out of the year, in the gathering of your labors from your field.

**Exodus 23:17**

Three times of the year every male of yours shall appear before the Lord your God.

**Exodus 23:18**

For when I cast out nations from before you and widen your borders, you shall not sacrifice the blood of my sacrifice with leaven, nor shall the fat of my feast lie down until morning.

**Exodus 23:19**

You shall bring the firstfruits of the first produce of your land into the house of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother's milk.

**Exodus 23:20**

And behold, I send my angel before your face to keep you on the way, so that he may bring you into the land that I have prepared for you.

**Exodus 23:21**

Pay attention to yourself and listen to him, and do not disobey him, for he will never yield to you, because my name is upon him.

**Exodus 23:22**

If you truly hear my voice and do all that I command you and keep my covenant, you shall be for me a people of special possession out of all nations, for all the earth is mine. And you shall be for me a royal priesthood and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the sons of Israel. If you truly hear my voice and do all that I say to you, I will be hostile to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.

**Exodus 23:23**

For my angel shall go leading you and bring you to the Amorite and Hittite and Perizzite and Canaanite and Girgashite and Hivite and Jebusite, and I will wipe them out.

**Exodus 23:24**
