**Judges 16:24**

And the people saw him and praised their gods and said, Our god gave our enemy into our hand, the one ravaging our land, who multiplied our wounded.

**Judges 16:25**

And it came to be when their heart grew good, they said, Call Samson out of the prison house and let him play before us. And they called Samson out of the prison house, and they mocked him, and they set him between the two pillars.

**Judges 16:26**

And Samson said to the young servant guiding his hand, Let me rest now and let me feel the pillars upon which the house has been supported, and I will lean upon them. And the boy did so.

**Judges 16:27**

And the house was full of men and women, and all the satraps of the foreigners were there, and on the roof were about three thousand men and women looking on as Samson was mocked.

**Judges 16:28**

And Samson cried out to the Lord and said, Lord, Lord, remember me and strengthen me now, only this once, and I will exact one vengeance for my two eyes from the foreigners.

**Judges 16:29**

And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house had been supported and leaned upon them, one with his right hand and one with his left.

**Judges 16:30**

And Samson said, Let my soul die with the foreigners. And he bent in strength, and the house fell upon the satraps and upon all the people in it, and the dead whom Samson killed in his death were more than those whom he killed in his life.

**Judges 16:31**

And his brothers and all the house of his father went down and took him and went up and buried him between Zorah and between Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.

#### Chapter 17

**Judges 17:1**

And there was a man from the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name was Micah.

**Judges 17:2**

And he said to his mother, The eleven hundred silver pieces taken from you, about which you pronounced an oath and spoke in my ears, behold, the silver is with me; I took it. And his mother said, Blessed be my son to the Lord.

**Judges 17:3**

And he returned the eleven hundred silver pieces to his mother, and his mother said, With consecration I consecrated the silver to the Lord from my hand alone, to make a carved image and a molten image, and now I will return them to you and give it back to you.

**Judges 17:4**

And he returned the silver to his mother, and his mother took two hundred silver pieces and gave it to the metalworker, and he made it into a carved image and a molten image, and it came to be in the house of Micah.

**Judges 17:5**

And the man Micah had a house of God, and he made an ephod and teraphim and filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became priest for him.

**Judges 17:6**

In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was good in his own eyes.

**Judges 17:7**

And there was a young man from Bethlehem, clan of Judah, from the family of Judah, and he was a Levite, and he was staying there as a resident.

**Judges 17:8**

And the man went from the city of Judah, from Bethlehem, to reside wherever he might find, and he came to the hill-country of Ephraim, as far as the house of Micah, to make his way.

**Judges 17:9**

And Micah said to him, From where do you come? And he said to him, I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to reside wherever I may find.

**Judges 17:10**

And Micah said to him, Stay with me and become to me as father and as priest, and I will give you ten silver pieces for days, and a pair of garments, and your living. And the Levite went.

**Judges 17:11**

And he began to reside with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.

**Judges 17:12**

And Micah filled the hand of the Levite, and the young man became his priest and was in the house of Micah.

**Judges 17:13**

And Micah said, Now I know that the Lord has done me good, because the Levite has become my priest.

#### Chapter 18

**Judges 18:1**

In those days there was no king in Israel, and in those days the tribe of Dan was seeking for itself an inheritance to dwell in, because until those days no inheritance had fallen to it in the midst of the tribes of Israel.

**Judges 18:2**

And the sons of Dan sent from their families five men from among them, sons of strength, from Zorah and Eshtaol, to inspect the land and to search it out, and they said to them, Go and search out the land. And they came to the hill-country of Ephraim as far as the house of Micah and rested there.

**Judges 18:3**

While they were by the house of Micah, they recognized the voice of the young Levite, and they turned aside there and said to him, Who brought you here, and what are you doing in this place, and what do you have here?

**Judges 18:4**

And he said to them, Thus and thus Micah did for me, and he hired me, and I became his priest.

**Judges 18:5**

And they said to him, Inquire now of God, and we will know whether our way on which we are going will prosper.

**Judges 18:6**

And the priest said to them, Go in peace. Before the Lord is your way in which you are going.

**Judges 18:7**

And the five men went and came to Laish and saw the people dwelling in it, sitting in confidence according to the judgment of the Sidonians, being quiet in confidence and unable to speak a word, because they are far from Sidon and have no dealings with Syria.

**Judges 18:8**

And the five men came to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them, Why are you sitting here?

**Judges 18:9**

And they said, Rise and let us go up against them, because we entered and walked through the land as far as Laish and saw the people dwelling in it in confidence according to the custom of the Sidonians, and they are far from Sidon and have no dealings with Syria. But rise and let us go up against them, because we found the land, and behold, it is very good, and you keep silent. Do not hesitate to go, to enter and inherit the land.

**Judges 18:10**

When you enter, you will come to a trusting people, and the land is broad, because God has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is in the land.

**Judges 18:11**

And from the family of Dan, from Zorah and Eshtaol, six hundred men girded with the weapons of war set out.

**Judges 18:12**

And they went up and encamped in Kirjathjearim in Judah. Therefore that place was called Camp of Dan until this day; behold, it is behind Kirjathjearim.

**Judges 18:13**

They passed on from there and came to the hill-country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.

**Judges 18:14**

And the five men going to inspect the land answered and said to their brothers, Do you know that in these houses there are an ephod and teraphim and a carved image and a molten image? And now know what you will do.

**Judges 18:15**

And they turned aside there and entered into the house of the young Levite, into the house of Micah, and greeted him.

**Judges 18:16**

And the six hundred men girded with the weapons of war, from the sons of Dan, stood by the doorway of the gate.

**Judges 18:17**

And the five men going to inspect the land went up there and took the carved image and the ephod and the teraphim and the molten image, while the priest stood by the doorway of the gate and the six hundred men girded with the weapons of war.

**Judges 18:18**

And these entered into the house of Micah and took the carved image and the ephod and the teraphim and the molten image. And the priest said to them, What are you doing?

**Judges 18:19**

And they said to him, Be silent; put your hand upon your mouth and come with us, and you shall be to us as father and as priest. Is it not better for you to be priest to the house of one man than for you to become priest to a tribe and a family in Israel?

**Judges 18:20**

And the heart of the priest was gladdened, and he took the ephod and the teraphim and the carved image and the molten image and entered into the midst of the people.

**Judges 18:21**

And they turned and went away, and they placed the household and the possessions and his glorious things before them.

**Judges 18:22**

And when they had gone a good distance from the house of Micah, behold, Micah and the men with the house with Micah cried out after the sons of Dan.

**Judges 18:23**

And the sons of Dan turned their faces and said to Micah, What is wrong with you, that you cried out?

**Judges 18:24**

And Micah said, My carved image that I made for myself you took, and the priest, and you went away. And what remains to me now? And why do you say to me, Why do you cry out?

**Judges 18:25**

And the sons of Dan said to him, Let your voice not be heard with us, lest bitter-souled men fall upon you and you lose your life and the life of your household.

**Judges 18:26**

And the sons of Dan went on their way, and Micah saw that they were stronger than he, and he turned aside and returned to his house.

**Judges 18:27**

And they took what Micah had made and the priest who was his, and they came to Laish, to a people quiet and confident, and struck them with the edge of the sword and burned the city with fire.

**Judges 18:28**

And there was no deliverer, because it is far from the Sidonians, and they have no dealings with men, and it is in the valley that belongs to the house of Rehob. And they built the city and dwelt in it.

**Judges 18:29**

And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of their father who was born to Israel, though the name of the city formerly was Laish.

**Judges 18:30**

And the sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image of Micah, and Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Moses, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.

**Judges 18:31**

And they set up for themselves the carved image of Micah that he made all the days that the house of God was in Shiloh.

#### Chapter 19

**Judges 19:1**

And it came to be in those days, and there was no king in Israel, and there was a Levite man residing in the flanks of the hill-country of Ephraim, and the man took for himself a concubine wife from Bethlehem of Judah.

**Judges 19:2**

And his concubine became angry with him and went away from him to the house of her father in Bethlehem of Judah and was there four months.

**Judges 19:3**

And her husband rose and went after her to speak to her heart, to reconcile her to himself and bring her back again to him, with his servant with him and a pair of pack animals. And he went to the house of her father, and the father of the young woman saw him and came joyfully to meet him.

**Judges 19:4**

And his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, brought him in and he stayed with him three days, and they ate and drank and slept there.

**Judges 19:5**

And it came to be on the fourth day, they rose early in the morning, and he arose to depart, and the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread, and after this you may go.

**Judges 19:6**

And they sat and both of them ate together and drank, and the father of the young woman said to the man, Begin now, lodge overnight, and let your heart be glad.

**Judges 19:7**

And the man rose to depart, and his father-in-law constrained him, and again he lodged there.

**Judges 19:8**

And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart, and the father of the young woman said, Strengthen your heart with bread and make camp until the day declines. And both of them ate and drank.

**Judges 19:9**

And the man rose to depart, he and his concubine and his servant, and his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, Behold now, toward evening the day has declined; lodge here still today, and let your heart be glad, and rise early tomorrow for your journey, and you will go to your tent.

**Judges 19:10**

But the man was not willing to lodge, and he rose and went away and came opposite Jebus, this is Jerusalem, and with him was a pair of saddled pack animals, and his concubine was with him.

**Judges 19:11**

While they were still near Jebus and the day had declined greatly, the servant said to his master, Come now and let us turn aside into this city of the Jebusite and lodge in it.

**Judges 19:12**

And his master said to him, I will certainly not turn aside into a city of foreigners who are not of the sons of Israel, but we will pass on as far as Gibeah.

**Judges 19:13**

And he said to his servant, Come and let us enter one of the places and lodge in Gibeah or in Ramah.

**Judges 19:14**

And they passed by and went on, for the sun set near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.

**Judges 19:15**

And they turned aside there to enter to lodge in Gibeah, and they entered and sat in the square of the city, and there was no man bringing them into the house to lodge.

**Judges 19:16**

And behold, an old man came in from his work out of the field at evening, and the man was from the hill-country of Ephraim and he resided in Gibeah, but the men of the place were sons of Benjamin.

**Judges 19:17**

And lifting up his eyes, he saw the traveling man in the square of the city, and the old man said, Where are you going and from where do you come?

**Judges 19:18**

And he said to him, We are passing through from Bethlehem of Judah to the flanks of the hill-country of Ephraim; I am from there, and I went to Bethlehem of Judah, and I am turning back to my house, and there is no man bringing me into the house.

**Judges 19:19**

And indeed there is straw and fodder for our donkeys, and there is bread and wine for me and for your maidservant and for the servant with your servants; there is no lack of anything.

**Judges 19:20**

And the old man said, Peace to you. Only let all your lack be upon me; only do not lodge in the square.

**Judges 19:21**

And he brought him into his house and fed his pack animals, and they washed their feet and ate and drank.

**Judges 19:22**

And while their hearts were gladdened, behold, the men of the city, sons of lawlessness, surrounded the house and beat on the door and said to the man, the master of the house, the old man, saying, Bring out the man who entered your house, so that we may know him.

**Judges 19:23**

And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, No, brothers, do not do evil, after this man has entered my house do not do this folly.

**Judges 19:24**

Behold, my virgin daughter and his concubine, I will bring them out now, and humble them and do to them what is good in your eyes, but to this man do not do this word of folly.

**Judges 19:25**

And the men were not willing to listen to him, and the man took hold of his concubine and brought her out to them outside, and they knew her and abused her all night until morning and sent her away when dawn was rising.

**Judges 19:26**

And the woman came toward morning and fell by the door of the gate of the man's house where her master was, until it became light.

**Judges 19:27**

And her master rose in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way, and behold, his concubine wife had fallen by the door, and her hands were on the threshold.

**Judges 19:28**

And he said to her, Rise and let us go. And she did not answer him, but had died. And he lifted her onto the pack animal, and the man rose and went to his place.

**Judges 19:29**

And he entered into his house and took the sword and took hold of his concubine and cut her up according to her bones into twelve parts and sent them into all the tribes of Israel.

**Judges 19:30**

And it came to be, everyone seeing said, Such a thing neither happened nor was seen from the day the sons of Israel came up from Egypt until this day. And he commanded the men to whom he sent them, saying, Thus you shall say to every man of Israel: Has this matter happened from the day the sons of Israel came up from Egypt until this day? Set counsel for yourselves about her and speak.

#### Chapter 20

**Judges 20:1**

And all the sons of Israel went out, and all the congregation was assembled as one man from Dan and as far as Beersheba and the land of Gilead, to the Lord at Mizpah.

**Judges 20:2**

And the whole assembly of the people, all the tribes of Israel, stood in the gathering of the people of God, four hundred thousand foot men drawing sword.

**Judges 20:3**

And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to the Lord at Mizpah. And the sons of Israel said, Speak, where did this evil happen?

**Judges 20:4**

And the Levite man, husband of the murdered woman, answered and said, I came to Gibeah of Benjamin, I and my concubine, to lodge.

**Judges 20:5**

And the men from Gibeah rose against me and surrounded the house against me by night, and they wanted to kill me, and they humbled my concubine and abused her, and she died.

**Judges 20:6**

And I took hold of my concubine and cut her up and sent her through every border of the inheritance of Israel, because they committed folly in Israel.

**Judges 20:7**

Behold, all of you are sons of Israel; give to yourselves word and counsel.

**Judges 20:8**

And all the people rose as one man, saying, We will not go, man into his tent, and we will not turn aside, man to his house.

**Judges 20:9**

And now this is the word that we will do to Gibeah: we will go up against it by lot.

**Judges 20:10**

And we will take ten men by the hundred and a hundred by the thousand and a thousand by the ten thousand, to take provisions for the people, for those entering to execute against Gibeah of Benjamin according to all the folly that they did in Israel.

**Judges 20:11**

And all Israel, man from the cities, was gathered as one man, coming together.

**Judges 20:12**

And the tribes of Israel sent men in every tribe of Benjamin, saying, What is this evil that happened among you?

**Judges 20:13**

And now give the men, the ungodly ones in Gibeah, the sons of Belial, and we will put them to death and remove evil from Israel. But the sons of Benjamin were not willing to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.

**Judges 20:14**

And the sons of Benjamin were gathered from their cities to Gibeah to go out to fight with the sons of Israel.

**Judges 20:15**

And the sons of Benjamin were counted on that day from the cities, twenty-five thousand men drawing sword, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah; these were counted, seven hundred chosen young men.

**Judges 20:16**

All these were ambidextrous slingers, throwing stones at a hair and not missing.

**Judges 20:17**

And every man of Israel was counted apart from the sons of Benjamin, four hundred thousand men drawing sword; all these were men of war.

**Judges 20:18**

And they arose and went up to Bethel and inquired of God, and the sons of Israel said, Who will go up for us, leading to fight with Benjamin? And the Lord said, Judah shall go up, leading.

**Judges 20:19**

And the sons of Israel rose and encamped against Gibeah.

**Judges 20:20**

And every man of Israel went out to war with Benjamin, and the men of Israel lined up with them for battle against Gibeah.

**Judges 20:21**

And the sons of Benjamin went out from the city and destroyed from Israel on that day twenty-two thousand men to the ground.

**Judges 20:22**

And the men of Israel strengthened themselves and again lined up for battle in the place where they lined up on the first day.

**Judges 20:23**

And the sons of Israel went up and wept before the Lord until evening and inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I again draw near to battle with Benjamin my brother? And the Lord said, Go up against him.

**Judges 20:24**

And the sons of Israel approached Benjamin on the second day.

**Judges 20:25**

And Benjamin went out from Gibeah to meet them on the second day and destroyed from the people eighteen thousand men to the ground, all these drawing sword.

**Judges 20:26**

And all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel and wept before the Lord and fasted on that day and offered whole burnt offerings of salvation before the Lord.

**Judges 20:27**

And the sons of Israel inquired of the Lord, and there the ark of the covenant of the Lord was in those days,

**Judges 20:28**

and Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron stood before it in those days, saying, Shall I again go out to war with the sons of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the Lord said, Go up, because tomorrow I will give him into your hand.

**Judges 20:29**

And the sons of Israel set an ambush around Gibeah.

**Judges 20:30**

And Israel lined up against Benjamin on the third day and arrayed themselves against Gibeah as once and again.

**Judges 20:31**

And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet the people and were drawn away from the city and began to strike from the people as once and again on the roads, one going up to Bethel and one going up to Gibeah in the field, about thirty men in Israel.

**Judges 20:32**

And the sons of Benjamin said, They are stumbling before us as at first. But the sons of Israel said, Let us flee and draw them out from the city to the roads.

**Judges 20:33**

And every man of Israel rose from his place and arrayed themselves at Baaltamar, and the ambush of Israel came out from its place from the west of Gibeah.

**Judges 20:34**

And opposite Gibeah came ten thousand chosen men from all Israel, and the battle became heavy, and they did not know that evil was touching them.

**Judges 20:35**

And the Lord routed Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed in Benjamin on that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men, all these drawing sword.

**Judges 20:36**

And Benjamin saw that it had been routed. And the men of Israel gave place to Benjamin because they relied on the ambush that they had set against Gibeah.

**Judges 20:37**

And the ambush rushed and spread out toward Gibeah, and the ambush went and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.

**Judges 20:38**

And the signal between the men of Israel and the ambush was for them to bring up from the city a torch of smoke.

**Judges 20:39**

And the men of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin had begun striking down wounded men in Israel, about thirty men, because they said, Surely by defeat they are defeated before us as in the former battle.

**Judges 20:40**

And the torch began to go up from the city, a pillar of smoke, and Benjamin looked behind him, and behold, the whole destruction of the city went up to heaven.

**Judges 20:41**

And the men of Israel turned back, and the man of Benjamin was terrified, and he saw that evil had touched him.

**Judges 20:42**

And they turned before the men of Israel to the way of the wilderness, and the battle overtook him, and those from the cities destroyed him in their midst.

**Judges 20:43**

And they cut down Benjamin, giving him no rest, and trampled him down as far as opposite Gibeah from the east of the sun.

**Judges 20:44**

And there fell from Benjamin eighteen thousand men; with all these were mighty men.

**Judges 20:45**

And they turned aside and fled into the wilderness to the rock Rimmon, and they gleaned five thousand men on the roads and clung after him as far as Gadaam and struck from them two thousand men.

**Judges 20:46**

And all those falling in Benjamin were twenty-five thousand men drawing sword on that day, with all these mighty men.

**Judges 20:47**

And six hundred men turned aside and fled into the wilderness to the rock Rimmon and sat at the rock Rimmon four months.

**Judges 20:48**

And the men of Israel shut in the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword from the city onward to beast and to everything found; all the cities they found they sent out in fire.

#### Chapter 21

**Judges 21:1**

And a man of Israel swore at Mizpah, saying, No man from us will give his daughter to Benjamin as wife.

**Judges 21:2**

And all the people came to Mizpah and Bethel and sat there until evening before God and lifted up their voice and wept with great weeping.

**Judges 21:3**

And they said, Why, Lord God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that one tribe should be missing in Israel today?

**Judges 21:4**

And it came to be on the next day, the people rose early and built there an altar and offered whole burnt offerings of salvation.

**Judges 21:5**

And the sons of Israel said, Who is there that did not go up in the assembly from all the tribes of Israel to the Lord? For a great oath had been made against whoever did not go up to the Lord at Mizpah, saying, He shall surely die.

**Judges 21:6**

And the sons of Israel were moved concerning Benjamin their brother and said, One tribe has been taken away from Israel today.

**Judges 21:7**

What shall we do for those left for wives, since we swore by the Lord not to give them from our daughters as wives?

**Judges 21:8**

And they said, Which one from the tribes of Israel is it that did not go up to the Lord at Mizpah? And behold, no man had come from Jabesh Gilead to the camp to the assembly.

**Judges 21:9**

And the people were counted, and behold, there was no man there from the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead.

**Judges 21:10**

And the congregation sent there twelve thousand men from the sons of might and commanded them, saying, Go and strike all dwelling in Jabesh Gilead with the edge of the sword, and the women and the people.

**Judges 21:11**

And this is the word that you shall do: every male and every woman knowing the bed of a male you shall devote to destruction.

**Judges 21:12**

And they found from the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead four hundred young women, virgins who had not known man by the bed of a male, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.

**Judges 21:13**

And all the congregation sent and spoke to Benjamin at the rock Rimmon and called them to peace.

**Judges 21:14**

And Benjamin returned to the sons of Israel at that time, and they gave them the women who had been from the women of Jabesh Gilead, and it pleased them thus.

**Judges 21:15**

And the people were moved for Benjamin because the Lord made a break in the tribes of Israel.

**Judges 21:16**

And the elders of the congregation said, What shall we do for the rest for wives, because woman has been wiped out from Benjamin?

**Judges 21:17**

And they said, A preserved inheritance belongs to Benjamin, and a tribe shall certainly not be blotted out from Israel.

**Judges 21:18**

And we are not able to give them wives from our daughters, because the sons of Israel swore, saying, Cursed is the one giving a wife to Benjamin.

**Judges 21:19**

And they said, Behold, a feast to the Lord at Shiloh from days to days, which is north of Bethel toward the rising of the sun, on the road going up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.

**Judges 21:20**

And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying, Go and lie in ambush in the vineyards.

**Judges 21:21**

And you shall watch, and behold, when the daughters of those dwelling in Shiloh come out in Shiloh to dance in dances, then you shall come out from the vineyards and each man seize for himself a wife from the daughters of Shiloh and go away to the land of Benjamin.

**Judges 21:22**

And it shall be when their fathers or their brothers come to contend with us, we will say to them, Show mercy to them, because not each man took his wife in the war. For you did not give to them at the proper time; otherwise you would have trespassed.

**Judges 21:23**

And the sons of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number from the dancers whom they carried off, and they went away and returned to their inheritance and built for themselves cities and dwelt in them.

**Judges 21:24**

And the sons of Israel walked from there at that time, each man to his tribe and to his family, and each man went away from there to his inheritance.

**Judges 21:25**

In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was right in his own eyes.

### Ruth

#### Chapter 1

**Ruth 1:1**

And it came to be in the judging of the judges, and there was famine in the land, and a man from Bethlehem of Judah went to reside in the field of Moab, he and his wife and his sons.

**Ruth 1:2**

And the name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the names of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah, and they came into the field of Moab and were there.

**Ruth 1:3**

And Elimelech, husband of Naomi, died, and she was left, she and her two sons.

**Ruth 1:4**

And they took for themselves Moabite women; the name of the one was Orpah and the name of the second Ruth, and they dwelt there about ten years.

**Ruth 1:5**

And both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left without her husband and without her two sons.

**Ruth 1:6**

And she rose, she and her two daughters-in-law, and they returned from the field of Moab, because she heard in the field of Moab that the Lord had visited his people to give them bread.

**Ruth 1:7**

And she went out from the place where she had been there, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they were going on the road to return to the land of Judah.

**Ruth 1:8**

And Naomi said to her daughters-in-law, Go now, return each to her mother's house. May the Lord deal with you in mercy, as you dealt with the dead and with me.

**Ruth 1:9**

May the Lord give to you, and may each of you find rest in the house of her husband. And she kissed them, and they lifted up their voice and wept.

**Ruth 1:10**

And they said to her, With you we will return to your people.

**Ruth 1:11**

And Naomi said, Return now, my daughters. Why are you going with me? Are there yet sons in my womb, and will they be husbands for you?

**Ruth 1:12**

Return now, my daughters, because I have grown old, not to belong to a husband. For if I said, There is hope for me to belong to a husband and bear sons,

**Ruth 1:13**

would you wait for them until they grow up? Or would you be restrained on account of them from belonging to a husband? No, my daughters, because it has become very bitter for me concerning you, because the hand of the Lord has gone out against me.

**Ruth 1:14**

And they lifted up their voice and wept again, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and returned to her people, but Ruth followed her.

**Ruth 1:15**

And Naomi said to Ruth, Behold, your fellow daughter-in-law turned back to her people and to her gods. Turn back now, you also, after your fellow daughter-in-law.

**Ruth 1:16**

And Ruth said, Do not press me to leave you or to turn back from behind you, because wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you lodge, I will lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.

**Ruth 1:17**

And wherever you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. Thus may the Lord do to me, and thus may he add, because only death will divide between me and you.

**Ruth 1:18**

And Naomi saw that she was strong in going with her, and she ceased speaking to her any more.

**Ruth 1:19**

And both of them went until they came to Bethlehem, and all the city sounded over them, and they said, Is this Naomi?

**Ruth 1:20**

And she said to them, Do not call me Naomi; call me Bitter, because the Mighty One has made things very bitter in me.

**Ruth 1:21**

I went away full, and the Lord brought me back empty. And why do you call me Naomi, when the Lord humbled me and the Mighty One afflicted me?

**Ruth 1:22**

And Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter-in-law with her, returning from the field of Moab. And they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of barley harvest.

#### Chapter 2

**Ruth 2:1**

And for Naomi there was a known man to her husband, and the man was mighty in strength from the kindred of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.

**Ruth 2:2**

And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, Let me now go to the field and glean among the ears behind whoever I find favor in his eyes. And she said to her, Go, daughter.

**Ruth 2:3**

And she went and gleaned in the field behind the reapers, and it happened by chance upon the portion of the field of Boaz, who was from the kindred of Elimelech.

**Ruth 2:4**

And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, The Lord be with you. And they said to him, May the Lord bless you.

**Ruth 2:5**

And Boaz said to his young servant set over the reapers, Whose young woman is this?

**Ruth 2:6**

And the young servant set over the reapers answered and said, She is the Moabite girl who returned with Naomi from the field of Moab.

**Ruth 2:7**

And she said, Let me now glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers. And she came and has stood from early morning until evening; she did not rest in the field except a little.

**Ruth 2:8**

And Boaz said to Ruth, Have you not heard, daughter? Do not go to another field to glean, and do not go from here. Here stay close with my girls.

**Ruth 2:9**

Let your eyes be on the field where they reap, and go behind them. Behold, I commanded the young men not to touch you, and whenever you thirst, go to the vessels and drink from where the young men draw water.

**Ruth 2:10**

And she fell on her face and bowed to the ground and said to him, Why did I find favor in your eyes, that you should notice me, when I am a foreign woman?

**Ruth 2:11**

And Boaz answered and said to her, It was fully reported to me all that you have done with your mother-in-law after the death of your husband, and how you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth and went to a people you did not know yesterday or the day before.

**Ruth 2:12**

May the Lord repay your work, and may your wage be full from the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings you came to trust.

**Ruth 2:13**

And she said, May I find favor in your eyes, lord, because you comforted me and because you spoke to the heart of your servant, and behold, I shall be as one of your maidservants.

**Ruth 2:14**

And Boaz said to her, Already it is time to eat; come here and eat of the bread and dip your morsel in the vinegar. And Ruth sat beside the reapers, and Boaz heaped parched grain for her, and she ate and was filled and left some.

**Ruth 2:15**

And she rose to glean, and Boaz commanded his young men, saying, Indeed let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not shame her.

**Ruth 2:16**

And in carrying, carry for her; indeed in dropping, drop for her from the armfuls and leave them, and she will glean, and you shall not rebuke her.

**Ruth 2:17**

And she gleaned in the field until evening and beat out what she had gleaned, and it came to be about an ephah of barley.

**Ruth 2:18**

And she took it and went into the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And Ruth brought out and gave to her what she had left from what satisfied her.

**Ruth 2:19**

And her mother-in-law said to her, Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the one noticing you. And Ruth reported to her mother-in-law where she worked and said, The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz.

**Ruth 2:20**

And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, Blessed is he by the Lord, because he did not forsake his mercy with the living and with the dead. And Naomi said to her, The man is near to us; he is from those redeeming us.

**Ruth 2:21**

And Ruth said to her mother-in-law, Indeed he also said to me, Stay close with my young men until they finish all the harvest that belongs to me.

**Ruth 2:22**

And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, It is good, daughter, that you went with his girls, and they will not meet you in another field.

**Ruth 2:23**

And Ruth stayed close to the girls of Boaz, gleaning until the barley harvest and the wheat harvest were finished, and she lived with her mother-in-law.

#### Chapter 3

**Ruth 3:1**

And Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, Daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, so that it may be well with you?

**Ruth 3:2**

And now, is not Boaz our kinsman, with whose girls you were? Behold, he winnows the threshing floor of barley tonight.

**Ruth 3:3**

And you shall wash and anoint yourself and put your garment upon yourself and go up to the threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to the man until he finishes eating and drinking.

**Ruth 3:4**

And it shall be when he lies down, you will know the place where he lies there, and you will come and uncover the things at his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what you shall do.

**Ruth 3:5**

And Ruth said to her, Everything that you say I will do.

**Ruth 3:6**

And she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law commanded her.

**Ruth 3:7**

And Boaz ate and his heart was made glad, and he came to lie down at the edge of the heap, and she came secretly and uncovered the things at his feet.

**Ruth 3:8**

And it happened at midnight, and the man was startled and disturbed, and behold, a woman lay at his feet.

**Ruth 3:9**

And he said, Who are you? And she said, I am Ruth your servant, and you shall spread your wing over your servant, because you are a redeemer.

**Ruth 3:10**

And he said, Blessed are you by the Lord God, daughter, because you made your latter mercy better than the first, by not going after young men, whether poor or rich.

**Ruth 3:11**

And now, daughter, do not fear. Everything that you say I will do for you, for every tribe of my people knows that you are a woman of strength.

**Ruth 3:12**

And now, truly I am a redeemer, and yet there is a redeemer nearer than I.

**Ruth 3:13**

Lodge here tonight, and it shall be in the morning, if he redeems you, good, let him redeem; but if he does not want to redeem you, I will redeem you, as the Lord lives. Sleep until morning.

**Ruth 3:14**

And she slept at his feet until morning, and she rose before one man could recognize his neighbor. And Boaz said, Let it not be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.

**Ruth 3:15**

And he said to her, Bring the mantle that is upon you. And she held it, and he measured six of barley and put it on her, and she went into the city.

**Ruth 3:16**

And Ruth entered to her mother-in-law, and she said, Who are you, daughter? And she told her everything that the man did for her.

**Ruth 3:17**

And she said to her, He gave me these six of barley, because he said to me, Do not enter empty to your mother-in-law.

**Ruth 3:18**

And she said, Sit, daughter, until you know how the matter will fall, for the man will certainly not rest until he completes the matter today.

#### Chapter 4

**Ruth 4:1**

And Boaz went up to the gate and sat there, and behold, the redeemer was passing by whom Boaz had spoken of, and Boaz said to him, Turn aside, sit here, hidden one. And he turned aside and sat.

**Ruth 4:2**

And Boaz took ten men from the elders of the city and said, Sit here. And they sat.

**Ruth 4:3**

And Boaz said to the redeemer, The portion of the field that belongs to our brother Elimelech is being given to Naomi who returned from the field of Moab.

**Ruth 4:4**

And I said, I will uncover your ear, saying, Buy it before those sitting here and before the elders of my people. If you redeem, redeem; but if you do not redeem, tell me, and I will know, because there is none besides you to redeem, and I am after you. And he said, I am; I will redeem.

**Ruth 4:5**

And Boaz said, On the day of your acquiring the field from the hand of Naomi, and from Ruth the Moabitess, wife of the dead man, it is necessary for you also to acquire her for yourself, so as to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance.

**Ruth 4:6**

And the redeemer said, I will not be able to redeem for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. Redeem my redemption-right for yourself, because I will not be able to redeem.

**Ruth 4:7**

And this was the custom formerly in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to establish every word: a man would loosen his sandal and give it to his neighbor redeeming his right, and this was a witness in Israel.

**Ruth 4:8**

And the redeemer said to Boaz, Acquire my redemption-right for yourself, and he loosened his sandal and gave it to him.

**Ruth 4:9**

And Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, You are witnesses today that I acquired everything of Elimelech and everything belonging to Chilion and to Mahlon from the hand of Naomi.

**Ruth 4:10**

And indeed Ruth the Moabitess, wife of Mahlon, I acquired for myself as wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, and the name of the dead shall not be blotted out from among his brothers and from the tribe of his people. You are witnesses today.

**Ruth 4:11**

And all the people at the gate said, Witnesses. And the elders said, May the Lord make your wife entering into your house like Rachel and like Leia, who both built the house of Israel, and may they make strength in Ephrathah, and may your name be in Bethlehem.

**Ruth 4:12**

And may your house become like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, from the seed that the Lord will give you from this servant girl.

**Ruth 4:13**

And Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife, and he went in to her, and the Lord gave her conception, and she bore a son.

**Ruth 4:14**

And the women said to Naomi, Blessed be the Lord, who did not leave you without a redeemer today, and may your name be called in Israel.

**Ruth 4:15**

And he shall be for you a restoring of soul and to nourish your old age, because your daughter-in-law who loved you bore him, she who is good to you beyond seven sons.

**Ruth 4:16**

And Naomi took the child and placed him in her bosom, and she became nurse to him.

**Ruth 4:17**

And the neighboring women called his name, saying, A son has been born to Naomi, and they called his name Obed; he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

**Ruth 4:18**

And these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron,

**Ruth 4:19**

and Hezron fathered Haran, and Haran fathered Amminadab,

**Ruth 4:20**

and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,

**Ruth 4:21**

and Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed,

**Ruth 4:22**

and Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

### 1 Samuel

#### Chapter 1

**1 Samuel 1:1**

There was a man from Ramathaim-Zophim, from the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, in Zuph Ephraim.

**1 Samuel 1:2**

And to him were two wives; the name of the one was Hannah and the name of the second Peninnah, and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no child.

**1 Samuel 1:3**

And the man went up from days to days from his city, from Ramathaim-Zophim, to bow down and sacrifice to the Lord God of hosts at Shiloh, and there were Eli and his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, priests of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:4**

And it came to be on the day Elkanah sacrificed, that he gave to Peninnah his wife and to her sons and her daughters portions,

**1 Samuel 1:5**

but to Hannah he gave one portion, because she had no child; yet Elkanah loved Hannah beyond this one, and the Lord had closed the things of her womb.

**1 Samuel 1:6**

Because the Lord had not given her a child, according to her affliction and according to the discouragement of her affliction, and because of this she was disheartened, because the Lord had shut the things of her womb from giving her a child.

**1 Samuel 1:7**

Thus he did year by year, when she went up to the house of the Lord, and she was disheartened and wept and did not eat.

**1 Samuel 1:8**

And Elkanah her husband said to her, Hannah. And she said to him, Behold, here I am, lord. And he said to her, What is wrong with you, that you weep, and why do you not eat, and why does your heart strike you? Am I not good to you beyond ten children?

**1 Samuel 1:9**

And Hannah rose after they ate in Shiloh and stood before the Lord, and Eli the priest was sitting upon the seat by the posts of the temple of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:10**

And she was bitter in soul and prayed to the Lord, and weeping she wept.

**1 Samuel 1:11**

And she vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, Lord, Lord my God of hosts, if you will indeed look upon the humiliation of your servant and remember me and give to your servant seed of men, then I will give him before you as a given thing until the day of his death, and wine and intoxicating drink he shall not drink, and iron shall not come upon his head.

**1 Samuel 1:12**

And it came to be, while she multiplied in praying before the Lord, Eli the priest watched her mouth.

**1 Samuel 1:13**

And she was speaking in her heart, and her lips were moving, but her voice was not heard, and Eli counted her as a drunken woman.

**1 Samuel 1:14**

And the servant Eli said to her, How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine and go from the presence of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:15**

And Hannah answered and said, No, lord. I am a woman of hard day, and I have not drunk wine or intoxicating drink, but I pour out my soul before the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:16**

Do not give your servant as a daughter of pestilence, because out of the abundance of my musing I have stretched on until now.

**1 Samuel 1:17**

And Eli answered and said to her, Go in peace. The God of Israel give you every request of yours that you asked from him.

**1 Samuel 1:18**

And she said, Your servant found favor in your eyes. And the woman went on her way and entered into her lodging and ate with her husband and drank, and her face did not fall any more.

**1 Samuel 1:19**

And they rose early in the morning and bowed down to the Lord and went on their way, and Elkanah entered into his house at Ramathaim-Zophim and knew Hannah his wife, and the Lord remembered her.

**1 Samuel 1:20**

And she conceived, and it came to be at the turn of the days, that she bore a son and called his name Samuel, and said, Because from the Lord God of hosts I asked him.

**1 Samuel 1:21**

And the man Elkanah went up, and all his house, to sacrifice in Shiloh the sacrifice of the days and his vows and all the tithes of his land.

**1 Samuel 1:22**

But Hannah did not go up with him, because she said to her husband, Until the child goes up, when I wean him, then he will be seen before the face of the Lord and sit there forever.

**1 Samuel 1:23**

And Elkanah her husband said to her, Do what is good in your eyes; sit until you wean him. Only may the Lord establish what went out from your mouth. And the woman sat and nursed her son until she weaned him.

**1 Samuel 1:24**

And she went up with him to Shiloh with a three-year-old calf and breads and an ephah of fine flour and a skin of wine, and she entered into the house of the Lord in Shiloh, and the child was with them.

**1 Samuel 1:25**

And they brought him before the Lord, and his father slaughtered the sacrifice that he made from days to days to the Lord, and he brought the child and slaughtered the calf, and Hannah, the mother of the child, brought him to Eli.

**1 Samuel 1:26**

And she said, Please, lord, as your soul lives: I am the woman who stood before you in praying to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 1:27**

For this child I prayed, and the Lord gave me my request that I asked from him.

**1 Samuel 1:28**

And I lend him to the Lord all the days that he lives, a use to the Lord.

#### Chapter 2

**1 Samuel 2:1**

And she said, My heart was strengthened in the Lord, my horn was lifted up in my God, my mouth was widened against enemies, I rejoiced in your salvation.

**1 Samuel 2:2**

Because there is no holy one like the Lord, and there is none righteous like our God; there is no holy one besides you.

**1 Samuel 2:3**

Do not boast and do not speak lofty things; let no high-sounding speech go out from your mouth, because the Lord is a God of knowledge and a God preparing his purposes.

**1 Samuel 2:4**

The bow of the mighty weakened, and the weak girded themselves with strength.

**1 Samuel 2:5**

Those full of bread were brought low, and the hungry left the land, because the barren one bore seven, and the one with many children became weak.

**1 Samuel 2:6**

The Lord kills and makes alive; he brings down to Hades and brings up.

**1 Samuel 2:7**

The Lord makes poor and makes rich, humbles and lifts up.

**1 Samuel 2:8**

He raises the poor from the earth and lifts the needy from the dung heap, to seat him with the rulers of peoples and to allot to them a throne of glory.

**1 Samuel 2:9**

Giving prayer to the one praying, and he blessed the years of the righteous, because not by strength is a man mighty.

**1 Samuel 2:10**

The Lord will make his adversary weak; the Lord is holy. Let not the wise boast in his wisdom, and let not the strong boast in his strength, and let not the rich boast in his wealth, but in this let the boasting one boast: to understand and know the Lord and to do judgment and righteousness in the midst of the earth. The Lord went up into the heavens and thundered; he will judge the ends of the earth and gives strength to our kings and will lift up the horn of his anointed.

**1 Samuel 2:11**

And they left him there before the Lord and went away to Ramathaim-Zophim, and the child was ministering before the face of the Lord before Eli the priest.

**1 Samuel 2:12**

And the sons of Eli the priest were sons of pestilence, not knowing the Lord.

**1 Samuel 2:13**

And the ordinance of the priest from the people, everyone sacrificing, was this: the servant of the priest came while the meat was boiling, and a three-pronged flesh-hook was in his hand,

**1 Samuel 2:14**

and he struck it into the great cauldron or into the bronze pot or into the cooking pot. Everything that came up with the flesh-hook the priest took for himself. According to these things they were doing to all Israel who came to sacrifice to the Lord in Shiloh.

**1 Samuel 2:15**

And before the fat was burned, the servant of the priest came and said to the man sacrificing, Give meat for roasting to the priest, and I will certainly not take boiled meat from you out of the cauldron.

**1 Samuel 2:16**

And the sacrificing man said, Let the fat first be burned as is proper, and take for yourself from everything your soul desires. And he said, No, because you shall give now, and if not, I will take by force.

**1 Samuel 2:17**

And the sin of the young servants before the Lord was very great, because they were despising the sacrifice of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 2:18**

And Samuel was ministering before the Lord, a child girded with a linen ephod.

**1 Samuel 2:19**

And his mother made for him a small doublet and brought it up to him from days to days when she went up with her husband to sacrifice the sacrifice of the days.

**1 Samuel 2:20**

And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, saying, May the Lord repay you seed from this woman in place of the loan that you loaned to the Lord. And the man went to his place.

**1 Samuel 2:21**

And the Lord visited Hannah, and she bore yet three sons and two daughters, and the child Samuel was magnified before the Lord.

**1 Samuel 2:22**

And Eli was very old and heard what his sons were doing to the sons of Israel.

**1 Samuel 2:23**

And he said to them, Why are you doing according to this word that I hear from the mouth of all the people of the Lord?

**1 Samuel 2:24**

No, children, because the report that I hear is not good. Do not do so, because the reports that I hear are not good, of the people not serving God.

**1 Samuel 2:25**

If a man sins by sinning against a man, then they will pray concerning him to the Lord, but if someone sins against the Lord, who will pray concerning him? And they were not listening to the voice of their father, because the Lord deliberately desired to destroy them.

**1 Samuel 2:26**

And the child Samuel was going on and growing and good both with the Lord and with men.

**1 Samuel 2:27**

And a man of God came to Eli and said, Thus says the Lord: In revealing did I reveal myself to the house of your father while they were in the land of Egypt, servants to the house of Pharaoh?

**1 Samuel 2:28**

And I chose the house of your father from all the scepters of Israel for myself, to serve as priest and to go up upon my altar and to burn incense and to lift the ephod, and I gave to the house of your father all the fire-offerings of the sons of Israel for food.

**1 Samuel 2:29**

And why did you look upon my incense and upon my sacrifice with shameless eye, and glorify your sons beyond me, to bless yourselves from the firstfruits of every sacrifice of Israel before me?

**1 Samuel 2:30**

Because of this thus said the Lord God of Israel: I said, Your house and the house of your father will pass before me forever. And now, says the Lord, let it not be to me; rather those glorifying me I will glorify, and the one despising me will be dishonored.

**1 Samuel 2:31**

Behold, days are coming, and I will destroy your seed and the seed of your father's house.

**1 Samuel 2:32**

And there shall not be an old man of yours in my house all the days.

**1 Samuel 2:33**

And a man I will not destroy for you from my altar, to fail his eyes and make his soul melt away, and everyone remaining of your house shall fall by the sword of men.

**1 Samuel 2:34**

And this will be the sign to you that will come upon these your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: in one day both will die.

**1 Samuel 2:35**

And I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will do all the things in my heart and the things in my soul, and I will build for him a faithful house, and he will pass before my anointed all the days.

**1 Samuel 2:36**

And it shall be that the one left over in your house will come to bow down to him for an obol of silver, saying, Cast me beside one of your priesthoods that I may eat bread.

#### Chapter 3

**1 Samuel 3:1**

And the child Samuel was ministering to the Lord before Eli the priest, and the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no vision making distinction.

**1 Samuel 3:2**

And it came to be on that day, and Eli was sleeping in his place, and his eyes began to grow heavy and he was not able to see.

**1 Samuel 3:3**

And the lamp of God was before being set in order, and Samuel was sleeping in the temple where the ark of God was.

**1 Samuel 3:4**

And the Lord called, Samuel, Samuel. And he said, Behold, here I am.

**1 Samuel 3:5**

And he ran to Eli and said, Behold, here I am, because you called me. And he said, I did not call you; go back, sleep. And he went back and slept.

**1 Samuel 3:6**

And the Lord added and called, Samuel, Samuel. And he went to Eli a second time and said, Behold, here I am, because you called me. And he said, I did not call you; go back, sleep.

**1 Samuel 3:7**

And Samuel was before knowing God and before the word of the Lord was revealed to him.

**1 Samuel 3:8**

And the Lord added to call Samuel a third time, and he rose and went to Eli and said, Behold, here I am, because you called me. And Eli understood that the Lord had called the child.

**1 Samuel 3:9**

And he said, Go back, sleep, child, and it shall be if he calls you, then you shall say, Speak, Lord, because your servant hears. And Samuel went and lay down in his place.

**1 Samuel 3:10**

And the Lord came and stood and called him as once and again, and Samuel said, Speak, because your servant hears.

**1 Samuel 3:11**

And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I am doing my words in Israel, so that whoever hears them, both his ears will ring.

**1 Samuel 3:12**

In that day I will raise upon Eli all that I spoke against his house; I will begin and I will complete.

**1 Samuel 3:13**

And I have announced to him that I am avenging his house forever for the injustices of his sons, because his sons were blaspheming God and he was not warning them, not even so.

**1 Samuel 3:14**

I swore to the house of Eli whether the injustice of the house of Eli will be propitiated by incense and by sacrifices forever.

**1 Samuel 3:15**

And Samuel slept until morning and rose early in the morning and opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and Samuel feared to report the vision to Eli.

**1 Samuel 3:16**

And Eli said to Samuel, Samuel, child. And he said, Behold, here I am.

**1 Samuel 3:17**

And he said, What is the word spoken to you? Do not hide it from me. Thus may God do to you and thus may he add, if you hide from me a word of all the words spoken to you in your ears.

**1 Samuel 3:18**

And Samuel reported all the words and did not hide from him, and Eli said, He is the Lord; what is good before him he will do.

**1 Samuel 3:19**

And Samuel grew great, and the Lord was with him, and not one of all his words fell to the ground.

**1 Samuel 3:20**

And all Israel knew, from Dan and as far as Beersheba, that Samuel was faithful as a prophet to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 3:21**

And the Lord again made himself known in Shiloh, because the Lord was revealed to Samuel, and Samuel was entrusted to become prophet to the Lord for all Israel from the end of the land to end. And Eli was very old, and his sons were going on and their way was evil before the Lord.

#### Chapter 4

**1 Samuel 4:1**

And it came to be in those days, and foreigners were gathered for war against Israel, and Israel went out to meet them for war, and they camped by Ebenezer, and the foreigners camped in Aphek.

**1 Samuel 4:2**

And the foreigners lined up for battle against Israel, and the battle turned, and a man of Israel stumbled before the foreigners, and four thousand men were struck down in battle in the field.

**1 Samuel 4:3**

And the people came into the camp, and the elders of Israel said, Why did the Lord make us stumble today before the foreigners? Let us take the ark of our God from Shiloh, and let it come out in our midst and save us from the hand of our enemies.

**1 Samuel 4:4**

And the people sent to Shiloh, and they took from there the ark of the Lord seated on cherubim, and both sons of Eli were with the ark, Hophni and Phinehas.

**1 Samuel 4:5**

And it came to be, when the ark of the Lord came into the camp, all Israel cried out with a great voice, and the earth resounded.

**1 Samuel 4:6**

And the foreigners heard the sound of the cry and said, What is this great cry in the camp of the Hebrews? And they knew that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp.

**1 Samuel 4:7**

And the foreigners were afraid and said, These gods have come to them into the camp. Woe to us, Lord, rescue us today, because such a thing has not happened yesterday or the day before.

**1 Samuel 4:8**

Woe to us. Who will rescue us from the hand of these strong gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague and in the wilderness.

**1 Samuel 4:9**

Be strong and become men, foreigners, lest you serve the Hebrews as they served us. And become men and fight them.

**1 Samuel 4:10**

And they fought them, and a man of Israel stumbled, and each fled to his tent, and there was a very great blow, and thirty thousand ranks fell from Israel.

**1 Samuel 4:11**

And the ark of God was taken, and both sons of Eli died, Hophni and Phinehas.

**1 Samuel 4:12**

And a Benjamite man ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh on that day, and his garments were torn and earth was on his head.

**1 Samuel 4:13**

And he came, and behold, Eli was sitting on the seat by the gate, watching the road, because his heart was beside itself concerning the ark of God. And the man entered into the city to report, and the city cried out.

**1 Samuel 4:14**

And Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said, What is this cry of this sound? And the man hurried and entered and reported to Eli.

**1 Samuel 4:15**

And Eli was ninety years old, and his eyes had become fixed, and he did not see, and Eli said to the men standing around him, What is the voice of this sound?

**1 Samuel 4:16**

And the man hurried and came near to Eli and said to him, I am the one coming from the camp, and I fled from the battle line today. And he said, What is the matter, child?

**1 Samuel 4:17**

And the young servant answered and said, A man of Israel fled from before the foreigners, and there was a great blow among the people, and both your sons have died, and the ark of God has been taken.

**1 Samuel 4:18**

And it came to be, when he mentioned the ark of God, he fell from the seat backward near the gate, and his back was broken and he died, because the man was old and heavy, and he judged Israel twenty years.

**1 Samuel 4:19**

And his daughter-in-law, wife of Phinehas, had conceived to give birth, and she heard the news that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, and she crouched down and gave birth, because her labor pains turned upon her.

**1 Samuel 4:20**

And at the time of her dying the women standing by her said to her, Do not fear, because you have borne a son. But she did not answer, and her heart did not understand.

**1 Samuel 4:21**

And she called the child Ichabod because of the ark of God and because of her father-in-law and because of her husband.

**1 Samuel 4:22**

And they said, Glory has departed from Israel in the taking of the ark of the Lord.

#### Chapter 5

**1 Samuel 5:1**

And the foreigners took the ark of God and brought it in from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

**1 Samuel 5:2**

And the foreigners took the ark of the Lord and brought it into the house of Dagon and set it beside Dagon.

**1 Samuel 5:3**

And the people of Ashdod rose early and entered into the house of Dagon, and behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of God. And they raised up Dagon and set him in his place, and the hand of the Lord grew heavy upon the people of Ashdod, and he tormented them and struck them in their seats, Ashdod and its borders.

**1 Samuel 5:4**

And it came to be when they rose early in the morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the head of Dagon and both the prints of his hands were removed upon the front threshold, each one, and both palms of his hands had fallen on the threshold; only the back of Dagon was left.

**1 Samuel 5:5**

Because of this the priests of Dagon and everyone entering the house of Dagon do not step upon the step of the house of Dagon in Ashdod until this day, because in passing over they pass over it.

**1 Samuel 5:6**

And the hand of the Lord grew heavy upon Ashdod and brought upon them and boiled out for them in their ships, and in the midst of its region mice sprang up, and there was a great confusion of death in the city.

**1 Samuel 5:7**

And the men of Ashdod saw that it was so and said, The ark of the God of Israel will not remain with us, because his hand is hard upon us and upon Dagon our god.

**1 Samuel 5:8**

And they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners to them and said, What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel? And the Gittites said, Let the ark of God come over to us. And the ark of God came over to Gath.

**1 Samuel 5:9**

And it came to be after it came over, the hand of the Lord was in the city, a very great disturbance, and he struck the men of the city from small to great and struck them in their seats, and the Gittites made seats for themselves.

**1 Samuel 5:10**

And they sent away the ark of God to Ashkelon, and it came to be when the ark of God entered into Ashkelon, the Ashkelonites cried out, saying, Why did you return to us the ark of the God of Israel, to kill us and our people?

**1 Samuel 5:11**

And they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners and said, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it sit in its place, and it shall certainly not kill us and our people, because there was confusion of death in the whole city, very heavy, as the ark of the God of Israel entered there.

**1 Samuel 5:12**

And the living who did not die were struck in their seats, and the cry of the city went up to heaven.

#### Chapter 6

**1 Samuel 6:1**

And the ark was in the field of the foreigners seven months, and their land boiled out mice.

**1 Samuel 6:2**

And the foreigners call the priests and their diviners and enchanters, saying, What shall we do with the ark of the Lord? Make known to us in what way we shall send it to its place.

**1 Samuel 6:3**

And they said, If you send away the ark of the covenant of the Lord God of Israel, by no means send it away empty, but in repaying repay it for the torment, and then you will be healed and it will be propitiated for you. Will not his hand depart from you?

**1 Samuel 6:4**

And they say, What is the thing of torment that we shall repay to it? And they said, According to the number of the satraps of the foreigners, five golden seats, because the same fall is on you and on your rulers and on the people.

**1 Samuel 6:5**

And golden mice, likeness of your mice destroying the land, and you shall give glory to the Lord, so that he may lighten his hand from you and from your gods and from your land.

**1 Samuel 6:6**

And why do you harden your hearts as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? Was it not when he mocked them that they sent them away and they went?

**1 Samuel 6:7**

And now take and make a new wagon and two first-calving cows apart from their calves, and yoke the cows to the wagon and lead away the calves from behind them into the house.

**1 Samuel 6:8**

And you will take the ark and put it on the wagon, and the gold objects that you repay to it for the torment you shall place in a chest beside it, and you shall send it away and drive it out, and it will go.

**1 Samuel 6:9**

And you will see whether it goes on the road of its borders toward Beth-shemesh; he did to us this great evil. But if not, then we shall know that it was not his hand that touched us, but this happened to us by chance.

**1 Samuel 6:10**

And the foreigners did so, and they took two first-calving cows and yoked them to the wagon, and they shut up their calves in the house.

**1 Samuel 6:11**

And they set the ark upon the wagon and the chest and the gold mice.

**1 Samuel 6:12**

And the cows went straight on the road, on the road to Beth-shemesh, in one path they went, and they toiled and did not turn aside right or left, and the satraps of the foreigners went after it until the borders of Beth-shemesh.

**1 Samuel 6:13**

And those in Beth-shemesh were reaping wheat harvest in the valley, and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark of the Lord and rejoiced to meet it.

**1 Samuel 6:14**

And the wagon came into the field of Hoshea in Beth-shemesh, and they stood there by a great stone, and they split the wood of the wagon and offered the cows as a whole burnt offering to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 6:15**

And the Levites brought up the ark of the Lord and the chest with it and the gold items upon it and placed them on the great stone, and the men of Beth-shemesh offered whole burnt offerings and sacrifices on that day to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 6:16**

And the five satraps of the foreigners saw and returned to Ashkelon on that day.

**1 Samuel 6:17**

And these are the golden seats that the foreigners repaid to the Lord for the torment: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, one for Ekron,

**1 Samuel 6:18**

and the golden mice according to the number of all the cities of the foreigners of the five satraps, from fortified city and to village of the Perizzite, and to the great stone on which they placed the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the one in the field of Hoshea the Baithsamyisite.

**1 Samuel 6:19**

And the sons of Iechoniou were not pleased among the men of Beth-shemesh because they saw the ark of the Lord, and he struck among them seventy men and fifty thousand men, and the people mourned because the Lord struck the people with a very great blow.

**1 Samuel 6:20**

And the men from Beth-shemesh said, Who will be able to go through before this holy Lord, and to whom will the ark of the Lord go up from us?

**1 Samuel 6:21**

And they send messengers to those dwelling in Kirjathjearim, saying, The foreigners have returned the ark of the Lord. Come down and bring it up to yourselves.

#### Chapter 7

**1 Samuel 7:1**

And the men of Kirjathjearim come and bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord and bring it into the house of Amminadab on the hill, and they consecrated Eleazar his son to guard the ark of the covenant of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 7:2**

And it came to be from the day the ark was in Kirjathjearim, the days multiplied and became twenty years, and all the house of Israel looked after the Lord.

**1 Samuel 7:3**

And Samuel said to all the house of Israel, saying, If with your whole heart you are turning to the Lord, remove the foreign gods from your midst and the groves, and prepare your hearts toward the Lord and serve him alone, and he will deliver you from the hand of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 7:4**

And the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the groves of Ashtaroth and served the Lord alone.

**1 Samuel 7:5**

And Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray concerning you to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 7:6**

And they gathered to Mizpah and drew water and poured it out before the Lord upon the ground and fasted on that day and said, We sinned before the Lord. And Samuel was judging the sons of Israel in Mizpah.

**1 Samuel 7:7**

And the foreigners heard that all the sons of Israel had gathered to Mizpah, and the satraps of the foreigners went up against Israel. And the sons of Israel heard and feared from before the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 7:8**

And the sons of Israel said to Samuel, Do not be silent away from us from crying to the Lord your God, and he will save us from the hand of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 7:9**

And Samuel took one suckling lamb and offered it up whole with all the people to the Lord, and Samuel cried out to the Lord concerning Israel, and the Lord listened to him.

**1 Samuel 7:10**

And Samuel was offering up the whole burnt offering, and the foreigners drew near for battle against Israel, and the Lord thundered with a great voice on that day against the foreigners and confused them, and they stumbled before Israel.

**1 Samuel 7:11**

And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the foreigners and struck them as far as below Baithchor.

**1 Samuel 7:12**

And Samuel took one stone and set it between Mizpah and between the old place and called its name Ebenezer, Stone of the Helper, and said, Until here the Lord has helped us.

**1 Samuel 7:13**

And the Lord humbled the foreigners, and they no longer continued to come into the border of Israel, and the hand of the Lord was upon the foreigners all the days of Samuel.

**1 Samuel 7:14**

And the cities that the foreigners took from the sons of Israel were given back, and they restored them to Israel from Ashkelon to Azob, and the border of Israel they removed from the hand of the foreigners. And there was peace between Israel and between the Amorite.

**1 Samuel 7:15**

And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

**1 Samuel 7:16**

And he went year by year and made circuit of Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah and judged Israel in all these consecrated places.

**1 Samuel 7:17**

And his return was to Ramathaim-Zophim, because there was his house, and there he judged Israel, and he built there an altar to the Lord.

#### Chapter 8

**1 Samuel 8:1**

And it came to be when Samuel grew old that he appointed his sons as judges for Israel.

**1 Samuel 8:2**

And these are the names of his sons: firstborn Joel, and the name of the second Abijah, judges in Beersheba.

**1 Samuel 8:3**

And his sons did not walk in his way, and they turned aside after gain and were taking gifts and turning aside judgments.

**1 Samuel 8:4**

And the men of Israel gathered together and came to Ramathaim-Zophim to Samuel.

**1 Samuel 8:5**

And they said to him, Behold, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your way, and now appoint over us a king to judge us, as also the rest of the nations have.

**1 Samuel 8:6**

And the word was evil in the eyes of Samuel as they said, Give us a king to judge us, and Samuel prayed to the Lord.

**1 Samuel 8:7**

And the Lord said to Samuel, Hear the voice of the people according to whatever they say to you, because they have not despised you, but me they have despised, from reigning over them.

**1 Samuel 8:8**

According to all the deeds that they did to me from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day, and they forsook me and served other gods, so they also are doing to you.

**1 Samuel 8:9**

And now hear their voice; only in protesting protest to them and declare to them the right of the king who will reign over them.

**1 Samuel 8:10**

And Samuel spoke every word of the Lord to the people asking from him a king.

**1 Samuel 8:11**

And he said, This will be the right of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and place them in his chariots and among his horsemen and as runners before his chariots,

**1 Samuel 8:12**
