**1 Samuel 8:13**

And your daughters he will take as perfumers and cooks and bakers.

**1 Samuel 8:14**

And your fields and your vineyards and your good olive groves he will take and give to his servants.

**1 Samuel 8:15**

And your seeds and your vineyards he will tithe and give to his eunuchs and to his servants.

**1 Samuel 8:16**

And your male servants and your female servants and your good cattle and your donkeys he will take and tithe for his works.

**1 Samuel 8:17**

And your flocks he will tithe, and you will be his servants.

**1 Samuel 8:18**

And you will cry out in that day because of your king whom you chose for yourselves, and the Lord will not listen to you in those days, because you chose a king for yourselves.

**1 Samuel 8:19**

And the people was not willing to hear Samuel, and they said to him, No, but a king shall be over us.

**1 Samuel 8:20**

And we also will be like all the nations, and our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our war.

**1 Samuel 8:21**

And Samuel heard all the words of the people and spoke them into the ears of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 8:22**

And the Lord said to Samuel, Hear their voice and make a king reign over them. And Samuel said to the men of Israel, Let each man run back to his city.

#### Chapter 9

**1 Samuel 9:1**

And there was a man from the sons of Benjamin, and his name was Kish, son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Bechorath, son of Aphek, son of a Benjamite man, a mighty man.

**1 Samuel 9:2**

And he had a son, and his name was Saul, a well-grown good man, and there was not among the sons of Israel a better man than he; from his shoulders and above he was taller than all the people.

**1 Samuel 9:3**

And the donkeys of Kish, father of Saul, were lost, and Kish said to Saul his son, Take with yourself one of the young men, rise, and go seek the donkeys.

**1 Samuel 9:4**

And they passed through the hill-country of Ephraim, and they passed through the land of Salcah and did not find them, and they passed through the land of Shaalim and it was not there, and they passed through the land of Jakim and did not find them.

**1 Samuel 9:5**

When they came into Zuph, Saul said to his young man who was with him, Come, let us turn back, lest my father leave off about the donkeys and be anxious about us.

**1 Samuel 9:6**

And the young man said to him, Behold now, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is honored; everything whatever he may speak, when it comes, it will stand. And now let us go there, so he may report to us the road on which we have gone.

**1 Samuel 9:7**

And Saul said to his young man who was with him, And behold, we will go, but what shall we bring to the man of God? Because the breads have failed from our vessels, and there is no more with us to carry in to the man of God. What have we with us?

**1 Samuel 9:8**

And the young man answered Saul again and said, Behold, a quarter-shekel of silver has been found in my hand, and I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our road.

**1 Samuel 9:9**

Formerly in Israel each one used to say these things when going to inquire of God: Come, let us go to the seer, because the people formerly called the prophet the seer.

**1 Samuel 9:10**

And Saul said to his young man, Good word. Come, let us go. And they went into the city where the man of God was there.

**1 Samuel 9:11**

As they were going up the ascent of the city, they found young girls who had come out to draw water, and they say to them, Is the seer here?

**1 Samuel 9:12**

And the girls answered them and say to them, He is; behold, before your face now. For today he has come into the city, because there is a sacrifice today for the people at the high place.

**1 Samuel 9:13**

As soon as you enter the city, so you will find him in the city before he goes up to the high place to eat. Because the people certainly will not eat until he enters, because he blesses the sacrifice, and after these things the guests eat. And now go up, because today you will find him.

**1 Samuel 9:14**

And they go up to the city. As they were entering into the middle of the city, behold, Samuel came out to meet them, to go up to the high place.

**1 Samuel 9:15**

And the Lord had uncovered the ear of Samuel one day before Saul came to him, saying,

**1 Samuel 9:16**

About this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you will anoint him as a ruler over my people Israel, and he will save my people from the hand of foreigners, because I have looked upon the humiliation of my people, because their cry has come to me.

**1 Samuel 9:17**

And Samuel saw Saul, and the Lord answered him, Behold, the man of whom I spoke to you; this one will rule among my people.

**1 Samuel 9:18**

And Saul came near to Samuel in the middle of the city and said, Tell me now, where is the house of the seer?

**1 Samuel 9:19**

And Samuel answered Saul and said, I am he. Go up before me to the high place and eat with me today, and I will send you away in the morning, and all the things in your heart I will report to you.

**1 Samuel 9:20**

And concerning your donkeys that were lost three days ago today, do not set your heart on them, because they have been found. And for whom are the beautiful things of Israel? Are they not for you and for your father’s house?

**1 Samuel 9:21**

And Saul answered and said, Am I not son of a Benjamite man, from the least scepter of a tribe of Israel, and my tribe the least from the whole scepter of Benjamin? And why have you spoken to me according to this word?

**1 Samuel 9:22**

And Samuel took Saul and his young man and brought them into the guest room and set for them a place among the first of those who had been called, about seventy men.

**1 Samuel 9:23**

And Samuel said to the cook, Give me the portion that I gave to you, which I said to you to set beside you.

**1 Samuel 9:24**

And the cook lifted up the haunch and set it before Saul, and Samuel said to Saul, Behold, what has been left over; set it before you and eat, because it has been kept for you for this appointed witness beside the others. And Saul ate with Samuel on that day.

**1 Samuel 9:25**

And he came down from the high place into the city, and they spread a bed for Saul on the roof.

**1 Samuel 9:26**

And he slept. And it came to be, as dawn was rising, Samuel called Saul on the roof, saying, Rise, and I will send you away. And Saul rose, and both he and Samuel went out.

**1 Samuel 9:27**

As they were going down to the outskirts of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Tell the young man, and let him pass on before us. But you stand like today, and hear the word of God.

#### Chapter 10

**1 Samuel 10:1**

And Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head and kissed him and said to him, Has not the Lord anointed you as a ruler over his people, over Israel? And you will rule among the people of the Lord, and you will save him from the hand of his enemies round about. And this is the sign to you that the Lord has anointed you over his inheritance as a ruler.

**1 Samuel 10:2**

When you depart from me today, you will find two men by the tombs of Rachel in the border of Benjamin, speaking great things, and they will say to you, The donkeys that you went to seek have been found, and behold, your father has shaken off the matter of the donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, What shall I do concerning my son?

**1 Samuel 10:3**

And you will pass on from there and beyond, and you will come as far as the oak of Tabor, and you will find there three men going up to God at Bethel, one carrying three kids, one carrying three vessels of breads, and one carrying a skin of wine.

**1 Samuel 10:4**

And they will ask you the things of peace, and they will give you two firstfruits of breads, and you will take them from their hand.

**1 Samuel 10:5**

And after these things you will enter the hill of God, where the station of the foreigners is, there at Zuph the foreigner. And it will be when you enter there into the city, you will meet a chorus of prophets coming down from the high place, and before them harp and tambourine and flute and lyre, and they prophesying.

**1 Samuel 10:6**

And the Spirit of the Lord will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be turned into another man.

**1 Samuel 10:7**

And it will be when these signs come upon you, do everything whatever your hand finds, because God is with you.

**1 Samuel 10:8**

And you will go down before me to Gilgal, and behold, I am coming down to you to offer up whole burnt offerings and sacrifices of peace. Seven days you will wait until my coming to you, and I will make known to you what you shall do.

**1 Samuel 10:9**

And it came to be when he turned his shoulder to depart from Samuel, God turned for him another heart, and all these signs came on that day.

**1 Samuel 10:10**

And he comes from there to the hill, and behold, a chorus of prophets came opposite him, and the Spirit of God leapt upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.

**1 Samuel 10:11**

And it came to be, all who knew him yesterday and the third day saw, and behold, he was in the midst of the prophets, and each person said to his neighbor, What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among prophets?

**1 Samuel 10:12**

And one of them answered and said, And who is his father? Because of this it became a proverb, Is Saul also among prophets?

**1 Samuel 10:13**

And he finished prophesying and comes to the hill.

**1 Samuel 10:14**

And his kinsman said to him and to his young man, Where did you go? And they said, To seek the donkeys, and we saw that they are not there, and we entered to Samuel.

**1 Samuel 10:15**

And the kinsman said to Saul, Tell me now, what did Samuel say to you?

**1 Samuel 10:16**

And Saul said to his kinsman, He plainly told me that the donkeys have been found. But the word of the kingship he did not tell him.

**1 Samuel 10:17**

And Samuel summoned all the people to the Lord at Mizpah,

**1 Samuel 10:18**

and he said to the sons of Israel, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, saying, I brought up the sons of Israel from Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt and from all the kingdoms afflicting you.

**1 Samuel 10:19**

And you today have counted as nothing your God, who himself is your savior from all your evils and afflictions, and you said, No, but you will appoint a king over us. And now stand before the Lord by your scepters and by your tribes.

**1 Samuel 10:20**

And Samuel brought near all the scepters of Israel, and the scepter of Benjamin was taken by lot.

**1 Samuel 10:21**

And he brings near the scepter of Benjamin by tribes, and the tribe of Matrites is taken by lot. And they bring near the tribe of Matrites by men, and Saul son of Kish was taken by lot. And they sought him, and he was not found.

**1 Samuel 10:22**

And Samuel inquired yet again of the Lord whether the man comes here. And the Lord said, Behold, he is hidden among the baggage.

**1 Samuel 10:23**

And they ran and take him from there, and he stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than all the people from the shoulder and upward.

**1 Samuel 10:24**

And Samuel said to all the people, Have you seen whom the Lord has chosen for himself, that there is none like him among all of you? And all the people knew and said, Long live the king.

**1 Samuel 10:25**

And Samuel told the people the righteous judgment of the king, and he wrote it in a scroll and set it before the Lord. And Samuel sent away all the people, and each went to his place.

**1 Samuel 10:26**

And Saul went to his house at Gibeah, and sons of powers whose hearts God had touched went with Saul.

**1 Samuel 10:27**

And pestilent sons said, How will this one save us? And they dishonored him and did not bring him gifts.

#### Chapter 11

**1 Samuel 11:1**

And it came to be as after a month, Nahash the Ammonite went up and camped against Jabesh Gilead, and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash the Ammonite, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.

**1 Samuel 11:2**

And Nahash the Ammonite said to them, On this condition I will make a covenant with you: that I gouge out every right eye of yours, and I will set reproach on Israel.

**1 Samuel 11:3**

And the men of Jabesh say to him, Leave us for seven days, and we will send messengers into every border of Israel. And if there is no one saving us, we will come out to you.

**1 Samuel 11:4**

And the messengers come to Gibeah to Saul and speak the words into the ears of the people, and all the people lifted up their voice and wept.

**1 Samuel 11:5**

And behold, Saul came after the morning from the field, and Saul said, Why is the people weeping? And they recount to him the words of the sons of Jabesh.

**1 Samuel 11:6**

And the Spirit of the Lord leapt upon Saul as he heard these words, and his anger was greatly kindled against them.

**1 Samuel 11:7**

And he took two oxen and cut them in pieces and sent them through every border of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, Whoever is not coming out after Saul and after Samuel, thus they will do to his oxen. And the astonishment of the Lord came upon the people of Israel, and they cried out like one man.

**1 Samuel 11:8**

And he musters them at Bezek on the high place, every man of Israel six hundred thousand, and men of Judah seventy thousand.

**1 Samuel 11:9**

And he said to the messengers who came, Thus you will say to the men of Jabesh, Tomorrow salvation is for you, when the sun grows warm. And the messengers came into the city and report to the men of Jabesh, and they rejoiced.

**1 Samuel 11:10**

And the men of Jabesh said to Nahash the Ammonite, Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us what is good in your sight.

**1 Samuel 11:11**

And it came to be on the next day that Saul set the people in three heads, and they entered the middle of the camp in the morning watch and were striking the sons of Ammon until the day grew warm. And the ones left were scattered, and not two among them were left together.

**1 Samuel 11:12**

And the people said to Samuel, Who is the one who said, Shall Saul not reign over us? Hand over the men, and we will put them to death.

**1 Samuel 11:13**

And Saul said, No one will be put to death on this day, because today the Lord has worked salvation in Israel.

**1 Samuel 11:14**

And Samuel said to the people, saying, Let us go to Gilgal, and let us renew the kingship there.

**1 Samuel 11:15**

And all the people went to Gilgal, and Samuel anointed Saul there as king before the Lord in Gilgal, and he sacrificed there sacrifices, even peaceful ones, before the Lord. And Samuel and all Israel rejoiced there very greatly.

#### Chapter 12

**1 Samuel 12:1**

And Samuel said to every man of Israel, Behold, I have listened to your voice in everything whatever you said to me, and I made a king reign over you.

**1 Samuel 12:2**

And now behold, the king goes before you, and I have grown old and will sit, and behold, my sons are among you, and behold, I have gone before you from my youth until this day.

**1 Samuel 12:3**

Behold me. Answer against me before the Lord and before his anointed. Whose calf have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken, or whom of you have I oppressed, or whom have I crushed, or from whose hand have I taken a propitiation, even sandals? Answer against me, and I will restore it to you.

**1 Samuel 12:4**

And they said to Samuel, You have not wronged us, and you have not oppressed us, and you have not crushed us, and you have not taken anything from the hand of anyone.

**1 Samuel 12:5**

And Samuel said to the people, The Lord is witness among you, and his anointed is witness today in this day, that you have not found anything in my hand. And they said, Witness.

**1 Samuel 12:6**

And Samuel said to the people, saying, The Lord is witness, the one who made Moses and Aaron, the one who brought our fathers up from Egypt.

**1 Samuel 12:7**

And now stand, and I will judge you before the Lord, and I will recount to you all the righteousness of the Lord, what things he did among you and among your fathers.

**1 Samuel 12:8**

When Jacob and his sons entered into Egypt, and Egypt humbled them, our fathers cried out to the Lord, and the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and brought our fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

**1 Samuel 12:17**

**1 Samuel 12:19**

**1 Samuel 12:20**

**1 Samuel 12:21**

**1 Samuel 12:23**

**1 Samuel 12:24**

**1 Samuel 12:25**

#### Chapter 14

**1 Samuel 14:1**

**1 Samuel 16:1**

**1 Samuel 16:22**

**1 Samuel 16:23**

And Saul clothed David with a cloak and put a bronze helmet around his head.

**1 Samuel 17:39**

And David girded on his sword over his cloak and labored to walk once and twice, and David said to Saul, I certainly will not be able to go in these things, because I have not tried them. And they take them off from him.

**1 Samuel 17:40**

**1 Samuel 17:42**

And Goliad saw David and dishonored him, because he was a youth, and he was ruddy, with the beauty of eyes.

**1 Samuel 17:43**

And the foreigner said to David, Am I like a dog, that you come against me with staff and stones? And David said, No, but worse than a dog’s hand. And the foreigner cursed David by his gods.

**1 Samuel 17:44**

And the foreigner said to David, Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and to the beasts of the earth.

**1 Samuel 17:45**

And David said to the foreigner, You come to me with sword and spear and shield, but I go to you in the name of the Lord of hosts, God of the battle-line of Israel, whom you have reproached today.

**1 Samuel 17:46**

And the Lord will shut you up into my hand today, and I will kill you and remove your head from you, and I will give your limbs and the limbs of the camp of the foreigners in this day to the birds of the sky and to the beasts of the earth, and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.

**1 Samuel 17:47**

And all this assembly will know that the Lord does not save with sword and spear, because the battle is the Lord’s, and the Lord will deliver you into our hands.

**1 Samuel 17:48**

And the foreigner rose and went to meet David.

**1 Samuel 17:49**

**1 Samuel 17:51**

And David ran and stood over him and took his sword and killed him and removed his head. And the foreigners saw that their mighty one had died, and they fled.

**1 Samuel 17:52**

**1 Samuel 17:53**

**1 Samuel 17:54**

And David took the head of the foreigner and brought it into Jerusalem, and his equipment he placed in his tent.

#### Chapter 20

**1 Samuel 20:1**

And David persuaded his men with words and did not let them rise to put Saul to death, and Saul rose and went down on the road.

**1 Samuel 24:9**

And David rose after him from the cave and cried out behind Saul, saying, Lord king. And Saul looked behind him, and David bent his face to the ground and bowed down to him.

**1 Samuel 24:10**

And David said to Saul, Why do you listen to the words of the people saying, Behold, David seeks your life?

**1 Samuel 24:11**

Behold, on this day your eyes have seen that the Lord delivered you today into my hand in the cave, and I was not willing to kill you, and I spared you and said, I will not put my hand upon my lord, because he is anointed of the Lord.

**1 Samuel 24:12**

And behold, the wing of your double cloak is in my hand. I removed the wing and did not kill you. Know and see today that there is no evil in my hand, nor impiety and revolt, and I have not sinned against you, but you bind my life to take it.

**1 Samuel 24:13**

May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me from you, but my hand will not be upon you.

**1 Samuel 24:14**

As the ancient proverb says, From lawless ones wrongdoing will go out, but my hand will not be upon you.

**1 Samuel 24:15**

And now, after whom do you come out, king of Israel? After whom do you pursue? After a dead dog and after one flea.

**1 Samuel 24:16**

May the Lord become judge and justice between me and you. May the Lord see and judge my judgment and give me justice from your hand.

**1 Samuel 24:17**

And it came to be, when David finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, Is this your voice, child David? And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.

**1 Samuel 24:18**

And Saul said to David, You are more righteous than I, because you repaid me good things, but I repaid you evil things.

**1 Samuel 24:19**

And you reported to me today what good things you did to me, how the Lord shut me up today into your hands and you did not kill me.

**1 Samuel 24:20**

And because if anyone should find his enemy in affliction and send him away on a good road, then the Lord will repay him good things, as you have done today.

**1 Samuel 24:21**

And now, behold, I know that in reigning you will reign, and the kingdom of Israel will stand in your hands.

**1 Samuel 24:22**

And now swear to me by the Lord that you will not destroy my seed after me and will not wipe out my name from the house of my father.

**1 Samuel 24:23**

And David swore to Saul, and Saul went away to his place, and David and his men went up to the narrow stronghold.

#### Chapter 25

**1 Samuel 25:1**

And Samuel died, and all Israel gathered and mourned for him and buried him in his house at Ramathaim-Zophim. And David rose and went down into the wilderness of Maon.

**1 Samuel 25:7**

**1 Samuel 25:13**

**1 Samuel 25:15**

**1 Samuel 25:16**

**1 Samuel 25:17**

**1 Samuel 25:18**

**1 Samuel 25:19**

**1 Samuel 25:20**

**1 Samuel 25:21**

And David said, Perhaps in vain I have guarded all his things in the wilderness, and we did not command taking anything from all his things, and he repaid me evil instead of good.

**1 Samuel 25:22**

Thus may God do to David and thus may he add, if I leave from all the things of Nabal until morning one who urinates against a wall.

**1 Samuel 25:23**

And Abigail saw David and hurried and sprang down from the donkey and fell before David on her face and bowed down to him on the ground.

**1 Samuel 25:24**

At his feet she said, In me, my lord, is the wrongdoing. Let your servant speak into your ears now, and hear the word of your servant.

**1 Samuel 25:25**

Let not my lord set his heart on this pestilent man, because as his name, so he is: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your servant, did not see your young men whom you sent.

**1 Samuel 25:26**

And now, my lord, as the Lord lives and as your life lives, just as the Lord kept you back from coming into innocent blood and from saving your hand for yourself, now let your enemies and the ones seeking evil for my lord become like Nabal.

**1 Samuel 25:27**

And now take this blessing that your servant has brought to my lord, and you will give it to the young men standing by my lord.

**1 Samuel 25:28**

Take away the lawless deed of your servant, because in doing the Lord will make for my lord a faithful house, because my lord fights the battles of the Lord, and evil will not be found in you ever.

**1 Samuel 25:29**

And a man will rise up pursuing you and seeking your life, and the life of my lord will be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord your God, and the life of your enemies you will sling out in the middle of the sling.

**1 Samuel 25:30**

And it will be that the Lord will do for my lord all the good things he spoke concerning you, and the Lord will appoint you as a leader over Israel.

**1 Samuel 25:31**

And this will not be to you an abomination and a stumbling for my lord, to pour out innocent blood for nothing and for the hand of my lord to save for himself. And the Lord will do good to my lord, and you will remember your servant to do good to her.

**1 Samuel 25:32**

And David said to Abigail, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who sent you today on this day to meet me.

**1 Samuel 25:33**

And blessed be your discernment, and blessed are you, who kept me back today on this day from coming into bloods and from saving my hand for myself.

**1 Samuel 25:34**

**1 Samuel 25:37**

**1 Samuel 25:38**

**1 Samuel 25:39**

**1 Samuel 25:40**

**1 Samuel 25:41**

**1 Samuel 25:42**

**1 Samuel 25:43**

**1 Samuel 26:1**

**1 Samuel 27:1**

**1 Samuel 28:1**

**1 Samuel 28:9**

**1 Samuel 28:10**

**1 Samuel 28:11**

And the woman said, Whom shall I bring up for you? And he said, Bring up Samuel for me.

**1 Samuel 28:15**

And Samuel said, Why have you disturbed me, to bring me up? **1 Samuel 28:16**

And Samuel said, Why do you ask me, since the Lord has departed from you and has come to be with your neighbor?

**1 Samuel 28:17**

And the Lord has done for you just as he spoke by my hand, and the Lord will tear your kingdom from your hand and give it to your neighbor, to David.

**1 Samuel 28:18**

**1 Samuel 28:19**

And the Lord will deliver Israel with you into the hands of the foreigners, and tomorrow you and your sons with you will fall, and the camp of Israel the Lord will give into the hands of the foreigners.

**1 Samuel 28:20**

And Saul hurried and fell standing to the ground, and he feared greatly from the words of Samuel, and there was no strength in him still, because he had not eaten bread all that day and all that night.

**1 Samuel 28:21**

And the woman came in to Saul and saw that he had been greatly shaken, and she said to him, Behold now, your servant listened to your voice and set my life in my hand, and I listened to the words you spoke to me.

**1 Samuel 28:22**

And now listen now to the voice of your servant, and I will set before you a morsel of bread, and eat, and there will be strength in you because you will go on the road.

**1 Samuel 28:23**

**1 Samuel 28:24**

And the woman had a grazing heifer in the house, and she hurried and slaughtered it and took flour and kneaded it and baked unleavened bread.

**1 Samuel 28:25**

**1 Samuel 29:1**

to those in Bethzur and to those in Ramah of the south and to those in Ietthor,

**1 Samuel 30:28**

and to those in Aroer and to those in Ammadi and to those in Siphmoth and to those in Esthie, and to those in Gath and to those in Kinan and to those in Saphek and to those in Thimath,

**1 Samuel 30:29**

and to those in Carmel and to those in the cities of Jerahmeelites and to those in the cities of the Kenezite,

**1 Samuel 30:30**

and to those in Jerimoth and to those in Beersheba and to those in Noo,

**1 Samuel 30:31**

and to those in Hebron and to all the places through which David passed, he and his men.

#### Chapter 31

**1 Samuel 31:1**

And the foreigners were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the foreigners and fell wounded on Mount Gilboa.

**1 Samuel 31:2**

And the foreigners closed with Saul and his sons, and the foreigners struck Jonathan and Amminadab and Melchishua, sons of Saul.

**1 Samuel 31:3**

And the battle grew heavy against Saul, and the men, the archers, found him, and he was wounded in the flanks.

**1 Samuel 31:4**

And Saul said to the one carrying his equipment, Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised ones come and pierce me and mock me. But the one carrying his equipment was not willing, because he feared greatly. And Saul took the sword and fell upon it.

**1 Samuel 31:5**

And the one carrying his equipment saw that Saul had died, and he too fell upon his own sword and died with him.

**1 Samuel 31:6**

And Saul died, and his three sons, and the one carrying his equipment, on that day together.

**1 Samuel 31:7**

And the men of Israel who were beyond the valley and those beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, and they abandoned their cities and fled, and the foreigners come and live in them.

**1 Samuel 31:8**

And it came to be on the next day, the foreigners came to strip the dead, and they find Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

**1 Samuel 31:9**

And they turned him and stripped off his equipment and send them throughout the land of the foreigners round about, proclaiming good news to their idols and to their people.

**1 Samuel 31:10**

And they placed his equipment in the temple of Ashtaroth, and his body they fixed in the wall of Bethshan.

**1 Samuel 31:11**

And the inhabitants of Jabesh of Gileadites heard what the foreigners had done to Saul.

**1 Samuel 31:12**

And every mighty man rose and went all the night and took the body of Saul and the body of Jonathan his son from the wall of Bethshan and bring them into Jabesh and burn them there.

**1 Samuel 31:13**

And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh and fasted seven days.

### 2 Samuel

#### Chapter 1

**2 Samuel 1:1**

And it came to be after the death of Saul, David returned from striking Amalek, and David sat in Ziklag two days.

**2 Samuel 1:2**

And it came to be on the third day, behold, a man came from the camp from the people of Saul, and his garments were torn and earth was on his head. And it came to be when he entered to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down to him.

**2 Samuel 1:3**

And David said to him, From where do you come? And he said to him, I have escaped from the camp of Israel.

**2 Samuel 1:4**

And David said to him, What is this word? Report to me. And he said, The people fled from the battle, and many of the people have fallen and died, and both Saul and Jonathan his son have died.

**2 Samuel 1:5**

And David said to the young man reporting to him, How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son have died?

**2 Samuel 1:6**

And the young man reporting to him said, By chance I happened on Mount Gilboa, and behold, Saul had leaned upon his spear, and behold, the chariots and the horse-commanders had joined close to him.

**2 Samuel 1:7**

And he looked behind him and saw me and called me, and I said, Behold, here I am.

**2 Samuel 1:8**

And he said to me, Who are you? And I said, I am an Amalekite.

**2 Samuel 1:9**

And he said to me, Stand now over me and put me to death, because terrible darkness seized me, because all my life is still in me.

**2 Samuel 1:10**

And I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he would not live after his fall. And I took the kingship-band that was on his head and the bracelet that was on his arm and have brought them here to my lord.

**2 Samuel 1:11**

And David seized his garments and tore them, and all the men with him tore their garments.

**2 Samuel 1:12**

And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening over Saul and over Jonathan his son and over the people of Judah and over the house of Israel, because they were struck by the sword.

**2 Samuel 1:13**

And David said to the young man reporting to him, From where are you? And he said, I am son of a sojourning Amalekite man.

**2 Samuel 1:14**

And David said to him, How were you not afraid to bring your hand to destroy the anointed of the Lord?

**2 Samuel 1:15**

And David called one of his young men and said, Come near, strike him. And he struck him, and he died.

**2 Samuel 1:16**

And David said to him, Your blood is on your head, because your mouth answered against you, saying, I myself killed the anointed of the Lord.

**2 Samuel 1:17**

And David lamented this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son.

**2 Samuel 1:18**

And he said to teach the sons of Judah; behold, it is written in the Book of the Upright.

**2 Samuel 1:19**

Set up, O Israel, over your dead, upon your high places the wounded. How the mighty have fallen.

**2 Samuel 1:20**

Do not report it in Gath, and do not proclaim good news in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the foreigners rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

**2 Samuel 1:21**

Mountains of Gilboa, let no dew come down on you and no rain on you, nor fields of firstfruits, because there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul not anointed with oil.

**2 Samuel 1:22**

From the blood of the wounded, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back empty, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

**2 Samuel 1:23**

Saul and Jonathan, the beloved and beautiful, not separated, lovely in their life and in their death they were not divided; swifter than eagles, they were made stronger than lions.

**2 Samuel 1:24**

Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, the one clothing you in scarlet with your ornament, the one bringing golden ornament upon your garments.

**2 Samuel 1:25**

How the mighty have fallen in the midst of battle. Jonathan, wounded on your high places.

**2 Samuel 1:26**

I am in pain for you, my brother Jonathan. You were made very beautiful to me; your love to me was made wonderful beyond the love of women.

**2 Samuel 1:27**

How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished.

#### Chapter 2

**2 Samuel 2:1**

And it came to be after these things, David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah? And the Lord said to him, Go up. And David said, Where shall I go up? And he said, To Hebron.

**2 Samuel 2:2**

And David went up there to Hebron, and both his wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

**2 Samuel 2:3**

And the men with him, each and his household, and they lived in the cities of Hebron.

**2 Samuel 2:4**

And the men of Judah come and anoint David there to reign over the house of Judah. And they reported to David, saying that the men of Jabesh of Gileadites buried Saul.

**2 Samuel 2:5**

And David sent messengers to the leaders of Jabesh of Gileadites and said to them, Blessed are you to the Lord, because you did this mercy for your lord, for Saul the anointed of the Lord, and buried him and Jonathan his son.

**2 Samuel 2:6**

And now may the Lord do mercy and truth with you, and indeed I will do these good things with you, because you did this word.

**2 Samuel 2:7**

And now let your hands be strengthened, and become sons of strength, because your lord Saul has died, and indeed the house of Judah has anointed me over themselves as king.

**2 Samuel 2:8**

And Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul, took Ishbosheth son of Saul and brought him up from the camp into Mahanaim.

**2 Samuel 2:9**

And he made him king over Gileadites and over Ashurites and over Jezreel and over Ephraim and over Benjamin and over all Israel.

**2 Samuel 2:10**

Forty years old was Ishbosheth son of Saul when he reigned over Israel, and he reigned two years, except that the house of Judah was following David.

**2 Samuel 2:11**

And the days that David reigned in Hebron over the house of Judah were seven years and six months.

**2 Samuel 2:12**

And Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ishbosheth son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

**2 Samuel 2:13**

And Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out from Hebron and met them by the pool of Gibeon together. And these sat by the pool of Gibeon on this side, and those by the pool on that side.

**2 Samuel 2:14**

And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men rise now and play before us. And Joab said, Let them rise.

**2 Samuel 2:15**

And they rose and passed over by number, twelve of the sons of Benjamin belonging to Ishbosheth son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.

**2 Samuel 2:16**

And each seized the head of his neighbor by the hand, and his knife into the side of his neighbor, and they fall together. And the name of that place was called Portion of the Plotters, which is in Gibeon.

**2 Samuel 2:17**

And the battle became very hard on that day, and Abner and the men of Israel stumbled before the servants of David.

**2 Samuel 2:18**

And there were there three sons of Zeruiah: Joab and Abishai and Asahel, and Asahel was swift in his feet like one gazelle in the field.

**2 Samuel 2:19**

And Asahel pursued behind Abner, and he did not turn aside in going to the right or to the left from behind Abner.

**2 Samuel 2:20**

And Abner looked behind him and said, Are you this Asahel? And he said, I am.

**2 Samuel 2:21**

And Abner said to him, Turn aside to the right or to the left and seize for yourself one of the young men and take for yourself his armor. But Asahel did not want to turn aside from behind him.

**2 Samuel 2:22**

And Abner added still, saying to Asahel, Stand away from me, lest I strike you to the ground. And how shall I lift my face to Joab your brother? And where are these things? Turn toward Joab your brother.

**2 Samuel 2:23**

And he was not willing to stand away, and Abner struck him with the back of the spear in the belly, and the spear came out from behind him, and he fell there and died under him. And it came to be, everyone coming to the place where Asahel fell there and died, would stand still.

**2 Samuel 2:24**

And Joab and Abishai pursued behind Abner, and the sun went down, and they came as far as the hill of Ammah, which is opposite Giah on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.

**2 Samuel 2:25**

And the sons of Benjamin gathered behind Abner and became one meeting group, and they stood on the head of one hill.

**2 Samuel 2:26**

And Abner called to Joab and said, Will the sword devour into victory? Do you not know that it will be bitter at the end? And until when will you not tell the people to turn back from after our brothers?

**2 Samuel 2:27**

And Joab said, As the Lord lives, if you had not spoken, then from morning the people would have gone up, each from after his brother.

**2 Samuel 2:28**

And Joab sounded with the trumpet, and all the people stood back and did not pursue after Israel, and they no longer added to fight.

**2 Samuel 2:29**

And Abner and his men went away westward all that night and crossed the Jordan and went the whole extended route and come to the camp.

**2 Samuel 2:30**

And Joab turned back from after Abner and gathered all the people, and they were missing from the servants of David nineteen men and Asahel.

**2 Samuel 2:31**

And the servants of David struck from the sons of Benjamin, from the men of Abner, three hundred and sixty men beside him.

**2 Samuel 2:32**

And they take Asahel and bury him in the tomb of his father in Bethlehem, and Joab and the men with him went all night, and it grew light for them in Hebron.

#### Chapter 3

**2 Samuel 3:1**

And the war became long between the house of Saul and between the house of David, and the house of David was going and growing strong, and the house of Saul was going and growing weak.

**2 Samuel 3:2**

**2 Samuel 3:3**

and his second Dalouia by Abigail the Carmelite, and the third Absalom son of Maachah daughter of Talmai king of Gesir,

**2 Samuel 3:4**

and the fourth Adonijah son of Haggith, and the fifth Shephatiah by Abital,

**2 Samuel 3:5**

and the sixth Ietheraam by Aigla wife of David. These were born to David in Hebron.

**2 Samuel 3:6**

**2 Samuel 3:7**

**2 Samuel 3:8**

And Abner became very angry over the word of Ishbosheth and said to him, Am I a dog’s head? Today I did mercy with the house of Saul your father and with brothers and acquaintances, and I did not defect to the house of David, and yet you seek against me over the wrongdoing of a woman today.

**2 Samuel 3:9**

Thus may God do to Abner and thus may he add to him, because as the Lord swore to David, thus I will do for him on this day,

**2 Samuel 3:10**

to take away the kingdom from the house of Saul and to raise up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah from Dan to Beersheba.

**2 Samuel 3:11**

And Ishbosheth was no longer able to answer Abner a word, because he feared him.

**2 Samuel 3:12**

And Abner sent messengers to David in Thailaim, where he was at once, saying, Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand is with you, to turn all the house of Israel to you.

**2 Samuel 3:13**

And David said, I will well make a covenant with you; only one word I ask from you, saying, You will not see my face unless you bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see my face.

**2 Samuel 3:14**

And David sent messengers to Ishbosheth son of Saul, saying, Give back to me my wife Michal, whom I took for one hundred foreskins of foreigners.

**2 Samuel 3:15**

And Ishbosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Laish.

**2 Samuel 3:16**

And her husband went with her, weeping behind her until Bahurim, and Abner said to him, Go, return. And he returned.

**2 Samuel 3:17**

And Abner spoke to the elders of Israel, saying, Yesterday and the third day you were seeking David to reign over you.

**2 Samuel 3:18**

And now do it, because the Lord spoke concerning David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save Israel from the hand of the foreigners and from the hand of all their enemies.

**2 Samuel 3:19**

And Abner spoke in the ears of Benjamin, and Abner went to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that pleased in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.

**2 Samuel 3:20**

And Abner came to David in Hebron, and with him were twenty men, and David made a feast for Abner and for the men with him.

**2 Samuel 3:21**

And Abner said to David, I will rise now and go and gather to my lord the king all Israel, and I will make a covenant with you, and you will reign over all that your soul desires. And David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.

**2 Samuel 3:22**

And behold, the servants of David and Joab were coming from the raid and bringing much spoil with them, and Abner was not with David in Hebron, because he had sent him away and he had gone in peace.

**2 Samuel 3:23**

And Joab and all his army were brought in, and it was reported to Joab, saying, Abner son of Ner came to David, and he sent him away, and he went in peace.

**2 Samuel 3:24**

And Joab came in to the king and said, What is this you have done? Behold, Abner came to you, and why did you send him away and he has gone in peace?

**2 Samuel 3:25**

Do you not know the evil of Abner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you and to know your going out and your coming in and to know all that you do?

**2 Samuel 3:26**

And Joab turned back from David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Seiram, and David did not know.

**2 Samuel 3:27**

And Abner returned to Hebron, and Joab turned him aside by the side of the gate to speak with him in ambush, and struck him there in the belly, and he died for the blood of Asahel brother of Joab.

**2 Samuel 3:28**

And David heard after this and said, Innocent am I and my kingdom from the Lord forever from the bloods of Abner son of Ner.

**2 Samuel 3:29**

Let them come down on the head of Joab and on all the house of his father, and let there not fail from the house of Joab one with discharge and leper and one holding a staff and one falling by the sword and one lacking breads.

**2 Samuel 3:30**

And Joab and Abishai his brother were lying in wait for Abner, because he killed Asahel their brother in Gibeon in the battle.

**2 Samuel 3:31**

And David said to Joab and to all the people with him, Tear your garments and gird on sackcloth and mourn before Abner. And King David was going behind the bier.

**2 Samuel 3:32**

And they bury Abner in Hebron, and the king lifted up his voice and wept over his tomb, and all the people wept over Abner.

**2 Samuel 3:33**

And the king lamented over Abner and said, Should Abner die according to the death of Nabal?

**2 Samuel 3:34**

Your hands were not bound, your feet were not in fetters; you fell as Nabal falls before the sons of wrongdoing. And all the people gathered to weep for him.

**2 Samuel 3:35**

And all the people came to make David dine with breads while it was still day, and David swore, saying, Thus may God do to me and thus may he add, if before the sun goes down I taste bread or anything whatever.

**2 Samuel 3:36**

And all the people knew, and it was pleasing before them, all that the king did before the people.

**2 Samuel 3:37**

And all the people and all Israel knew on that day that it did not come from the king to put Abner son of Ner to death.

**2 Samuel 3:38**

And the king said to his servants, Do you not know that a great leader has fallen on this day in Israel?

**2 Samuel 3:39**

And I am today a relative and appointed by a king, but these men, sons of Zeruiah, are harsher than I. The Lord will repay the one doing evil according to his evil.

#### Chapter 4

**2 Samuel 4:1**

And Ishbosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, and his hands were loosed, and all the men of Israel were let down.

**2 Samuel 4:3**

And the Beerothites fled into Gittaim and were sojourning there until this day.

**2 Samuel 4:4**

And to Jonathan son of Saul there was a son, stricken in the feet, five years old. He was this age when the news came of Saul and Jonathan his son from Jezreel, and his nurse took him up and fled. And it came to be as she hurried and withdrew, he fell and became lame, and his name was Mephibosheth.

**2 Samuel 4:5**

And sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baana, went and entered in the heat of the day into the house of Ishbosheth, and he was sleeping on the bed at noon.

**2 Samuel 4:6**

And behold, the doorkeeper of the house was cleaning wheat and became drowsy and slept, and Rechab and Baana the brothers escaped notice.

**2 Samuel 4:7**

And they entered into the house, and Ishbosheth was sleeping on his bed in his bedroom, and they strike him and kill him and remove his head, and they took his head and went the road westward all night.

**2 Samuel 4:8**

And they brought the head of Ishbosheth to David in Hebron and said to the king, Behold, the head of Ishbosheth son of Saul your enemy who sought your life, and the Lord has given to my lord the king vengeance from your enemies as this day, from Saul your enemy and from his seed.

**2 Samuel 4:9**

And David answered Rechab and Baana his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from every affliction,

**2 Samuel 4:10**

**2 Samuel 4:11**

And now evil men have killed a righteous man in his house on his bed, and now I will seek out his blood from your hand and wipe you out from the earth.

**2 Samuel 4:12**

And David commanded his young men, and they kill them and cut off their hands and their feet and hanged them by the pool in Hebron. And they buried the head of Ishbosheth in the tomb of Abner son of Ner.

#### Chapter 5

**2 Samuel 5:1**

And all the tribes of Israel come to David in Hebron and said to him, Behold, we are your bones and your flesh.

And all the elders of Israel come to the king in Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord, and they anointed David as king over all Israel.

**2 Samuel 5:15**

**2 Samuel 5:16**

and Elishama and Eliada and Elpalet, Samae, Iessibath, Nathan, Galamaan, Iebaar, Elishua, Eliphalet, Nogahd, Nepheg, Ianatha, Leasamys, Baalimath, Elpalet.

**2 Samuel 5:17**

And the foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David, and David heard and went down into the stronghold.

**2 Samuel 5:18**

And the foreigners come and fell in the Valley of the Titans.

**2 Samuel 5:19**

And David inquired through the Lord, saying, Shall I go up against the foreigners, and will you deliver them into my hands? And the Lord said to David, Go up, because in delivering I will deliver the foreigners into your hands.

**2 Samuel 5:20**

**2 Samuel 5:21**

And they leave their gods there, and David and the men with him took them.

**2 Samuel 5:22**

And the foreigners again added to go up and fell in the Valley of the Titans.

**2 Samuel 5:23**

And David inquired through the Lord, and the Lord said, You will not go up to meet them; turn away from them and come upon them near the grove of weeping.

**2 Samuel 5:24**

And it will be, when you hear the voice of the closing together of the grove of weeping, then you will go down to them, because then the Lord will go out before you to strike in the battle of the foreigners.

**2 Samuel 5:25**

#### Chapter 6

**2 Samuel 6:1**

And David gathered again every young man from Israel, about seventy thousand.

**2 Samuel 6:2**

And David rose and all the people with him from the leaders of Judah, in the ascent to bring up from there the ark of God, on which the name of the Lord of hosts seated upon the cherubim over it had been called.

**2 Samuel 6:3**

And they set the ark of the Lord on a new wagon and took it up from the house of Amminadab on the hill, and Uzzah and his brothers, sons of Amminadab, were leading the wagon.

**2 Samuel 6:4**

With the ark, and his brothers were going before the ark.

**2 Samuel 6:5**

And David and the sons of Israel were playing before the Lord with fitted instruments in strength and with songs and with lyres and with harps and with tambourines and with cymbals and with pipes.

**2 Samuel 6:6**

**2 Samuel 6:7**

**2 Samuel 6:8**

**2 Samuel 6:9**

**2 Samuel 6:10**

**2 Samuel 6:11**

**2 Samuel 6:12**

And it was reported to King David, saying, The Lord has blessed the house of Obededom and all his things for the sake of the ark of God. And David went and brought up the ark of the Lord from the house of Obededom into the City of David with gladness.

**2 Samuel 6:13**

And with them were seven circles carrying the ark, and sacrifice: a calf and a lamb.

**2 Samuel 6:14**

And David was beating time with fitted instruments before the Lord, and David was clothed in an exquisite robe.

**2 Samuel 6:15**

And David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting and with the voice of a trumpet.

**2 Samuel 6:16**

And it came to be, as the ark was coming as far as the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul was looking through the window, and she saw King David dancing and beating time before the Lord, and she counted him as nothing in her heart.

**2 Samuel 6:17**

And they bring the ark of the Lord and set it in its place in the midst of the tent that David pitched for it, and David offered whole burnt offerings before the Lord and peace offerings.

**2 Samuel 6:18**

And David finished offering the whole burnt offerings and the peace offerings and blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts.

**2 Samuel 6:19**

And he distributed to all the people, to all the host of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, from man to woman, to each a cake of bread and a roasted cake and a pan-cake, and all the people went away, each to his house.

**2 Samuel 6:20**

And David returned to bless his house, and Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet David and blessed him and said, How glorious today was the king of Israel, who was uncovered today in the eyes of the servant-girls of his servants, just as one of the dancers uncovers himself in being uncovered.

**2 Samuel 6:21**

And David said to Michal, I will dance before the Lord. Blessed be the Lord, who chose me over your father and over all his house, to appoint me as a leader over his people, over Israel, and I will play and dance before the Lord.

**2 Samuel 6:22**

And I will uncover myself still more thus, and I will be worthless in your eyes, but with the servant-girls of whom you spoke, with them I will be glorified.

**2 Samuel 6:23**

And to Michal daughter of Saul there came to be no child until the day of her death.

#### Chapter 7

**2 Samuel 7:1**

And it came to be when the king sat in his house, and the Lord gave him inheritance-rest all around from all his enemies around him,

**2 Samuel 7:2**

that the king said to Nathan the prophet, Behold now, I dwell in a cedar house, and the ark of God sits in the midst of the tent.

**2 Samuel 7:3**

And Nathan said to the king, All things whatever are in your heart, go and do, because the Lord is with you.

**2 Samuel 7:4**

And it came to be on that night, the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,

**2 Samuel 7:5**

Go and say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord: You will not build me a house for my dwelling in it.

**2 Samuel 7:6**

Because I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought up the sons of Israel from Egypt until this day, but I was walking about in lodging and in tent.

**2 Samuel 7:7**

In all the things through which I passed in all Israel, did I ever speak a word to one tribe of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, Why have you not built me a cedar house?

**2 Samuel 7:8**

And now thus you will say to my servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty, I took you from the fold of the sheep, for you to be leader over my people, over Israel.

**2 Samuel 7:9**

And I was with you in all things wherever you went, and I destroyed all your enemies from before you and made you a name like the name of the great ones upon the earth.

**2 Samuel 7:10**

And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and I will plant him, and he will tabernacle by himself and will no longer be anxious, and a son of wrongdoing will no longer add to humble him as from the beginning,

**2 Samuel 7:11**

from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord reports to you that you will build a house for him.

**2 Samuel 7:12**

And it will be, if your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who will be from your belly, and I will make his kingdom ready.

**2 Samuel 7:13**

He will build a house for my name, and I will set upright his throne forever.

**2 Samuel 7:14**

I will be to him for a father, and he will be to me for a son, and if his wrongdoing comes, I will reprove him with the rod of men and with touches of the sons of men.

**2 Samuel 7:15**

But my mercy I will not remove from him, just as I removed it from those whom I removed from before my face.

**2 Samuel 7:16**

And his house and his kingdom will be made faithful forever before me, and his throne will be set upright forever.

**2 Samuel 7:17**

According to all these words and according to all this vision, thus Nathan spoke to David.

**2 Samuel 7:18**

And King David entered and sat before the Lord and said, Who am I, my Lord, O Lord, and what is my house, that you have loved me up to these things?

**2 Samuel 7:19**

And this was made a very small thing before you, my Lord, O Lord, and you spoke concerning the house of your servant for a long time to come. And this is the law of the human, my Lord, O Lord.

**2 Samuel 7:20**

And what will David add still to speak to you? And now you know your servant, my Lord, O Lord.

**2 Samuel 7:21**

For the sake of your word you have done and according to your heart you have done all this greatness to make it known to your servant.

**2 Samuel 7:22**

Because of making you great, my Lord, O Lord, because there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, in all things that we heard in our ears.

**2 Samuel 7:23**

And who is like your people Israel, another nation on the earth, as God led him to redeem for himself a people, to set for yourself a name, to do greatness and splendor by driving out before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt nations and tents?

**2 Samuel 7:24**

And you prepared for yourself your people Israel as a people forever, and you, Lord, became for them as God.

**2 Samuel 7:25**

And now, my Lord, O Lord, the word that you spoke concerning your servant and his house, establish forever, O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, and now just as you spoke.

**2 Samuel 7:26**

May your name be magnified forever.

**2 Samuel 7:27**

Lord Almighty, God of Israel, you uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, I will build you a house. Because of this your servant found his heart to pray to you this prayer.

**2 Samuel 7:28**

And now, my Lord, O Lord, you are God, and your words will be true, and you spoke these good things concerning your servant.

**2 Samuel 7:29**

And now begin and bless the house of your servant, for it to be forever before you, because you, my Lord, O Lord, have spoken, and from your blessing the house of your servant will be blessed forever.

#### Chapter 8

**2 Samuel 8:1**

And it came to be after these things, David struck the foreigners and routed them, and David took the separated thing from the hand of the foreigners.

**2 Samuel 8:2**

**2 Samuel 8:3**

And David struck Hadadezer son of Rehob king of Zobah, as he was going to set up his hand on the river Euphrates.

**2 Samuel 8:4**

And David pre-took from his men one thousand chariots and seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand footmen, and David lamed all the chariots, and from them one hundred chariots were left.

**2 Samuel 8:5**

And Syria of Damascus comes to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, and David struck among the Syrians twenty-two thousand men.

**2 Samuel 8:6**

And David placed a garrison in Syria by Damascus, and Syria became to David as servants bringing gifts, and the Lord saved David in all things wherever he went.

**2 Samuel 8:7**

And David took the golden bracelets that were upon the servants of Hadadezer king of Zobah and brought them to Jerusalem. And Shishak king of Egypt took them when he came up to Jerusalem in the days of Rehoboam son of Solomon.

**2 Samuel 8:8**

And from Masbak, from the chosen cities of Hadadezer, King David took very much bronze. In it Solomon made the bronze sea and the pillars and the basins and all the vessels.

**2 Samuel 8:9**

And Toi king of Hamath heard that David struck all the force of Hadadezer,

**2 Samuel 8:10**

**2 Samuel 8:11**

And King David consecrated these things to the Lord, along with the silver and along with the gold that he consecrated from all the cities that he subdued,

**2 Samuel 8:12**

from Edom and from the land of Moab and from the sons of Ammon and from the foreigners and from Amalek and from the spoils of Hadadezer son of Rehob king of Zobah.

**2 Samuel 8:13**

And David made a name, and on his return he struck Edom in Gaimel, eighteen thousand.

**2 Samuel 8:14**

And he placed a garrison in Edom; in all Edom he placed a garrison, and all the Edomites became servants to the king, and the Lord saved David in all things wherever he went.

**2 Samuel 8:15**

And David reigned over Israel, and David was doing judgment and righteousness over all his people.

**2 Samuel 8:16**

And Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahijah was over the records,

**2 Samuel 8:17**

and Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Asa the scribe,

**2 Samuel 8:18**

and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was counselor, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and sons of David were chiefs of the court.

#### Chapter 9

**2 Samuel 9:1**

And David said, Is there still one left of the house of Saul, that I may do mercy with him for the sake of Jonathan?

**2 Samuel 9:2**

And from the house of Saul there was a servant, and his name was Ziba, and they call him to David, and the king said to him, Are you Ziba? And he said, I am your servant.

**2 Samuel 9:3**

And the king said, Is there still a man left from the house of Saul, that I may do mercy of God with him? And Ziba said to the king, There is still a son for Jonathan, stricken in the feet.

**2 Samuel 9:4**

And the king said, Where is he? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.

**2 Samuel 9:5**

And King David sent and took him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lodebar.

**2 Samuel 9:6**

And Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul comes to King David and fell on his face and bowed down to him, and David said to him, Mephibosheth. And he said, Behold, your servant.

**2 Samuel 9:7**

And David said to him, Do not fear, because in doing I will do mercy with you for the sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the field of Saul father of your father, and you will eat bread at my table continually.

**2 Samuel 9:8**

And Mephibosheth bowed down and said, What am I, your servant, that you looked upon the dead dog, one like me?

**2 Samuel 9:9**

And the king called Ziba, the young servant of Saul, and said to him, All things whatever belong to Saul and to all his house I have given to the son of your lord.

**2 Samuel 9:10**

And work the land for him, you and your sons and your servants, and you will bring breads to the son of your lord, and he will eat them. And Mephibosheth son of your lord will continually eat bread at my table. And Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

**2 Samuel 9:11**

And Ziba said to the king, According to all things whatever my lord the king has commanded his servant, thus your servant will do. And Mephibosheth was eating at David’s table as one of the sons of the king.

**2 Samuel 9:12**

And to Mephibosheth there was a little son, and his name was Micha, and all the dwelling of the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.

**2 Samuel 9:13**

And Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he continually was eating at the table of the king, and he was lame in both his feet.

#### Chapter 10

**2 Samuel 10:1**

And it came to be after these things, the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned instead of him.

**2 Samuel 10:2**

And David said, I will do mercy with Hanun son of Nahash, in the way his father did mercy with me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants concerning his father, and the servants of David came into the land of the sons of Ammon.

**2 Samuel 10:3**

And the rulers of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, Is it to glorify your father before you that David sent comforters to you? Is it not to search the city and spy it out and inspect it that David sent his servants to you?

**2 Samuel 10:4**

And Hanun took the servants of David and shaved their beards and cut their cloaks in the middle up to their buttocks and sent them away.

**2 Samuel 10:5**

**2 Samuel 10:6**

And the sons of Ammon saw that the people of David had been put to shame, and the sons of Ammon sent and hired Syria of Bethrehob, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maachah, one thousand men, and Ishtob, twelve thousand men.

**2 Samuel 10:7**

And David heard and sent Joab and all the force, the mighty men.

**2 Samuel 10:8**

And the sons of Ammon went out and arrayed for war by the entrance of the gate, and Syria of Zobah and Rehob and Ishtob and Maachah were alone in the field.

**2 Samuel 10:9**

And Joab saw that the front of the battle had come to be against him from the front opposite and from the rear, and he chose from all the young men of Israel and arrayed them opposite Syria.

**2 Samuel 10:10**

**2 Samuel 10:11**

**2 Samuel 10:12**

**2 Samuel 10:13**

And Joab and the people with him came near to war against Syria, and they fled from before him.

**2 Samuel 10:14**

**2 Samuel 10:15**

And Syria saw that it had stumbled before Israel, and they were gathered together.

**2 Samuel 10:16**

And Hadarezer sent and gathered Syria from beyond the river Helam, and they came to Helam, and Shobach, chief of the force of Hadarezer, was before them.

**2 Samuel 10:17**

And it was reported to David, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came to Helam, and Syria arrayed opposite David and fought with him.

**2 Samuel 10:18**

And Syria fled from before Israel, and David killed from Syria seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen, and Shobach the chief of his force he struck, and he died there.

**2 Samuel 10:19**

#### Chapter 11

**2 Samuel 11:1**

And it came to be at the turning of the year, at the season of the campaigns of kings, David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they ravaged the sons of Ammon and sat down against Rabbah, but David sat in Jerusalem.

**2 Samuel 11:2**

And it came to be toward evening, David rose from his bed and was walking on the roof of the king’s house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful in appearance.

**2 Samuel 11:3**

And David sent and asked about the woman, and someone said, Is not this Bathsheba daughter of Eliab, wife of Uriah the Hittite?

**2 Samuel 11:4**

And David sent messengers and took her, and he went in to her and lay with her, and she was sanctifying herself from her uncleanness, and she returned to her house.

**2 Samuel 11:5**

And the woman conceived, and having sent, she reported to David and said, I am with child.

**2 Samuel 11:6**

And David sent to Joab, saying, Send to me Uriah the Hittite, and Joab sent Uriah to David.

**2 Samuel 11:7**

And Uriah comes and entered to him, and David asked concerning the peace of Joab and concerning the peace of the people and concerning the peace of the war.

**2 Samuel 11:8**

And David said to Uriah, Go down to your house and wash your feet. And Uriah went out from the king’s house, and the king’s carrying gift went out after him.

**2 Samuel 11:9**

And Uriah slept by the door of the king’s house with the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.

**2 Samuel 11:10**

And they reported to David, saying that Uriah did not go down to his house, and David said to Uriah, Do you not come from a road? Why is it that you did not go down to your house?

**2 Samuel 11:11**

And Uriah said to David, The ark and Israel and Judah dwell in tents, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord camp on the face of the field, and shall I enter into my house to eat and drink and to lie with my wife? As your life lives, if I do this thing.

**2 Samuel 11:12**

And David said to Uriah, Sit here today also, and tomorrow I will send you away. And Uriah sat in Jerusalem on that day and the next day.

**2 Samuel 11:13**

And David called him, and he ate before him and drank, and he made him drunk, and he went out in the evening to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but to his own house he did not go down.

**2 Samuel 11:14**

And it came to be in the morning, David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.

**2 Samuel 11:15**

And he wrote in the letter, saying, Bring Uriah into the front of the hard battle and turn back from behind him, and he will be struck and die.

**2 Samuel 11:16**

And it came to be while Joab was guarding the city, he put Uriah in the place where he knew men of strength were there.

**2 Samuel 11:17**

And the men of the city came out and were fighting with Joab, and some of the people from the servants of David fell, and also Uriah the Hittite died.

**2 Samuel 11:18**

And Joab sent and reported to the king all the words of the war,

**2 Samuel 11:19**

and he commanded the messenger, saying, When you finish speaking all the words of the war to the king,

**2 Samuel 11:20**
