**2 Samuel 11:21**

Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbaal? Did not a woman throw a piece of millstone upon him from above the wall, and he died at Thebez? Why did you go near the wall? Then you will say, And also your servant Uriah the Hittite died.

**2 Samuel 11:22**

And the messenger of Joab went to the king in Jerusalem and came and reported to David all that Joab reported to him, all the words of the war. And David became angry at Joab and said to the messenger, Why did you go near the city to fight? Did you not know that you would be struck from the wall? Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbaal? Did not a woman throw a piece of millstone on him from the wall, and he died in Thebez? Why did you go near the wall?

**2 Samuel 11:23**

And the messenger said to David, Because the men grew strong against us and came out against us into the field, and we came against them as far as the door of the gate,

**2 Samuel 11:24**

and the archers shot at your servants from above the wall, and some of the servants of the king died, and also your servant Uriah the Hittite died.

**2 Samuel 11:25**

And David said to the messenger, Thus you will say to Joab: Let not this word be evil in your eyes, because once thus and once thus the sword will eat. Strengthen your battle against the city and tear it down, and strengthen him.

**2 Samuel 11:26**

And the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband had died, and she mourned for her husband.

**2 Samuel 11:27**

And the mourning passed, and David sent and gathered her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the word that David had done appeared evil in the eyes of the Lord.

#### Chapter 12

**2 Samuel 12:1**

And the Lord sent Nathan the prophet to David, and he entered to him and said to him, There were two men in one city, one rich and one poor.

**2 Samuel 12:2**

And the rich man had very many flocks and herds.

**2 Samuel 12:3**

And to the poor man there was nothing except one little ewe lamb, which he acquired and kept alive and nourished, and it grew up with him and with his sons together. From his bread it would eat and from his cup it would drink and in his bosom it would sleep, and it was to him as a daughter.

**2 Samuel 12:4**

And a traveler came to the rich man, and he spared to take from his flocks and from his herds to prepare for the stranger traveler who came to him, and he took the ewe lamb of the poor man and prepared it for the man who came to him.

**2 Samuel 12:5**

And the anger of David burned greatly against the man, and David said to Nathan, As the Lord lives, the man who did this is a son of death.

**2 Samuel 12:6**

And he will repay the ewe lamb sevenfold, because he did this thing and because he did not spare.

**2 Samuel 12:7**

And Nathan said to David, You are the man who did this. Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I am the one who anointed you as king over Israel, and I am the one who delivered you from the hand of Saul,

**2 Samuel 12:8**

and I gave you the house of your lord and the wives of your lord into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah, and if this is little, I will add to you according to these things.

**2 Samuel 12:9**

Why did you count the word of the Lord as little, to do the evil in his eyes? Uriah the Hittite you struck with the sword, and his wife you took for yourself as wife, and him you killed with the sword of the sons of Ammon.

**2 Samuel 12:10**

And now the sword will not depart from your house forever, because you counted me as nothing and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.

**2 Samuel 12:11**

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am raising evils against you out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives before this sun.

**2 Samuel 12:12**

Because you did it in secret, but I will do this word in front of all Israel and before this sun.

**2 Samuel 12:13**

And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said to David, And the Lord has caused your sin to pass over; you certainly will not die.

**2 Samuel 12:14**

Only because in provoking you provoked the enemies of the Lord by this word, indeed the son born to you will surely die.

**2 Samuel 12:15**

And Nathan went to his house, and the Lord struck the child whom the wife of Uriah bore to David, and he became sick.

**2 Samuel 12:16**

And David sought God concerning the little boy, and David fasted a fast and entered and lodged in sackcloth on the ground.

**2 Samuel 12:17**

And the elders of his house stood over him to raise him up from the ground, and he was not willing, and he did not eat bread with them.

**2 Samuel 12:18**

And it came to be on the seventh day, the little boy died, and the servants of David feared to report to him that the little boy had died, because they said, Behold, while the little boy was still living we spoke to him, and he did not listen to our voice, and how shall we say to him that the little boy has died? He will do evil.

**2 Samuel 12:19**

And David understood that his servants were whispering, and David discerned that the little boy had died, and David said to his servants, Has the little boy died? And they said, He has died.

**2 Samuel 12:20**

And David rose from the ground and washed and anointed himself and changed his garments and entered into the house of God and bowed down to him. And he entered into his house and asked for bread to eat, and they set bread before him, and he ate.

**2 Samuel 12:21**

And his servants said to him, What is this word that you have done? For the little boy, while he was still alive, you were fasting and weeping and keeping watch, and when the little boy died, you rose and ate bread and have drunk.

**2 Samuel 12:22**

And David said, While the little boy was still living, I fasted and wept, because I said, Who knows whether the Lord will have mercy on me and the little boy will live?

**2 Samuel 12:23**

And now he has died. Why now am I fasting? Shall I be able to bring him back still more? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.

**2 Samuel 12:24**

And David comforted Bathsheba his wife and entered to her and lay with her, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Solomon, and the Lord loved him.

**2 Samuel 12:25**

And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Idedi because of the Lord.

**2 Samuel 12:26**

And Joab fought at Rabbah of the sons of Ammon and captured the city of the kingdom.

**2 Samuel 12:27**

And Joab sent messengers to David and said, I fought at Rabbah and captured the city of waters.

**2 Samuel 12:28**

And now gather the rest of the people and camp against the city and capture it beforehand, lest I capture the city and my name be called upon it.

**2 Samuel 12:29**

And David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah and fought in it and captured it.

**2 Samuel 12:30**

And he took the crown of their king from his head, and its weight was a talent of gold and precious stone, and it was on David’s head, and he brought out the spoils of the city very greatly.

**2 Samuel 12:31**

And the people in it he brought out and set with the saw and with the iron threshing sledges and made them pass through the brickworks. And thus he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

#### Chapter 13

**2 Samuel 13:1**

And it came to be after these things, to Absalom son of David there was a sister very beautiful in appearance, and her name was Tamar, and Amnon son of David loved her.

**2 Samuel 13:2**

And Amnon was distressed so as to become sick because of Tamar his sister, because she was a virgin, and it was over-large in the eyes of Amnon to do anything to her.

**2 Samuel 13:3**

And to Amnon there was a companion, and his name was Jonadab son of Shimeah, brother of David, and Jonadab was a very wise man.

**2 Samuel 13:4**

And he said to him, Why are you thus weak, son of the king, morning by morning? Will you not report to me? And Amnon said to him, I love Tamar, sister of Absalom my brother.

**2 Samuel 13:5**

And Jonadab said to him, Lie on your bed and make yourself weak, and your father will enter to see you, and you will say to him, Let Tamar my sister now come to me and feed me morsels and prepare food before my eyes, so that I may see and eat from her hands.

**2 Samuel 13:6**

And Amnon lay down and became sick, and the king entered to see him, and Amnon said to the king, Let Tamar my sister now come to me and make before my eyes two cakes, and I will eat from her hand.

**2 Samuel 13:7**

And David sent to Tamar to the house, saying, Go now to the house of Amnon your brother and make food for him.

**2 Samuel 13:8**

And Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down, and she took dough and kneaded it and made cakes before his eyes and baked the cakes.

**2 Samuel 13:9**

And she took the pan and emptied it out before him, and he was not willing to eat. And Amnon said, Put out every man from me, and they put out every man from him.

**2 Samuel 13:10**

And Amnon said to Tamar, Bring the food into the inner room, and I will eat from your hand. And Tamar took the cakes that she had made and brought them in to Amnon her brother into the bedroom.

**2 Samuel 13:11**

And she brought them near to him to eat, and he seized her and said to her, Come, lie with me, my sister.

**2 Samuel 13:12**

And she said to him, No, my brother, do not humble me, because thus it will not be done in Israel. Do not do this folly.

**2 Samuel 13:13**

And I, where will I carry away my reproach? And you, you will be as one of the fools in Israel. And now speak now to the king, because he certainly will not withhold me from you.

**2 Samuel 13:14**

And Amnon was not willing to hear her voice, and he grew strong beyond her and humbled her and lay with her.

**2 Samuel 13:15**

And Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, because the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he loved her. And Amnon said to her, Rise and go.

**2 Samuel 13:16**

And Tamar said to him, No, my brother, because this last evil is greater than the first, which you did with me, by sending me away. And Amnon was not willing to hear her voice.

**2 Samuel 13:17**

And he called his young servant, the one standing over his house, and said to him, Send this one away from me outside, and bar the door behind her.

**2 Samuel 13:18**

And upon her was a full-length tunic, because thus the king’s virgin daughters were clothed with their robes. And his attendant brought her out and barred the door behind her.

**2 Samuel 13:19**

And Tamar took ashes and put them upon her head, and the full-length tunic that was upon her she tore, and she put her hands on her head and went on, going and crying out.

**2 Samuel 13:20**

And Absalom her brother said to her, Has Amnon your brother been with you? And now, my sister, be deaf, because he is your brother; do not set your heart to speak concerning this word. And Tamar sat desolate in the house of Absalom her brother.

**2 Samuel 13:21**

And King David heard all these words and was greatly angered, and he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, because he was his firstborn.

**2 Samuel 13:22**

And Absalom did not speak with Amnon from evil to good, because Absalom hated Amnon over the matter in which he humbled Tamar his sister.

**2 Samuel 13:23**

And it came to be at a two-year cycle of days, they were shearing for Absalom at Baal-hazor by Ephraim, and Absalom called all the sons of the king.

**2 Samuel 13:24**

And Absalom came to the king and said, Behold now, they are shearing for your servant. Let the king and his servants now go with your servant.

**2 Samuel 13:25**

And the king said to Absalom, No, my son, let us not all go, and we certainly will not weigh heavily upon you. And he pressed him, and he was not willing to go, and he blessed him.

**2 Samuel 13:26**

And Absalom said, And if not, let Amnon my brother now go with us. And the king said to him, Why should he go with you?

**2 Samuel 13:27**

And Absalom pressed him, and he sent with him Amnon and all the sons of the king, and Absalom made a feast like the feast of the king.

**2 Samuel 13:28**

And Absalom commanded his young men, saying, See when the heart of Amnon is made good with wine, and I say to you, Strike Amnon and kill him. Do not fear, because am not I the one commanding you? Be manly and become sons of strength.

**2 Samuel 13:29**

And the young men of Absalom did to Amnon just as Absalom commanded them, and all the sons of the king rose and mounted, each on his mule, and fled.

**2 Samuel 13:30**

And it came to be while they were on the road, the report came to David, saying, Absalom struck all the sons of the king, and not one was left from them.

**2 Samuel 13:31**

And the king rose and tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants standing around him tore their garments.

**2 Samuel 13:32**

And Jonadab son of Shimeah brother of David answered and said, Let not my lord the king say that he killed all the young men, the sons of the king, because only Amnon has died, because by the mouth of Absalom it was laid from the day when he humbled Tamar his sister.

**2 Samuel 13:33**

And now let not my lord the king set on his heart a word, saying, All the sons of the king have died, because only Amnon has died.

**2 Samuel 13:34**

And Absalom fled. And the young man, the watchman, lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold, many people were coming on the road behind him from the side of the mountain on the descent, and the watchman came and reported to the king and said, I have seen men from the road of Oronen from the side of the mountain.

**2 Samuel 13:35**

And Jonadab said to the king, Behold, the sons of the king are coming. According to the word of your servant, thus it came to be.

**2 Samuel 13:36**

And it came to be when he finished speaking, behold, the sons of the king came and lifted up their voice and wept, and also the king and all his servants wept with a very great weeping.

**2 Samuel 13:37**

And Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, to the land of Machad, and King David mourned for his son all the days.

**2 Samuel 13:38**

And Absalom fled and went to Geshur and was there three years.

**2 Samuel 13:39**

And the spirit of the king ceased from going out after Absalom, because he was comforted over Amnon, because he died.

#### Chapter 14

**2 Samuel 14:1**

And Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the heart of the king was upon Absalom.

**2 Samuel 14:2**

And Joab sent to Tekoa and took from there a wise woman and said to her, Mourn now and put on mourning garments and do not anoint with oil, and you will be as a woman mourning over one dead for many days.

**2 Samuel 14:3**

And you will come to the king and speak to him according to this word. And Joab put the words in her mouth.

**2 Samuel 14:4**

And the Tekoah woman entered to the king and fell on her face to the ground and bowed down to him and said, Save, king, save.

**2 Samuel 14:5**

And the king said to her, What is with you? And she said, Truly I am a widow woman, and my husband died.

**2 Samuel 14:6**

And indeed your servant had two sons, and both fought in the field, and there was no one separating between them, and the one struck his brother and killed him.

**2 Samuel 14:7**

And behold, the whole clan rose against your servant and said, Give the one striking his brother, and we will put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and we will remove also your heir. And they will quench my coal left behind, so as not to set for my husband remnant and name on the face of the earth.

**2 Samuel 14:8**

And the king said, Go to your house in health, and I myself will command concerning you.

**2 Samuel 14:9**

And the Tekoah woman said to the king, Upon me, my lord king, be the lawlessness, and upon my father’s house, and the king and his throne are innocent.

**2 Samuel 14:10**

And the king said, Who is speaking to you? And you will bring him to me, and he will not add still to touch him.

**2 Samuel 14:11**

And she said, Let the king now remember the Lord his God, that the avenger of blood not multiply to destroy, and they certainly will not remove my son. And he said, As the Lord lives, if a hair of your son falls to the ground.

**2 Samuel 14:12**

And the woman said, Let your servant now speak a word to my lord the king. And he said, Speak.

**2 Samuel 14:13**

And the woman said, Why have you reckoned such a thing against the people of God? Even from the mouth of the king this word is like an offense, in that the king does not bring back his banished one.

**2 Samuel 14:14**

Because in death we will die, and like the water poured down upon the ground, which will not be gathered, and God will take a life, yet he devises ways for the banished one not to remain banished from him.

**2 Samuel 14:15**

And now that I came to speak this word to my lord the king is because the people will see me, and your servant will say, Let me now speak to the king, if perhaps the king will do the word of his servant.

**2 Samuel 14:16**

Because the king will listen to rescue his servant from the hand of the man seeking to remove me and my son from the inheritance of God.

**2 Samuel 14:17**

And the woman said, Let the word of my lord the king now be as an offering, because as an angel of God so is my lord the king, to hear the good and the evil, and the Lord your God will be with you.

**2 Samuel 14:18**

And the king answered and said to the woman, Do not hide from me now a word which I ask you. And the woman said, Let my lord the king speak.

**2 Samuel 14:19**

And the king said, Is the hand of Joab with you in all this? And the woman said to the king, As your life lives, my lord king, there is not to the right or to the left from all that my lord the king spoke, because your servant Joab, he himself commanded me, and he himself put in the mouth of your servant all these words.

**2 Samuel 14:20**

For the sake of turning the face of this matter, your servant Joab did this thing, and my lord is wise like the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all the things on the earth.

**2 Samuel 14:21**

And the king said to Joab, Behold now, I have done for you according to this word of yours. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.

**2 Samuel 14:22**

And Joab fell on his face to the ground and bowed down and blessed the king, and Joab said, Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord king, because my lord the king has done the word of his servant.

**2 Samuel 14:23**

And Joab rose and went to Geshur and brought Absalom into Jerusalem.

**2 Samuel 14:24**

And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. And Absalom turned to his house, and he did not see the face of the king.

**2 Samuel 14:25**

And as for Absalom, there was no man in all Israel praised so greatly. From the sole of his foot to his crown there was no blemish in him.

**2 Samuel 14:26**

And when he cut his head, and it came to be from the beginning of days to days as he would cut it because it weighed heavily upon him, cutting it he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the royal shekel.

**2 Samuel 14:27**

And there were born to Absalom three sons and one daughter, and her name was Tamar. She was a very beautiful woman and became wife to Rehoboam son of Solomon and bore to him Abijah.

**2 Samuel 14:28**

And Absalom sat in Jerusalem two years of days, and he did not see the face of the king.

**2 Samuel 14:29**

And Absalom sent to Joab to send him to the king, and he was not willing to come to him, and he sent a second time to him, and he was not willing to come.

**2 Samuel 14:30**

And Absalom said to his servants, See, the portion in the field of Joab lies next to mine, and barley is there. Go and burn it with fire. And the servants of Absalom burned them, and the servants of Joab came to him with garments torn and said, The servants of Absalom burned the portion with fire.

**2 Samuel 14:31**

And Joab rose and came to Absalom at the house and said to him, Why did your servants burn my portion with fire?

**2 Samuel 14:32**

And Absalom said to Joab, Behold, I sent to you, saying, Come here and I will send you to the king, saying, Why did I come from Geshur? It was good for me still to be there. And now behold, I have not seen the face of the king, and if there is wrongdoing in me, then put me to death.

**2 Samuel 14:33**

And Joab entered to the king and reported to him, and he called Absalom, and he entered to the king and bowed down to him and fell on his face to the ground before the king, and the king kissed Absalom.

#### Chapter 15

**2 Samuel 15:1**

And it came to be after these things, Absalom made for himself chariots and horses and fifty men to run before him.

**2 Samuel 15:2**

And Absalom rose early and stood by the side of the road of the gate, and it came to be every man who had a judgment came to the king for judgment, and Absalom would cry out to him and say to him, From what city are you? And the man would say, Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel.

**2 Samuel 15:3**

And Absalom said to him, Behold, your words are good and easy, but there is no one hearing you from the king.

**2 Samuel 15:4**

And Absalom said, Who will appoint me judge in the land? And to me every man with dispute and judgment will come, and I will justify him.

**2 Samuel 15:5**

And it came to be, when a man came near to bow down to him, he stretched out his hand and took hold of him and kissed him.

**2 Samuel 15:6**

And Absalom did according to this word to all Israel who were coming for judgment to the king, and Absalom was stealing the heart of the men of Israel.

**2 Samuel 15:7**

And it came to be at the end of forty years, Absalom said to his father, I will now go and pay my vows that I vowed to the Lord in Hebron.

**2 Samuel 15:8**

Because your servant vowed a vow while I was dwelling in Geshur in Syria, saying, If in returning the Lord returns me to Jerusalem, I will serve the Lord.

**2 Samuel 15:9**

And the king said to him, Go in peace. And rising, he went to Hebron.

**2 Samuel 15:10**

And Absalom sent spies into all the tribes of Israel, saying, When you hear the sound of the horn, then you will say, King Absalom has become king in Hebron.

**2 Samuel 15:11**

And with Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem, invited and going in their simplicity, and they knew no word.

**2 Samuel 15:12**

And Absalom sent and called Ahithophel the Gilonite, counselor of David, from his city, from Giloh, while he was sacrificing, and the conspiracy became strong, and the people going with Absalom were many.

**2 Samuel 15:13**

And the one reporting came to David, saying, The heart of the men of Israel has come to be behind Absalom.

**2 Samuel 15:14**

And David said to all his servants with him in Jerusalem, Rise, and let us flee, because there is no salvation for us from before Absalom. Hurry to go, lest he hurry and overtake us and drive evil upon us and strike the city with the mouth of the sword.

**2 Samuel 15:15**

And the servants of the king said to the king, According to all things whatever my lord the king chooses, behold, your servants.

**2 Samuel 15:16**

And the king went out and all his house on their feet, and the king left ten women, his concubines, to guard the house.

**2 Samuel 15:17**

And the king went out and all his servants on foot, and they stood at the far house.

**2 Samuel 15:18**

And all his servants were passing by his side, and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites stood by the olive tree in the wilderness, and all the people were passing on near him, and all those around him and all the stout men and all the fighters, six hundred men, and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come on their feet from Gath, were going before the king.

**2 Samuel 15:19**

And the king said to Ittai the Gittite, Why are you also going with us? Return and dwell with the king, because you are a foreigner and because you have migrated from your place.

**2 Samuel 15:20**

Yesterday you came, and today shall I move you with us? And indeed you will migrate your place? Yesterday your coming, and today shall I move you with us to go? And I will go wherever I go. Return and return your brothers with you, and the Lord will do mercy and truth with you.

**2 Samuel 15:21**

And Ittai answered the king and said, As the Lord lives and as my lord the king lives, in the place where my lord is, whether for death or for life, there your servant will be.

**2 Samuel 15:22**

And the king said to Ittai, Come and pass over with me. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his servants and all the crowd with him.

**2 Samuel 15:23**

And all the land was weeping with a great voice, and all the people were passing in the wadi Kidron, and the king crossed the wadi Kidron, and all the people and the king were passing on toward the road of the wilderness.

**2 Samuel 15:24**

And behold, also Zadok and all the Levites with him carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord from Abiathar, and they set the ark of God down, and Abiathar went up until all the people ceased passing out of the city.

**2 Samuel 15:25**

And the king said to Zadok, Turn back the ark of God into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the Lord, he will return me and show me it and its beauty.

**2 Samuel 15:26**

And if he says thus, I have not delighted in you, behold, here I am; let him do to me according to the good in his eyes.

**2 Samuel 15:27**

And the king said to Zadok the priest, See, you are returning into the city in peace, and Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons with you.

**2 Samuel 15:28**

See, I am encamping in the plains of the wilderness until a word comes from you to report to me.

**2 Samuel 15:29**

And Zadok and Abiathar turned the ark into Jerusalem and sat there.

**2 Samuel 15:30**

And David was going up in the ascent of the olives, going up and weeping, and his head covered, and he was going barefoot, and all the people with him covered each man his head, and they were going up, going up and weeping.

**2 Samuel 15:31**

And it was reported to David, saying, And Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, Scatter now the counsel of Ahithophel, Lord my God.

**2 Samuel 15:32**

And David was coming as far as the summit where he bowed there to God, and behold, to meet him was Cushi, chief companion of David, with his tunic torn and earth on his head.

**2 Samuel 15:33**

And David said to him, If you cross over with me, you will be a burden upon me.

**2 Samuel 15:34**

But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, Your brothers have passed through, and the king behind me, your father, has passed through, and now I am your servant, king; then I was your father's servant, and now again I am your servant, and you will scatter for me the counsel of Ahithophel.

**2 Samuel 15:35**

And behold, with you there are Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and every word whatever you hear from the house of the king, you will report to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

**2 Samuel 15:36**

Behold, there with them are their two sons, Ahimaaz to Zadok and Jonathan to Abiathar, and you will send by their hand to me every word whatever you hear.

**2 Samuel 15:37**

And Cushi, companion of David, entered into the city, and Absalom was entering into Jerusalem.

#### Chapter 16

**2 Samuel 16:1**

And David passed a little from the summit, and behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth came to meet him, and a pair of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves and one hundred raisins and one hundred dates and a skin of wine.

**2 Samuel 16:2**

And the king said to Ziba, What are these to you? And Ziba said, The pack animals are for the house of the king to sit on, and the loaves and the dates for food to the young men, and the wine for the ones faint in the wilderness to drink.

**2 Samuel 16:3**

And the king said, And where is the son of your lord? And Ziba said to the king, Behold, he sits in Jerusalem, because he said, Today the house of Israel will return to me the kingdom of my father.

**2 Samuel 16:4**

And the king said to Ziba, Behold, yours are all the things that belong to Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, Bowing down, May I find favor in your eyes, my lord king.

**2 Samuel 16:5**

And King David came as far as Bahurim, and behold, from there a man was coming out from the kin of the house of Saul, and his name was Shimei son of Gera. He came out going and cursing,

**2 Samuel 16:6**

and throwing stones at David and all the servants of King David, and all the people were there and all the mighty ones at the right and at the left of the king.

**2 Samuel 16:7**

And thus Shimei was saying while cursing him: Go out, go out, man of bloods and lawless man.

**2 Samuel 16:8**

The Lord has returned upon you all the bloods of the house of Saul, because you reigned instead of him, and the Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son, and behold, you are in your evil, because you are a man of bloods.

**2 Samuel 16:9**

And Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, Why is this dead dog cursing my lord the king? I will pass over now and remove his head.

**2 Samuel 16:10**

And the king said, What is to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah? Leave him and thus let him curse, because the Lord told him to curse David, and who will say, Why did you do thus?

**2 Samuel 16:11**

And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, Behold, my son who came out of my belly seeks my life, and how much more now this Benjamite. Leave him to curse, because the Lord told him.

**2 Samuel 16:12**

If perhaps the Lord will look upon my humiliation and return to me good instead of his curse on this day.

**2 Samuel 16:13**

And David and his men were going on the road, and Shimei was going on the side of the mountain next to him, going and cursing and throwing stones from his side and casting dust.

**2 Samuel 16:14**

And the king came and all his people faint, and they refreshed themselves there.

**2 Samuel 16:15**

And Absalom and every man of Israel entered into Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

**2 Samuel 16:16**

And it came to be, when Cushi, chief companion of David, came to Absalom, Cushi said to Absalom, Long live the king.

**2 Samuel 16:17**

And Absalom said to Cushi, Is this your mercy with your companion? Why did you not go with your companion?

**2 Samuel 16:18**

And Cushi said to Absalom, No, but behind whom the Lord chose and this people and every man of Israel, to him I will belong and with him I will sit.

**2 Samuel 16:19**

And the second thing: whom shall I serve? Shall it not be before his son? As I served before your father, so I will be before you.

**2 Samuel 16:20**

And Absalom said to Ahithophel, Bring counsel for yourselves. What shall we do?

**2 Samuel 16:21**

And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Go in to the concubines of your father whom he left to guard his house, and all Israel will hear that you have put your father to shame, and the hands of all those with you will be strengthened.

**2 Samuel 16:22**

And they pitched the tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to the concubines of his father before the eyes of all Israel.

**2 Samuel 16:23**

And the counsel of Ahithophel that he counseled in the former days was as if one inquired in the word of God. Thus was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both to David and to Absalom.

#### Chapter 17

**2 Samuel 17:1**

And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Let me choose for myself twelve thousand men, and I will rise and pursue David by night.

**2 Samuel 17:2**

And I will come upon him while he is weary and slack of hands, and I will throw him into panic, and all the people with him will flee, and I will strike the king alone.

**2 Samuel 17:3**

And I will return all the people to you, just as a bride returns to her husband. It is only the life of one man you seek, and all the people will be at peace.

**2 Samuel 17:4**

And the word was right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.

**2 Samuel 17:5**

And Absalom said, Call now also Cushi the Arachite, and let us hear what too is in his mouth.

**2 Samuel 17:6**

And Cushi came to Absalom, and Absalom said to him, saying, Ahithophel has spoken according to this word. Shall we do according to his word? But if not, you speak.

**2 Samuel 17:7**

And Cushi said to Absalom, This time the counsel that Ahithophel has counseled is not good.

**2 Samuel 17:8**

And Cushi said, You know your father and his men, that they are very mighty and bitter in soul, like a bear robbed of cubs in the field, and like a wild boar in the open country. And your father is a man of war and will not lodge with the people.

**2 Samuel 17:9**

For behold, even now he is hidden in one of the hills or in one of the places, and it will happen, when some fall among them at the first attack, that whoever hears will say, A slaughter has happened among the people following Absalom.

**2 Samuel 17:10**

Then even a son of strength, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will utterly melt, because all Israel knows that your father is mighty and the men with him are sons of strength.

**2 Samuel 17:11**

But this is the counsel I have counseled: let all Israel from Dan to Beersheba be gathered to you, like the sand by the sea in multitude, and let your own face go in their midst.

**2 Samuel 17:12**

And we will come upon him in one of the places where we find him there, and we will camp against him as the dew falls on the ground, and we will not leave among him and the men with him even one.

**2 Samuel 17:13**

And if he withdraws into a city, all Israel will take ropes to that city, and we will drag it down into the torrent-bed until not even a stone is left there.

**2 Samuel 17:14**

And Absalom and every man of Israel said, The counsel of Cushi the Arachite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the Lord commanded the good counsel of Ahithophel to be scattered, so that the Lord might bring all these evils upon Absalom.

**2 Samuel 17:15**

And Cushi the Arachite said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I counseled.

**2 Samuel 17:16**

And now send quickly and report to David, saying, Do not lodge tonight at the crossings of the wilderness, but hurry and cross over, lest the king and all the people with him be swallowed up.

**2 Samuel 17:17**

And Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been standing at the spring Enrogel, and the maidservant went and reported to them, and they were going to report to King David, because they could not be seen entering the city.

**2 Samuel 17:18**

But a young man saw them and reported it to Absalom, and the two went quickly and entered the house of a man in Bahurim, and he had a well in his court, and they went down there.

**2 Samuel 17:19**

And the woman took the covering and spread it over the face of the well, and she scattered crushed grain over it, and no matter was known.

**2 Samuel 17:20**

And the servants of Absalom came to the woman at the house and said, Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said to them, They passed a little beyond the water. And they searched and did not find them and returned to Jerusalem.

**2 Samuel 17:21**

And it came to be after they left, that they came up out of the well and went and reported to King David, and they said to David, Rise and cross the water quickly, because thus Ahithophel has counseled against you.

**2 Samuel 17:22**

And David rose, and all the people with him, and they crossed the Jordan until the morning light. Not one was missing who had not crossed the Jordan.

**2 Samuel 17:23**

And Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been done, and he saddled his donkey and rose and went to his home, to his own city, and he gave orders to his house and hanged himself, and he died and was buried in the tomb of his father.

**2 Samuel 17:24**

And David crossed over to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.

**2 Samuel 17:25**

And Absalom appointed Amasa in place of Joab over the army. And Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who went in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.

**2 Samuel 17:26**

And Israel and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.

**2 Samuel 17:27**

And it came to be when David came to Mahanaim, Ouesbi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and Machir son of Ammiel from Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,

**2 Samuel 17:28**

brought ten beds and coverings and ten cauldrons and earthenware vessels and wheat and barley and flour and parched grain and beans and lentils,

**2 Samuel 17:29**

and honey and butter and sheep and curds from cattle. And they brought them to David and to the people with him to eat, because they said, The people are hungry and faint and thirsty in the wilderness.

#### Chapter 18

**2 Samuel 18:1**

And David mustered the people with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

**2 Samuel 18:2**

And David sent out the people, one third by the hand of Joab, one third by the hand of Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and one third by the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And David said to the people, I myself will surely go out with you.

**2 Samuel 18:3**

But they said, You must not go out, because if we flee they will not set their heart on us, and if half of us die they will not set their heart on us, because you are like ten thousand of us. And now it is better that you be for us help from the city by helping.

**2 Samuel 18:4**

And the king said to them, Whatever is good in your eyes I will do. And the king stood by the side of the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

**2 Samuel 18:5**

And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Spare for my sake the young man Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave orders to all the commanders concerning Absalom.

**2 Samuel 18:6**

And all the people went out into the forest opposite Israel, and the battle came to be in the forest of Ephraim.

**2 Samuel 18:7**

And the people of Israel stumbled there before the servants of David, and the great slaughter there on that day was twenty thousand men.

**2 Samuel 18:8**

And the battle there was spread over the face of all the land, and the forest multiplied to devour more of the people than the sword devoured of the people on that day.

**2 Samuel 18:9**

And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom was mounted on his mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of the great oak, and his head was caught in the oak, and he was suspended between heaven and earth, and the mule under him passed on.

**2 Samuel 18:10**

And one man saw and reported to Joab and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in the oak.

**2 Samuel 18:11**

And Joab said to the man reporting to him, And behold, you saw him. Why then did you not strike him there to the ground? Then I would have given you ten silver pieces and one belt.

**2 Samuel 18:12**

But the man said to Joab, Even if a thousand silver shekels were weighed into my hands, I would never put my hand against the king's son. For in our hearing the king charged you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Guard for my sake the young man Absalom.

**2 Samuel 18:13**

Otherwise, if I had done lawlessness against his life, no word would be hidden from the king, and you yourself would have stood opposite.

**2 Samuel 18:14**

And Joab said, I will not linger thus before you. And Joab took three darts in his hand and drove them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the heart of the oak.

**2 Samuel 18:15**

And ten young men carrying the armor of Joab surrounded Absalom and struck him and put him to death.

**2 Samuel 18:16**

And Joab sounded with the trumpet, and the people turned back from pursuing after Israel, because Joab spared the people.

**2 Samuel 18:17**

And they took Absalom and cast him into a great pit in the forest and raised over him a very large heap of stones, and all Israel fled, a man to his tent.

**2 Samuel 18:18**

And Absalom had taken and set up for himself in his lifetime the pillar in the King's Valley, because he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance. And he called the pillar by his own name, and it is called Hand of Absalom to this day.

**2 Samuel 18:19**

And Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, Let me run now and bring good news to the king, because the Lord has judged for him against the hand of his enemies.

**2 Samuel 18:20**

And Joab said to him, You are not a bearer of good news on this day, but you may bring good news on another day. On this day you shall not bring good news, because the king's son is dead.

**2 Samuel 18:21**

And Joab said to Cushi, Go, report to the king what you have seen. And Cushi bowed to Joab and ran.

**2 Samuel 18:22**

And Ahimaaz son of Zadok again added and said to Joab, Whatever may happen, let me run too after Cushi. And Joab said, Why would you run, my son, since no payment of good news is for you?

**2 Samuel 18:23**

And he said, Whatever may happen, I will run. And he said to him, Run. And Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain and passed Cushi.

**2 Samuel 18:24**

And David was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof of the gate by the wall and lifted his eyes and saw, and behold, one man was running alone.

**2 Samuel 18:25**

And the watchman called out and reported to the king. And the king said, If he is alone, good news is in his mouth. And he came, going and coming near.

**2 Samuel 18:26**

And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called out to the gatekeeper and said, Behold, another man runs alone. And the king said, This one too is bringing good news.

**2 Samuel 18:27**

And the watchman said, I see the running of the first like the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man and comes in good news.

**2 Samuel 18:28**

And Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, Peace. And he bowed before the king with his face to the ground and said, Blessed be the Lord your God, who shut up the men who lifted their hand against my lord the king.

**2 Samuel 18:29**

And the king said, Is it well with the young man Absalom? And Ahimaaz said, I saw the great crowd when Joab sent the servant of the king and your servant, and I did not know what was there.

**2 Samuel 18:30**

And the king said, Turn aside, stand here. And he turned aside and stood.

**2 Samuel 18:31**

And behold, Cushi arrived and said to the king, Let my lord the king receive good news, because the Lord has judged for you today against the hand of all those rising against you.

**2 Samuel 18:32**

And the king said to Cushi, Is it well with the young man Absalom? And Cushi said, May the enemies of my lord the king and all who have risen up against him for evil become like that young man.

#### Chapter 19

**2 Samuel 19:1**

And the king was troubled and went up to the upper room of the gate and wept, and thus he said as he went, My son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom. Who will give my death instead of you? I, instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son.

**2 Samuel 19:2**

And it was reported to Joab, saying, Behold, the king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.

**2 Samuel 19:3**

And the victory on that day became mourning for all the people, because the people heard on that day, saying, The king grieves over his son.

**2 Samuel 19:4**

And the people were slipping into the city on that day, as the people slip in ashamed when they flee in battle.

**2 Samuel 19:5**

And the king hid his face, and the king cried out with a loud voice, saying, My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son.

**2 Samuel 19:6**

And Joab came to the king in the house and said, Today you have put to shame the face of all your servants, those who are rescuing you today and the lives of your sons and your daughters and the lives of your wives and your concubines,

**2 Samuel 19:7**

by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. For you declared today that your commanders and servants are nothing, because I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us today dead, then it would have been right in your eyes.

**2 Samuel 19:8**

And now rise, go out, and speak to the heart of your servants, because by the Lord I have sworn that if you do not go out, not a man will lodge with you tonight, and know for yourself that this will be worse for you than all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now.

**2 Samuel 19:9**

And the king rose and sat in the gate, and all the people reported, saying, Behold, the king sits in the gate. And all the people came before the king. And Israel fled, a man to his tents.

**2 Samuel 19:10**

And all the people were disputing in all the tribes of Israel, saying, King David rescued us from all our enemies and himself delivered us from the hand of the foreigners, and now he has fled from the land and from his kingdom because of Absalom.

**2 Samuel 19:11**

And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. So now why are you silent about bringing back the king? And the word of all Israel came to the king.

**2 Samuel 19:12**

And King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, Why do you become the last to bring back the king to his house, since the word of all Israel has come to the king?

**2 Samuel 19:13**

You are my brothers; you are my bones and my flesh. Why then do you become the last to bring back the king to his house?

**2 Samuel 19:14**

And you shall say to Amasa, Are you not my bone and my flesh? Thus may God do to me, and thus may he add, if you shall not be commander of the army before me all the days in place of Joab.

**2 Samuel 19:15**

And he inclined the heart of every man of Judah as one man, and they sent to the king, saying, Return, you and all your servants.

**2 Samuel 19:16**

And the king returned and came as far as the Jordan, and the men of Judah came to Gilgal to go and meet the king, to bring the king across the Jordan.

**2 Samuel 19:17**

And Shimei son of Gera a Benjamite from Bahurim hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David.

**2 Samuel 19:18**

And with him were one thousand men from Benjamin and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons with him and his twenty servants with him, and they made straight for the Jordan before the king.

**2 Samuel 19:19**

And they performed the service of bringing the king across, and the crossing went over to carry the house of the king across and to do what was right in his eyes. And Shimei son of Gera fell on his face before the king as he was crossing the Jordan.

**2 Samuel 19:20**

And he said to the king, Let not my lord reckon lawlessness against me, and do not remember how your servant did wrong on the day when my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, so that the king should put it to heart.

**2 Samuel 19:21**

For your servant knows that I have sinned. And behold, I came today first of all the house of Joseph to come down and meet my lord the king.

**2 Samuel 19:22**

And Abishai son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the anointed of the Lord?

**2 Samuel 19:23**

And David said, What is it to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah, that today you become an enemy to me? Today shall any man in Israel be put to death? For do I not know that today I reign over Israel?

**2 Samuel 19:24**

And the king said to Shimei, You shall not die. And the king swore to him.

**2 Samuel 19:25**

And Mephibosheth son of Jonathan son of Saul came down to meet the king, and he had not cared for his feet, nor trimmed his nails, nor tended his mustache, nor washed his garments from the day the king left until the day he came in peace.

**2 Samuel 19:26**

And it came to be when he entered Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?

**2 Samuel 19:27**

And Mephibosheth said to him, My lord king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said to him, Saddle the donkey for me, and I will mount it and go with the king, because your servant is lame.

**2 Samuel 19:28**

And he schemed against your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God. So do what is good in your eyes.

**2 Samuel 19:29**

For all the house of my father were nothing but men of death to my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those eating at your table. And what right have I still, even to cry out further to the king?

**2 Samuel 19:30**

And the king said to him, Why do you still speak your words? I have said, You and Ziba shall divide the field.

**2 Samuel 19:31**

And Mephibosheth said to the king, Indeed, let him take all, after my lord the king has come in peace to his house.

**2 Samuel 19:32**

And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and crossed with the king over the Jordan to escort him over the Jordan.

**2 Samuel 19:33**

And Barzillai was a very old man, a son of eighty years, and he had sustained the king while he stayed in Mahanaim, because he was a very great man.

**2 Samuel 19:34**

And the king said to Barzillai, You shall cross over with me, and I will sustain your old age with me in Jerusalem.

**2 Samuel 19:35**

And Barzillai said to the king, How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

**2 Samuel 19:36**

I am eighty years old today. Will I still know between good and evil? Will your servant still taste what I eat or what I drink? Will I still hear the voice of singers and singing women? Why then should your servant still be a burden to my lord the king?

**2 Samuel 19:37**

Your servant will just cross the Jordan a little way with the king. Why should the king repay me with this repayment?

**2 Samuel 19:38**

Let your servant sit now, and I will die in my city, beside the tomb of my father and my mother. And behold, your servant Chimham will cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your eyes.

**2 Samuel 19:39**

And the king said, Chimham shall cross with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes, and whatever you choose from me, I will do for you.

**2 Samuel 19:40**

And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed. And the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his place.

**2 Samuel 19:41**

And the king crossed into Gilgal, and Chimham crossed with him, and all the people of Judah crossing with the king, and also half the people of Israel.

**2 Samuel 19:42**

And behold, every man of Israel came to the king and said to the king, Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal you away and bring the king and his house across the Jordan, and all David's men with him?

**2 Samuel 19:43**

And every man of Judah answered the man of Israel, and they said, Because the king is near to me. And why have you been angered about this matter? Did we eat by eating from the king, or did he give us a gift, or did he lift something for us?

**2 Samuel 19:44**

And the man of Israel answered the man of Judah and said, I have ten hands in the kingdom, and I am firstborn more than you, and indeed I have more claim in David than you. So why did you treat me lightly? And was not my word first for bringing back my king? But the word of the men of Judah was harsher than the word of the men of Israel.

#### Chapter 20

**2 Samuel 20:1**

And there happened to be there a lawless man, and his name was Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite man. And he sounded the horn and said, We have no share in David, nor inheritance for us in the son of Jesse. Each man to your tents, O Israel.

**2 Samuel 20:2**

And every man of Israel went up from following David after Sheba son of Bichri, but the men of Judah clung to their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.

**2 Samuel 20:3**

And David entered his house at Jerusalem, and the king took the ten women, his concubines, whom he had left to guard the house, and gave them into a house of custody and sustained them, but he did not go in to them. And they were shut away until the day of their death, living as widows.

**2 Samuel 20:4**

And the king said to Amasa, Summon for me the men of Judah within three days, and you yourself stand here.

**2 Samuel 20:5**

And Amasa went to summon Judah, but he delayed beyond the set time that David had appointed for him.

**2 Samuel 20:6**

And David said to Abishai, Now Sheba son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. So now take with you the servants of your lord and pursue after him, lest he find fortified cities for himself and hide from our eyes.

**2 Samuel 20:7**

And after him went out the men of Joab and the Cherethite and the Pelethites and all the mighty men, and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sheba son of Bichri.

**2 Samuel 20:8**

And they were by the great stone that is in Gibeon, and Amasa came before them. And Joab was girded with his cloak, his garment, and over it he was girded with a sword fastened at his waist in its sheath, and the sword came out and fell.

**2 Samuel 20:9**

And Joab said to Amasa, Are you well, my brother? And the right hand of Joab took hold of the beard of Amasa to kiss him.

**2 Samuel 20:10**

And Amasa did not guard against the sword in the hand of Joab, and Joab struck him with it in the belly, and his entrails poured out on the ground, and he did not strike him a second time, and he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba son of Bichri.

**2 Samuel 20:11**

And a man from the young men of Joab stood over him and said, Whoever delights in Joab and whoever belongs to David, after Joab.

**2 Samuel 20:12**

**2 Samuel 20:13**

And when he was removed from the road, every man of Israel passed on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba son of Bichri.

**2 Samuel 20:14**

**2 Samuel 20:15**

**2 Samuel 20:16**

And a wise woman cried out from the wall and said, Hear, hear. Tell Joab now, Come near here, and I will speak to him.

**2 Samuel 20:17**

**2 Samuel 20:18**

And she said, saying, In earlier times they spoke a word, saying, They surely asked in Abel and in Dan whether what the faithful of Israel established had failed, and thus they ended matters.

**2 Samuel 20:19**

I am one of the peaceful, of the strongholds of Israel, but you seek to put to death a city and a mother-city in Israel. Why are you drowning the inheritance of the Lord?

**2 Samuel 20:20**

And Joab answered and said, Far be it from me, far be it from me, if I should drown or if I should destroy.

**2 Samuel 20:21**

This is not the matter, but a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri is his name, and he lifted his hand against King David. Give him to me alone, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said to Joab, Behold, his head will be thrown to you through the wall.

**2 Samuel 20:22**

And the woman went to all the people and spoke to all the city in her wisdom, and they removed the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. And he sounded the horn, and they were scattered from the city, each man to his tents. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

**2 Samuel 20:23**

And Joab was over all the army of Israel, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethite and over the Pelethites.

**2 Samuel 20:24**

**2 Samuel 20:25**

And Sheva was secretary, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests.

**2 Samuel 20:26**

And Ira the Jairite too was priest to David.

#### Chapter 21

**2 Samuel 21:1**

And there was famine in the days of David three years, year following year. And David sought the face of the Lord, and the Lord said, There is guilt on Saul and on his house for blood, because he put the Gibeonites to death.

**2 Samuel 21:2**

And King David called the Gibeonites and said to them. Now the Gibeonites are not from the sons of Israel, but from the remnant of the Amorite, and the sons of Israel had sworn to them, yet Saul sought to strike them in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah.

**2 Samuel 21:3**

And David said to the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you, and by what shall I make atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the Lord?

**2 Samuel 21:4**

**2 Samuel 21:5**

And they said to the king, The man brought us to an end and pursued us, he who schemed to wipe us out. Let us destroy him from having any standing in all the border of Israel.

**2 Samuel 21:6**

**2 Samuel 21:7**

**2 Samuel 21:8**

**2 Samuel 21:9**

And he gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they exposed them to the sun on the mountain before the Lord. And the seven fell together, and they were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of barley harvest.

**2 Samuel 21:10**

And Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock from the beginning of barley harvest until water dripped on them from heaven, and she did not allow the birds of heaven to rest on them by day nor the beasts of the field by night.

**2 Samuel 21:11**

And it was reported to David what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, concubine of Saul, had done, and they were released, and Dan son of Ioa from the offspring of the giants took hold of them.

**2 Samuel 21:12**

And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered the bones of the ones exposed to the sun.

**2 Samuel 21:14**

**2 Samuel 21:15**

And again there was war for the foreigners with Israel, and David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought with the foreigners, and David grew faint.

**2 Samuel 21:16**

**2 Samuel 21:17**

And Abishai son of Zeruiah helped him, and he struck the foreigner and put him to death. Then the men of David swore, saying, You shall no longer go out with us to battle, and you shall not extinguish the lamp of Israel.

**2 Samuel 21:18**

And after these things there was again war at Gath with the foreigners. Then Sebocha the Astathothite struck Sepph, one of the offspring of Rapha.

**2 Samuel 21:19**

And there was war at Gob with the foreigners, and Elhanan son of Ariorgim the Bethlehemite struck Goliath the Gittite, and the shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam.

**2 Samuel 21:20**

And again there was war at Gath, and there was a man of measure, and the fingers of his hands and the fingers of his feet were six and six, twenty-four in number, and he too was born to Rapha.

**2 Samuel 21:21**

**2 Samuel 21:22**

#### Chapter 22

**2 Samuel 22:1**

And David spoke to the Lord the words of this song in the day when the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

**2 Samuel 22:2**

And he said, O Lord, my rock and my fortress and my rescuer for me,

**2 Samuel 22:3**

my God will be my guard; I will trust in him, my shield and horn of my salvation, my supporter and my refuge of salvation; from injustice you will save me.

**2 Samuel 22:4**

I will call upon the Lord, worthy of praise, and I will be saved from my enemies.

**2 Samuel 22:5**

For breakers of death surrounded me; torrents of lawlessness terrified me.

**2 Samuel 22:6**

The birth-pangs of death encircled me; hardnesses of death came before me.

**2 Samuel 22:7**

When I was afflicted, I will call on the Lord, and I will cry out to my God, and he will hear my voice from his temple, and my cry will be in his ears.

**2 Samuel 22:8**

And the earth was shaken and quaked, and the foundations of heaven were troubled and convulsed, because the Lord was angry with them.

**2 Samuel 22:9**

Smoke went up in his anger, and fire from his mouth devours; coals were kindled from it.

**2 Samuel 22:10**

And he bent the heavens and came down, and gloom was under his feet.

**2 Samuel 22:11**

And he rode on cheroubin and flew, and he was seen on the wings of wind.

**2 Samuel 22:12**

And he made darkness his hiding place around him, his tent, dark water thickened in the clouds of air.

**2 Samuel 22:13**

From the brightness before him coals of fire were kindled.

**2 Samuel 22:14**

The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice.

**2 Samuel 22:15**

And he sent arrows and scattered them, lightning and threw them into panic.

**2 Samuel 22:16**

And the channels of the sea were seen, and the foundations of the world were uncovered at the rebuke of the Lord, from the breath of the spirit of his wrath.

**2 Samuel 22:17**

He sent from on high and took me; he drew me out of many waters.

**2 Samuel 22:18**

He rescued me from my strong enemies, from those hating me, because they were stronger than I.

**2 Samuel 22:19**

They came before me in the day of my affliction, and the Lord became my support.

**2 Samuel 22:20**

And he brought me out into breadth and delivered me, because he delighted in me.

**2 Samuel 22:21**

And the Lord repaid me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he repaid me.

**2 Samuel 22:22**

Because I kept the ways of the Lord and did not act impiously away from my God.

**2 Samuel 22:23**

Because all his judgments were before me, and his ordinances I did not turn away from.

**2 Samuel 22:24**

And I will be blameless with him, and I will keep myself from my lawlessness.

**2 Samuel 22:25**

And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.

**2 Samuel 22:26**

With the holy one you will be holy, and with the perfect man you will be perfect.

**2 Samuel 22:27**

And with the chosen one you will be chosen, and with the crooked you will be twisted.

**2 Samuel 22:28**

And you will save the poor people, and the eyes of the proud you will humble.

**2 Samuel 22:29**

Because you are my lamp, O Lord, and the Lord will light up my darkness.

**2 Samuel 22:30**

Because in you I will run as a raider, and in my God I will leap over a wall.

**2 Samuel 22:31**

The Mighty One, blameless is his way; the word of the Lord is strongly refined by fire; he is a shield for all who trust in him.

**2 Samuel 22:32**

For who is mighty besides the Lord, and who will be a creator besides our God?

**2 Samuel 22:33**

The Mighty One who strengthens me with power and made my way blameless,

**2 Samuel 22:34**

making my feet like deer's feet and setting me upon the heights,

**2 Samuel 22:35**

teaching my hands for war and bending a bronze bow with my arms.

**2 Samuel 22:36**

And you gave me the shield of my salvation, and your attentive hearing multiplied me.

**2 Samuel 22:37**

You widened my steps under me, and my ankles did not give way.

**2 Samuel 22:38**

I will pursue my enemies and destroy them, and I will not turn back until I finish them.

**2 Samuel 22:39**

And I will crush them, and they will not rise; they will fall under my feet.

**2 Samuel 22:40**

And you will strengthen me with power for battle; you will bend under me those rising against me.

**2 Samuel 22:41**

And you gave me the back of my enemies, those hating me, and I destroyed them.

**2 Samuel 22:42**

They will cry out, and there is no helper, to the Lord, and he did not answer them.

**2 Samuel 22:43**

And I beat them small as dust of the earth; like the mud of exits I crushed them thin.

**2 Samuel 22:44**

And you will rescue me from the strivings of peoples; you will keep me as head of nations. A people I had not known served me.

**2 Samuel 22:45**

Sons of foreigners lied to me; at the hearing of the ear they listened to me.

**2 Samuel 22:46**

Sons of foreigners will fall away and stagger out of their enclosures.

**2 Samuel 22:47**

The Lord lives, and blessed is my guard, and the God, the guard of my salvation, will be exalted,

**2 Samuel 22:48**

the mighty Lord who gives avenges to me, disciplining peoples under me,

**2 Samuel 22:49**

and bringing me out from my enemies. And you will lift me high above those rising against me; from a man of injustices you will rescue me.

**2 Samuel 22:50**

Because of this I will confess you, Lord, among the nations, and to your name I will sing psalms,

**2 Samuel 22:51**

magnifying the salvations of his king and doing mercy for his anointed, for David and for his seed forever.

#### Chapter 23

**2 Samuel 23:1**

And these are the last words of David: Faithful is David son of Jesse, and faithful the man whom the Lord raised up to be the anointed of the God of Jacob, and beautiful are the psalms of Israel.

**2 Samuel 23:2**

The Spirit of the Lord spoke in me, and his word was on my tongue.

**2 Samuel 23:3**

The God of Israel says; the guard of Israel spoke to me: I will speak a parable. In humanity, how will you make strong the fear of God?

**2 Samuel 23:4**

And in God: morning light, when the sun rises at morning, a morning not passed over from brightness, and as grass from the earth after rain.

**2 Samuel 23:5**

For not so is my house with the Mighty One? For he set for me an everlasting covenant, ready in every time, guarded, because all my salvation and every desire, shall not the lawless one sprout?

**2 Samuel 23:6**

But all the lawless are like a thorn thrown out, because they are not taken by hand.

**2 Samuel 23:7**

And the man who touches them will arm himself with full iron and the shaft of a spear, and they shall be utterly burned with fire in their shame.

**2 Samuel 23:8**

These are the names of the mighty men of David: Ishbosheth the Canaanite, chief of the third. This is Adinon the Asonaean. He drew his sword over eight hundred wounded at one time.

**2 Samuel 23:9**

And after him Eleazar son of his father's brother, son of a Sousite, among the three mighty men. He was with David at Serran, and when he reproached him among the foreigners, they were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel went up.

**2 Samuel 23:10**

He rose and struck among the foreigners until his hand grew weary and his hand clung to the sword. And the Lord worked a great deliverance on that day, and the people returned after him only to strip the slain.

**2 Samuel 23:11**

And after him Sammaia son of Asa the Aruchite. And the foreigners gathered into a troop, and there was a plot of the field full of lentils, and the people fled from before the foreigners.

**2 Samuel 23:12**

And he stood firm in the middle of the plot and rescued it and struck the foreigners, and the Lord worked a great deliverance.

**2 Samuel 23:13**

And three from the thirty went down and came at harvest to David at the cave of Adullam, and a troop of foreigners had camped in the valley of Rephaim.

**2 Samuel 23:14**

And David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the foreigners was then in Bethlehem.

**2 Samuel 23:15**

And David desired and said, Who will give me water to drink from the well at Bethlehem that is by the gate? And the station of the foreigners was then in Bethlehem.

**2 Samuel 23:16**

And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the foreigners and drew water from the well at Bethlehem that is by the gate and took it and came to David, but he would not drink it, and poured it out to the Lord.

**2 Samuel 23:17**

And he said, Be it far from me, Lord, to do this. Shall I drink the blood of the men who went in their lives? And he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

**2 Samuel 23:18**

And Abishai brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, he was chief among the three, and he lifted his spear against three hundred wounded, and he had a name among the three.

**2 Samuel 23:21**

He struck the Egyptian man, a man worth seeing, and in the hand of the Egyptian was a spear like a weavers' beam. And he went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear from the hand of the Egyptian and killed him with his own spear.

**2 Samuel 23:22**

These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.

**2 Samuel 23:23**

He was honored among the three, but to the three he did not come, and David set him over his audience.

**2 Samuel 23:25**

Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,

**2 Samuel 23:26**

Helez the Phelothite, Ira son of Ikkesh the Thekoite,

**2 Samuel 23:27**

Abiezer the Anathothite, from the sons of the Hushathite,

**2 Samuel 23:28**

Zalmon the Aonite, Moore the Netophathite,

**2 Samuel 23:29**

Ela son of Baana the Netophathite, Ittai son of Ribai from Gabaeth of Benjamin,

**2 Samuel 23:31**

Abiel son of the Arabothite, Azmaveth the Barsamite,

**2 Samuel 23:32**

Eliahba the Shaalbonite, sons of Jashen, Jonathan,

**2 Samuel 23:33**

Shammah the Arodite, Achian son of Sarad the Hararite,

**2 Samuel 23:34**

Eliphaleth son of the Ahasbai, son of the Maachathite, Eliab son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,

**2 Samuel 23:35**

Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Erchi,

**2 Samuel 23:36**

Igal son of Nathan from Dynaimea, son of Gaddi,

Zelek the Ammonite, Gelorai the Beerothite, carrying the arms of Joab son of Zeruiah,

**2 Samuel 23:38**

Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
