Uriah the Hittite, altogether thirty-seven.

#### Chapter 24

**2 Samuel 24:1**

And again the anger of the Lord burned in Israel, and he shook David among them, saying, Go, number Israel and Judah.

**2 Samuel 24:2**

And the king said to Joab, commander of the strength with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and count the people, and I will know the number of the people.

**2 Samuel 24:3**

And Joab said to the king, May the Lord your God add to the people as they are and a hundredfold more, with the eyes of my lord the king seeing. But why does my lord the king delight in this thing?

**2 Samuel 24:4**

But the word of the king prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the force, and Joab and the commanders of the force went out from before the king to count the people of Israel.

**2 Samuel 24:5**

And they crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, to the right of the city in the middle of the ravine, Gad and Eliezer.

**2 Samuel 24:6**

And they came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi, which is Adasai, and they came to Danidan and Udan and went around to Sidon.

**2 Samuel 24:7**

And they came to Mapsar of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivite and the Canaanite, and they came south of Judah to Beersheba.

**2 Samuel 24:8**

And they went around in all the land and came at the end of nine months and twenty days to Jerusalem.

**2 Samuel 24:9**

And Joab gave the number of the counting of the people to the king, and Israel became eight hundred thousand men of strength drawing sword, and the men of Judah five hundred thousand fighting men.

**2 Samuel 24:10**

And David's heart struck him after he had counted the people. And David said to the Lord, I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, Lord, please cause the lawlessness of your servant to pass over, because I have acted very foolishly.

**2 Samuel 24:11**

And David rose in the morning, and the word of the Lord came to Gad the prophet, the seer of David, saying,

**2 Samuel 24:12**

Go and speak to David, saying, Thus says the Lord: Three things I am lifting upon you, and choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.

**2 Samuel 24:13**

And Gad came to David and reported to him and said to him, Choose for yourself whether three years of famine shall come to you in your land, or three months of your fleeing before your enemies while they pursue you, or three days of death to be in your land. Now then know and see what word I should answer the one who sent me.

**2 Samuel 24:14**

And David said to Gad, Distress presses me greatly from every side. Let me now fall into the hand of the Lord, because his mercies are very many. But into the hands of man I will not fall. And David chose death for himself.

**2 Samuel 24:15**

And it was the days of wheat harvest, and the Lord gave death in Israel from morning until the dinner hour, and the break in the people began, and from the people, from Dan to Beersheba, seventy thousand men died.

**2 Samuel 24:16**

And the angel of God stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, and the Lord relented concerning the evil and said to the angel destroying among the people, Enough now, let your hand go. And the angel of the Lord was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

**2 Samuel 24:17**

And David said to the Lord when he saw the angel striking among the people, and he said, Behold, I am the one who did wrong, and I am the shepherd who did evil. But these sheep, what have they done? Let your hand now be against me and against my father's house.

**2 Samuel 24:18**

And Gad came to David on that day and said to him, Go up and set up an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

**2 Samuel 24:19**

And David went up according to the word of Gad, just as the Lord commanded him.

**2 Samuel 24:20**

And Araunah looked down and saw the king and his servants passing along above him, and Araunah went out and bowed to the king with his face to the ground.

**2 Samuel 24:21**

And Araunah said, Why has my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the Lord, and the plague will be restrained from upon the people.

**2 Samuel 24:22**

And Araunah said to David, Let my lord the king take and offer to the Lord what is good in his eyes. Behold, the oxen are for whole burnt offerings, and the wheels and the implements of the oxen are for wood.

**2 Samuel 24:23**

Araunah gave all these things to the king. And Araunah said to the king, May the Lord your God bless you.

**2 Samuel 24:24**

And the king said to Araunah, No, because in buying I will buy from you for a price, and I will not offer to the Lord my God a whole burnt offering for nothing. And David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

**2 Samuel 24:25**

And David built there an altar to the Lord and offered whole burnt offerings and peace offerings, and afterward Solomon added to the altar, because it had been small at first. And the Lord listened to the land, and the plague was restrained from over Israel.

### 1 Kings

#### Chapter 1

**1 Kings 1:1**

And King David was old, advanced in days, and they covered him with garments, but he did not get warm.

**1 Kings 1:2**

And his servants said, Let them seek for my lord the king a virgin young woman, and she will stand before the king and be warming him and will lie with him, and my lord the king will get warm.

**1 Kings 1:3**

And they sought a beautiful young woman from all the border of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

**1 Kings 1:4**

And the young woman was very beautiful, and she was warming the king and ministering to him, but the king did not know her.

**1 Kings 1:5**

And Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will reign. And he made for himself chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run before him.

**1 Kings 1:6**

And his father had never restrained him, saying, Why have you done thus? And he too was very handsome in appearance, and she had borne him after Absalom.

**1 Kings 1:7**

And his words were with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they were helping after Adonijah.

**1 Kings 1:8**

But Zadok the priest and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and Nathan the prophet and Shimei and Rei and the mighty men of David were not after Adonijah.

**1 Kings 1:9**

And Adonijah sacrificed sheep and calves and lambs beside the stone of Zoheleth, which was near the spring Enrogel, and he called all his brothers and all the nobles of Judah, the servants of the king.

**1 Kings 1:10**

But Nathan the prophet and Benaiah and the mighty men and Solomon his brother he did not call.

**1 Kings 1:11**

And Nathan said to Beersheba mother of Solomon, saying, Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David did not know?

**1 Kings 1:12**

And now come, let me counsel you with counsel, and rescue your life and the life of your son Solomon.

**1 Kings 1:13**

Come, go in to King David and say to him, Did you not, my lord king, swear to your servant, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne? Then why has Adonijah become king?

**1 Kings 1:14**

And behold, while you are still speaking there with the king, I will come in after you and fill out your words.

**1 Kings 1:15**

And Beersheba entered to the king in the chamber. And the king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was ministering to the king.

**1 Kings 1:16**

And Beersheba bowed and did obeisance to the king, and the king said, What is with you?

**1 Kings 1:17**

And she said, My lord king, you swore by the Lord your God to your servant, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.

**1 Kings 1:18**

And now behold, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord king, did not know.

**1 Kings 1:19**

And he sacrificed calves and lambs and sheep in abundance and called all the sons of the king and Abiathar the priest and Joab commander of the force, but Solomon your servant he did not call.

**1 Kings 1:20**

And you, my lord king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, for you to report to them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

**1 Kings 1:21**

And it will be, when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be sinners.

**1 Kings 1:22**

And behold, while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came.

**1 Kings 1:23**

And it was reported to the king, Behold, Nathan the prophet. And he entered before the king and bowed to the king with his face to the ground.

**1 Kings 1:24**

And Nathan said, My lord king, did you say, Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne?

**1 Kings 1:25**

For he went down today and sacrificed calves and lambs and sheep in abundance and called all the sons of the king and the commanders of the force and Abiathar the priest. And behold, they are eating and drinking before him, and they said, Long live King Adonijah.

**1 Kings 1:26**

But me, your servant, and Zadok the priest and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and Solomon your servant he did not call.

**1 Kings 1:27**

Has this thing happened by my lord the king, and have you not made known to your servant who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?

**1 Kings 1:28**

And David answered and said, Call Beersheba to me. And she entered before the king and stood before him.

**1 Kings 1:29**

And the king swore and said, As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from every affliction,

**1 Kings 1:30**

that as I swore to you by the Lord God of Israel, saying, Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne instead of me, so I will do on this day.

**1 Kings 1:31**

And Beersheba bowed with her face to the ground and did obeisance to the king and said, May my lord King David live forever.

**1 Kings 1:32**

And King David said, Call Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada to me. And they entered before the king.

**1 Kings 1:33**

And the king said to them, Take the servants of your lord with you and mount my son Solomon on my mule and lead him down to Gihon.

**1 Kings 1:34**

And let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel, and sound the horn and say, Long live King Solomon.

**1 Kings 1:35**

And he will sit on my throne, and he will reign instead of me, and I have commanded him to be ruler over Israel and Judah.

**1 Kings 1:36**

And Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king and said, May it be so. May the Lord God of my lord the king confirm it.

**1 Kings 1:37**

Just as the Lord was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he enlarge his throne beyond the throne of my lord King David.

**1 Kings 1:38**

And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and the Cherethite and the Pelethites went down and set Solomon upon the mule of King David and led him to Gihon.

**1 Kings 1:39**

And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon, and they sounded the horn, and all the people said, Long live King Solomon.

**1 Kings 1:40**

And all the people went up after him, and they were dancing in dances and rejoicing with great joy, and the earth split at their sound.

**1 Kings 1:41**

And Adonijah heard, and all his invited guests with him, and they themselves finished eating. And Joab heard the sound of the horn and said, What is the sound of the city in uproar?

**1 Kings 1:42**

While he was still speaking, behold, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came, and Adonijah said, Come in, for you are a man of strength and bring good news.

**1 Kings 1:43**

And Jonathan answered and said, And truly, our lord King David has made Solomon king.

**1 Kings 1:44**

And the king sent with him Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Benaiah son of Jehoiada and the Cherethite and the Pelethites, and they set him upon the mule of the king.

**1 Kings 1:45**

And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him as king at Gihon, and they came up from there rejoicing, and the city rang. This is the sound that you heard.

**1 Kings 1:46**

And Solomon has sat upon the throne of the kingdom.

**1 Kings 1:47**

And the servants of the king entered to bless our lord King David, saying, May God make the name of Solomon your son better than your name, and may he enlarge his throne beyond your throne. And the king bowed on his bed.

**1 Kings 1:48**

And thus too the king said, Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who gave today one from my seed sitting on my throne, and my eyes are seeing it.

**1 Kings 1:49**

And all the invited guests of Adonijah were terrified and rose up, and each man went on his way.

**1 Kings 1:50**

And Adonijah feared before Solomon, and he rose and went away and took hold of the horns of the altar.

**1 Kings 1:51**

And it was reported to Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonijah feared King Solomon and has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.

**1 Kings 1:52**

And Solomon said, If he becomes a son of strength, not one hair of his will fall to the ground, but if evil is found in him, he will die.

**1 Kings 1:53**

And King Solomon sent and brought him down from the altar, and he entered and bowed to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, Go to your house.

#### Chapter 2

**1 Kings 2:1**

And the days drew near for David to die, and he commanded Solomon his son, saying,

**1 Kings 2:2**

I am going on the way of all the earth, and you must be strong and become a man.

**1 Kings 2:3**

And you must keep the charge of the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his commandments and his ordinances and his judgments, the things written in the law of Moses, so that you may understand what you will do according to all that I command you.

**1 Kings 2:4**

So that the Lord may establish his word that he spoke, saying, If your sons guard their way to walk before me in truth, with all their heart and with all their soul, there will not be destroyed for you a man from upon the throne of Israel.

**1 Kings 2:5**

And indeed, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the forces of Israel, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether, and he killed them and assigned blood of war in peace and put innocent blood on the belt on his waist and on the sandal on his foot.

**1 Kings 2:6**

And you will do according to your wisdom, and you will not bring his gray hair down in peace to Hades.

**1 Kings 2:7**

And to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite you will do mercy, and they will be among those eating at your table, because thus they came near to me when I was fleeing from before Absalom your brother.

**1 Kings 2:8**

And behold, with you is Shimei son of Gera a Benjamite from Bahurim, and he cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I was going to the Camps. And he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, I will not put you to death by the sword.

**1 Kings 2:9**

And now do not hold him guiltless, because you are a wise man and will know what you will do to him, and you will bring his gray hair down in blood to Hades.

**1 Kings 2:10**

And David slept with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.

**1 Kings 2:11**

And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years. In Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem thirty-three years.

**1 Kings 2:12**

And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, a son of twelve years, and his kingdom was greatly prepared.

**1 Kings 2:13**

And Adonijah son of Haggith entered to Beersheba mother of Solomon and bowed to her. And she said, Is your coming peace? And he said, Peace.

**1 Kings 2:14**

And he said, A word is mine to you. And she said to him, Speak.

**1 Kings 2:15**

And he said to her, You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel set its face on me for the king, but the kingdom turned and became my brother's, because it came to him from the Lord.

**1 Kings 2:16**

And now I ask one request from you. Do not turn away your face. And Beersheba said to him, Speak.

**1 Kings 2:17**

And he said to her, Speak now to King Solomon, for he will not turn his face from you, and let him give me Abishag the Shunammite as wife.

**1 Kings 2:18**

And Beersheba said, Good. I will speak to the king concerning you.

**1 Kings 2:19**

And Beersheba entered to King Solomon to speak to him concerning Adonijah. And the king rose to meet her and kissed her and sat on his throne, and a throne was set for the mother of the king, and she sat at his right hand.

**1 Kings 2:20**

And she said to him, I ask one small request from you. Do not turn away your face. And the king said to her, Ask, my mother, for I will not turn you away.

**1 Kings 2:21**

And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as wife.

**1 Kings 2:22**

And King Solomon answered and said to his mother, And why did you ask Abishag for Adonijah? Ask the kingdom for him too, because he is my elder brother greater than I, and he has Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah the commander as companion.

**1 Kings 2:23**

And King Solomon swore by the Lord, saying, Thus may God do to me, and thus may he add, because Adonijah spoke this word against his own life.

**1 Kings 2:24**

And now, as the Lord lives, who prepared me and set me on the throne of David my father and made me a house as the Lord spoke, today Adonijah will be put to death.

**1 Kings 2:25**

And King Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him and Adonijah died on that day.

**1 Kings 2:26**

And to Abiathar the priest the king said, Run away to Anathoth, to your field, because you are a man of death on this day. But I will not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord before my father and because you were afflicted in all the things in which my father was afflicted.

**1 Kings 2:27**

And Solomon cast out Abiathar from being priest of the Lord, for the word of the Lord to be fulfilled, which he spoke against the house of Eli at Shallum.

**1 Kings 2:28**

And the report came to Joab son of Zeruiah, because Joab had inclined after Adonijah, but after Solomon he did not incline. And Joab fled to the tent of the Lord and took hold of the horns of the altar.

**1 Kings 2:29**

And it was reported to Solomon, saying that Joab fled to the tent of the Lord, and behold, he holds the horns of the altar. And Solomon sent to Joab, saying, What has happened to you that you fled to the altar? And Joab said, Because I feared from before you, and I fled to the Lord. And King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, Go and kill him and bury him.

**1 Kings 2:30**

And Benaiah son of Jehoiada came to Joab at the tent of the Lord and said to him, Thus says the king: Come out. And Joab said, I will not come out, because I will die here. And Benaiah son of Jehoiada turned back and said to the king, Thus Joab has spoken, and thus he answered me.

**1 Kings 2:31**

And the king said to him, Go and do to him just as he said, and kill him and bury him, and you will remove today the blood that Joab poured out for nothing from me and from the house of my father.

**1 Kings 2:32**

And the Lord turned the blood of his injustice onto his head, because he met two men more righteous and better than he and killed them by the sword, and my father David did not know their blood: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah.

**1 Kings 2:33**

And their blood returned upon his head and upon the head of his seed forever, but for David and for his seed and for his house and for his throne, may there be peace forever from the Lord.

**1 Kings 2:34**

And Benaiah son of Jehoiada met Joab and killed him and buried him at his house in the wilderness.

**1 Kings 2:35**

And the king gave Benaiah son of Jehoiada in his place over the generalship, and the kingdom was being set right in Jerusalem, and the king gave Zadok the priest as first priest instead of Abiathar. And the Lord gave understanding to Solomon and very much wisdom and breadth of heart like the sand that is beside the sea. And the understanding of Solomon was multiplied greatly beyond the understanding of all the ancients and beyond all the wise of Egypt. And he took the daughter of Pharaoh and brought her into the City of David until he finished his own house and the house of the Lord first and the wall of Jerusalem all around. In seven years he made it and finished it. And Solomon had seventy thousand carrying burdens and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain. And Solomon made the Sea and the bases and the great basins and the pillars and the fountain of the court and the bronze sea. And he built the citadel and its battlements and cut through the City of David. Thus the daughter of Pharaoh was going up from the City of David into her house that he built for her. Then he built the citadel. And Solomon offered up three times in the year whole burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he built to the Lord and was burning incense before the Lord and finished the house. And these were the rulers set over the works of Solomon, three thousand six hundred overseers of the people doing the works. And he built Asshur and Magdo and Gezer and upper Bethhoron and Baalath. But after he built the house of the Lord and the wall of Jerusalem all around, after these things he built these cities. And while David was still living he commanded Solomon, saying, Behold, with you is Shimei son of Gera, of Benjamite seed from Hebron. He cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I was going to the Camps, and he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, He shall not be put to death by the sword. And now do not hold him guiltless, because you are a prudent man and you will know what you will do to him, and you will bring his gray hair down in blood to Hades.

**1 Kings 2:36**

And the king called Shimei and said to him, Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, and do not go out from there anywhere.

**1 Kings 2:37**

And it will be on the day of your going out and crossing the torrent Kidron, knowing you will know that you will die by death. Your blood will be on your head. And the king made him swear on that day.

**1 Kings 2:38**

And Shimei said to the king, Good is the word that you spoke, my lord king. Thus your servant will do. And Shimei sat in Jerusalem three years.

**1 Kings 2:39**

And it came to be after three years that two slaves of Shimei ran away to Achish son of Maachah king of Gath, and it was reported to Shimei, saying, Behold, your slaves are in Gath.

**1 Kings 2:40**

And Shimei rose and saddled his donkey and went to Gath to Achish to seek his slaves, and Shimei went and brought his slaves from Gath.

**1 Kings 2:41**

And it was reported to Solomon, saying that Shimei went from Jerusalem to Gath and brought back his slaves.

**1 Kings 2:42**

And the king sent and called Shimei and said to him, Did I not make you swear by the Lord and testify against you, saying, On whatever day you go out from Jerusalem and go to the right or to the left, knowing you will know that you will die by death?

**1 Kings 2:43**

And why did you not keep the oath of the Lord and the commandment that I commanded against you?

**1 Kings 2:44**

And the king said to Shimei, You know all your evil, which your heart knew, what you did to David my father, and the Lord has returned your evil upon your head.

**1 Kings 2:45**

And King Solomon is blessed, and the throne of David will be prepared before the Lord forever.

**1 Kings 2:46**

And King Solomon commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck him and he died. And King Solomon was very understanding and wise, and Judah and Israel were exceedingly many, like the sand on the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing. And Solomon was ruler over all the kingdoms, and they were bringing gifts and serving Solomon all the days of his life. And Solomon began opening the domains of Lebanon. And he built Thermai in the wilderness. And this was Solomon's provision: thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of beaten flour, ten choice calves and twenty pasture-fed cattle and one hundred sheep, besides deer and gazelles and choice fatted birds. For he was ruler over everything beyond the river, from Raphi to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the river. And he had peace from all his sides all around, and Judah and Israel lived trusting, each under his vine and under his fig tree, eating and drinking, from Dan to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon. And these were the chiefs of Solomon: Azariah son of Zadok the priest, and Orniou son of Nathan, chief of the overseers, and Edram over his house, and Shisha secretary, and Basa son of Achithalam recorder, and Abi son of Joab commander in chief, and Achire son of Edrai over the levies, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the court guard and over the brickwork, and Zachour son of Nathan the counselor. And Solomon had forty thousand brood mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. And he was ruler in all the kingdoms from the river to the land of the foreigners and to the borders of Egypt. Solomon son of David reigned over Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.

#### Chapter 3

**1 Kings 3:2**

Yet the people were burning incense on the high places, because a house was not yet built for the name of the Lord until now.

**1 Kings 3:3**

And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the ordinances of David his father, except that on the high places he was sacrificing and burning incense.

**1 Kings 3:4**

And he rose and went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, because that was the highest and greatest high place. Solomon offered one thousand whole burnt offerings on the altar in Gibeon.

**1 Kings 3:5**

And the Lord appeared to Solomon in sleep by night, and the Lord said to Solomon, Ask what request for yourself.

**1 Kings 3:6**

And Solomon said, You did great mercy with your servant David my father, just as he walked before you in truth and in righteousness and in the uprightness of heart with you, and you kept for him this great mercy, to give his son upon his throne, as on this day.

**1 Kings 3:7**

And now, Lord my God, you gave your servant instead of David my father, and I am a small child and do not know my going out and my coming in.

**1 Kings 3:8**

And your servant is in the midst of your people whom you chose, a numerous people who will not be numbered.

**1 Kings 3:9**

And you will give your servant a heart that hears and discerns your people in righteousness, to understand between good and evil. For who will be able to judge this heavy people of yours?

**1 Kings 3:10**

And it was pleasing before the Lord that Solomon asked this word.

**1 Kings 3:11**

And the Lord said to him, Because you asked from me this word and did not ask for yourself many days and did not ask riches and did not ask the lives of your enemies, but asked for yourself understanding to hear judgment,

**1 Kings 3:12**

behold, I have done according to your word. Behold, I have given you a wise and understanding heart. One like you did not come to be before you, and after you none like you will arise.

**1 Kings 3:13**

And what you did not ask I have given you too, both riches and glory, so that no man like you has come to be among kings.

**1 Kings 3:14**

And if you walk in my way, keeping my commandments and my ordinances as David your father walked, I will multiply your days.

**1 Kings 3:15**

And Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream. And he rose and comes to Jerusalem and stood before the altar that was before the ark of the covenant of the Lord in Zion and offered whole burnt offerings and made peace offerings and made a great drinking-feast for himself and for all his servants.

**1 Kings 3:16**

Then two prostitute women appeared to the king and stood before him.

**1 Kings 3:17**

And the one woman said, In me, my lord, I and this woman live in one house, and we gave birth in the house.

**1 Kings 3:18**

And it came to be on the third day after I gave birth, that this woman also gave birth, and we were together, and there was no one with us except the two of us in the house.

**1 Kings 3:19**

And the son of this woman died in the night, because she lay on him.

**1 Kings 3:20**

And she rose in the middle of the night and took my son from my embrace while your servant was sleeping and laid him in her bosom, and her dead son she laid in my bosom.

**1 Kings 3:21**

And I rose in the morning to nurse my son, and he was dead. And behold, I considered him in the morning, and behold, he was not my son whom I bore.

**1 Kings 3:22**

And the other woman said, No, but my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one. And they were speaking before the king.

**1 Kings 3:23**

And the king said to them, You say, This is my living son, and this one's son is the dead one. And you say, No, but my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.

**1 Kings 3:24**

And the king said, Bring me a sword. And they brought the sword before the king.

**1 Kings 3:25**

And the king said, Divide the living nursing child into two, and give half of him to this one and half of him to this one.

**1 Kings 3:26**

And the woman whose son was the living one answered and said to the king, because her womb was troubled over her son, In me, my lord, give her the child, and by death do not put him to death. But the other said, Let him be neither mine nor hers. Divide him.

**1 Kings 3:27**

And the king answered and said, Give the child to the one who said, Give him to her, and by death do not put him to death. She is his mother.

**1 Kings 3:28**

And all Israel heard this judgment that the king judged, and they feared before the king, because they saw that understanding of God was in him for doing justice.

#### Chapter 4

**1 Kings 4:1**

And King Solomon was reigning over Israel.

And these were his rulers: Azariah son of Zadok,

and Elihoreph and Ahijah sons of Shisha, secretaries, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, recorder,

and Sadouch and Abiathar, priests,

and Azariah son of Nathan over those appointed, and Zabud son of Nathan, companion of the king,

and Achiel household steward, and Eliab son of Saph over the family line, and Adoniram son of Abda over the levies,

**1 Kings 4:9**

Son of Rechab in Makaz and Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh and Elon as far as Elon-beth-hanan, one.

Son of Esoth: Berbethnema, Lousamencha, and Hepher.

Abinadab and Anaphathi. The man of Taphath, daughter of Solomon, was his wife, one.

Baana son of Ahilud: Taanach and Megiddo and all the house of San that was beside Beth-shean below Esrae, from Baisaphoud to Abelmeholah to Maeber Loukam, one.

Son of Gibbar in Ramath Gilead. To this one belonged the line-measure of Eregaba that is in Bashan, sixty great walled cities and bronze bars.

**1 Kings 4:15**

Ahimaaz in Naphtali, and he took Basemmath daughter of Solomon as wife, one.

Baana son of Cushi in Mahlahth, one.

**1 Kings 4:17**

Shimei son of Elah in Benjamin.

**1 Kings 4:18**

Gibbar son of Adai in the land of Gad, land of Seon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, and Nasiph one in the land of Judah.

Jehoshaphat son of Phouasoud in Issachar.

#### Chapter 5

**1 Kings 5:1**

And the appointed officers were thus providing for King Solomon and all the charges upon the table of the king, each in his month. They did not alter a word. And they were bringing the barley and the straw for the horses and the chariots to the place where the king might be, each according to his arrangement.

**1 Kings 5:2**

And these were the needs for Solomon in one day: thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of beaten flour,

**1 Kings 5:3**

and ten choice calves and twenty pasture-fed cattle and one hundred sheep, besides deer and gazelles and choice fatted birds.

**1 Kings 5:4**

For he was ruler beyond the river, and he had peace from all sides all around.

**1 Kings 5:9**

And the Lord gave understanding to Solomon and very great wisdom and breadth of heart like the sand that is beside the sea.

**1 Kings 5:10**

And Solomon was greatly multiplied in understanding beyond the understanding of all the ancient men and beyond all the wise of Egypt.

**1 Kings 5:11**

And he became wiser than all the men, wiser than Ethan the Ezrite and Heman and Chalcala and Darda, sons of Mal.

**1 Kings 5:12**

And Solomon spoke three thousand parables, and his songs were five thousand.

**1 Kings 5:13**

And he spoke concerning trees, from the cedar in Lebanon even to the hyssop that comes out through the wall, and he spoke concerning cattle and concerning birds and concerning creeping things and concerning fish.

**1 Kings 5:14**

And all the peoples were coming to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and he was receiving gifts from all the kings of the earth, all who were hearing his wisdom. And Solomon took the daughter of Pharaoh for himself as wife and brought her into the City of David until he finished the house of the Lord and his own house and the wall of Jerusalem. Then Pharaoh king of Egypt went up and took Gezer beforehand and burned it, and the Canaanite who lived in Mergab, and Pharaoh gave them as gifts to his daughter, wife of Solomon, and Solomon built Gezer.

**1 Kings 5:15**

And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to anoint Solomon in place of David his father, because Hiram loved David all his days.

**1 Kings 5:16**

And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

**1 Kings 5:17**

You know David my father, that he was not able to build a house for the name of the Lord my God because of the wars that encircled him, until the Lord gave them under the soles of his feet.

**1 Kings 5:18**

And now the Lord my God has given me rest all around. There is no adversary, and there is no evil encounter.

**1 Kings 5:19**

And behold, I say that I will build a house for the name of the Lord my God, just as the Lord God spoke to David my father, saying, Your son, whom I will give instead of you upon your throne, he will build the house for my name.

**1 Kings 5:20**

And now command, and let them cut wood for me from Lebanon. And behold, my servants are with your servants, and I will give you the wage of your service according to all that you say, because you know that there is no one among us knowing how to cut wood like the Sidonians.

**1 Kings 5:21**

And it came to be when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly and said, Blessed is God today, who gave to David a wise son over this many people.

**1 Kings 5:22**

And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, I have heard concerning all that you sent to me. I will do all your desire concerning cedar wood and fir wood.

**1 Kings 5:23**

My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea. I will place them in rafts to the place that you send to me, and I will shake them out there, and you will take them. And you will do my will by giving bread to my house.

**1 Kings 5:24**

And Hiram was giving cedars to Solomon and all his desire.

**1 Kings 5:25**

And Solomon gave to Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat and provision for his house and twenty thousand baths of beaten oil. According to this Solomon was giving to Hiram year by year.

**1 Kings 5:26**

And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon just as he spoke to him, and there was peace between Hiram and between Solomon, and they cut a covenant between themselves.

**1 Kings 5:27**

And King Solomon raised a levy from all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men.

**1 Kings 5:28**

And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand in the month by turns. One month they were in Lebanon and two months in their houses, and Adoniram was over the levy.

**1 Kings 5:29**

And Solomon had seventy thousand carrying burdens and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain,

**1 Kings 5:30**

except for the chiefs appointed over the works of Solomon, three thousand six hundred overseers doing the works.

**1 Kings 5:32**

And they prepared the stones and the timbers for three years.

#### Chapter 6

**1 Kings 6:1**

And it came to be in the four hundred and fortieth year of the coming out of the sons of Israel from Egypt, in the fourth year, in the second month, of King Solomon reigning over Israel. And the king commanded, and they took great costly stones for the foundation of the house, and unhewn stones. And the sons of Solomon and the sons of Hiram dressed them and laid them. In the fourth year he founded the house of the Lord in the month Niso, the second month. In the eleventh year, in the month Baal, this is the eighth month, the house was completed in every word of it and in every arrangement of it.

**1 Kings 6:2**

And the house that King Solomon built to the Lord: forty cubits was its length and twenty cubits in breadth and twenty-five cubits in height.

**1 Kings 6:3**

And the porch before the nave was twenty cubits in length, according to the breadth of the house, and its breadth before the house was ten cubits. And he built the house and finished it.

**1 Kings 6:4**

And he made to the house windows looking out, concealed.

**1 Kings 6:5**

And he set beam-structures upon the wall of the house all around, for the nave and for the debir, and he made side chambers all around.

**1 Kings 6:6**

**1 Kings 6:7**

And the house, while it was being built, was built with quarry-cut prepared stones, and hammer and axe and every iron tool was not heard in the house while it was being built.

**1 Kings 6:8**

And the doorway of the lower side chamber was under the shoulder of the house on the right side, and a winding ascent led to the middle and from the middle to the third stories.

**1 Kings 6:9**

And he built the house and finished it and paneled the house with cedars.

**1 Kings 6:10**

And he built the bonds across the whole house, five cubits its height, and he fastened the bond with cedar woods.

**1 Kings 6:15**

And he built the walls of the house with cedar woods, from the floor of the house to the rafters and to the walls, and he paneled them continuously with woods inside, and he encircled the inside of the house with pine boards.

**1 Kings 6:16**

And he built the twenty cubits from the end of the house, the one side from the floor to the rafters, and he made the debir from it as the holy of holies.

**1 Kings 6:17**

And the nave in front was forty cubits.

**1 Kings 6:19**

The debir was in the middle of the house within, to place there the ark of the covenant of the Lord.

**1 Kings 6:20**

Twenty cubits was its length and twenty cubits its breadth and twenty cubits its height, and he encircled it with shut-up gold and made an altar.

**1 Kings 6:21**

It was before the face of the debir, and he encircled it with gold.

**1 Kings 6:22**

And the whole house he encircled with gold until the completion of the whole house.

**1 Kings 6:23**

And he made in the debir two cheroubin, ten cubits in size, proportioned.

**1 Kings 6:24**

And five cubits was one wing of the one cheroub and five cubits its second wing, ten cubits from part of its wing to part of its wing.

**1 Kings 6:25**

**1 Kings 6:26**

And the height of the one cheroub was ten cubits, and so the second cheroub.

**1 Kings 6:27**

And he put both the cheroubin in the middle of the innermost house, and they spread out their wings, and one wing touched the wall and one wing touched the second wall, and their wings in the middle of the house touched wing to wing.

**1 Kings 6:28**

And he encircled the cheroubin with gold.

**1 Kings 6:29**

And all the walls of the house all around he engraved with a stylus, cheroubin and palms, the inner and the outer.

**1 Kings 6:30**

And the floor of the house he encircled with gold, of the innermost and of the outermost.

**1 Kings 6:31**

And for the doorway of the debir he made doors of juniper wood, and the doorposts were fivefold.

**1 Kings 6:32**

And two doors of pine wood, and carved upon them were engraved cheroubin and palms and spread petals, and he encircled them with gold, and the gold came down upon the cheroubin and upon the palms.

**1 Kings 6:33**

And thus he made for the gateway of the nave doorposts of juniper wood, four-sided porches.

**1 Kings 6:34**

And on both doors were pine woods, two folds on the one door and their turnings, and two folds on the second door turning.

**1 Kings 6:35**

Carved cheroubin and palms and spread petals, and covered with gold being brought down upon the impression.

**1 Kings 6:36**

And he built the innermost court, three rows of hewn stone and a row of worked cedar all around. And he built a curtain for the court of the porch of the house that was before the nave.

#### Chapter 7

**1 Kings 7:1**

And King Solomon sent and took Hiram from Tyre,

**1 Kings 7:2**

son of a widow woman, and he was from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a Tyrian man, a craftsman in bronze, and he was filled with skill and understanding and knowledge to do every work in bronze. And he was brought to King Solomon and did all the works.

**1 Kings 7:3**

**1 Kings 7:15**

**1 Kings 7:17**

**1 Kings 7:18**

And handles were in the wheels in the stand, and the height of one wheel was a cubit and a half.

**1 Kings 7:19**

**1 Kings 7:20**

**1 Kings 7:21**

And upon the top of the stand was half a cubit in size, round all around, upon the top of the stand, and the beginning of its handles and its enclosures, and it opened out toward the beginnings of its handles.

**1 Kings 7:22**

**1 Kings 7:23**

**1 Kings 7:24**

And he made ten bronze wash-basins, each wash-basin holding forty baths by measure, one wash-basin upon each of the ten stands.

**1 Kings 7:25**

**1 Kings 7:26**

And Hiram made the pots and the shovels and the bowls, and Hiram completed doing all the works that he did for King Solomon in the house of the Lord:

**1 Kings 7:27**

**1 Kings 7:28**

the four hundred pomegranates for both networks, two rows of pomegranates for the one network, to cover both twisted works upon both pillars,

**1 Kings 7:29**

and the ten stands and the ten wash-basins upon the stands,

**1 Kings 7:30**

and the one Sea and the twelve oxen under the Sea,

**1 Kings 7:31**

and the pots and the shovels and the bowls and all the vessels that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the Lord, and the forty-eight pillars of the house of the king and of the house of the Lord, all the works of the king that Hiram made, all entirely of bronze.

**1 Kings 7:32**

There was no weight for the bronze from which he made all these works because of the very great abundance. There was no end to the weighing of the bronze.

**1 Kings 7:33**

**1 Kings 7:34**

And King Solomon gave the vessels that he made in the house of the Lord: the golden altar, and the golden table on which were the loaves of offering,

**1 Kings 7:35**

and the lampstands, five at the right and five at the left before the debir, of closed gold, and the lamps and the wicks and the libation-bowls of gold,

**1 Kings 7:36**

and the doorposts and the nails and the bowls and the pans and the censers of closed gold, and the hinges of the doors of the innermost house, holy of holies, and the doors of the house of the nave, of gold.

**1 Kings 7:37**

And all the work that Solomon made for the house of the Lord was completed, and Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father and all the holy things of Solomon, the silver and the gold and the vessels, and he put them into the treasuries of the house of the Lord.

**1 Kings 7:38**

And Solomon built his own house in thirteen years.

**1 Kings 7:39**

And he built the House of the Forest of Lebanon, one hundred cubits its length and fifty cubits its breadth and thirty cubits its height, with three rows of cedar pillars and cedar shoulders upon the pillars.

**1 Kings 7:40**

And he roofed the house above upon the sides of the pillars, and the number of the pillars was forty-five, fifteen in a row.

**1 Kings 7:41**

And three beam-frames, and opening facing opening, threefold.

**1 Kings 7:42**

And all the doors and the openings were squared with beam-work, and from door to door, threefold.

**1 Kings 7:43**

And the Porch of the Pillars was fifty cubits in length and thirty in breadth, fitted in balance, a porch before them, and pillars and a thickness before it for the porches.

**1 Kings 7:44**

And the Porch of the Throne, where he would judge there, the Porch of Judgment.

**1 Kings 7:45**

And his house where he would sit there, one court winding around these, according to this work, and a house for the daughter of Pharaoh whom Solomon took, according to this porch.

**1 Kings 7:46**

All these were of costly stones, dressed according to interval, inside and from the foundation to the coping and outside to the great court,

**1 Kings 7:47**

founded with costly stones, great stones, ten-cubit stones and eight-cubit stones,

**1 Kings 7:48**

and above with costly stones according to the measure of hewn stones and cedars,

**1 Kings 7:49**

the great court all around, three rows of hewn stones and a row of dressed cedar,

**1 Kings 7:50**

and Solomon completed his whole house.

#### Chapter 8

**1 Kings 8:1**

And it came to be when Solomon finished building the house of the Lord and his own house, after twenty years, then King Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel in Zion, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the City of David, this is Zion.

**1 Kings 8:2**

In the month Athanin.

**1 Kings 8:3**

And the priests lifted the ark,

**1 Kings 8:4**

and the tent of witness and all the holy vessels that were in the tent of witness,

**1 Kings 8:5**

and the king and all Israel before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle beyond number.

**1 Kings 8:6**

And the priests bring the ark to its place, into the debir of the house, into the holy of holies, under the wings of the cheroubin,

**1 Kings 8:7**

because the cheroubin had their wings spread over the place of the ark, and the cheroubin were covering the ark and its holy things from above.

**1 Kings 8:8**

And the holy poles projected, and the heads of the holy poles were seen from the holy place before the debir, but they were not visible outside.

**1 Kings 8:9**

There was nothing in the ark except two stone tablets, tablets of the covenant, which Moses put there in Horeb, which the Lord covenanted with the sons of Israel when they came out from the land of Egypt.

**1 Kings 8:10**

And it came to be, as the priests came out from the holy place, that the cloud filled the house,

**1 Kings 8:11**

and the priests were not able to stand to minister because of the cloud, because the glory of the Lord filled the house.

**1 Kings 8:14**

And the king turned his face and the king blessed all Israel, and all the assembly of Israel was standing.

**1 Kings 8:15**

And he said, Blessed is the Lord God of Israel today, who spoke with his mouth concerning David my father and with his hands fulfilled it, saying,

**1 Kings 8:16**

From the day I brought out my people Israel from Egypt, I did not choose a city in one scepter of Israel to build a house for my name to be there, but I chose Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I chose David to be over my people Israel.

**1 Kings 8:17**

And it came to be upon the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

**1 Kings 8:18**

And the Lord said to David my father, Because it came upon your heart to build a house for my name, you did well, because it came upon your heart.

**1 Kings 8:19**

Yet you shall not build the house, but only your son, the one coming out from your sides, he will build the house for my name.

**1 Kings 8:20**

And the Lord raised up his word that he spoke, and I rose in place of David my father and sat upon the throne of Israel just as the Lord spoke, and I built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.

**1 Kings 8:21**

And I placed there a place for the ark, in which is there the covenant of the Lord, which the Lord covenanted with our fathers when he brought them out from the land of Egypt.

**1 Kings 8:22**

And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the sight of all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven,

**1 Kings 8:23**

and said, O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above and upon the earth below, keeping covenant and mercy for your servant who walks before you with all his heart,

**1 Kings 8:24**

the things which you kept for your servant David my father, and you spoke with your mouth and fulfilled with your hands, as on this day.

**1 Kings 8:25**

And now, Lord God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father the things you spoke to him, saying, A man for you will not be lifted away from before me, sitting upon the throne of Israel, if only your children keep their ways to walk before me as you walked before me.

**1 Kings 8:26**

And now, Lord God of Israel, let your word be made firm for David my father.

**1 Kings 8:27**

For will God truly dwell with humans upon the earth? If heaven and heaven of heaven will not suffice for you, much less this house that I built for your name.

**1 Kings 8:28**

And yet look upon my petition, Lord God of Israel, to hear the delight with which your servant prays before you today,

**1 Kings 8:29**

for your eyes to be opened toward this house day and night, toward the place of which you said, My name will be there, to hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place day and night,

**1 Kings 8:30**

and you will hear the petition of your servant and of your people Israel, whatever they pray toward this place. And you will hear in the place of your dwelling in heaven, and you will act and be gracious.

**1 Kings 8:31**

Whatever each person sins against his neighbor, and if he takes upon himself a curse to curse him, and comes and declares openly before your altar in this house,

**1 Kings 8:32**

then you will hear from heaven and act and judge your people Israel, to condemn the lawless by giving his way upon his own head, and to justify the righteous by giving to him according to his righteousness.

**1 Kings 8:33**

When your people Israel stumble before enemies because they sinned against you, and they turn back and confess to your name and pray and entreat in this house,

**1 Kings 8:34**

then you will hear from heaven and be gracious to the sins of your people Israel and return them to the land that you gave to their fathers.

**1 Kings 8:35**

When heaven is shut and rain does not come because they sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and confess to your name and turn back from their sins when you humble them,

**1 Kings 8:36**

then you will hear from heaven and be gracious to the sins of your servant and of your people Israel, because you will show them the good way to walk in it, and you will give rain upon the land that you gave to your people for an inheritance.

**1 Kings 8:37**

If famine happens, if death happens, if blight happens, mildew, locust, rust, if his enemy afflicts him in one of his cities, every encounter, every pain,

**1 Kings 8:38**

every prayer, every petition, whatever happens to any person, as each knows the touch of his own heart and spreads out his hands toward this house,

**1 Kings 8:39**

then you will hear from heaven from your ready dwelling place and be gracious and act and give to each man according to his ways, as you know his heart, because you alone know the heart of all the sons of humans,

**1 Kings 8:40**

so that they may fear you all the days they live upon the land that you gave to our fathers.

**1 Kings 8:41**

And also for the foreigner who is not from this people of yours,

**1 Kings 8:42**

and they will come and pray toward this place,

**1 Kings 8:43**

then you will hear from heaven from your ready dwelling place and do according to all that the foreigner calls on you for, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do, and may know that your name is called upon this house that I built.

**1 Kings 8:44**

When your people go out to war against their enemies by the way that you send them, and they pray in the name of the Lord in the direction of the city that I chose in it and of the house that I built for your name,

**1 Kings 8:45**

then you will hear from heaven their petition and their prayer and do justice for them.

**1 Kings 8:46**

Because they will sin against you, for there is no human who will not sin, and you will bring against them and deliver them before enemies, and those who capture them will carry them captive to a far land or near,

**1 Kings 8:47**

and they will turn their hearts back in the land where they were carried there and turn and entreat you in the land of their migration, saying, We sinned, we acted lawlessly, we did wrong,

**1 Kings 8:48**

and turn to you with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies where you carried them away, and they pray toward you in the direction of their land that you gave to their fathers, the city that I chose and the house that I built for your name,

**1 Kings 8:49**

then you will hear from heaven from your ready dwelling place

**1 Kings 8:50**

and be gracious to their wrongs by which they sinned against you and to all their rebellions with which they rebelled against you, and you will give them into compassions before those taking them captive, and they will pity them,

**1 Kings 8:51**

because they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out from the land of Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace.

**1 Kings 8:52**

And let your eyes and your ears be opened toward the petition of your servant and toward the petition of your people Israel, to hear them in all things whatsoever they call on you for,

**1 Kings 8:53**

because you set them apart to yourself for an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, just as you spoke by the hand of your servant Moses, when you brought out our fathers from the land of Egypt, O Lord, Lord. Then Solomon spoke concerning the house, as he finished building it: The sun the Lord made known in heaven. He said he would dwell in gloom. Build my house, a splendid house for yourself, for dwelling in newness. Behold, is not this written in the Book of the Song?

**1 Kings 8:54**

And it came to be when Solomon finished praying to the Lord all this prayer and petition, he rose from before the altar of the Lord, kneeling upon his knees and his hands spread out toward heaven,

**1 Kings 8:55**

and stood and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,

**1 Kings 8:56**

Blessed is the Lord today, who gave rest to his people Israel according to all that he spoke. Not one word failed from all his good words that he spoke by the hand of Moses his servant.

**1 Kings 8:57**

May the Lord our God be with us just as he was with our fathers. May he not leave us nor turn away from us,

**1 Kings 8:58**

to incline our hearts toward him, to walk in all his ways and keep all his commandments and his ordinances, which he commanded our fathers.

**1 Kings 8:59**

And let these words, which I have entreated before the Lord our God, be near to the Lord our God day and night, to do the justice of your servant and the justice of his people Israel, each day's matter on its day,

**1 Kings 8:60**

so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord, he is God, and there is no other.

**1 Kings 8:61**

And let our hearts be perfect toward the Lord our God and holy in walking in his ordinances and keeping his commandments, as on this day.

**1 Kings 8:62**

And the king and all the sons of Israel sacrificed a sacrifice before the Lord.

**1 Kings 8:63**

And King Solomon sacrificed the sacrifices of peace offerings that he sacrificed to the Lord, twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. And the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.

**1 Kings 8:64**

On that day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the Lord, because there he made the whole burnt offering and the sacrifices and the fats of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that was before the Lord was too small to carry the whole burnt offering and the sacrifices of the peace offerings.

**1 Kings 8:65**

And Solomon kept the feast on that day, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God, in the house that he built, eating and drinking and rejoicing before the Lord our God for seven days.

**1 Kings 8:66**

And on the eighth day he sent away the people and blessed them, and they went each to his tents, rejoicing and good of heart over the good things that the Lord did for David his servant and for Israel his people.

#### Chapter 9

**1 Kings 9:1**

And it came to be, when Solomon finished building the house of the Lord and the house of the king and all the workmanship of Solomon, whatever he desired to do,

**1 Kings 9:2**

that the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, just as he appeared at Gibeon.

**1 Kings 9:3**

And the Lord said to him, I have heard the voice of your prayer and your petition with which you petitioned before me. I have done for you according to all your prayer. I have made this house holy that you built, to put my name there forever, and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.

**1 Kings 9:4**

And you, if you walk before me just as David your father walked, in holiness of heart and in uprightness, doing according to all that I commanded him, and if you keep my ordinances and my commandments,

**1 Kings 9:5**

then I will raise up the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, just as I spoke to David your father, saying, A man leading in Israel will not be lifted away from you.

**1 Kings 9:6**

But if by turning away you turn away, you and your children, from me and do not keep my commandments and my ordinances that Moses gave before you, and you go and serve other gods and bow to them,

**1 Kings 9:7**

**1 Kings 9:8**

And this house, exalted as it is, everyone passing through it will be astonished and will hiss, and they will say, For what cause did the Lord do thus to this land and to this house?

**1 Kings 9:9**

And they will say, Because they forsook the Lord their God who brought their fathers out of Egypt, from the house of slavery, and they held fast to foreign gods and bowed to them and served them. Therefore the Lord brought upon them this evil. Then Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh from the City of David to his house that he built for himself in those days.

**1 Kings 9:10**

Twenty years in which Solomon built the two houses, the house of the Lord and the house of the king,

**1 Kings 9:11**

Hiram king of Tyre had supported Solomon with cedar woods and pine woods and with gold and with all his desire. Then the king gave to Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.

**1 Kings 9:12**

And Hiram went out from Tyre and went to Galilee to see the cities that Solomon gave him, and they were not pleasing to him.

**1 Kings 9:13**

And he said, What are these cities that you gave me, brother? And he called them Border until this day.

**1 Kings 9:14**

And Hiram brought to Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold.

**1 Kings 9:26**

And King Solomon made a ship at Eziongeber, which is near Elath on the shore of the last sea, in the land of Edom.

**1 Kings 9:27**

And Hiram sent in the ship his servants, seafaring men skilled to drive the sea, with the servants of Solomon.

**1 Kings 9:28**

And they came to Ophir and took from there one hundred and twenty talents of gold and brought them to King Solomon.

#### Chapter 10

**1 Kings 10:1**

And the queen of Sheba heard Solomon's name and the name of the Lord and came to test him with riddles.

**1 Kings 10:2**

And she came to Jerusalem with a very heavy force and camels carrying spices and very much gold and costly stone, and she entered to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her heart.

**1 Kings 10:3**

And Solomon reported to her all her words. There was not a word hidden from the king that he did not report to her.

**1 Kings 10:4**

And the queen of Sheba saw all the understanding of Solomon and the house that he built,

**1 Kings 10:5**

and the foods of Solomon and the seating of his servants and the standing of his ministers and his clothing and his cupbearers and his whole burnt offering that he offered up in the house of the Lord, and she was beside herself.

**1 Kings 10:6**

And she said to King Solomon, True is the word that I heard in my land concerning your words and concerning your understanding.

**1 Kings 10:7**

And I did not believe those speaking to me until I came and my eyes saw. And behold, it is not even half according to what they reported to me. You have added goodness to all the report that I heard in my land.

**1 Kings 10:8**

Blessed are your women. Blessed are these servants of yours who stand before you continually, hearing all your understanding.

**1 Kings 10:9**

May the Lord your God be blessed, who delighted in you to give you upon the throne of Israel, because the Lord loved Israel to establish it forever, and he set you as king over them to do judgment in righteousness and in their judgments.

**1 Kings 10:10**

And she gave to Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold and very many spices and costly stone. Such a multitude of spices as those that the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon had not come again.

**1 Kings 10:11**

And the ship of Hiram, carrying the gold from Ophir, brought very many worked timbers and costly stone.

**1 Kings 10:12**

And the king made the worked timbers into supports for the house of the Lord and for the house of the king and lyres and harps for the singers. Such worked timbers had not come upon the earth nor been seen anywhere until this day.

**1 Kings 10:13**

And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired, whatever she asked, besides all that he had given her by the hand of King Solomon. And she turned and went to her land, she and all her servants.

**1 Kings 10:14**

And the weight of the gold coming to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,

**1 Kings 10:15**

besides the levies of the subjects and the merchants and all the kings from beyond and the satraps of the land.

**1 Kings 10:16**

And Solomon made three hundred beaten-gold spears. Three hundred gold pieces were upon each spear.

**1 Kings 10:17**

And three hundred beaten-gold shields, three minas of gold were in each shield, and he put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

**1 Kings 10:18**

And the king made a great ivory throne and covered it around with refined gold.

**1 Kings 10:19**

Six steps belonged to the throne, and backs of calves belonged to the throne behind it, and hands on this side and on that side of the seat, and two lions standing beside the hands.

**1 Kings 10:20**

And twelve lions standing upon the six steps on this side and on that. Thus it was not made for any kingdom.

**1 Kings 10:21**

And all the drinking vessels of Solomon were golden, and the wash-basins were golden, all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon, of closed gold. There was no silver, because it was not reckoned in the days of Solomon.

**1 Kings 10:22**

For the king had a ship of Tarshish in the sea with the ships of Hiram. Once every three years a ship from Tarshish would come to the king, bringing gold and silver and carved and hewn stones. This was the undertaking of the spoil that King Solomon brought up, to build the house of the Lord and the house of the king and the wall of Jerusalem and the citadel, to fence the enclosure of the City of David, and Asshur and Magdan and Gezer and upper Bethhoron and Iethermath and all the chariot-cities and all the horse-cities and the enterprise of Solomon that he undertook to build in Jerusalem and in all the land from the beginning of his rule. All the people remaining from the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Canaanite and the Hivite and the Jebusite and the Girgashite, who were not from the sons of Israel, whose children remained after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel were not able to destroy utterly, Solomon brought them up into levy until this day. But from the sons of Israel Solomon did not assign any to forced work, because they were the warrior men and his servants and his rulers of his chariots and his horsemen.

**1 Kings 10:23**

And Solomon was made greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and understanding.

**1 Kings 10:24**

And all the kings of the earth were seeking the face of Solomon to hear his understanding that the Lord put in his heart.

**1 Kings 10:25**

And they were bringing each his gifts: golden vessels and clothing and myrrh and spices and horses and mules, according to year by year.

**1 Kings 10:26**

And Solomon had four thousand brood mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he placed them in the cities of the chariots and with the king in Jerusalem. And he was ruling all the kings from the river even to the land of the foreigners and to the borders of Egypt.

**1 Kings 10:27**

And the king made the gold and the silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars he made like the sycamores in the plain in multitude.

**1 Kings 10:28**

And the export of the horses of Solomon was from Egypt and from Kue. The merchants of the king were receiving them from Kue by exchange.

**1 Kings 10:29**

And an export chariot would come up from Egypt for one hundred silver pieces and a horse for fifty silver pieces, and so they would go out by sea for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.

#### Chapter 11

**1 Kings 11:1**

And King Solomon was a lover of women, and he had seven hundred wives who were rulers and three hundred concubines, and he took foreign wives, and the daughter of Pharaoh, Moabites, Ammonites, Syrians, Edomites, Hittites, and Amorites,

**1 Kings 11:2**

from the nations of which the Lord said to the sons of Israel, You shall not go in to them, and they shall not go in to you, lest they turn your hearts aside after their idols. To these Solomon clung, to love.

**1 Kings 11:4**

And it came to be in the time of Solomon's old age, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God like the heart of David his father, and the foreign women turned aside his heart after their gods.

**1 Kings 11:5**

Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, idol of Moab, and for their king, idol of the sons of Ammon,

**1 Kings 11:6**

and for Ashtaroth, abomination of the Sidonians.

**1 Kings 11:7**

And thus he did for all his foreign wives, burning incense and sacrificing to their idols.

**1 Kings 11:8**

And Solomon did evil before the Lord. He did not walk after the Lord as David his father did.

**1 Kings 11:9**

And the Lord was angered against Solomon because he turned his heart away from the Lord God of Israel, who appeared to him twice,

**1 Kings 11:10**

and who had commanded him concerning this matter, not at all to go after other gods, and to keep and do what the Lord God commanded him.

**1 Kings 11:11**

And the Lord said to Solomon, Because these things came to be with you and you did not keep my commandments and my ordinances that I commanded you, in tearing I will tear your kingdom out of your hand and give it to your servant.

**1 Kings 11:12**

Yet in your days I will not do it, for the sake of David your father. From the hand of your son I will take it.

**1 Kings 11:13**

Yet I will not take the whole kingdom. I will give one scepter to your son for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I chose.

**1 Kings 11:14**

And the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, and Hezron son of Eliada, who was in Ramah, of Hadadezer king of Zobah his lord. And men were gathered to him, and he was the chief of a band, and he took Damascus beforehand, and they were an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon. And Hadad the Edomite was from the seed of the kingdom in Edom.

**1 Kings 11:15**

And it happened when David was destroying Edom, when Joab commander of the army went to bury the wounded, they cut down every male in Edom.

**1 Kings 11:16**

For six months Joab and all Israel sat there in Edom until he destroyed every male from Edom.

**1 Kings 11:17**

And Hadad fled, he and all the Edomite men from the servants of his father with him, and they entered into Egypt, and Hadad was a small boy.

**1 Kings 11:18**

And men rose from the city of Midian and came to Paran and took men with them and came to Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Hadad entered to Pharaoh, and he gave him a house and appointed bread for him.

**1 Kings 11:19**

And Hadad found favor before Pharaoh greatly, and he gave him as wife the sister of his own wife, sister of Tahpenes the elder.

**1 Kings 11:20**

And the sister of Tahpenes bore to Hadad Genubath her son, and Tahpenes weaned him in the midst of the sons of Pharaoh, and Genubath was in the midst of the sons of Pharaoh.

**1 Kings 11:21**

And Hadad heard in Egypt that David had slept with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army had died, and Hadad said to Pharaoh, Send me away, and I will return to my land.

**1 Kings 11:22**

And Pharaoh said to Hadad, In what are you lacking with me? And behold, you seek to go away to your land. And Hadad said to him, In sending away, send me away. And Hadad returned to his land.

**1 Kings 11:25**

This was the evil that Hadad did, and he was disgusted with Israel, and he reigned in the land of Edom.

**1 Kings 11:26**

And Jeroboam son of Nebat, the Ephrathite from Zereda, son of a widow woman, a servant of Solomon,

**1 Kings 11:27**

and this was the matter in which he lifted his hands against King Solomon: he built the citadel; he closed up the breach of the City of David his father.

**1 Kings 11:28**

And the man Jeroboam was strong in power, and Solomon saw the young man that he was a man of works, and he appointed him over the burdens of the house of Joseph.

**1 Kings 11:29**

And it came to be at that time that Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and Ahijah the Shilonite the prophet found him on the road, and he pulled him off the road. And Ahijah was clothed with a new garment, and both were in the open country.

**1 Kings 11:30**

And Ahijah took hold of his new garment that was upon him and tore it into twelve pieces.

**1 Kings 11:31**

And he said to Jeroboam, Take for yourself ten pieces, because thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I am tearing the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten scepters.

**1 Kings 11:32**

And two scepters will belong to him for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I chose in it from all the tribes of Israel,

**1 Kings 11:33**

because he forsook me and did to Ashtaroth, abomination of the Sidonians, and to Chemosh and to the idols of Moab and to their king, provocation of the sons of Ammon, and he did not walk in my ways to do what is right before me, as David his father did.

**1 Kings 11:34**

And I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand, because in resisting I will resist him all the days of his life for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose.

**1 Kings 11:35**

And I will take the kingdom from the hand of his son and give you the ten scepters.

**1 Kings 11:36**

And to his son I will give the two scepters, so that there may be a setting for my servant David all the days before me in Jerusalem, the city that I chose for myself to put my name there.

**1 Kings 11:37**

And I will take you, and you will reign over whatever your soul desires, and you will be king over Israel.

**1 Kings 11:38**

And it will be, if you keep all that I command you and walk in my ways and do what is right before me, to keep my commandments and my ordinances just as David my servant did, then I will be with you and build for you a faithful house just as I built for David.

**1 Kings 11:40**

And Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death, and he rose and fled into Egypt to Shishak king of Egypt and was in Egypt until Solomon died.

**1 Kings 11:41**

And the rest of the matters of Solomon and all that he did and all his understanding, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of Solomon?

**1 Kings 11:42**

And the days that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem were forty years.

**1 Kings 11:43**

And Solomon slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David his father. And it happened when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard, while he was still in Egypt, as he fled from before Solomon and sat in Egypt, that he set straight and comes to his city, to the land of Zereda in the hill country of Ephraim. And King Solomon slept with his fathers, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

#### Chapter 12

**1 Kings 12:1**

And King Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel was coming to Shechem to make him king.

**1 Kings 12:3**

And the people spoke to King Rehoboam, saying,

**1 Kings 12:4**

Your father made our yoke heavy, and you now lighten from the hard service of your father and from his heavy yoke that he put upon us, and we will serve you.

**1 Kings 12:5**

And he said to them, Go away until three days and return to me. And they went away.

**1 Kings 12:6**

And the king gave charge to the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he still lived, saying, How do you counsel, and shall I answer this people a word?

**1 Kings 12:7**

And they spoke to him, saying, If on this day you will be servant to this people and serve them and speak good words to them, they will be your servants all the days.

**1 Kings 12:8**

But he forsook the counsel of the elders, what they had counseled him, and took counsel with the young men reared with him who stood before his face.

**1 Kings 12:9**

And he said to them, What do you counsel, and what shall I answer this people, who spoke to me, saying, Lighten from the yoke that your father put upon us?

**1 Kings 12:10**

And the young men reared with him, those standing before his face, spoke to him, saying, Thus you will speak to this people who said to you, Your father made our yoke heavy, and you now lighten from us. Thus you will speak to them: My littleness is thicker than my father's loins.

**1 Kings 12:11**

And now my father laid a heavy yoke upon you, and I will add upon your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.

**1 Kings 12:12**

And all Israel came to King Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king spoke to them, saying, Return to me on the third day.

**1 Kings 12:13**

And the king answered the people harshly, and Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the elders that they counseled him,

**1 Kings 12:14**

and he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add upon your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.

**1 Kings 12:15**

And the king did not hear the people, because the turnabout was from the Lord, so that he might establish his word that he spoke by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.

**1 Kings 12:16**

And all Israel saw that their king did not hear them, and the people answered the king, saying, What share is ours in David, and there is no inheritance for us in the son of Jesse. Turn away, Israel, to your tents. Now shepherd your own house, David. And Israel went away to their tents.

**1 Kings 12:18**

And the king sent Adoniram, the one over the levy, and all Israel stoned him with stones and he died. And King Rehoboam hurried to go up to flee to Jerusalem.

**1 Kings 12:19**

And Israel rebelled against the house of David until this day.

**1 Kings 12:20**

And it came to be when all Israel heard that Jeroboam came back from Egypt, they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over Israel, and there was none after the house of David except the scepter of Judah and Benjamin alone.

**1 Kings 12:21**

And Rehoboam entered Jerusalem and assembled the congregation of Judah and the scepter of Benjamin, one hundred twenty thousand young men who make war, to fight against the house of Israel, to return the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.

**1 Kings 12:22**

And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,

**1 Kings 12:23**

Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and to the remnant of the people, saying,

**1 Kings 12:24**

Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight with your brothers, sons of Israel. Let each return to his own house, because this word has happened from me. And they heard the word of the Lord and stopped from going according to the word of the Lord. And King Solomon sleeps with his fathers and is buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place in Jerusalem, being sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twelve years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Naanan daughter of Anan son of Nahash king of the sons of Ammon, and he did evil before the Lord and did not walk in the way of David his father. And there was a man from the hill country of Ephraim, servant to Solomon, and his name was Jeroboam, and his mother's name was Zereda, a prostitute woman, and Solomon gave him as chief officer of the staff over the burdens of the house of Joseph, and he built for Solomon Zereda in the hill country of Ephraim, and he had three hundred chariots of horses. This one built the citadel among the burdens of the house of Ephraim. This one closed up the City of David and was being lifted up against the kingdom. And Solomon sought to put him to death, and he feared and fled to Shishak king of Egypt and was with him until Solomon died. And Jeroboam heard in Egypt that Solomon died, and he spoke into the ears of Shishak king of Egypt, saying, Send me away, and I will depart to my land. And Shishak said to him, Ask what request and I will give it to you. And Shishak gave to Jeroboam the elder sister of Tahpenes, his own wife, for a wife. She was great among the daughters of the king and bore to Jeroboam Abijah his son. And Jeroboam said to Shishak, Truly send me away, and I will depart. And Jeroboam went out from Egypt and came to the land of Zereda in the hill country of Ephraim and gathered there all the scepter of Ephraim and built a fort there. And his young child became very sick with a very severe sickness, and Jeroboam went to inquire concerning the child, and he said to Ano his wife, Rise and go inquire of God concerning the child, whether he will live from his sickness. And there was a man in Shallum, and his name was Ahijah, and he was sixty years old, and the word of the Lord was with him. And Jeroboam said to his wife, Rise and take in your hand to the man of God loaves and cakes for his children and grapes and a jar of honey. And the woman rose and took in her hand loaves and two cakes and grapes and a jar of honey for Ahijah, and the man was old and his eyes were dim from seeing. And she rose from Zereda and went.
