And it came to be when she entered the city to Ahijah the Shilonite, Ahijah said to his young servant, Go out now to meet Ano wife of Jeroboam and say to her, Come in and do not stand still, because thus says the Lord: Hard things I am sending upon you. And Ano entered to the man of God, and Ahijah said to her, Why have you brought me loaves and grapes and cakes and a jar of honey? Thus says the Lord: Behold, you will depart from me, and it will be when you enter the gate into Zereda and your maidens come out to meet you and say to you, The child has died, because thus says the Lord: Behold, I will destroy from Jeroboam one urinating against a wall, and those dying of Jeroboam in the city dogs will devour, and the one dying in the field the birds of heaven will devour, and for the child they will mourn. Alas, Lord, because a good word concerning the Lord was found in him. And the woman departed when she heard, and it came to be when she entered into Zereda, the child died and the cry went out to meet her. And Jeroboam went to Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and gathered there the tribes of Israel, and Rehoboam son of Solomon went up there. And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the Elamite, saying, Take for yourself a new garment not yet entered into water and tear it into twelve pieces, and give them to Jeroboam and say to him, Thus says the Lord: Take for yourself ten pieces to put on, and Jeroboam took them, and Shemaiah said, Thus says the Lord concerning the ten tribes of Israel. And the people said to Rehoboam son of Solomon, Your father made his yoke heavy upon us and made the foods of his table heavy. And now, if you lighten things upon us, we will serve you. And Rehoboam said to the people, In three days I will answer you a word. And he said, Bring in to me the elders and I will take counsel with them what word I should answer the people on the third day. And Rehoboam spoke into their ears, just as the people sent to him, and the elders said, Thus the people spoke to you. And Rehoboam scattered their counsel, and it was not pleasing before him, and he sent and brought in his companions and spoke these same things to them: Thus the people sent to me. And his companions said, Thus you will speak to the people, saying, My littleness is thicker than my father's loin. My father whipped you with whips, but I will rule you with scorpions. And the word was pleasing before Rehoboam, and he answered the people just as his companions, the young men, counseled him. And all the people cried out as one man, each to his neighbor, and they all cried aloud, saying, There is no share for us in David and no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel, because this man is not for ruler nor for leader. And all the people were scattered from Sikim and each went to his tent, and Rehoboam prevailed and went and mounted his chariot and entered into Jerusalem, and all the scepter of Judah and all the scepter of Benjamin went after him. And it came to be at the turn of the year, and Rehoboam gathered all the men of Judah and Benjamin and went up to war against Jeroboam at Shechem. And the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying, Speak to Rehoboam king of Judah and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and to the remnant of the people, saying, Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight against your brothers the sons of Israel. Return each to his house, because this word has happened from me. And they heard the word of the Lord and held back from going according to the word of the Lord.

**1 Kings 12:25**

And Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived in it, and he went out from there and built Penuel.

**1 Kings 12:26**

And Jeroboam said in his heart, Behold, now the kingdom will turn back to the house of David.

**1 Kings 12:27**

If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, then the heart of the people will turn back to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me.

**1 Kings 12:28**

And the king took counsel and went and made two golden heifers and said to the people, Let it be enough for you to go up to Jerusalem. Behold your gods, Israel, that brought you up out of the land of Egypt.

**1 Kings 12:29**

And he placed one in Bethel and one he gave in Dan.

**1 Kings 12:30**

And this word became sin, and the people went before the one as far as Dan.

**1 Kings 12:31**

And he made houses upon high places and made priests from a part of the people, who were not from the sons of Levi.

**1 Kings 12:32**

And Jeroboam made a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, according to the feast in the land of Judah, and he went up upon the altar that he made in Bethel to sacrifice to the heifers that he made, and he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places that he made.

**1 Kings 12:33**

And he went up upon the altar that he made on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the feast that he devised from his own heart, and he made a feast for the sons of Israel and went up upon the altar to offer incense.

#### Chapter 13

**1 Kings 13:1**

And behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the word of the Lord, and Jeroboam had stood by the altar to sacrifice.

**1 Kings 13:2**

And he cried against the altar by the word of the Lord and said, Altar, altar, thus says the Lord: Behold, a son is being born to the house of David, Josiah his name, and he will sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who sacrifice upon you, and he will burn human bones upon you.

**1 Kings 13:3**

And on that day he gave a sign, saying, This is the word that the Lord spoke, saying, Behold, the altar is splitting apart, and the fat upon it will be poured out.

**1 Kings 13:4**

And it came to be when King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God, the one who cried against the altar in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, Seize him. And behold, his hand that he stretched out against him dried up, and he could not turn it back to himself.

**1 Kings 13:5**

And the altar split apart, and the fat was poured out from the altar according to the sign that the man of God gave by the word of the Lord.

**1 Kings 13:6**

And King Jeroboam said to the man of God, Entreat the face of the Lord your God, and let my hand return to me. And the man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and the king's hand returned to him and became as before.

**1 Kings 13:7**

And the king spoke to the man of God, Come in with me into the house and breakfast, and I will give you a gift.

**1 Kings 13:8**

And the man of God said to the king, If you give me half your house, I will not go in with you, and I will certainly not eat bread nor certainly drink water in this place.

**1 Kings 13:9**

For thus the Lord commanded me by word, saying, Eat no bread and drink no water and do not return by the way in which you went.

**1 Kings 13:10**

And he went away by another road and did not return by the road on which he came into Bethel.

**1 Kings 13:11**

And one old prophet lived in Bethel, and his sons came and recounted to him all the deeds that the man of God did on that day in Bethel and the words that he spoke to the king, and they told them before their father.

**1 Kings 13:12**

And their father spoke to them, saying, Which road did he go? And his sons showed him the road by which the man of God who came from Judah went up.

**1 Kings 13:13**

And he said to his sons, Saddle the donkey for me. And they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.

**1 Kings 13:14**

And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak, and said to him, Are you the man of God who came from Judah? And he said to him, I am.

**1 Kings 13:15**

And he said to him, Come with me and eat bread.

**1 Kings 13:16**

And he said, I am certainly not able to return with you, and I will certainly not eat bread nor drink water in this place.

**1 Kings 13:17**

For thus it has been commanded me by the word of the Lord, saying, Eat no bread there and drink no water there and do not return by the road in which you went.

**1 Kings 13:18**

And he said to him, I also am a prophet as you are, and an angel spoke to me by a word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with yourself into your house, and let him eat bread and drink water. But he lied to him.

**1 Kings 13:19**

And he brought him back, and he ate bread and drank water in his house.

**1 Kings 13:20**

And it came to be while they were sitting at the table, the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back.

**1 Kings 13:21**

And he said to the man of God who came from Judah, saying, Thus says the Lord: Because you defied the word of the Lord and did not keep the commandment that the Lord your God commanded you,

**1 Kings 13:22**

and you turned back and ate bread and drank water in the place of which he spoke to you, saying, Eat no bread and drink no water, your body shall certainly not enter into the tomb of your fathers.

**1 Kings 13:23**

And it came to be after he ate bread and drank water, the donkey was saddled for him, and he went back.

**1 Kings 13:24**

And he went away, and a lion found him on the road and killed him, and his body was thrown on the road, and the donkey stood beside it, and the lion stood beside the body.

**1 Kings 13:25**

And behold, men passing by saw the corpse thrown on the road and the lion standing next to the corpse, and they came in and spoke in the city where the old prophet lived.

**1 Kings 13:26**

And the one who brought him back from the road heard and said, This is the man of God who defied the word of the Lord.

**1 Kings 13:28**

And he went and found his body thrown on the road, and the donkey and the lion had stood beside the body. The lion had not eaten the body of the man of God and had not crushed the donkey.

**1 Kings 13:29**

And the prophet lifted the body of the man of God and put it upon the donkey and brought him back into the city, the prophet to bury him.

**1 Kings 13:30**

And they laid him in his own tomb, and they mourned for him, Alas, brother.

**1 Kings 13:31**

And it came to be after mourning for him, he said to his sons, saying, If I die, bury me in this tomb where the man of God has been buried. Put me beside his bones, so that my bones may be preserved with his bones.

**1 Kings 13:32**

For the word that he spoke by the word of the Lord against the altar in Bethel and against the houses of the high places in Samaria will surely happen.

**1 Kings 13:33**

And after this word Jeroboam did not turn back from his evil, and he turned again and made priests of high places from every part of the people. Whoever wished, he filled his hand, and he became priest for the high places.

**1 Kings 13:34**

And this word became sin to the house of Jeroboam, and for ruin and for destruction from the face of the earth.

#### Chapter 14

**1 Kings 14:21**

And Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned over Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the Lord chose to put his name there from all the tribes of Israel, and his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.

**1 Kings 14:22**

And Rehoboam did evil before the Lord and provoked him to jealousy by all that his fathers did and by their sins that they sinned.

**1 Kings 14:23**

And they built for themselves high places and pillars and groves upon every high hill and under every shady tree.

**1 Kings 14:24**

And a conspiracy came to be in the land, and they acted according to all the abominations of the nations that the Lord drove out from before the sons of Israel.

**1 Kings 14:25**

And it came to be in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.

**1 Kings 14:26**

And he took all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house, and the golden spears that David took from the hand of the sons of Hadadezer king of Zobah and brought them into Jerusalem. He took everything, the golden arms.

**1 Kings 14:27**

And King Rehoboam made bronze arms in their place, and the chiefs of the runners, those guarding the gate of the king's house, were set over them.

**1 Kings 14:28**

And it came to be whenever the king entered into the house of the Lord, the runners carried them and returned them to the chamber of the runners.

**1 Kings 14:29**

And the rest of the matters of Rehoboam and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Judah?

**1 Kings 14:30**

And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days.

**1 Kings 14:31**

And Rehoboam slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Abijam his son reigned in his place.

#### Chapter 15

**1 Kings 15:1**

And in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam son of Rehoboam reigned over Judah.

**1 Kings 15:2**

And he reigned six years, and his mother's name was Maachah daughter of Absalom.

**1 Kings 15:3**

And he walked in the sins of his father that he did before him, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God like the heart of David his father.

**1 Kings 15:4**

For on account of David the Lord gave him a remnant, to set up his children after him and to establish Jerusalem.

**1 Kings 15:5**

Because David did what was right before the Lord and did not turn aside from all that he commanded him all the days of his life.

**1 Kings 15:7**

And the rest of the matters of Abijam and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

**1 Kings 15:8**

And Abijam slept with his fathers in the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Asa his son reigned in his place.

**1 Kings 15:9**

In the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa reigned over Judah.

**1 Kings 15:10**

And he reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Anah daughter of Absalom.

**1 Kings 15:11**

And Asa did what was right before the Lord, as David his father did.

**1 Kings 15:12**

And he removed the rites from the land and sent away all the practices that his fathers made.

**1 Kings 15:13**

And he removed Anah his mother from being leader, because she made an assembly in her grove, and Asa cut down her recesses and burned them with fire in the Kidron wadi.

**1 Kings 15:14**

But the high places he did not remove. Yet the heart of Asa was perfect with the Lord all his days.

**1 Kings 15:15**

And he brought the pillars of his father, and his own pillars he brought into the house of the Lord, silver and gold and vessels.

**1 Kings 15:16**

And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all the days.

**1 Kings 15:17**

And Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and built Ramah so that there might not be one going out or one coming in to Asa king of Judah.

**1 Kings 15:18**

And Asa took the silver and the gold found in the treasures of the king's house and gave them into the hands of his servants, and King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimon son of Hezion, king of Syria, the one dwelling in Damascus, saying,

**1 Kings 15:19**

Make a covenant between me and you and between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you gifts, silver and gold. Come, scatter your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, and he will go up from me.

**1 Kings 15:20**

And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the cities of Israel and struck Ijon and Dan and Abel-beth-maachah and all Cinneroth as far as all the land of Naphtali.

**1 Kings 15:21**

And it came to be when Baasha heard, he stopped building Ramah and returned to Tirzah.

**1 Kings 15:22**

And King Asa gave charge to all Judah without exception, and they carried off the stones of Ramah and its timbers that Baasha built, and King Asa built with them all the hill of Benjamin and the watchtower.

**1 Kings 15:23**

And the rest of the matters of Asa and all his dominion that he exercised, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Judah? Yet in the time of his old age his feet were in pain.

**1 Kings 15:24**

And Asa slept and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.

**1 Kings 15:25**

And Nadab son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

**1 Kings 15:26**

And he did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of his father and in his sins by which he made Israel sin.

**1 Kings 15:27**

And Baasha son of Ahijah of the house of Belaan conspired against him and struck him at Gibbethon of the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.

**1 Kings 15:28**

And Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa son of Abijam king of Judah and reigned in his place.

**1 Kings 15:29**

And it came to be when he reigned, he struck the house of Jeroboam and left no breathing thing of Jeroboam until he destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke by the hand of his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,

**1 Kings 15:30**

because of the sins of Jeroboam, as he made Israel sin, and by his provocation with which he provoked the Lord God of Israel.

**1 Kings 15:31**

And the rest of the matters of Nadab and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel?

**1 Kings 15:33**

And in the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah reigned over Israel in Tirzah twenty-four years.

**1 Kings 15:34**

And he did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins by which he made Israel sin.

#### Chapter 16

**1 Kings 16:1**

And the word of the Lord came by the hand of Jehu son of Anani against Baasha,

**1 Kings 16:2**

Because I lifted you up from the earth and gave you as a leader over my people Israel, and you walked in the way of Jeroboam and made my people Israel sin, to provoke me by their vanities,

**1 Kings 16:3**

behold, I am raising up after Baasha and after his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

**1 Kings 16:4**

The dead one of Baasha in the city, dogs will eat him, and the dead one of his in the field, birds of the sky will eat him.

**1 Kings 16:5**

And the rest of the matters of Baasha and all that he did and his acts of power, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel?

**1 Kings 16:6**

And Baasha slept with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and Ela his son reigned in his place in the twentieth year of King Asa.

**1 Kings 16:7**

And by the hand of Jehu son of Anani the Lord spoke against Baasha and against his house, all the evil that he did before the Lord, provoking him by the works of his hands, by becoming like the house of Jeroboam and because he struck him.

**1 Kings 16:8**

And Ela son of Baasha reigned over Israel two years in Tirzah.

**1 Kings 16:9**

And Zimri, commander of half the cavalry, conspired against him, while he was in Tirzah drinking himself drunk in the house of Osa the steward in Tirzah.

**1 Kings 16:10**

And Zimri went in and struck him and killed him and reigned in his place.

**1 Kings 16:11**

And it came to be when he reigned, when he sat upon his throne, he struck the whole house of Baasha.

**1 Kings 16:12**

This happened according to the word that the Lord spoke against the house of Baasha through Jehu the prophet,

**1 Kings 16:13**

because of all the sins of Baasha and Ela his son, by which they made Israel sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel by their vanities.

**1 Kings 16:14**

And the rest of the matters of Ela and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel?

**1 Kings 16:15**

And Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah, and the camp of Israel was at Gibbethon of the Philistines.

**1 Kings 16:16**

And the people in the camp heard them saying, Zimri has conspired and has struck the king, and on that day in the camp they made Omri, commander of the army, king over Israel.

**1 Kings 16:17**

And Omri went up, and all Israel with him, from Gibbethon and they besieged Tirzah.

**1 Kings 16:18**

And it came to be when Zimri saw that his city had been seized, he entered into the citadel of the king's house and burned the king's house over himself with fire and died,

**1 Kings 16:19**

because of his sins that he did, by doing evil before the Lord, by walking in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins by which he made Israel sin.

**1 Kings 16:20**

And the rest of the matters of Zimri and his conspiracies that he conspired, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel?

**1 Kings 16:21**

Then the people of Israel were divided: half the people were behind Tibni son of Ginath to make him king, and half the people were behind Omri.

**1 Kings 16:22**

The people who were behind Omri prevailed over the people who were behind Tibni son of Ginath, and Tibni died, and Joram his brother at that time, and Omri reigned after Tibni.

**1 Kings 16:23**

In the thirty-first year of King Asa, Omri reigned over Israel twelve years; in Tirzah he reigned six years.

**1 Kings 16:24**

And Omri bought the mountain of Shemer from Shemer, lord of the mountain, for two talents of silver, and built the mountain and called the name of the mountain that he built by the name of Shemer, lord of the mountain, Shemer.

**1 Kings 16:25**

And Omri did evil before the Lord and did worse than all those who came before him.

**1 Kings 16:26**

And he walked in every way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sins by which he made Israel sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel by their vanities.

**1 Kings 16:27**

And the rest of the matters of Omri and all that he did and his dominion, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel?

**1 Kings 16:28**

And Omri slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigned in his place. And in the eleventh year of Omri, Jehoshaphat son of Asa reigned, thirty-five years old in his reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. And he walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right before the Lord, except the high places they did not remove; they sacrificed on the high places and burned incense. And the rest of the alliances that Jehoshaphat made and all the dominion that he exercised and those against whom he fought, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Judah? And the rest of the entanglements that were imposed in the days of Asa his father he removed from the land. And there was no king in Syria, only a deputy. And King Jehoshaphat made a ship for Tarshish to go to Sophir for gold, and it did not go because the ship was broken at Eziongeber. Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, I will send your servants and my servants in the ship, and Jehoshaphat was not willing. And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Joram his son reigned in his place.

**1 Kings 16:29**

In the second year of Jehoshaphat, Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.

**1 Kings 16:30**

And Ahab did evil before the Lord. He did worse than all those before him.

**1 Kings 16:31**

And it was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and he took Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians for a wife and went and served Baal and bowed down to him.

**1 Kings 16:32**

And he set up an altar to Baal in the house of his abominations, which he built in Samaria.

**1 Kings 16:33**

And Ahab made a grove, and Ahab added by making provocations, provoking his own soul toward destruction. He did evil beyond all the kings of Israel who came before him.

**1 Kings 16:34**

In his days Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho. In Abiram his firstborn he founded it, and in Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke by the hand of Joshua son of Nun.

#### Chapter 17

**1 Kings 17:1**

And Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Thesbon of Gilead, said to Ahab, As the Lord God of hosts, God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, these years there shall be no dew and rain except by the word of my mouth.

**1 Kings 17:2**

And the word of the Lord came to Elijah,

**1 Kings 17:3**

Go from here eastward and hide yourself by the wadi Cherith, the one before the Jordan.

**1 Kings 17:4**

And it shall be, you will drink water from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.

**1 Kings 17:5**

And Elijah did according to the word of the Lord and sat by the wadi Cherith before the Jordan.

**1 Kings 17:6**

And the ravens brought him breads in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the wadi.

**1 Kings 17:7**

And it came to be after days, the wadi dried up because no rain came upon the land.

**1 Kings 17:8**

And the word of the Lord came to Elijah,

**1 Kings 17:9**

Rise and go to Sarepta of Sidonia. Behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to feed you.

**1 Kings 17:10**

And he rose and went to Sarepta, to the gate of the city, and behold, there a widow woman was gathering sticks. And Elijah cried after her and said to her, Please fetch me a little water in a vessel and I will drink.

**1 Kings 17:11**

And as she went to fetch it, Elijah cried after her and said, Please take for me a morsel of bread in your hand.

**1 Kings 17:12**

And the woman said, As the Lord your God lives, I have no cake except as much as a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug, and behold, I am gathering two little sticks and will go in and make it for myself and my children, and we will eat and die.

**1 Kings 17:13**

And Elijah said to her, Take courage. Go in and do according to your word, but first make for me from there a little cake and bring it out to me, and for yourself and your children you will make it afterward.

**1 Kings 17:14**

For thus says the Lord: the jar of flour will not fail and the jug of oil will not lessen until the day the Lord gives rain upon the land.

**1 Kings 17:15**

And the woman went and did, and she and he and her children were eating.

**1 Kings 17:16**

And the jar of flour did not fail, and the jug of oil did not lessen, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke by the hand of Elijah.

**1 Kings 17:17**

And it came to be after these things, the son of the woman, mistress of the house, became sick, and his sickness was very severe until no breath was left in him.

**1 Kings 17:18**

And she said to Elijah, What is to me and to you, man of God? You entered to me to bring my injustices to remembrance and to put my son to death.

**1 Kings 17:19**

And Elijah said to the woman, Give me your son. And he took him from her bosom and brought him up into the upper room where he himself sat there and laid him upon his bed.

**1 Kings 17:20**

And Elijah cried out and said, Alas, Lord, witness of the widow with whom I dwell, with her you have done evil, by putting her son to death?

**1 Kings 17:21**

And he breathed on the child three times and called upon the Lord and said, Lord my God, let the soul of this child now return into him.

**1 Kings 17:22**

And it came to be so, and the child cried out.

**1 Kings 17:23**

And he brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother, and Elijah said, Look, your son lives.

**1 Kings 17:24**

And the woman said to Elijah, Behold, I now know that you are a man of God and the word of the Lord in your mouth is true.

#### Chapter 18

**1 Kings 18:1**

And it came to be after many days, the word of the Lord came to Elijah in the third year, saying, Go and appear to Ahab, and I will give rain upon the face of the earth.

**1 Kings 18:2**

And Elijah went to appear to Ahab, and the famine was severe in Samaria.

**1 Kings 18:3**

And Ahab called Obadiah the steward, and Obadiah was fearing the Lord greatly.

**1 Kings 18:4**

And it came to be when Jezebel was striking the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took one hundred prophet-men and hid them by fifty in a cave and fed them with bread and water.

**1 Kings 18:5**

And Ahab said to Obadiah, Come, let us pass through the land, to the springs of the waters and to the wadis, if somehow we may find grass and preserve horses and mules, and they will not be destroyed from among the livestock.

**1 Kings 18:6**

And they divided for themselves the road to pass through it. Ahab went one road alone, and Obadiah went another road alone.

**1 Kings 18:7**

And Obadiah was on the road alone, and Elijah came to meet him alone, and Obadiah hurried and fell upon his face and said, Are you really my lord Elijah?

**1 Kings 18:8**

And Elijah said to him, I am. Go, tell your lord, Behold, Elijah.

**1 Kings 18:9**

And Obadiah said, What have I sinned, that you are giving your servant into the hand of Ahab to kill me?

**1 Kings 18:10**

As the Lord your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you, and they said, He is not here, and he bound the kingdom and its regions by oath that it had not found you.

**1 Kings 18:11**

And now you say, Go, announce to your lord, Behold, Elijah.

**1 Kings 18:12**

And it will be, if I go away from you, the Spirit of the Lord will carry you to a land that I do not know, and I will go in to report to Ahab, and he will kill me. Yet your servant has been fearing the Lord from his youth.

**1 Kings 18:13**

Was it not reported to you, my lord, what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the Lord, that I hid one hundred men of the prophets of the Lord, fifty by fifty in a cave, and fed them with breads and water?

**1 Kings 18:14**

And now you say to me, Go, tell your lord, Behold, Elijah, and he will kill me.

**1 Kings 18:15**

And Elijah said, As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, today I will appear to him.

**1 Kings 18:16**

And Obadiah went to meet Ahab and reported to him, and Ahab ran out and went to meet Elijah.

**1 Kings 18:17**

And it came to be when Ahab saw Elijah, Ahab said to Elijah, Are you really the one disturbing Israel?

**1 Kings 18:18**

And Elijah said, I am not disturbing Israel, but you and your father's house, in that you forsook the Lord your God and went after the Baalim.

**1 Kings 18:19**

And now send, gather to me all Israel at Mount Carmel and the prophets of the Shame, four hundred fifty, and the prophets of the groves, four hundred, eating Jezebel's table.

**1 Kings 18:20**

And Ahab sent to all Israel and gathered all the prophets at Mount Carmel.

**1 Kings 18:21**

And Elijah came near to all and said to them, How long will you limp on both knees? If the Lord is God, go after him; but if Baal is, go after him. And the people did not answer a word.

**1 Kings 18:22**

And Elijah said to the people, I alone am left as a prophet of the Lord, utterly alone, and the prophets of Baal are four hundred fifty men and the prophets of the grove four hundred.

**1 Kings 18:23**

Let them give us two calves, and let them choose one for themselves and butcher it and place it upon the woods, and put no fire. And I will prepare the other bull, and I will certainly place no fire.

**1 Kings 18:24**

And call aloud on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord my God, and the god who answers by fire, he is God. And all the people answered and said, Good is the word that you spoke.

**1 Kings 18:25**

And Elijah said to the prophets of the Shame, Choose for yourselves the one calf and prepare it first, because you are many, and call on the name of your god, but put no fire.

**1 Kings 18:26**

And they took the calf and prepared it, and they kept calling in the name of Baal from morning until midday and said, Answer us, O Baal, answer us. And there was no voice, and there was no hearing, and they ran about on the altar that they made.

**1 Kings 18:27**

And it came to be at midday, Elijah the Tishbite mocked them and said, Call with a loud voice, because he is god. Surely he has talk on his mind, or perhaps he is occupied, or perhaps he sleeps and will awaken.

**1 Kings 18:28**

And they called with a loud voice and cut themselves according to their custom with swords and lances until blood poured out upon them.

**1 Kings 18:29**

And they prophesied until the evening passed, and it came to be at the time for the sacrifice to go up, and there was no voice. And Elijah the Tishbite spoke to the prophets of the abominations, saying, Stand aside now, and I will make my whole burnt offering. And they stood aside and went away.

**1 Kings 18:30**

And Elijah said to the people, Come near to me. And all the people came near to him.

**1 Kings 18:31**

And Elijah took twelve stones according to the number of the tribes of Israel, as the Lord spoke to him, saying, Israel shall be your name.

**1 Kings 18:32**

And he built the stones in the name of the Lord and healed the torn-down altar and made a trench around the altar, able to hold two measures of seed.

**1 Kings 18:33**

And he stacked the split wood upon the altar that he made and cut up the whole burnt offering and placed it upon the wood and stacked it upon the altar.

**1 Kings 18:34**

And he said, Take for me four jars of water and pour it upon the whole burnt offering and upon the wood. And they did so. And he said, Do it a second time, and they did it a second time. And he said, Do it a third time, and they did it a third time.

**1 Kings 18:35**

And the water kept going around the altar, and they filled the trench with water.

**1 Kings 18:36**

And Elijah cried out to heaven and said, Lord God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel, answer me, Lord, answer me today by fire, and let all this people know that you are Lord, God of Israel, and I am your servant, and because of you I have done these works.

**1 Kings 18:37**

Answer me, Lord, answer me by fire, and let this people know that you are the Lord, God, and you have turned back the heart of this people.

**1 Kings 18:38**

And fire from the Lord fell from heaven and devoured the whole burnt offering and the split wood and the water in the trench, and the fire licked up the stones and the dust.

**1 Kings 18:39**

And all the people fell on their faces and said, Truly the Lord, he is God, he is God.

**1 Kings 18:40**

And Elijah said to the people, Seize the prophets of Baal. Let not one of them be saved. And they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the wadi Kishon and slaughtered them there.

**1 Kings 18:41**

And Elijah said to Ahab, Go up, eat and drink, because there is a sound of the feet of rain.

**1 Kings 18:42**

And Ahab went up to eat and drink, and Elijah went up upon Carmel and bent to the ground and put his face between his knees.

**1 Kings 18:43**

And he said to his servant-boy, Go up and look in the direction of the sea. And the servant-boy looked and said, There is nothing. And Elijah said, Then return seven times, and the servant-boy returned seven times.

**1 Kings 18:44**

And it came to be at the seventh time, behold, a little cloud like a man's footprint bringing up water, and he said, Go up and tell Ahab, Harness your chariot and go down, lest the rain overtake you.

**1 Kings 18:45**

And it came to be here and there, and the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and a great rain came, and Ahab wept and went to Jezreel.

**1 Kings 18:46**

And the hand of the Lord was upon Elijah, and he girded up his waist and ran before Ahab as far as Jezreel.

#### Chapter 19

**1 Kings 19:1**

And Ahab reported to Jezebel his wife all that Elijah did and how he killed the prophets with the sword.

**1 Kings 19:2**

And Jezebel sent to Elijah and said, If you are Elijah and I am Jezebel, may God do thus to me and add thus, because by this time tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them.

**1 Kings 19:3**

And Elijah feared and rose and went for his own life, and he came to Beersheba of Judah and left his servant-boy there.

**1 Kings 19:4**

And he himself went in the wilderness a day's road and came and sat under one broom plant, and he asked for his life to die and said, Let it be enough now. Take away my life from me, Lord, because I am no better than my fathers.

**1 Kings 19:5**

And he lay down and slept there under a plant, and behold, someone touched him and said to him, Rise and eat.

**1 Kings 19:6**

And Elijah looked, and behold, at his head was a barley cake and a jug of water. And he rose and ate and drank and turned back and slept.

**1 Kings 19:7**

And the angel of the Lord returned a second time and touched him and said to him, Rise, eat, because the road is too much for you.

**1 Kings 19:8**

And he rose and ate and drank and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights as far as Mount Horeb.

**1 Kings 19:9**

And he entered there into the cave and lodged there. And behold, the word of the Lord came to him and said, What are you doing here, Elijah?

**1 Kings 19:10**

And Elijah said, In zeal I have been very zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel forsook you, they tore down your altars, and they killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone am left, utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.

**1 Kings 19:11**

And he said, You will go out tomorrow and stand before the Lord on the mountain. Behold, the Lord will pass by, and a great strong wind, dissolving mountains and crushing rocks before the Lord. The Lord was not in the wind. And after the wind, an earthquake. The Lord was not in the earthquake.

**1 Kings 19:12**

And after the earthquake, fire. The Lord was not in the fire. And after the fire, a voice of a thin breeze, and there the Lord.

**1 Kings 19:13**

And it came to be as Elijah heard, he covered his face with his sheepskin cloak and went out and stood under the cave. And behold, a voice came to him and said, What are you doing here, Elijah?

**1 Kings 19:14**

And Elijah said, In zeal I have been very zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel forsook your covenant, they pulled down your altars, and they killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone am left, utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.

**1 Kings 19:15**

And the Lord said to him, Go, return on your way, and you will come to the wilderness road of Damascus, and you will anoint Hazael king of Syria.

**1 Kings 19:16**

And Jehu son of Nimshi you will anoint king over Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat from Abelmeholah you will anoint prophet in your place.

**1 Kings 19:17**

And it shall be, the one escaping from the sword of Hazael, Jehu will put to death, and the one escaping from the sword of Jehu, Elisha will put to death.

**1 Kings 19:18**

And you will leave in Israel seven thousand men, every knee that did not bend knee to Baal and every mouth that did not bow to him.

**1 Kings 19:19**

And he went away from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat, and he was plowing with twelve pairs of oxen before him, and he himself was with the twelve, and Elijah came upon him and threw his sheepskin cloak upon him.

**1 Kings 19:20**

And Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah and said, Let me kiss my father, and I will follow after you. And Elijah said, Return, because what have I done to you?

**1 Kings 19:21**

And he turned back from after him and took the pairs of oxen and sacrificed and boiled them with the gear of the oxen and gave them to the people, and they ate. And he rose and went after Elijah and ministered to him.

#### Chapter 20

**1 Kings 20:1**

And one vineyard belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite beside the threshing floor of Ahab king of Samaria.

**1 Kings 20:2**

And Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, Give me your vineyard, and it shall be for me as a garden of vegetables because it is near to my house, and I will give you another vineyard, better than it. But if it pleases before you, I will give you silver, the exchange-price of this vineyard, and it shall be for me as a garden of vegetables.

**1 Kings 20:3**

And Naboth said to Ahab, May it not be for me from my God to give the inheritance of my fathers to you.

**1 Kings 20:4**

And Ahab's spirit became troubled, and he lay upon his bed and covered his face and did not eat bread.

**1 Kings 20:5**

And Jezebel his wife came in to him and spoke to him, Why is your spirit troubled and you are not eating bread?

**1 Kings 20:6**

And he said to her, Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite, saying, Give me your vineyard for silver, and if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in place of it, and he said, I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.

**1 Kings 20:7**

And Jezebel his wife said to him, Do you now act as king over Israel? Rise, eat bread, and become your own man. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.

**1 Kings 20:8**

And she wrote a letter in the name of Ahab and sealed it with his seal and sent the letter to the elders and the free men living with Naboth.

**1 Kings 20:9**

And it was written in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.

**1 Kings 20:10**

And seat two men, sons of lawlessness, opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, He blessed God and the king. And let them bring him out and stone him, and let him die.

**1 Kings 20:11**

And the men of his city, the elders and the free men dwelling in his city, did just as Jezebel sent to them, just as it was written in the letters that she sent to them.

**1 Kings 20:12**

They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

**1 Kings 20:13**

And two men, sons of lawlessness, came and sat opposite him and testified against him, saying, You blessed God and the king. And they brought him out outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.

**1 Kings 20:14**

And they sent to Jezebel, saying, Naboth has been stoned and is dead.

**1 Kings 20:15**

And it came to be when Jezebel heard, she said to Ahab, Rise, inherit the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, who did not give it to you for silver, because Naboth is not alive; he is dead.

**1 Kings 20:16**

And it came to be when Ahab heard that Naboth the Jezreelite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth, and after these things Ahab rose and went down into the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to inherit it.

**1 Kings 20:17**

And the Lord said to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

**1 Kings 20:18**

Rise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, the one in Samaria. Behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth because he has gone down there to inherit it.

**1 Kings 20:19**

And you will speak to him, saying, Thus says the Lord: As you murdered and inherited, because of this thus says the Lord: In every place where the sows and the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, there the dogs will lick your blood, and the prostitutes will wash in your blood.

**1 Kings 20:20**

And Ahab said to Elijah, Have you found me, my enemy? And he said, I have found you, because you have vainly sold yourself to do evil before the Lord, provoking him.

**1 Kings 20:21**

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon you and will burn after you and destroy from Ahab one pissing against a wall, hemmed in and forsaken in Israel.

**1 Kings 20:22**

And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocations by which you provoked and made Israel sin.

**1 Kings 20:23**

And concerning Jezebel the Lord spoke, saying, Dogs will eat her in the forewall of Jezreel.

**1 Kings 20:24**

The dead one of Ahab in the city, dogs will eat, and the dead one of his in the field, the birds of the sky will eat.

**1 Kings 20:25**

Yet vainly Ahab sold himself to do evil before the Lord, because Jezebel his wife turned him aside.

**1 Kings 20:26**

And he was greatly abominated by going after abominations, according to all that the Amorite did, whom the Lord destroyed from before the sons of Israel.

**1 Kings 20:27**

And because of the word, as Ahab was cut to the heart before the Lord and went weeping, he tore his tunic and girded sackcloth upon his body and fasted and put on sackcloth on the day when he struck Naboth the Jezreelite.

**1 Kings 20:28**

And the word of the Lord came by the hand of his servant Elijah concerning Ahab, and the Lord said,

**1 Kings 20:29**

Have you seen how Ahab was cut to the heart before me? I will not bring the evil in his days, but in the days of his son I will bring the evil.

#### Chapter 21

**1 Kings 21:1**

And Ben-hadad gathered all his force and went up and besieged Samaria, and thirty-two kings with him and all horse and chariot, and they went up and besieged Samaria and fought against it.

**1 Kings 21:2**

And he sent to Ahab king of Israel into the city.

**1 Kings 21:3**

And he said to him, Thus says Ben-hadad: Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your children are mine.

**1 Kings 21:4**

And the king of Israel answered and said, According as you spoke, my lord king, I am yours and all that is mine.

**1 Kings 21:5**

And the messengers returned and said, Thus says Ben-hadad: I sent to you, saying, Your silver and your gold and your wives and your children you will give to me.

**1 Kings 21:6**

For by this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants, and whatever is the desire of their eyes, upon it they will lay their hands and take it.

**1 Kings 21:7**

And the king of Israel called all the elders and said, Know now and see that this one is seeking evil, because he sent to me concerning my wives and my sons and my daughters. My silver and my gold I did not withhold from him.

**1 Kings 21:8**

And the elders and all the people said to him, Do not listen and do not be willing.

**1 Kings 21:9**

And he said to the messengers of Ben-hadad, Tell your lord, All that you sent to your servant at first I will do, but this thing I cannot do. And the men departed and returned a word to him.

**1 Kings 21:10**

And Ben-hadad sent back to him, saying, Thus may God do to me and thus add, if the dust of Samaria will be enough for foxes, for all my footmen.

**1 Kings 21:11**

And the king of Israel answered and said, Let it be enough. Let not the bent one boast like the upright one.

**1 Kings 21:12**

And it came to be when he answered him this word, he himself was drinking, and all the kings with him, in tents, and he said to his servants, Build a palisade, and they set a palisade against the city.

**1 Kings 21:13**

And behold, one prophet came near to the king of Israel and said, Thus says the Lord: Have you seen all this great crowd? Behold, I am giving it today into your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord.

**1 Kings 21:14**

And Ahab said, By whom? And he said, Thus says the Lord: By the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions. And Ahab said, Who will join the battle? And he said, You.

**1 Kings 21:15**

And Ahab reviewed the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions, and they were two hundred thirty, and after these he reviewed the people, every son of strength, sixty thousand.

**1 Kings 21:16**

And they went out at midday, and Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in Socchoth, he and the thirty-two kings, helpers with him.

**1 Kings 21:17**

And the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions went out first, and they sent and reported to the king of Syria, saying, Men have come out from Samaria.

**1 Kings 21:18**

And he said to them, If these come out for peace, seize them alive, and if they come out for war, seize them alive.

**1 Kings 21:19**

And these came out from the city, the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions, and the force behind them.

**1 Kings 21:20**

Each struck the one by him, and each struck again the one by him, and Syria fled, and Israel pursued them, and Ben-hadad king of Syria escaped on horse with horseman.

**1 Kings 21:21**

And the king of Israel went out and took all the horses and the chariots and struck a great blow in Syria.

**1 Kings 21:22**

And the prophet came near to the king of Israel and said, Be strong, and know and see what you will do, because at the turn of the year Ben-hadad king of Syria comes up against you.

**1 Kings 21:23**

And the servants of the king of Syria said, The God of Israel is a god of mountains and not a god of valleys, because of this he prevailed over us. But if we fight them on the plain, will we not prevail over them?

**1 Kings 21:24**

And do this thing: remove the kings, each from his place, and put satraps in their place.

**1 Kings 21:25**

And we will replace for you a force according to the force that fell from you, and horse for horse and chariots for chariots, and we will fight them on the plain and prevail over them. And he listened to their voice and did so.

**1 Kings 21:26**

And it came to be at the turn of the year, Ben-hadad reviewed Syria and went up to Aphek to war against Israel.

**1 Kings 21:27**

And the sons of Israel were reviewed and came to meet them, and Israel camped opposite them like two flocks of goats, and Syria filled the land.

**1 Kings 21:28**

And the man of God came near and said to the king of Israel, Thus says the Lord: Because Syria said, The Lord God of Israel is a god of mountains and not a god of valleys, I will give all this great force into your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord.

**1 Kings 21:29**

And they encamped opposite these seven days, and it came to be on the seventh day the battle drew near, and Israel struck Syria, one hundred thousand footmen in one day.

**1 Kings 21:30**

And the rest fled to Aphek into the city, and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand men of the rest. And Ben-hadad fled and entered into the bedchamber, into the inner room.

**1 Kings 21:31**

And he said to his servants, I know that the kings of Israel are kings of mercy. Let us put sackcloth on our loins and ropes on our heads and go out to the king of Israel, if perhaps he will keep our lives alive.

**1 Kings 21:32**

And they tied sackcloth on their loins and set ropes on their heads and said to the king of Israel, Your servant Ben-hadad says, Let my life now live. And he said, If he still lives, he is my brother.

**1 Kings 21:33**

And the men took it as an omen and hurried and caught the word from his mouth and said, Your brother, Ben-hadad. And he said, Go in and fetch him. And Ben-hadad came out to him, and they brought him up to him on the chariot.

**1 Kings 21:34**

And he said to him, The cities that my father took from your father I will give back to you, and you will set streets for yourself in Damascus, just as my father set them in Samaria. And I, in covenant, will send you away. And he made a covenant with him and sent him away.

**1 Kings 21:35**

And one man from the sons of the prophets said to his neighbor by the word of the Lord, Strike me now. And the man was not willing to strike him.

**1 Kings 21:36**

And he said to him, Because you did not hear the voice of the Lord, behold, you are running away from me, and a lion will strike you. And he went away from him, and a lion found him and struck him.

**1 Kings 21:37**

And he found another man and said, Strike me now. And the man struck him, striking and shattering him.

**1 Kings 21:38**

And the prophet went and stood for the king of Israel by the road and bound his eyes with a band.

**1 Kings 21:39**

And it came to be as the king passed by, this one cried to the king and said, Your servant went out into the army of battle, and behold, a man brought to me a man and said to me, Guard this man. If by escaping he escapes, your life will be for his life, or you will weigh out a talent of silver.

**1 Kings 21:40**

And it came to be, your servant looked here and there, and he was not there. And the king of Israel said to him, Behold, you have also destroyed the snares set for me.

**1 Kings 21:41**

And he hurried and removed the band from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.

**1 Kings 21:42**

And he said to him, Thus says the Lord: Because you brought out from your hand a man appointed to destruction, your life shall be for his life and your people for his people.

**1 Kings 21:43**

And the king of Israel went away confounded and discouraged and came into Samaria.

#### Chapter 22

**1 Kings 22:1**

And they sat three years, and there was no war between Syria and Israel.

**1 Kings 22:2**

And it came to be in the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.

**1 Kings 22:3**

And the king of Israel said to his servants, Do you know that Ramoth Gilead belongs to us, and we are silent to take it from the hand of the king of Syria?

**1 Kings 22:4**

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Will you come up with us to Ramoth Gilead for war? And Jehoshaphat said, As I am, so are you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.

**1 Kings 22:5**

And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said to the king of Israel, Ask the Lord today.

**1 Kings 22:6**

And the king of Israel gathered all the prophets, about four hundred men, and the king said to them, Shall I go to Ramoth Gilead for war, or shall I hold back? And they said, Go up, and in giving, the Lord will give into the hands of the king.

**1 Kings 22:7**

And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, and shall we ask the Lord through him?

**1 Kings 22:8**

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, There is still one man by whom we may ask the Lord, and I hate him because he does not speak good concerning me, only evil: Micaiah son of Imlah. And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said, Let not the king speak so.

**1 Kings 22:9**

And the king of Israel called one eunuch and said, Quickly, Micaiah son of Imlah.

**1 Kings 22:10**

And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each upon his throne, armed, in the gates of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

**1 Kings 22:11**

And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made iron horns for himself and said, Thus says the Lord: With these you will gore Syria until it is finished.

**1 Kings 22:12**

And all the prophets prophesied thus, saying, Go up to Ramoth Gilead and prosper, and the Lord will give into your hands, and the king of Syria.

**1 Kings 22:13**

And the messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, Behold now, all the prophets speak with one mouth good things concerning the king. Be now also in your words like the words of one of these and speak good things.

**1 Kings 22:14**

And Micaiah said, As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, these things I will speak.

**1 Kings 22:15**

And he came to the king, and the king said to him, Micaiah, shall I go up to Ramoth Gilead for war, or shall I hold back? And he said, Go up and prosper, and the Lord will give into the hand of the king.

**1 Kings 22:16**

And the king said to him, How many times do I put you under oath, that you speak truth to me in the name of the Lord?

**1 Kings 22:17**

And Micaiah said, Not so. I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like a flock that has no shepherd, and the Lord said, There is no lord for these. Let each return to his own house in peace.

**1 Kings 22:18**

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Did I not tell you that this one does not prophesy good things to me, only evils?

**1 Kings 22:19**

And Micaiah said, Not so. Hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord God of Israel sitting upon his throne, and all the army of heaven stood around him, at his right hand and at his left.

**1 Kings 22:20**

And the Lord said, Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, and he will go up and fall in Ramoth Gilead? And one said this and another said this.

**1 Kings 22:21**

And a spirit went out and stood before the Lord and said, I will deceive him. And the Lord said to him, By what?

**1 Kings 22:22**

And he said, I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, You will deceive and indeed you will prevail. Go out and do so.

**1 Kings 22:23**

And now, behold, the Lord has given a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evils against you.

**1 Kings 22:24**

And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the jaw and said, What spirit of the Lord was this that spoke in you?

**1 Kings 22:25**

And Micaiah said, Behold, you will see on that day when you enter chamber within chamber to hide yourself.

**1 Kings 22:26**

And the king of Israel said, Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the ruler of the city and to Joash son of the king.

**1 Kings 22:27**

Say to put this one in prison and to feed him bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.

**1 Kings 22:28**

And Micaiah said, If returning you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken in me.

**1 Kings 22:29**

And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up with him to Ramoth Gilead.

**1 Kings 22:30**

And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I will disguise myself and enter into the battle, and you put on my clothing. And the king of Israel disguised himself and entered into the battle.

**1 Kings 22:31**

And the king of Syria commanded the rulers of his chariots, thirty-two, saying, Fight neither small nor great, only the king of Israel, utterly alone.

**1 Kings 22:32**

And it came to be when the rulers of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat king of Judah, they said, This one appears to be the king of Israel, and they surrounded him to fight, and Jehoshaphat cried out.

**1 Kings 22:33**

And it came to be when the rulers of the chariots saw that this one was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.

**1 Kings 22:34**

And one stretched the bow accurately and struck the king of Israel between the lung and between the breastplate, and he said to his charioteer, Turn your hands and bring me out from the battle, because I am wounded.

**1 Kings 22:35**

And the battle turned in that day, and the king was standing on the chariot opposite Syria from morning until evening, and the blood from the wound kept pouring into the bosom of the chariot, and he died at evening, and the blood of the stroke kept going out as far as the bosom of the chariot.

**1 Kings 22:36**

And the herald stood at sunset, saying, Each to his own city and to his own land.

**1 Kings 22:37**

Because the king is dead. And they came to Samaria and buried the king in Samaria.

**1 Kings 22:38**

And they washed the chariot at the spring of Samaria, and the sows and the dogs licked the blood, and the prostitutes bathed in the blood, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke.

**1 Kings 22:39**

And the rest of the matters of Ahab and all that he did and the ivory house that he built and all the cities that he made, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel?

**1 Kings 22:40**

And Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

**1 Kings 22:41**

And Jehoshaphat son of Asa reigned over Judah. In the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel he reigned.

**1 Kings 22:42**

Jehoshaphat was a son of thirty-five years when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

**1 Kings 22:43**

And he walked in every way of Asa his father, and he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord.

**1 Kings 22:44**

Yet he did not remove the high places. The people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

**1 Kings 22:45**

And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.

**1 Kings 22:46**

And the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat and his acts of power, what he did, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Judah?

**1 Kings 22:51**

And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father, and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

**1 Kings 22:52**

And Ahaziah son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.

**1 Kings 22:53**

And he did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Ahab his father and in the way of Jezebel his mother and in the sins of the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.

**1 Kings 22:54**

And he served the Baals and bowed down to them and provoked the Lord God of Israel according to all the things that came before him.

### 2 Kings

#### Chapter 1

**2 Kings 1:1**

And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.

**2 Kings 1:2**

And Ahaziah fell through the lattice in his upper room in Samaria and became sick, and he sent messengers and said to them, Come and seek in Baal of flies, god of Ekron, whether I will live from this sickness. And they went to inquire through him.

**2 Kings 1:3**

And the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying, Rise, come to meet the messengers of Ahaziah king of Samaria, and you will speak to them, Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to seek in Baal of flies, god of Ekron?

**2 Kings 1:4**

And not so, because thus says the Lord: The bed on which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, because by death you will die. And Elijah went and spoke to them.

**2 Kings 1:5**

And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, Why is it that you returned?

**2 Kings 1:6**

And they said to him, A man came up to meet us and said to us, Come, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him, Thus says the Lord: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to seek in Baal of flies, god of Ekron? And not so, the bed on which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, because by death you will die.

**2 Kings 1:7**

And he spoke to them, saying, What was the appearance of the man who came up to meet you and spoke to you these words?

**2 Kings 1:8**

And they said to him, A hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his waist. And he said, This is Elijah the Tishbite.

**2 Kings 1:9**

And he sent to him a captain of fifty and his fifty, and he went up and came to him. And behold, Elijah was sitting on the top of the mountain, and the captain of fifty spoke to him and said, Man of God, the king has called you. Come down.

**2 Kings 1:10**

And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, If I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and eat you and your fifty. And fire came down from heaven and ate him and his fifty.

**2 Kings 1:11**

And the king added and sent to him another captain of fifty and his fifty, and he went up and the captain of fifty spoke to him and said, Man of God, thus says the king: Quickly, come down.

**2 Kings 1:12**

And Elijah answered and spoke to him and said, If I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and eat you and your fifty. And fire came down from heaven and ate him and his fifty.

**2 Kings 1:13**

And the king added yet to send a third captain of fifty and his fifty, and the third captain of fifty came to him and bent upon his knees before Elijah and begged him and spoke to him and said, Man of God, let my life now be precious, and the life of these fifty servants of yours, in your eyes.

**2 Kings 1:14**

Behold, fire came down from heaven and ate the first two captains of fifty and their fifties. And now let the life of your servants be precious in your eyes.

**2 Kings 1:15**

And the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah and said, Go down with him. Do not fear from before them. And Elijah rose and went down with him to the king.

**2 Kings 1:16**

And Elijah spoke to him and said, Thus says the Lord: Why is it that you sent messengers to seek in Baal of flies, god of Ekron? And not so, the bed on which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, because by death you will die.

**2 Kings 1:17**

And he died according to the word of the Lord that Elijah spoke.

**2 Kings 1:18**

And the rest of the matters of Ahaziah, what he did, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Israel? And Joram son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria twelve years, in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. And he did evil before the Lord, yet not like his brothers nor like his mother. And he removed the pillars of Baal that his father made and shattered them. Yet in the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who made Israel sin, he clung and did not depart from them. And the anger of the Lord was enraged against the house of Ahab.

#### Chapter 2

**2 Kings 2:1**

And it came to be when the Lord was taking Elijah up in a storm as into heaven, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.

**2 Kings 2:2**

And Elijah said to Elisha, Stay here now, because the Lord has sent me as far as Bethel. And Elisha said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And they went to Bethel.

**2 Kings 2:3**

And the sons of the prophets in Bethel came to Elisha and said to him, Do you know that today the Lord is taking your lord away from over your head? And he said, I also know. Be silent.

**2 Kings 2:4**

And Elijah said to Elisha, Stay here now, because the Lord has sent me to Jericho. And Elisha said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And they came to Jericho.

**2 Kings 2:5**

And the sons of the prophets in Jericho came near to Elisha and said to him, Do you know that today the Lord is taking your lord away from over your head? And he said, I too know. Be silent.

**2 Kings 2:6**

And Elijah said to him, Stay here now, because the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan. And Elisha said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And both went on.

**2 Kings 2:7**

And fifty men from the sons of the prophets stood opposite at a distance, and both stood by the Jordan.

**2 Kings 2:8**

And Elijah took his sheepskin cloak and rolled it up and struck the water, and the water divided here and there, and both crossed in dry land.

**2 Kings 2:9**

And it came to be when they crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha, Ask what I should do for you before I am taken up from you. And Elisha said, Let a double share of your spirit now be upon me.

**2 Kings 2:10**

And Elijah said, You made the asking hard. If you see me being taken up from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall certainly not happen.

**2 Kings 2:11**

And it came to be as they were going on and talking, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire, and they separated between the two of them, and Elijah was taken up in a storm as into heaven.

**2 Kings 2:12**

And Elisha was watching and crying out, Father, father, chariot of Israel and its horseman. And he did not see him anymore, and he seized his garments and tore them into two tearings.

**2 Kings 2:13**

And he lifted up Elijah's sheepskin cloak that fell from above upon Elisha, and Elisha returned and stood on the lip of the Jordan.

**2 Kings 2:14**

And he took Elijah's sheepskin cloak that fell from above him and struck the water, and it did not divide, and he said, Where is the God of Elijah, indeed? And he struck the waters, and they split here and there, and Elisha crossed over.

**2 Kings 2:15**

And the sons of the prophets in Jericho saw him from opposite them and said, The spirit of Elijah has come to rest upon Elisha. And they came to meet him and bowed to him to the ground.

**2 Kings 2:16**

And they said to him, Behold now, with your servants are fifty men, sons of strength. Let them go now and seek your lord, lest the Spirit of the Lord lifted him and cast him into the Jordan or onto one of the mountains or onto one of the hills. And Elisha said, You shall not send.

**2 Kings 2:17**

And they pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said, Send them. And they sent fifty men, and they sought three days and did not find him.

**2 Kings 2:18**

And they returned to him, and he was sitting in Jericho, and Elisha said, Did I not tell you, Do not go?

**2 Kings 2:19**

And the men of the city said to Elisha, Behold, the dwelling of the city is good, as my lord sees, but the waters are bad and the land barren.

**2 Kings 2:20**

And Elisha said, Take for me a new little jar and put salt there. And they brought it to him.

**2 Kings 2:21**

And Elisha went out to the outflow of the waters and threw salt there and said, Thus says the Lord: I have healed these waters. There shall no longer be from there death and barrenness.

**2 Kings 2:22**

And the waters were healed until this day, according to the word Elisha spoke.

**2 Kings 2:23**

And he went up from there to Bethel, and as he was going up on the road, little boys came out from the city and mocked him and said to him, Go up, baldhead, go up.

**2 Kings 2:24**

And he turned after them and saw them and cursed them in the name of the Lord, and behold, two bears came out of the woodland and tore apart forty-two boys from among them.

**2 Kings 2:25**

And he went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

#### Chapter 3

**2 Kings 3:1**

And Joram son of Ahab reigned in Israel in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.

**2 Kings 3:2**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, yet not like his father and not like his mother, and he removed the pillars of Baal that his father made.

**2 Kings 3:3**

Yet he clung to the sin of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin. He did not depart from it.

**2 Kings 3:4**

And Mesha king of Moab was a sheep-breeder, and in the revolt he paid back to the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand rams in wool.

**2 Kings 3:5**

And it came to be after Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the kingdom of Israel.

**2 Kings 3:6**

And King Joram went out on that day from Samaria and reviewed Israel.

**2 Kings 3:7**

And he went and sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to Moab for war? And he said, I will go up. As I am, so you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.

**2 Kings 3:8**

And he said, By what road shall I go up? And he said, By the wilderness road of Edom.

**2 Kings 3:9**

And the king of Israel and the king of Judah and the king of Edom went, and they went around by a seven-days road, and there was no water for the camp and for the cattle at their feet.

**2 Kings 3:10**

And the king of Israel said, Alas, because the Lord has called these three passing kings to give them into the hand of Moab.

**2 Kings 3:11**

And Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, and shall we seek the Lord from him? And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.

**2 Kings 3:12**

And Jehoshaphat said, The word of the Lord is with him. And the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah and the king of Edom went down to him.

**2 Kings 3:13**

And Elisha said to the king of Israel, What is to me and to you? Go to the prophets of your father. And the king of Israel said to him, No, because the Lord has called these three kings to hand them over into the hands of Moab.

**2 Kings 3:14**

And Elisha said, As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, unless I regarded the face of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look toward you or see you.

**2 Kings 3:15**

And now bring me a musician. And it came to be, as the musician played, the hand of the Lord came upon him.

**2 Kings 3:16**

And he said, Thus says the Lord: Make this wadi pits, pits.

**2 Kings 3:17**

For thus says the Lord: You will not see wind and you will not see rain, and this wadi will be filled with water, and you will drink, you and your possessions and your cattle.

**2 Kings 3:18**

And this is light in the eyes of the Lord, and I will hand Moab over into your hand.

**2 Kings 3:19**

And you will strike every fortified city, and you will bring down every good tree, and you will stop up all springs of water, and every good tract you will spoil with stones.

**2 Kings 3:20**

And it came to be in the morning, as the sacrifice was going up, behold, waters were coming by the road of Edom, and the land was filled with water.

**2 Kings 3:21**

And all Moab heard that the kings had gone up to fight them, and they cried out from everyone girding on a belt and upward, and they stood at the border.

**2 Kings 3:22**

And they rose early in the morning, and the sun rose upon the waters, and Moab saw opposite them the waters red like blood.

**2 Kings 3:23**

And they said, This is blood of the sword. The kings fought and struck each man his neighbor. And now, Moab, to the spoils!

**2 Kings 3:24**

And they entered into the camp of Israel, and Israel rose and struck Moab, and they fled from before them, and they entered, going in and striking Moab.

**2 Kings 3:25**

And they tore down the cities, and on every good tract each man threw his stone and filled it, and they stopped up every spring of water and brought down every good tree until they left only the wall-stones of Kirharaseth torn down. And the slingers encircled it and struck it.

**2 Kings 3:26**

And the king of Moab saw that the battle had grown too strong against him, and he took with himself seven hundred men drawing sword to break through to the king of Edom, and they were not able.

**2 Kings 3:27**

And he took his firstborn son, who would reign in his place, and offered him as a whole burnt offering upon the wall, and great regret came upon Israel, and they withdrew from him and returned to the land.

#### Chapter 4

**2 Kings 4:1**

And one woman from the sons of the prophets cried to Elisha, saying, Your servant, my husband, has died, and you knew that your servant was fearing the Lord, and the creditor has come to take my two sons for himself as slaves.

**2 Kings 4:2**

And Elisha said, What shall I do for you? Tell me what you have in the house. And she said, There is nothing for your servant in the house except oil for anointing.

**2 Kings 4:3**

And he said to her, Go, ask for yourself vessels from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels. Do not make them few.

**2 Kings 4:4**

And you will go in and shut the door on yourself and on your sons, and you will pour into these vessels, and the filled one you will lift away.

**2 Kings 4:5**

And she went from him and did so, and she shut the door on herself and on her sons. They kept bringing the vessels near to her, and she kept pouring.

**2 Kings 4:6**

Until the vessels were filled, and she said to her sons, Bring another vessel near to me. And they said to her, There is no more vessel. And the oil stood still.

**2 Kings 4:7**

And she came and reported to the man of God, and Elisha said, Go and sell the oil and pay your interest, and you and your sons will live on the remaining oil.

**2 Kings 4:8**

And it came to be one day Elisha passed through to Shunem, and there was a great woman there, and she constrained him to eat bread. And it came to be, as often as he went in, he turned aside there to eat.

**2 Kings 4:9**

And the woman said to her husband, Behold now, I know that this one who continually passes over us is a holy man of God.

**2 Kings 4:10**

Let us make for him a little upper-room place, and let us put there for him a bed and a table and a chair and a lampstand, and it shall be, when he comes in to us, he will turn in there.

**2 Kings 4:11**

And it came to be one day, he went in there and turned in to the upper room and slept there.

**2 Kings 4:12**

And he said to Gehazi his servant-boy, Call this Shunammite for me. And he called her, and she stood before him.

**2 Kings 4:13**

And he said to him, Say now to her, Behold, you have stirred up for us all this concern. What needs to be done for you? Is there a word for you to the king or to the commander of the force? And she said, I dwell in the midst of my people.

**2 Kings 4:14**

And he said, What needs to be done for her? And Gehazi his servant-boy said, Truly she has no son, and her husband is old.

**2 Kings 4:15**

And he called her, and she stood by the door.

**2 Kings 4:16**

And Elisha said to her, At this time, as the living season returns, you will be embracing a son. And she said, No, my lord, do not lie to your servant.

**2 Kings 4:17**

And the woman conceived and bore a son at this time, as the living season returned, just as Elisha spoke to her.

**2 Kings 4:18**

And the boy grew strong, and it came to be when the boy went out to his father, to the reapers.

**2 Kings 4:19**

And he said to his father, My head, my head. And he said to the servant-boy, Carry him to his mother.

**2 Kings 4:20**

And he carried him to his mother, and he lay on her knees until midday and died.

**2 Kings 4:21**

And she brought him up and laid him on the bed of the man of God and shut the door upon him and went out.

**2 Kings 4:22**

And she called her husband and said, Send me now one of the servant-boys and one of the donkeys, and I will run as far as the man of God and return.

**2 Kings 4:23**

And he said, Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath. And she said, Peace.

**2 Kings 4:24**

And she saddled the donkey and said to her servant-boy, Lead on. Do not slow my riding unless I tell you.

**2 Kings 4:25**

So she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. And it came to be when Elisha saw her coming, he said to Gehazi his servant-boy, Behold now, that Shunammite.

**2 Kings 4:26**

Now run to meet her and say, Is there peace for you? Is there peace for your husband? Is there peace for the boy? And she said, Peace.

**2 Kings 4:27**

And she came to Elisha at the mountain and seized his feet, and Gehazi came near to push her away, and Elisha said, Leave her, because her soul is bitter within her, and the Lord hid it from me and did not tell me.

**2 Kings 4:28**

And she said, Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say, Do not mislead me?

**2 Kings 4:29**

And Elisha said to Gehazi, Gird your waist and take my staff in your hand and go, because if you meet a man you shall not bless him, and if a man blesses you, you shall not answer him, and you shall put my staff on the face of the boy.

**2 Kings 4:30**

And the mother of the boy said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. And Elisha rose and went after her.

**2 Kings 4:31**

And Gehazi passed before her and placed the staff on the face of the boy, but there was no voice and there was no hearing, and he returned to meet him and reported to him, saying, The boy did not wake up.

**2 Kings 4:32**

And Elisha entered into the house, and behold, the boy was dead, laid on his bed.

**2 Kings 4:33**

And Elisha went into the house and shut the door upon the two of them and prayed to the Lord.

**2 Kings 4:34**
