And he went up and lay upon the boy and put his mouth on his mouth and his eyes on his eyes and his hands on his hands and bent himself over him, and the flesh of the boy grew warm.

**2 Kings 4:35**

And he turned and walked in the house here and there and went up and bent himself over the boy until seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.

**2 Kings 4:36**

And Elisha cried out to Gehazi and said, Call this Shunammite. And he called her, and she came in to him, and Elisha said, Take your son.

**2 Kings 4:37**

And the woman came in and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground, and she took her son and went out.

**2 Kings 4:38**

And Elisha returned to Gilgal, and famine was in the land, and the sons of the prophets sat before him, and Elisha said to his servant-boy, Set on the great pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.

**2 Kings 4:39**

And one went out into the field to gather herbs and found a vine in the field and gathered from it wild gourds, his garment full, and put them into the pot of stew, because they did not know them.

**2 Kings 4:40**

And they poured it out for the men to eat, and it came to be while they were eating from the stew, behold, they cried out and said, Death in the pot, man of God, and they were not able to eat.

**2 Kings 4:41**

And he said, Take flour and throw it into the pot. And Elisha said to Gehazi the servant-boy, Pour out to the people and let them eat. And there was no longer any evil thing in the pot.

**2 Kings 4:42**

And a man came from Baalshalisha and brought to the man of God firstfruits, twenty barley loaves and fresh ears in a sack, and he said, Give to the people and let them eat.

**2 Kings 4:43**

And his attendant said, What shall I give this before one hundred men? And he said, Give to the people and let them eat, because thus says the Lord: They will eat and leave some.

**2 Kings 4:44**

And they ate and left some, according to the word of the Lord.

#### Chapter 5

**2 Kings 5:1**

And Naaman, commander of the force of Syria, was a great man before his lord and honored in face, because through him the Lord gave salvation to Syria; and the man was mighty in strength, afflicted with skin-disease.

**2 Kings 5:2**

And Syria had gone out in raiding bands and taken captive from the land of Israel a small young girl, and she was before the wife of Naaman.

**2 Kings 5:3**

And she said to her mistress, If only my lord were before the prophet of God in Samaria. Then he would remove him from his skin-disease.

**2 Kings 5:4**

And he went in and reported to his lord, saying, Thus and thus spoke the young girl from the land of Israel.

**2 Kings 5:5**

And the king of Syria said to Naaman, Come, go in, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel. And he went and took in his hand ten talents of silver and six thousand pieces of gold and ten changes of garments.

**2 Kings 5:6**

And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, And now, when this letter comes to you, behold, I have sent to you Naaman my servant, and you shall remove him from his skin-disease.

**2 Kings 5:7**

And it came to be, when the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his garments and said, Am I God, to kill and make alive, that this man sends to me to remove a man from his skin-disease? Only recognize now and see that he is seeking a pretext against me.

**2 Kings 5:8**

And it came to be, when Elisha heard that the king of Israel tore his garments, he sent to the king of Israel, saying, Why have you torn your garments? Let Naaman now come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel.

**2 Kings 5:9**

And Naaman came with horse and chariot and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.

**2 Kings 5:10**

And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, Go, wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will return to you, and you will be cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:11**

And Naaman grew angry and went away and said, Behold, I said to myself that he would surely come out to me and stand and call on the name of his God and put his hand on the place and remove the skin-diseased part.

**2 Kings 5:12**

Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than the Jordan and all the waters of Israel? If I go and wash in them, will I not be cleansed? And he turned aside and went away in anger.

**2 Kings 5:13**

And his servants came near and spoke to him, saying, Father, if the prophet had spoken a great word to you, would you not do it? How much more when he said to you, Wash and be cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:14**

And Naaman went down and immersed himself in the Jordan seven times according to the word of Elisha, and his flesh returned like the flesh of a small boy, and he was cleansed.

**2 Kings 5:15**

And he returned to Elisha, he and all his camp, and came and stood and said, Behold now, I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. And now take a blessing from your servant.

**2 Kings 5:16**

And Elisha said, As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not take it. And he pressed him to take it, but he refused.

**2 Kings 5:17**

And Naaman said, If not, then let there be given to your servant a load of red earth, as much as a pair of mules can carry, for your servant will no longer make whole-burnt-offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to the Lord.

**2 Kings 5:18**

In this matter may the Lord be merciful to your servant: when my lord enters the house of Rimmon to bow there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow in the house of Rimmon, when I bow in the house of Rimmon, may the Lord be merciful to your servant in this matter.

**2 Kings 5:19**

And Elisha said to Naaman, Go in peace. And he went away from him a short stretch of land.

**2 Kings 5:20**

And Gehazi, the servant-boy of Elisha, said, Behold, my lord spared this Naaman the Syrian by not taking from his hand what he brought. As the Lord lives, unless I run after him and take something from him.

**2 Kings 5:21**

And Gehazi pursued after Naaman, and Naaman saw him running after him and turned back from the chariot to meet him.

**2 Kings 5:22**

And he said, Peace. My lord has sent me, saying, Behold, now two servant-boys have come to me from the hill-country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of garments.

**2 Kings 5:23**

And Naaman said, Take two talents of silver. And he bound them in two bags, with two changes of garments, and gave them to two of his servant-boys, and they carried them before him.

**2 Kings 5:24**

And they came to the hidden place, and he took them from their hands and stored them in the house and sent the men away.

**2 Kings 5:25**

And he himself went in and stood by his lord. And Elisha said to him, Where have you come from, Gehazi? And Gehazi said, Your servant did not go here or there.

**2 Kings 5:26**

And Elisha said to him, Did not my heart go with you when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Is now the time to take silver and to take garments and olive-groves and vineyards and sheep and cattle and male servants and female servants?

**2 Kings 5:27**

And the skin-disease of Naaman will cling to you and to your seed forever. And he went out from before him afflicted with skin-disease like snow.

#### Chapter 6

**2 Kings 6:1**

And the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, Behold now, the place where we dwell before you is too narrow for us.

**2 Kings 6:2**

Let us go now as far as the Jordan, and let each man take from there one beam, and let us make for ourselves there a place to dwell there. And he said, Go.

**2 Kings 6:3**

And one said, Please come with your servants. And he said, I will go.

**2 Kings 6:4**

And he went with them. And they came to the Jordan and were cutting the wood.

**2 Kings 6:5**

And behold, one was felling the beam, and the iron fell into the water, and he cried out, Alas, master, and it was borrowed.

**2 Kings 6:6**

And the man of God said, Where did it fall? And he showed him the place, and he cut off a stick and threw it there, and the iron floated.

**2 Kings 6:7**

And he said, Lift it up for yourself. And he stretched out his hand and took it.

**2 Kings 6:8**

And the king of Syria was warring against Israel and consulted with his servants, saying, At such and such a place I will encamp.

**2 Kings 6:9**

And Elisha sent to the king of Israel, saying, Beware of passing by this place, because Syria is hidden there.

**2 Kings 6:10**

And the king of Israel sent to the place of which Elisha spoke to him and was on guard there, not once nor twice.

**2 Kings 6:11**

And the soul of the king of Syria was thrown into confusion over this matter, and he called his servants and said to them, Will you not tell me who is betraying me to the king of Israel?

**2 Kings 6:12**

And one of his servants said, No, my lord king. Rather Elisha the prophet in Israel tells the king of Israel all the words that you speak in the chamber of your bed.

**2 Kings 6:13**

And he said, Come, see where this man is, and I will send and take him. And they reported to him, saying, Behold, he is in Dothan.

**2 Kings 6:14**

And he sent there horse and chariot and a heavy force, and they came by night and surrounded the city.

**2 Kings 6:15**

And the servant of Elisha rose early and went out, and behold, a force was surrounding the city, with horse and chariot. And the servant-boy said to him, Alas, master, what shall we do?

**2 Kings 6:16**

And Elisha said, Do not fear, because those with us are more than those with them.

**2 Kings 6:17**

And Elisha prayed and said, Lord, open the eyes of the servant-boy and let him see. And the Lord opened his eyes, and he saw, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha.

**2 Kings 6:18**

And they came down toward him, and Elisha prayed to the Lord and said, Strike this nation with blindness now. And he struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.

**2 Kings 6:19**

And Elisha said to them, This is not the city, and this is not the way. Come after me, and I will lead you to the man whom you seek. And he led them into Samaria.

**2 Kings 6:20**

And it came to be, when they entered Samaria, Elisha said, Lord, open now their eyes and let them see. And the Lord opened their eyes and they saw, and behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.

**2 Kings 6:21**

And the king of Israel said, when he saw them, Shall I strike them down, father? Shall I strike them down?

**2 Kings 6:22**

And he said, You shall not strike them down. Would you strike down those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink and go to their lord.

**2 Kings 6:23**

And he set before them a great feast, and they ate and drank, and he sent them away, and they went to their lord. And raiding bands of Syria did not continue to come into the land of Israel.

**2 Kings 6:24**

And it came to be after this that Ben-hadad king of Syria gathered all his camp and went up and besieged Samaria.

**2 Kings 6:25**

And there was a great famine in Samaria, and behold, they besieged it until a donkey's head was fifty shekels of silver and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung was five shekels of silver.

**2 Kings 6:26**

And the king of Israel was passing over the wall, and a woman cried to him, saying, Save, my lord king.

**2 Kings 6:27**

And he said to her, If the Lord does not save you, from where shall I save you? From the threshing floor or from the winepress?

**2 Kings 6:28**

And the king said to her, What troubles you? And the woman said, This woman said to me, Give your son, and let us eat him today, and my son we will eat tomorrow.

**2 Kings 6:29**

And we boiled my son and ate him, and I said to her on the second day, Give your son and let us eat him, and she hid her son.

**2 Kings 6:30**

And it came to be, when the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his garments. And he was passing over the wall, and the people saw the sackcloth on his flesh within.

**2 Kings 6:31**

And he said, Thus may God do to me and thus may he add, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today.

**2 Kings 6:32**

And Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him, and the king sent a man from before him. Before the messenger came to him, Elisha said to the elders, Do you see that this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? See, when the messenger comes, shut the door and press him at the door. Is not the sound of the feet of his lord behind him?

**2 Kings 6:33**

While he was still speaking with them, behold, the messenger came down to him and said, Behold, this evil is from the Lord. Why should I wait for the Lord any longer?

#### Chapter 7

**2 Kings 7:1**

And Elisha said, Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: At this time tomorrow a measure of fine flour will be a shekel, and two measures of barley a shekel, at the gates of Samaria.

**2 Kings 7:2**

And the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered Elisha and said, Behold, if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, can this thing be? And Elisha said, Behold, you will see with your eyes, but from there you will not eat.

**2 Kings 7:3**

And four men afflicted with skin-disease were beside the gate of the city. And one man said to his neighbor, Why do we sit here until we die?

**2 Kings 7:4**

If we say, Let us enter the city, the famine is in the city, and we will die there. And if we sit here, we will die. And now come, let us fall into the camp of Syria. If they keep us alive, we will live; and if they put us to death, we will die.

**2 Kings 7:5**

And they rose in the dark to enter the camp of Syria and came to the edge of the camp of Syria, and behold, no man was there.

**2 Kings 7:6**

For the Lord had made the camp of Syria hear a sound of chariot and a sound of horse and a sound of great force, and one man said to his brother, Behold now, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us.

**2 Kings 7:7**

And they rose and fled in the dark and abandoned their tents and their horses and their donkeys, the camp just as it was, and fled for their own life.

**2 Kings 7:8**

And these men afflicted with skin-disease came to the edge of the camp and entered one tent and ate and drank and took from there silver and gold and clothing and went and hid them. And they returned and entered another tent and took from there and went and hid them.

**2 Kings 7:9**

And one man said to his neighbor, We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until the morning light, lawlessness will find us. And now come, let us go in and report to the house of the king.

**2 Kings 7:10**

And they went in and cried out to the gate of the city and reported to them, saying, We entered the camp of Syria, and behold, no man was there and no human voice, only horses tied and donkeys and the tents just as they were.

**2 Kings 7:11**

And the gatekeepers cried out and reported it inside the house of the king.

**2 Kings 7:12**

And the king rose by night and said to his servants, Let me now tell you what Syria has done to us. They know that we are hungry, and they went out from the camp and hid themselves in the field, saying, When they come out from the city, we will seize them alive and enter the city.

**2 Kings 7:13**

And one of his servants answered and said, Let them take now five of the horses left, which were left here. Behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel that has come to an end. Let us send and see.

**2 Kings 7:14**

And they took two mounted horsemen, and the king of Israel sent them after the king of Syria, saying, Go and see.

**2 Kings 7:15**

And they went after them as far as the Jordan, and behold, all the road was full of garments and vessels which Syria threw away in their panic. And the messengers returned and reported to the king.

**2 Kings 7:16**

And the people went out and plundered the camp of Syria. And a measure of fine flour became a shekel, and two measures of barley a shekel, according to the word of the Lord.

**2 Kings 7:17**

And the king had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned over the gate, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God spoke when the king came down to him.

**2 Kings 7:18**

And it came to be just as Elisha had spoken to the king, saying, Two measures of barley a shekel and a measure of fine flour a shekel will be at this time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria.

**2 Kings 7:19**

And the officer answered Elisha and said, Behold, if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, can this thing be? And Elisha said, Behold, you will see with your eyes, but from there you will not eat.

**2 Kings 7:20**

And so it happened to him, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

#### Chapter 8

**2 Kings 8:1**

And Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he restored to life, saying, Rise and go, you and your house, and sojourn where you may sojourn, because the Lord has called for famine upon the land, and it has come upon the land seven years.

**2 Kings 8:2**

And the woman rose and did according to the word of Elisha, and she and her house went and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.

**2 Kings 8:3**

And it came to be at the end of seven years that the woman returned from the land of the Philistines to the city, and she came to cry to the king concerning her house and concerning her fields.

**2 Kings 8:4**

And the king was speaking to Gehazi the servant-boy of Elisha, the man of God, saying, Tell me now all the great things Elisha did.

**2 Kings 8:5**

And it came to be, while he was recounting to the king how Elisha restored a dead son to life, behold, the woman whose son Elisha restored to life cried to the king concerning her house and her fields. And Gehazi said, My lord king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.

**2 Kings 8:6**

And the king asked the woman, and she recounted it to him. And the king gave her one eunuch, saying, Restore all that was hers and all the produce of her field from the day she left the land until now.

**2 Kings 8:7**

And Elisha came to Damascus, and Ben-hadad king of Syria was sick. And they reported to him, saying, The man of God has come here.

**2 Kings 8:8**

And the king said to Hazael, Take in your hand a gift, and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the Lord through him, saying, Shall I live from this sickness of mine?

**2 Kings 8:9**

And Hazael went to meet him and took in his hand a gift, even every good thing of Damascus, a load of forty camels, and came and stood before him and said to Elisha, Your son Ben-hadad king of Syria has sent me to you, saying, Shall I live from this sickness?

**2 Kings 8:10**

And Elisha said, Go, say to him, You will surely live, yet the Lord has shown me that he will surely die.

**2 Kings 8:11**

And he fixed his face and held it until shame, and the man of God wept.

**2 Kings 8:12**

And Hazael said, Why does my lord weep? And he said, Because I know what evils you will do to the sons of Israel. You will send their strongholds into fire, and their chosen men you will kill with the sword, and their infants you will dash, and their pregnant women you will rip open.

**2 Kings 8:13**

And Hazael said, What is your servant, this dead dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha said, The Lord has shown me you as king over Syria.

**2 Kings 8:14**

And he went from Elisha and entered to his lord, and he said to him, What did Elisha say to you? And he said, He said to me, You will surely live.

**2 Kings 8:15**

And it came to be on the next day that he took a coverlet and dipped it in water and spread it over his face, and he died. And Hazael reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 8:16**

In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king, king of Judah.

**2 Kings 8:17**

He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 8:18**

And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, because the daughter of Ahab was his wife, and he did evil before the Lord.

**2 Kings 8:19**

Yet the Lord did not wish to destroy Judah because of David his servant, as he said to give him a lamp and to his sons all the days.

**2 Kings 8:20**

In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah and made a king reign over themselves.

**2 Kings 8:21**

And Joram went over to Zair, and all the chariots with him. And it came to be, when he rose by night, he struck Edom that had encircled him and the commanders of the chariots, and the people fled to their tents.

**2 Kings 8:22**

And Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah until this day. Then Libnah rebelled at that time.

**2 Kings 8:23**

And the rest of the words of Joram and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 8:24**

And Joram slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 8:25**

In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Joram became king.

**2 Kings 8:26**

Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And the name of his mother was Athaliah, daughter of Omri king of Israel.

**2 Kings 8:27**

And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did evil before the Lord, like the house of Ahab.

**2 Kings 8:28**

And he went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead, and the Syrians struck Joram.

**2 Kings 8:29**

And King Joram returned to be healed in Jezreel from the wounds which they struck him at Ramoth when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah son of Joram went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was ill.

#### Chapter 9

**2 Kings 9:1**

And Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, Gird your loins and take this flask of oil in your hand and go to Ramoth Gilead.

**2 Kings 9:2**

And you will enter there and see there Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi, and you will go in and raise him up from the midst of his brothers and bring him into an inner room within a room.

**2 Kings 9:3**

Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed you as king over Israel. And you will open the door and flee and not stay.

**2 Kings 9:4**

And the servant-boy, the prophet, went to Ramoth Gilead.

**2 Kings 9:5**

And he entered, and behold, the commanders of the force were sitting, and he said, I have a word for you, commander. And Jehu said, For which one among all of us? And he said, For you, commander.

**2 Kings 9:6**

And he rose and entered the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel, I have anointed you as king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.

**2 Kings 9:7**

And you shall destroy the house of Ahab your lord, and I will avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the Lord from the hand of Jezebel.

**2 Kings 9:8**

And I will cut off from the house of Ahab everyone who urinates against a wall, and one held fast and left behind in Israel.

**2 Kings 9:9**

And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.

**2 Kings 9:10**

And the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there is none who buries. And he opened the door and fled.

**2 Kings 9:11**

And Jehu went out to the servants of his lord, and they said to him, Is all well? Why did this madman come to you? And he said to them, You know the man and his rambling.

**2 Kings 9:12**

And they said, It is false. Tell us now. And he said to them, Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying, Thus says the Lord, I have anointed you as king over Israel.

**2 Kings 9:13**

And hearing, they hurried, and each took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps, and they blew on a horn and said, Jehu reigns.

**2 Kings 9:14**

And Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. And Joram himself had been guarding Ramoth Gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Syria.

**2 Kings 9:15**

And Joram the king returned to be healed in Jezreel from the wounds with which the Syrians struck him when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Jehu said, If your soul is with me, let none escape from the city to go and report in Jezreel.

**2 Kings 9:16**

And Jehu mounted and went to Jezreel, because Joram was being healed there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.

**2 Kings 9:17**

And the watchman stood on the tower in Jezreel and saw the dust of Jehu as he came and said, I see dust. And Joram said, Take a rider and send him before them, and let him say, Is it peace?

**2 Kings 9:18**

And a horseman went to meet them and said, Thus says the king, Is it peace? And Jehu said, What is peace to you? Turn behind me. And the watchman reported, saying, The messenger came to them and did not return.

**2 Kings 9:19**

And he sent a second horseman, and he came to him and said, Thus says the king, Is it peace? And Jehu said, What is peace to you? Turn behind me.

**2 Kings 9:20**

And the watchman reported, saying, He came to them and did not return, and the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, because he drives furiously.

**2 Kings 9:21**

And Joram said, Harness. And they harnessed his chariot, and Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, to meet Jehu, and they found him in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite.

**2 Kings 9:22**

And it came to be, when Joram saw Jehu, he said, Is it peace, Jehu? And Jehu said, What peace, while the whoredoms of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries remain?

**2 Kings 9:23**

And Joram turned his hands to flee and said to Ahaziah, Treachery, Ahaziah!

**2 Kings 9:24**

And Jehu filled his hand with the bow and struck Joram between his arms, and the arrow went out through his heart, and he bent upon his knees.

**2 Kings 9:25**

And Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, Lift him and throw him into the portion of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite, because I remember, I and you riding on pairs behind Ahab his father, and the Lord took up this burden against him, saying,

**2 Kings 9:26**

Surely the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons I saw yesterday, says the Lord, and I will repay him in this portion, says the Lord. And now lift him and throw him into the portion according to the word of the Lord.

**2 Kings 9:27**

And Ahaziah king of Judah saw and fled by way of Baithaggan, and Jehu pursued after him and said, Strike him too. And they struck him in the chariot at the ascent of Gur, which is Ibleam, and he fled to Megiddo and died there.

**2 Kings 9:28**

And his servants set him on the chariot and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb in the city of David.

**2 Kings 9:29**

And in the eleventh year of Joram king of Israel, Ahaziah reigned over Judah.

**2 Kings 9:30**

And Jehu came to Jezreel, and Jezebel heard and painted her eyes and adorned her head and looked out through the window.

**2 Kings 9:31**

And as Jehu was entering the city, she said, Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his lord?

**2 Kings 9:32**

And he lifted his face to the window and saw her and said, Who are you? Come down with me. And two eunuchs looked down toward him.

**2 Kings 9:33**

And he said, Roll her down. And they rolled her down, and some of her blood was spattered on the wall and on the horses, and they trampled her.

**2 Kings 9:34**

And he entered and ate and drank and said, See now to this cursed woman and bury her, because she is a king's daughter.

**2 Kings 9:35**

And they went to bury her and found nothing of her except the skull and the feet and the palms of the hands.

**2 Kings 9:36**

And they returned and reported to him, and he said, This is the word of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel the dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel.

**2 Kings 9:37**

And corpse of Jezebel will be like dung on the face of the field in the portion of Jezreel, so that they cannot say, This is Jezebel.

#### Chapter 10

**2 Kings 10:1**

And Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote a letter and sent it into Samaria to the rulers of Samaria and to the elders and to the guardians of the sons of Ahab, saying,

**2 Kings 10:2**

And now when this letter comes to you, with you are the sons of your lord, and with you are the chariot and horses and fortified cities and weapons.

**2 Kings 10:3**

And you will look for the good and upright among the sons of your lord and set him on the throne of his father, and fight for the house of your lord.

**2 Kings 10:4**

And they feared greatly and said, Behold, the two kings did not stand before him, and how shall we stand?

**2 Kings 10:5**

And those over the house and those over the city and the elders and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, We are your servants, and whatever you say to us we will do. We will not make any man king. Do what is good in your eyes.

**2 Kings 10:6**

And he wrote to them a second letter, saying, If you are for me and obey my voice, take the heads of the men, the sons of your lord, and bring them to me at this time tomorrow in Jezreel. And the sons of the king, seventy men, were with the great men of the city, those rearing them.

**2 Kings 10:7**

And it came to be, when the letter came to them, they took the sons of the king and slaughtered them, seventy men, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him in Jezreel.

**2 Kings 10:8**

And the messenger came and reported, saying, They brought the heads of the sons of the king. And he said, Put them in two heaps by the doorway of the gate until morning.

**2 Kings 10:9**

And it came to be in the morning, he went out and stood in the gate of the city and said to all the people, You are righteous. Behold, I conspired against my lord and killed him, but who struck all these?

**2 Kings 10:10**

Know now that not one thing from the word of the Lord will fall to the ground, which the Lord spoke against the house of Ahab. And the Lord has done what he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah.

**2 Kings 10:11**

And Jehu struck all those left of the house of Ahab in Jezreel and all his great men and his acquaintances and his priests until he left him no remnant.

**2 Kings 10:12**

And he rose and went to Samaria, he at Beth-eked of the shepherds on the way.

**2 Kings 10:13**

And Jehu found the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, Who are you? And they said, We are brothers of Ahaziah, and we came down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the ruling lady.

**2 Kings 10:14**

And he said, Seize them alive. And they seized them alive and slaughtered them at Beth-eked, forty-two men. He left not a man from among them.

**2 Kings 10:15**

And he went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab on the way to meet him and blessed him and said to him, Is your heart straight with my heart, as my heart is with your heart? And Jehonadab said, It is. And Jehu said, If it is, give your hand. And he gave his hand, and he took him up to himself into the chariot.

**2 Kings 10:16**

And he said to him, Come with me and see in my zeal for the Lord of hosts. And he seated him in his chariot.

**2 Kings 10:17**

And he entered Samaria and struck all those left to Ahab in Samaria until destroying him, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke to Elijah.

**2 Kings 10:18**

And Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.

**2 Kings 10:19**

And now call to me all the prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests. Let not a man be overlooked, because I have a great sacrifice for Baal. Everyone who is overlooked will not live. And Jehu did it in deception, in order to destroy the servants of Baal.

**2 Kings 10:20**

And Jehu said, Sanctify a festival for Baal. And they proclaimed it.

**2 Kings 10:21**

And Jehu sent through all Israel, and all the servants of Baal and all his priests and all his prophets came. No one was left out who did not come. And they entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from mouth to mouth.

**2 Kings 10:22**

And Jehu said to the one over the wardrobe, Bring out garments for all the servants of Baal. And the dresser brought out garments for them.

**2 Kings 10:23**

And Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab entered the house of Baal and said to the servants of Baal, Search and see whether there is with you any of the servants of the Lord, because only the servants of Baal are here.

**2 Kings 10:24**

And they went in to offer the sacrifices and whole-burnt-offerings. And Jehu stationed for himself outside eighty men and said, The man who lets escape any from the men whom I bring into your hands, his life will be for that man's life.

**2 Kings 10:25**

And it came to be, when he finished offering the whole-burnt-offering, Jehu said to the runners and to the officers, Go in and strike them down. Let not a man come out. And they struck them with the edge of the sword, and the runners and the officers cast them out and went into the inner city of the house of Baal.

**2 Kings 10:26**

And they brought out the pillar of Baal and burned it.

**2 Kings 10:27**

And they tore down the pillars of Baal and demolished the house of Baal and made it latrines to this day.

**2 Kings 10:28**

And Jehu destroyed Baal from Israel.

**2 Kings 10:29**

Only, from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, Jehu did not turn away from after them, the golden calves in Bethel and in Dan.

**2 Kings 10:30**

And the Lord said to Jehu, Because you did well in doing what was right in my eyes and did to the house of Ahab all that was in my heart, fourth sons will sit for you on the throne of Israel.

**2 Kings 10:31**

And Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart. He did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.

**2 Kings 10:32**

In those days the Lord began to cut away in Israel, and Hazael struck them in every border of Israel,

**2 Kings 10:33**

from the Jordan toward sunrise, all the land of Gilead, of Gad and of Reuben and of Manasseh, from Aroer, which is on the lip of the wadi Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.

**2 Kings 10:34**

And the rest of the words of Jehu and all that he did and all his might, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 10:35**

And Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 10:36**

And the days which Jehu reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years in Samaria.

#### Chapter 11

**2 Kings 11:1**

And Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her sons were dead, and she destroyed all the royal seed.

**2 Kings 11:2**

And Iosabee daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of her brother and stole him from the midst of the sons of the king being put to death, him and his nurse, into the bedchamber, and hid him from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.

**2 Kings 11:3**

And he was with her hidden in the house of the Lord six years, while Athaliah was reigning over the land.

**2 Kings 11:4**

And in the seventh year Jehoiada the priest sent and took the centurions over the captains and the guard, and brought them to himself into the house of the Lord and made a covenant with them before the Lord and made them swear and showed them the king's son.

**2 Kings 11:5**

And he commanded them, saying, This is the word that you shall do: a third of you, those entering on the Sabbath, shall keep watch of the king's house at the gate.

**2 Kings 11:6**

And a third at the gate of the roads and a third at the gate behind the runners, and you shall keep the watch of the house.

**2 Kings 11:7**

And two divisions among you, all going out on the Sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the Lord for the king.

**2 Kings 11:8**

And surround the king all around, each man with his weapon in his hand, and the one entering within the ranks shall die. And be with the king in his going out and in his coming in.

**2 Kings 11:9**

And the centurions did all that Jehoiada the priest commanded, and each man took his men, those entering on the Sabbath along with those going out on the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.

**2 Kings 11:10**

And the priest gave to the centurions King David's spears and shields, those in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 11:11**

And the runners stood, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and the house, around the king.

**2 Kings 11:12**

And he brought out the king's son and put on him the crown and the testimony and made him king and anointed him, and they clapped with the hand and said, Let the king live.

**2 Kings 11:13**

And Athaliah heard the sound of the runners of the people and entered to the people in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 11:14**

And she saw, and behold, the king was standing by the pillar according to the custom, and the singers and the trumpets were by the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing with trumpets. And Athaliah tore her garments and cried, Conspiracy, conspiracy!

**2 Kings 11:15**

And Jehoiada the priest commanded the centurions, the officers of the force, and said to them, Bring her out from within the ranks, and whoever enters after her shall certainly be put to death by the sword, because the priest said, Let her not die in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 11:16**

And they laid hands on her, and she went by way of the horse entrance of the king's house, and she died there.

**2 Kings 11:17**

And Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that they should be a people to the Lord, and between the king and the people.

**2 Kings 11:18**

And all the people of the land entered the house of Baal and tore it down, and his altars and his images they broke well, and Matthan priest of Baal they killed before the altars. And the priest set overseers over the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 11:19**

And he took the centurions and the captains and the guard and all the people of the land and brought the king down from the house of the Lord and entered by way of the gate of the runners to the king's house, and they seated him on the throne of the kings.

**2 Kings 11:20**

And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, and they put Athaliah to death by the sword in the king's house.

#### Chapter 12

**2 Kings 12:1**

Joash was seven years old when he became king.

**2 Kings 12:2**

In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Abijah from Beersheba.

**2 Kings 12:3**

And Joash did what was right before the Lord all the days in which Jehoiada the priest instructed him.

**2 Kings 12:4**

Only, the high places were not removed, and there the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

**2 Kings 12:5**

And Joash said to the priests, All the silver of the holy things brought into the house of the Lord, silver of assessment, a man's silver from assessed value, every silver that comes up upon a man's heart to bring into the house of the Lord,

**2 Kings 12:6**

let the priests take it for themselves, each from his collection, and they themselves shall repair the breach of the house wherever any breach is found there.

**2 Kings 12:7**

And it came to be in the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the breach of the house.

**2 Kings 12:8**

And King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the priests and said to them, Why is it that you do not repair the breach of the house? And now do not take silver from your collections, because you will give it for the breach of the house.

**2 Kings 12:9**

And the priests agreed not to take silver from the people and not to repair the breach of the house.

**2 Kings 12:10**

And Jehoiada the priest took one chest and bored a hole in its lid and set it beside the altar, at the right side as a man enters the house of the Lord. And the priests keeping the threshold put there all the silver found in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 12:11**

And it came to be, when they saw that there was much silver in the chest, the king's scribe and the high priest went up and tied and counted the silver found in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 12:12**

And they gave the silver, weighed out, into the hands of those doing the works, the overseers of the house of the Lord, and they spent it on the carpenters of wood and on the builders doing work in the house of the Lord,

**2 Kings 12:13**

and on the masons and on the stonecutters to buy timber and quarried stones to hold together the breach of the house of the Lord, for everything laid out on the house to strengthen it.

**2 Kings 12:14**

Only, there were not made for the house of the Lord silver bowls, snuffers, basins, trumpets, any vessel of gold or vessel of silver, from the silver brought into the house of the Lord,

**2 Kings 12:15**

because they would give it to those doing the works, and they strengthened with it the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 12:16**

And they did not reckon with the men into whose hands they gave the silver to give to those doing the works, because they acted in faithfulness.

**2 Kings 12:17**

Silver for sin and silver for trespass, whatever was brought into the house of the Lord, became the priests'.

**2 Kings 12:18**

Then Hazael king of Syria went up and fought against Gath and took it, and Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 12:19**

And Joash king of Judah took all the holy things that Jehoshaphat and Joram and Ahaziah his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own holy things and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and sent them to Hazael king of Syria, and he went up away from Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 12:20**

And the rest of the words of Joash and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 12:21**

And his servants rose and bound a conspiracy and struck Joash at the house Mallo in Gaalla.

**2 Kings 12:22**

And Iezichar son of Iemouath and Iezebouth his servant, son of Shomer, struck him, and he died. And they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

#### Chapter 13

**2 Kings 13:1**

In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu reigned in Samaria seventeen years.

**2 Kings 13:2**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord and went after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin. He did not depart from them.

**2 Kings 13:3**

And the Lord grew angry in wrath against Israel and gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria and into the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael all the days.

**2 Kings 13:4**

And Jehoahaz entreated the face of the Lord, and the Lord listened to him, because he saw the oppression of Israel, that the king of Syria oppressed them.

**2 Kings 13:5**

And the Lord gave salvation to Israel, and he went out from under the hand of Syria, and the sons of Israel sat in their tents as formerly.

**2 Kings 13:6**

Only, they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who made Israel sin. In them they walked, and even the grove stood in Samaria.

**2 Kings 13:7**

**2 Kings 13:8**

And the rest of the words of Jehoahaz and all that he did and his acts of power, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 13:9**

And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in Samaria, and Joash his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 13:10**

In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Joash son of Jehoahaz reigned over Israel in Samaria sixteen years.

**2 Kings 13:11**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord. He did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin. In them he walked.

**2 Kings 13:12**

And the rest of the words of Joash and all that he did and his acts of power with which he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 13:13**

And Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne in Samaria among the sons of Israel.

**2 Kings 13:14**

And Elisha became sick with the sickness by which he died, and Joash king of Israel came down to him and wept over his face and said, My father, my father, chariot of Israel and its horseman.

**2 Kings 13:15**

And Elisha said to him, Take a bow and arrows. And he took for himself a bow and arrows.

**2 Kings 13:16**

And he said to the king, Lay your hand upon the bow. And Joash laid his hand upon the bow, and Elisha placed his hands upon the hands of the king.

**2 Kings 13:17**

And he said, Open the window toward the east. And he opened it. And Elisha said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, An arrow of salvation for the Lord and an arrow of salvation against Syria, and you will strike Syria at Aphek until completion.

**2 Kings 13:18**

And Elisha said to him, Take the arrows. And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, Strike into the ground. And the king struck three times and stopped.

**2 Kings 13:19**

And the man of God was grieved over him and said, If you had struck five or six times, then you would have struck Syria until completion. But now three times you will strike Syria.

**2 Kings 13:20**

And Elisha died, and they buried him. And raiding bands of Moab came into the land at the coming of the year.

**2 Kings 13:21**

And it came to be, while they were burying a man, behold, they saw the raiding band, and they threw the man into the tomb of Elisha. And he went and touched the bones of Elisha and lived and stood on his feet.

**2 Kings 13:22**

And Hazael oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

**2 Kings 13:23**

And the Lord had mercy on them and pitied them and looked toward them because of his covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and the Lord did not wish to destroy them and did not cast them from before his face until now.

**2 Kings 13:24**

And Hazael king of Syria died, and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 13:25**

And Joash son of Jehoahaz returned and took the cities from the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, which he took from the hand of Jehoahaz his father in war. Three times Joash struck him and recovered the cities of Israel.

#### Chapter 14

**2 Kings 14:1**

In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 14:2**

He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 14:3**

And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, but not like David his father. According to all that Joash his father did, he did.

**2 Kings 14:4**

**2 Kings 14:5**

**2 Kings 14:6**

**2 Kings 14:7**

He struck Edom in the Valley of Salt, ten thousand, and captured Petra in war and called its name Joktheel to this day.

**2 Kings 14:8**

**2 Kings 14:9**

And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thornbush in Lebanon sent to the cedar in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son for a wife. And the beasts of the field passed by, those in Lebanon, and trampled the thornbush.

**2 Kings 14:10**

Striking, you struck Edom, and your heart lifted you up. Be glorified by sitting in your house. Why do you provoke evil against yourself, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?

**2 Kings 14:11**

**2 Kings 14:12**

**2 Kings 14:13**

**2 Kings 14:14**

And he took the gold and the silver and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house and the hostages, and he returned to Samaria.

**2 Kings 14:15**

And the rest of the words of Joash, what he did in his might, how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 14:16**

And Joash slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 14:17**

And Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

**2 Kings 14:18**

And the rest of the words of Amaziah and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 14:19**

**2 Kings 14:20**

**2 Kings 14:21**

**2 Kings 14:22**

**2 Kings 14:23**

In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash reigned over Israel in Samaria forty-one years.

**2 Kings 14:24**

And he did evil before the Lord. He did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.

**2 Kings 14:25**

**2 Kings 14:26**

**2 Kings 14:27**

**2 Kings 14:28**

And the rest of the words of Jeroboam and all that he did and his acts of power, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 14:29**

And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and Azariah son of Amaziah reigned in place of his father.

#### Chapter 15

**2 Kings 15:1**

In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 15:21**

And the rest of the words of Menahem and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?

**2 Kings 15:23**

**2 Kings 15:26**

And the rest of the words of Pekahiah and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel.

**2 Kings 15:27**

**2 Kings 15:28**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord. He did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.

**2 Kings 15:29**

**2 Kings 15:30**

And Hoshea son of Ela made a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah and struck him and killed him and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Azariah.

**2 Kings 15:31**

And the rest of the words of Pekah and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel.

**2 Kings 15:32**

**2 Kings 15:33**

**2 Kings 15:34**

**2 Kings 15:35**

**2 Kings 15:36**

And the rest of the words of Jotham and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 15:37**

**2 Kings 15:38**

#### Chapter 16

**2 Kings 16:1**

In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 16:2**

Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and he did not do what was right in the eyes of the Lord his God faithfully, as David his father.

**2 Kings 16:3**

And he walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat king of Israel, and even his son he caused to pass through fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord drove out from before the sons of Israel.

**2 Kings 16:4**

And he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places and on the hills and under every leafy tree.

**2 Kings 16:5**

Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up against Jerusalem for war and besieged Ahaz, and they could not fight against him.

**2 Kings 16:6**

At that time Rezin king of Syria restored Elath to Syria and drove the Judeans from Elath, and Edomites came to Elath and dwelt there until this day.

**2 Kings 16:7**

And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglathpileser king of the Assyrians, saying, I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, those rising against me.

**2 Kings 16:8**

And Ahaz took the silver and the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the king's house and sent gifts to the king.

**2 Kings 16:9**

And the king of the Assyrians listened to him, and the king of the Assyrians went up to Damascus and captured it and deported it, and Rezin he killed.

**2 Kings 16:10**
