**2 Kings 16:11**

And Urijah the priest built the altar according to all that King Ahaz sent from Damascus.

**2 Kings 16:12**

And the king saw the altar and went up upon it.

**2 Kings 16:13**

And he burned his whole-burnt-offering and his sacrifice and his drink-offering and poured out the blood of his peace-offerings upon the altar.

**2 Kings 16:14**

And the bronze altar, the one before the Lord, he brought near from before the house of the Lord, from between the altar and from between the house of the Lord, and set it on the side of the altar toward the north.

**2 Kings 16:15**

And King Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, Upon the great altar offer the morning whole-burnt-offering and the evening sacrifice and the whole-burnt-offering of the king and his sacrifice and the whole-burnt-offerings of all the people of the land and their sacrifices and their drink-offerings, and pour on it all the blood of the whole-burnt-offering and all the blood of the sacrifice, but the bronze altar will be for me to inquire by.

**2 Kings 16:16**

And Urijah the priest did according to all that King Ahaz commanded him.

**2 Kings 16:17**

And King Ahaz cut down the frames of the bases and removed the laver from them, and he brought down the sea from the bronze oxen under it and set it on a stone base.

**2 Kings 16:18**

And the foundation of the seat he built in the house of the Lord, and the outer entrance of the king he turned within the house of the Lord because of the king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 16:19**

And the rest of the words of Ahaz, what he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 16:20**

And Ahaz slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

#### Chapter 17

**2 Kings 17:1**

In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Ela reigned in Samaria over Israel nine years.

**2 Kings 17:2**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, yet not like the kings of Israel who were before him.

**2 Kings 17:3**

Against him came up Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians, and Hoshea became his servant and brought tribute back to him.

**2 Kings 17:4**

And the king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Hoshea, because he sent messengers to So king of Egypt and did not bring tribute to the king of the Assyrians in that year. And the king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in prison.

**2 Kings 17:5**

And the king of the Assyrians came up in all the land and came up to Samaria and besieged it three years.

**2 Kings 17:6**

In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians and settled them in Halah and in Habor, rivers of Gozan, and mountains of the Medes.

**2 Kings 17:7**

And it came to be because the sons of Israel sinned against the Lord their God who brought them up from the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.

**2 Kings 17:8**

And they walked in the statutes of the nations whom the Lord drove out from before the sons of Israel, and in those of the kings of Israel, as many as they made.

**2 Kings 17:9**

And the sons of Israel secretly did matters not so against the Lord their God, and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from the tower of watchmen to fortified city.

**2 Kings 17:10**

And they set up for themselves pillars and groves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

**2 Kings 17:11**

And there they burned incense on all the high places, as the nations whom the Lord deported from before them, and they made companions and engraved things to provoke the Lord.

**2 Kings 17:12**

And they served idols, of which the Lord said to them, You shall not do this thing to the Lord.

**2 Kings 17:13**

And the Lord testified in Israel and in Judah by the hand of all his prophets, every seer, saying, Turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my ordinances and all the law.

**2 Kings 17:14**

And they did not listen and hardened their neck beyond the neck of their fathers.

**2 Kings 17:15**

And his testimonies, which he testified to them, they did not keep, and they went after vanities and became vain, and after the nations around them, concerning whom he commanded them not to do according to these.

**2 Kings 17:16**

They abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God and made for themselves cast images, two calves, and made groves and bowed down to all the force of heaven and served Baal.

**2 Kings 17:17**

And they made their sons and their daughters pass through fire and practiced divinations and omens and sold themselves to do evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke him.

**2 Kings 17:18**

And the Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from before his face, and none was left except the tribe of Judah alone.

**2 Kings 17:19**

Yet Judah also did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God, and they walked in the statutes of Israel which they made.

**2 Kings 17:20**

And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel and shook them and gave them into the hand of those plundering them until he cast them from before his face.

**2 Kings 17:21**

Because he tore Israel away from the house of David, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king, and Jeroboam thrust Israel away from following the Lord and made them sin a great sin.

**2 Kings 17:22**

And the sons of Israel walked in every sin of Jeroboam which he did. They did not depart from it,

**2 Kings 17:23**

until the Lord removed Israel from before his face, as the Lord spoke by the hand of all his servants the prophets, and Israel was deported from its land to the Assyrians until this day.

**2 Kings 17:24**

And the king of the Assyrians brought from Babylon and from Cuthah and from Ava and from Hamath and Sepharvaim and settled them in the cities of Samaria instead of the sons of Israel. And they inherited Samaria and dwelt in its cities.

**2 Kings 17:25**

And it came to be at the beginning of their dwelling there, they did not fear the Lord, and the Lord sent lions among them, and they were killing among them.

**2 Kings 17:26**

And they said to the king of the Assyrians, The nations whom you deported and settled in the cities of Samaria did not know the judgment of the god of the land, and he sent the lions among them, and behold, they are putting them to death because they do not know the judgment of the god of the land.

**2 Kings 17:27**

And the king of the Assyrians commanded, saying, Take there one of the priests whom you deported from there, and let him go and dwell there and enlighten them about the judgment of the god of the land.

**2 Kings 17:28**

And they brought one of the priests whom they deported from Samaria, and he dwelt in Bethel and was enlightening them how they should fear the Lord.

**2 Kings 17:29**

And nation by nation was making its own gods and putting them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans made, nation in the cities in which they were dwelling.

**2 Kings 17:30**

And the men of Babylon made Succothbenoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,

**2 Kings 17:31**

and the Evaites made Eblazer and Tartak, and the Seppharouaites were burning their sons in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, gods of Sepharvaim.

**2 Kings 17:32**

And they were fearing the Lord and appointing for themselves priests of the high places from among themselves, and they were making for them in the houses of the high places.

**2 Kings 17:33**

They feared the Lord and served their gods according to the custom of the nations from which he deported them there.

**2 Kings 17:34**

To this day they act according to their judgment. They fear, and they act according to their statutes and according to their judgment and according to the law and according to the commandment that the Lord commanded the sons of Jacob, whom he named Israel.

**2 Kings 17:35**

And the Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, You shall not fear other gods, and you shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them, and you shall not sacrifice to them,

**2 Kings 17:36**

but only the Lord who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great strength and with uplifted arm, him you shall fear and to him you shall bow and to him you shall sacrifice.

**2 Kings 17:37**

And the ordinances and the judgments and the law and the commandments which he wrote for you, you shall keep to do all the days, and you shall not fear other gods.

**2 Kings 17:38**

And the covenant which he made with you, you shall not forget, and you shall not fear other gods,

**2 Kings 17:39**

but the Lord your God you shall fear, and he will deliver you from all your enemies.

**2 Kings 17:40**

And you will not listen according to their judgment, which they do.

**2 Kings 17:41**

And these nations were fearing the Lord and were serving their carved images, and indeed their sons and the sons of their sons, just as their fathers did, they do until this day.

#### Chapter 18

**2 Kings 18:1**

And it came to be in the third year of Hoshea son of Ela, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah reigned.

**2 Kings 18:2**

He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Abou daughter of Zechariah.

**2 Kings 18:3**

And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that David his father did.

**2 Kings 18:4**

He removed the high places and crushed all the pillars and destroyed the groves and the bronze serpent which Moses made, because until those days the sons of Israel were burning incense to it, and he called it Nehushtan.

**2 Kings 18:5**

He hoped in the Lord God of Israel, and after him there was none like him among the kings of Judah and among those before him.

**2 Kings 18:6**

And he clung to the Lord and did not depart from behind him and kept his commandments which he commanded Moses.

**2 Kings 18:7**

And the Lord was with him. In all that he did, he prospered. And he rebelled against the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.

**2 Kings 18:8**

He struck the Philistines as far as Gaza and as far as its border, from the tower of watchmen to fortified city.

**2 Kings 18:9**

And it came to be in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Ela king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of the Assyrians came up against Samaria and was besieging it.

**2 Kings 18:10**

And he captured it at the end of three years, in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, and Samaria was captured.

**2 Kings 18:11**

And the king of the Assyrians deported Samaria to the Assyrians and set them in Halah and in Habor, river of Gozan, and mountains of the Medes,

**2 Kings 18:12**

because they did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God and transgressed his covenant, all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded, and they did not listen and did not do it.

**2 Kings 18:13**

And in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came up against the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

**2 Kings 18:14**

And Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians to Lachish, saying, I have sinned. Turn away from me. Whatever you impose on me I will bear. And the king of the Assyrians imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

**2 Kings 18:15**

And Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house.

**2 Kings 18:16**

At that time Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple of the Lord and the supports which Hezekiah king of Judah overlaid, and he gave them to the king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 18:17**

And the king of the Assyrians sent Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a heavy force against Jerusalem, and they came up and came to Jerusalem and stood by the conduit of the upper pool on the way of the fuller's field.

**2 Kings 18:18**

And they called to Hezekiah, and Eliakim son of Hilkiah the steward and Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came out to them.

**2 Kings 18:19**

And Rabshakeh said to them, Say now to Hezekiah, Thus says the great king, king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you have trusted?

**2 Kings 18:20**

You said, Only words of lips are counsel and strength for war. Now then, in whom have you trusted that you rebelled against me?

**2 Kings 18:21**

Now behold, you have trusted for yourself on this broken reed staff, on Egypt, on which if a man leans it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

**2 Kings 18:22**

And if you say to me, We have trusted in the Lord our God, is not this the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Before this altar in Jerusalem you shall bow?

**2 Kings 18:23**

And now make a bargain now with my lord king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses if you are able to give riders for them.

**2 Kings 18:24**

And how will you turn away the face of one governor from the least of the servants of my lord? And you trusted for yourself in Egypt for chariots and horsemen.

**2 Kings 18:25**

And now, was it without the Lord that we came up against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, Go up against this land and destroy it.

**2 Kings 18:26**

And Eliakim son of Hilkiah and Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh, Speak now to your servants in Syrian, because we understand, and do not speak with us in Judean. Why do you speak in the ears of the people upon the wall?

**2 Kings 18:27**

And Rabshakeh said to them, Was it to your lord and to you that my lord sent me to speak these words? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, to eat their dung and drink their urine with you?

**2 Kings 18:28**

And Rabshakeh stood and cried with a great voice in Judean and spoke and said, Hear the words of the great king, king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 18:29**

Thus says the king: Let not Hezekiah lift you up with words, because he will not be able to deliver you from my hand.

**2 Kings 18:30**

And let not Hezekiah make you hope in the Lord, saying, In delivering the Lord will deliver us. This city will not be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 18:31**

Do not listen to Hezekiah, because thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me, and each man will eat of his vine and each man will eat of his fig tree and each man will drink water from his cistern,

**2 Kings 18:32**

until I come and take you to a land like your land, a land of grain and wine and bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey, and you will live and not die. And do not listen to Hezekiah, because he deceives you, saying, The Lord will rescue us.

**2 Kings 18:33**

Have the gods of the nations, in delivering, delivered each his own land from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?

**2 Kings 18:34**

Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad? Where is the god of Sepharvaim? And have they delivered Samaria from my hand?

**2 Kings 18:35**

Who among all the gods of the lands delivered their lands from my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?

**2 Kings 18:36**

And they kept silent and did not answer him a word, because it was the king's command, saying, You shall not answer him.

**2 Kings 18:37**

And Eliakim son of Hilkiah the steward and Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with torn garments and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.

#### Chapter 19

**2 Kings 19:1**

And it came to be, when King Hezekiah heard, he tore his garments and wrapped himself in sackcloth and entered into the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 19:2**

And he sent Eliakim the steward and Shebna the scribe and the elders of the priests clothed in sackcloth to Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz.

**2 Kings 19:3**

And they said to him, Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of affliction and rebuke and provocation, because sons came as far as birth pains and there is no strength for the woman giving birth.

**2 Kings 19:4**

If perhaps the Lord your God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of the Assyrians his lord sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme in words which the Lord your God heard, then you shall take up prayer for the remnant that is found.

**2 Kings 19:5**

And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

**2 Kings 19:6**

And Isaiah said to them, Thus you shall say to your lord: Thus says the Lord, Do not fear from the words which you heard, with which the servant-boys of the king of the Assyrians blasphemed.

**2 Kings 19:7**

Behold, I am putting a spirit in him, and he will hear a report and return to his land, and I will bring him down by the sword in his land.

**2 Kings 19:8**

And Rabshakeh returned and found the king of the Assyrians warring against Libnah, because he heard that he departed from Lachish.

**2 Kings 19:9**

And he heard concerning Tirhakah king of the Ethiopians, saying, Behold, he came out to war with you. And he turned and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

**2 Kings 19:10**

Let not your God on whom you trust lift you up, saying, Jerusalem will not be given into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 19:11**

Behold, you heard all that the kings of the Assyrians did to all lands, to devote them. And will you be rescued?

**2 Kings 19:12**

Did the gods of the nations rescue them, those whom my fathers destroyed, both Gozan and Haran and Rezeph and sons of Eden in Thaesthen?

**2 Kings 19:13**

Where is the king of Hamath and the king of Arpad, and where is Sepharvaim, Anah, and Aua?

**2 Kings 19:14**

And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them, and he went up to the house of the Lord, and Hezekiah spread them out before the Lord.

**2 Kings 19:15**

And he said, Lord God of Israel, the one sitting upon the cherubim, you are God alone in all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.

**2 Kings 19:16**

Incline, Lord, your ear and hear. Open, Lord, your eyes and see. And hear the words of Sennacherib which he sent to reproach the living God.

**2 Kings 19:17**

Because truly, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians laid waste the nations

**2 Kings 19:18**

and gave their gods into the fire, because they are not gods but works of human hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.

**2 Kings 19:19**

And now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you alone, Lord, are God.

**2 Kings 19:20**

And Isaiah son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus says the Lord God of the forces, the God of Israel: I heard what you prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians.

**2 Kings 19:21**

This is the word which the Lord spoke against him: Virgin daughter of Zion despised you and mocked you. Daughter Jerusalem shook her head over you.

**2 Kings 19:22**

Whom did you reproach and blaspheme? Against whom did you raise your voice and lift your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.

**2 Kings 19:23**

By the hand of your messengers you reproached the Lord and said, By the multitude of my chariots I will go up to the heights of mountains, the sides of Lebanon, and I cut down the greatness of its cedar, its choice cypresses, and I came to the farthest part of its border, the forest of its Carmel.

**2 Kings 19:24**

I cooled and drank foreign waters, and with the sole of my foot I laid waste all rivers of a besieged land.

**2 Kings 19:25**

I formed it. Now I brought it, and it came to be for elevations of desolated settlements, fortified cities.

**2 Kings 19:26**

And those dwelling in them were weak of hand. They were dismayed and put to shame. They became like grass of the field and green herb, like grass of the rooftops and trampling before standing grain.

**2 Kings 19:27**

And your sitting and your going out and your going in I knew, and your rage against me.

**2 Kings 19:28**

Because you raged against me and your insolence went up in my ears, I will put my hooks in your nostrils and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back on the way by which you came.

**2 Kings 19:29**

And this to you is the sign: Eat this year what grows of itself, and in the second year the springing growth, and in the third sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

**2 Kings 19:30**

And the remnant of the house of Judah that escaped and was left will again take root downward and make fruit upward.

**2 Kings 19:31**

Because from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and one preserved from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord of forces will do this.

**2 Kings 19:32**

Not so. Thus says the Lord to the king of the Assyrians: He will not enter into this city and will not shoot there an arrow and will not come before it with shield and will certainly not cast up against it a mound.

**2 Kings 19:33**

By the way that he came, by it he will return, and into this city he will not enter, says the Lord.

**2 Kings 19:34**

And I will shield this city for my own sake and for David my servant.

**2 Kings 19:35**

And it came to be by night, and an angel of the Lord went out and struck in the camp of the Assyrians one hundred eighty-five thousand. And they rose early in the morning, and behold, all were dead bodies.

**2 Kings 19:36**

And Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed and went and returned and dwelt in Nineveh.

**2 Kings 19:37**

And it came to be, while he was bowing in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat, and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.

#### Chapter 20

**2 Kings 20:1**

In those days Hezekiah became sick unto death, and Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet entered to him and said to him, Thus says the Lord: Give command to your house, because you are dying and will not live.

**2 Kings 20:2**

And Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord, saying,

**2 Kings 20:3**

O Lord, remember now how I walked before you in truth and with a full heart and did what was good in your eyes. And Hezekiah wept with great weeping.

**2 Kings 20:4**

And Isaiah was in the middle court, and the word of the Lord came to him, saying,

**2 Kings 20:5**

Turn back and say to Hezekiah the leader of my people, Thus says the Lord God of David your father: I heard your prayer, I saw your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day you will go up into the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 20:6**

And I will add fifteen years to your days, and from the hand of the king of the Assyrians I will save you and this city, and I will shield this city for my own sake and for David my servant.

**2 Kings 20:7**

And he said, Let them take a cake of figs and let them put it upon the sore, and he will recover.

**2 Kings 20:8**

And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, What is the sign that the Lord will heal me and I will go up into the house of the Lord on the third day?

**2 Kings 20:9**

And Isaiah said, This is the sign from the Lord that the Lord will do the word which he spoke. Shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or shall it turn back ten steps?

**2 Kings 20:10**

And Hezekiah said, It is a light thing for the shadow to slope ten steps. No, but let the shadow turn back ten steps.

**2 Kings 20:11**

And Isaiah the prophet cried to the Lord, and the shadow turned back on the steps ten steps backward.

**2 Kings 20:12**

At that time Berodachbaladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, because he heard that Hezekiah was sick.

**2 Kings 20:13**

And Hezekiah rejoiced over them and showed them his whole treasure-house, the silver and the gold, the spices and the good oil and the house of the vessels and all that was found in his treasuries. There was not a thing which Hezekiah did not show them in his house and in all his dominion.

**2 Kings 20:14**

And Isaiah the prophet entered to King Hezekiah and said to him, What did these men say, and from where did they come to you? And Hezekiah said, They came to me from a far land, from Babylon.

**2 Kings 20:15**

And he said, What did they see in your house? And he said, They saw all that is in my house. There was not a thing in my house or in my treasuries that I did not show them.

**2 Kings 20:16**

And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, Hear the word of the Lord.

**2 Kings 20:17**

Behold, days are coming, and everything in your house and whatever your fathers stored up to this day will be taken to Babylon, and not a thing will be left, which the Lord said.

**2 Kings 20:18**

And from your sons who will come out from you, whom you will beget, they will take, and they will be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon.

**2 Kings 20:19**

And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, Good is the word of the Lord which you spoke. Let there be peace in my days.

**2 Kings 20:20**

And the rest of the words of Hezekiah and all his might and what he did, the spring and the conduit, and how he brought the water into the city, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 20:21**

And Hezekiah slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.

#### Chapter 21

**2 Kings 21:1**

Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Hephzibah.

**2 Kings 21:2**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord drove out from before the sons of Israel.

**2 Kings 21:3**

And he turned back and rebuilt the high places which Hezekiah his father tore down and raised up an altar to Baal and made groves, as Ahab king of Israel did, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.

**2 Kings 21:4**

And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which he said, In Jerusalem I will put my name.

**2 Kings 21:5**

And he built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 21:6**

And he made his sons pass through fire and practiced divination and omens and made spirit-mediums and knowers. He multiplied to do evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke him.

**2 Kings 21:7**

And he set the carved image of the grove in the house, of which the Lord said to David and to Solomon his son, In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name there forever.

**2 Kings 21:8**

And I will not again add to shake the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers, if only they keep all that I commanded, according to all the commandment which my servant Moses commanded them.

**2 Kings 21:9**

And they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do evil in the eyes of the Lord beyond the nations which the Lord destroyed from before the sons of Israel.

**2 Kings 21:10**

And the Lord spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying,

**2 Kings 21:11**

Because Manasseh king of Judah did these evil abominations, beyond all that the Amorite who was before him did, and even caused Judah to sin with their idols,

**2 Kings 21:12**

not so. Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing evils on Jerusalem and on Judah, so that whoever hears, both his ears will ring.

**2 Kings 21:13**

And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem as an alabaster vessel is wiped, being wiped and turned on its face.

**2 Kings 21:14**

And I will push away the remnant of my inheritance and give them into the hands of their enemies, and they will become plunder and spoil to all their enemies,

**2 Kings 21:15**

because they did evil in my eyes and were provoking me from the day I brought out their fathers from Egypt until this day.

**2 Kings 21:16**

And Manasseh also poured out very much innocent blood until he filled Jerusalem from mouth to mouth, besides his sins with which he made Judah sin by doing evil in the eyes of the Lord.

**2 Kings 21:17**

And the rest of the words of Manasseh and all that he did and the sin which he sinned, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 21:18**

And Manasseh slept with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza, and Amon his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 21:19**

Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.

**2 Kings 21:20**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as Manasseh his father did.

**2 Kings 21:21**

And he walked in every way in which his father walked and served the idols which his father served and bowed down to them.

**2 Kings 21:22**

And he abandoned the Lord God of his fathers and did not walk in the way of the Lord.

**2 Kings 21:23**

And the servants of Amon conspired against him and put the king to death in his house.

**2 Kings 21:24**

And all the people of the land struck down all those conspiring against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.

**2 Kings 21:25**

And the rest of the words of Amon, what he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 21:26**

And they buried him in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son reigned in his place.

#### Chapter 22

**2 Kings 22:1**

Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Jedidah daughter of Adaiah from Boscath.

**2 Kings 22:2**

And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord and walked in every way of David his father. He did not turn aside to the right or to the left.

**2 Kings 22:3**

And it came to be in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, in the eighth month, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah son of Meshullam, the scribe of the house of the Lord, saying,

**2 Kings 22:4**

Go up to Hilkiah the high priest and seal the silver brought into the house of the Lord, which the keepers of the threshold gathered from the people.

**2 Kings 22:5**

And let them give it into the hand of those doing the works, those appointed in the house of the Lord. And he gave it to those doing the works, those in the house of the Lord, to strengthen the breach of the house,

**2 Kings 22:6**

to the carpenters and the builders and the masons, and to buy timber and quarried stones to strengthen the breach of the house.

**2 Kings 22:7**

Only, they did not reckon with them the silver being given to them, because they act in faithfulness.

**2 Kings 22:8**

And Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, I found a book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.

**2 Kings 22:9**

And Shaphan brought it to King Josiah and brought word back to the king and said, Your servants poured out the silver found in the house of the Lord and gave it into the hand of those doing the works, those appointed in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 22:10**

And Shaphan the scribe said to the king, saying, Hilkiah the priest gave me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.

**2 Kings 22:11**

And it came to be, when the king heard the words of the book of the law, he tore his garments.

**2 Kings 22:12**

And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam son of Shaphan and Achbor son of Michaiah and Shaphan the scribe and Asaiah servant of the king, saying,

**2 Kings 22:13**

Go, seek the Lord concerning me and concerning all the people and concerning all Judah, concerning the words of this book that was found, because great is the anger of the Lord, which burns in us, because our fathers did not listen to all the words of this book to do according to all written for us.

**2 Kings 22:14**

And Hilkiah the priest and Ahikam and Achbor and Shaphan and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Hillel son of Tikvah son of Harhas keeper of the wardrobe, and she dwelt in Jerusalem in the Maseña, and they spoke to her.

**2 Kings 22:15**

And she said to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,

**2 Kings 22:16**

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this place and upon those dwelling in it, all the words of the book which the king of Judah read,

**2 Kings 22:17**

because they abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, so as to provoke me in all the works of their hands, and my wrath will burn in this place and will not be quenched.

**2 Kings 22:18**

And to the king of Judah who sent you to seek the Lord, thus you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord God of Israel concerning the words which you heard:

**2 Kings 22:19**

Because your heart was softened and you were ashamed from before the Lord when you heard what I spoke against this place and against those dwelling in it, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before me, I also heard, says the Lord.

**2 Kings 22:20**

Not so. Behold, I am adding you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your tomb in peace, and your eyes will not see among all the evils that I am bringing upon this place. And they returned word to the king.

#### Chapter 23

**2 Kings 23:1**

And the king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 23:2**

And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and every man of Judah and all those dwelling in Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people from small to great. And he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 23:3**

And the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk after the Lord and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his ordinances with all his heart and with all his soul, to establish the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

**2 Kings 23:4**

And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second order and the keepers of the threshold to bring out from the temple of the Lord all the vessels made for Baal and for the grove and for all the force of heaven, and he burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron and carried their dust to Bethel.

**2 Kings 23:5**

And he put an end to the idol-priests whom the kings of Judah appointed and who were burning incense in the high places and in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and those burning incense to Baal and to the sun and to the moon and to the Mazouroth and to all the force of heaven.

**2 Kings 23:6**

And he brought the grove out from the house of the Lord, outside Jerusalem to the wadi Kidron, and burned it in the wadi Kidron and beat it small to dust and threw its dust on the tombs of the sons of the people.

**2 Kings 23:7**

And he tore down the houses of the consecrated ones which were in the house of the Lord, where the women were weaving hangings for the grove.

**2 Kings 23:8**

And he brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests burned incense, from Gibeah to Beersheba, and he tore down the house of the gates by the entrance of the gate of Joshua governor of the city, those on the left at the gate of the city.

**2 Kings 23:9**

Only, the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, except they ate unleavened bread in the midst of their brothers.

**2 Kings 23:10**

And he defiled Topheth in the valley of the son of Hinnom, so as not to make a man bring his son or a man bring his daughter through fire to Moloch.

**2 Kings 23:11**

And he put an end to the horses which the kings of Judah gave to the sun at the entrance of the house of the Lord, in the treasury of Nathan the king's eunuch in the suburbs, and the chariot of the sun he burned with fire.

**2 Kings 23:12**

And the altars on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah made, and the altars which Manasseh made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, the king tore down and broke up there and threw their dust into the wadi Kidron.

**2 Kings 23:13**

And the house that was before Jerusalem, to the right of the mount of Mosoath, which Solomon king of Israel built to Ashtoreth, abomination of the Sidonians, and to Chemosh, abomination of Moab, and to Molochol, abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.

**2 Kings 23:14**

And he crushed the pillars and destroyed the groves and filled their places with human bones.

**2 Kings 23:15**

And indeed the altar in Bethel, the high place which Jeroboam son of Nebat made, who made Israel sin, indeed that altar and the high place he tore down and crushed its stones and beat them small to dust and burned the grove.

**2 Kings 23:16**

And Josiah turned and saw the tombs there in the city, and he sent and took the bones from the tombs and burned them upon the altar and defiled it, according to the word of the Lord which the man of God spoke.

**2 Kings 23:17**

And he said, What is that marker which I see? And the men of the city said to him, It is the man of God who came out from Judah and called out these words which he called out against the altar of Bethel.

**2 Kings 23:18**

And he said, Leave him. Let no man move his bones. And they preserved his bones with the bones of the prophet who came out from Samaria.

**2 Kings 23:19**

And also all the houses of the high places which were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel made to provoke the Lord, Josiah removed and did to them according to all the deeds that he did in Bethel.

**2 Kings 23:20**

And he sacrificed all the priests of the high places who were there upon the altars and burned the bones of humans upon them and returned to Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 23:21**

And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the Passover to the Lord our God, as it is written in this book of the covenant.

**2 Kings 23:22**

Because this Passover was not held from the days of the judges who judged Israel and all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah,

**2 Kings 23:23**

except in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was held to the Lord in Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 23:24**

And indeed the spirit-mediums and the knowers and the theraphin and the idols and all the abominations that had appeared in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem King Josiah removed, to establish the words of the law written upon the book which Hilkiah the priest found in the house of the Lord.

**2 Kings 23:25**

Like him there was no king before him who turned to the Lord with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength according to all the law of Moses, and after him none like him arose.

**2 Kings 23:26**

Only, the Lord did not turn away from the fury of his great anger, with which his anger burned in Judah, because of the provocations with which Manasseh provoked him.

**2 Kings 23:27**

And the Lord said, Also Judah I will remove from before my face, as I removed Israel, and I will reject this city which I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, My name will be there.

**2 Kings 23:28**

And the rest of the words of Josiah and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 23:29**

And in his days Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians by the river Euphrates, and Josiah went to meet him, and Necho put him to death in Megiddo when he saw him.

**2 Kings 23:30**

And his servants set him on the chariot, dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb in the city of David. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.

**2 Kings 23:31**

Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

**2 Kings 23:32**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his fathers did.

**2 Kings 23:33**

And Pharaoh Necho removed him in Riblah in the land of Hamath so that he should not reign in Jerusalem, and he imposed a penalty on the land of a hundred talents of silver and a hundred talents of gold.

**2 Kings 23:34**

And Pharaoh Necho made Eliakim son of Josiah king of Judah king in place of Josiah his father, and he changed his name to Joakim, and he took Jehoahaz and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.

**2 Kings 23:35**

And Joakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh, but he assessed the land to give the silver according to the mouth of Pharaoh. Each man according to his valuation they gave the silver and the gold with the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Necho.

**2 Kings 23:36**

Joakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.

**2 Kings 23:37**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his fathers did.

#### Chapter 24

**2 Kings 24:1**

In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Joakim became his servant three years, and he turned and rebelled against him.

**2 Kings 24:2**

And the Lord sent against him raiding bands of the Chaldeans and raiding bands of Syria and raiding bands of Moab and raiding bands of the sons of Ammon, and he sent them into the land of Judah to strengthen against it, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets.

**2 Kings 24:3**

Only, it was upon the anger of the Lord in Judah to remove him from before his face, because of the sins of Manasseh according to all that he did,

**2 Kings 24:4**

and indeed he poured out innocent blood and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord did not wish to be propitiated.

**2 Kings 24:5**

And the rest of the words of Joakim and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?

**2 Kings 24:6**

And Joakim slept with his fathers, and Joakim his son reigned in his place.

**2 Kings 24:7**

And the king of Egypt no longer added to go out from his land, because the king of Babylon took from the wadi of Egypt as far as the river Euphrates, all that belonged to the king of Egypt.

**2 Kings 24:8**

Joakim was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 24:9**

And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his father did.

**2 Kings 24:10**

At that time Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.

**2 Kings 24:11**

And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon entered into the city, and his servants were besieging it.

**2 Kings 24:12**

And Joakim king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his servants and his mother and his rulers and his eunuchs, and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.

**2 Kings 24:13**

And he carried out from there all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house and cut in pieces all the golden vessels which Solomon king of Israel made in the temple of the Lord, according to the word of the Lord.

**2 Kings 24:14**

And he deported Jerusalem and all the rulers and the mighty in strength, ten thousand in captivity, and every craftsman and every smith, and none was left except the poor of the land.

**2 Kings 24:15**

And he deported Joakim to Babylon, and the king's mother and the king's wives and his eunuchs and the mighty of the land he led away in exile from Jerusalem into Babylon.

**2 Kings 24:16**

And all the men of force, seven thousand, and the craftsman and the smith, a thousand, all mighty ones making war, the king of Babylon brought them as exiles into Babylon.

**2 Kings 24:17**

And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his kinsman king in his place and set his name Zedekiah.

**2 Kings 24:18**

Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah.

**2 Kings 24:19**

And he did evil before the Lord according to all that Joakim did.

**2 Kings 24:20**

Because it was upon the anger of the Lord against Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them from before his face. And Zedekiah rebelled against the kingdom of Babylon.

#### Chapter 25

**2 Kings 25:1**

And it came to be in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, and all his force, against Jerusalem, and they encamped against it and built a siege-wall around it.

**2 Kings 25:2**

And the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

**2 Kings 25:3**

On the ninth day of the month, famine became strong in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

**2 Kings 25:4**

And the city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night by way of the gate between the walls, which is by the king's garden, and the Chaldeans were around the city, and he went by way of the Arabah.

**2 Kings 25:5**

And the force of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his force was scattered from upon him.

**2 Kings 25:6**

And they captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and he spoke judgment with him.

**2 Kings 25:7**

And he slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and the eyes of Zedekiah he blinded, and he bound him in fetters and brought him into Babylon.

**2 Kings 25:8**

And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the chief guard, standing before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

**2 Kings 25:9**

And he burned the house of the Lord and the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great house he burned.

**2 Kings 25:10**

And the force of the Chaldeans that was with the chief guard tore down the walls of Jerusalem all around.

**2 Kings 25:11**

And the rest of the people left in the city and those who had fallen away, who fell to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the support Nebuzaradan the chief guard removed.

**2 Kings 25:12**

And from the poor of the land the chief guard left some for vinedressers and field-workers.

**2 Kings 25:13**

And the bronze pillars in the house of the Lord and the bases and the bronze sea in the house of the Lord the Chaldeans broke up and carried their bronze into Babylon.

**2 Kings 25:14**

And the pots and the shovels and the bowls and the censers and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered, he took.

**2 Kings 25:15**

And the firepans and the bowls, those of gold and those of silver, the chief guard took.

**2 Kings 25:16**

The two pillars, the one sea, and the bases which Solomon made for the house of the Lord, there was no weight to the bronze of all the vessels.

**2 Kings 25:17**

Eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and the bronze capital was upon it, and the height of the capital was three cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the capital round about, all bronze. And the same for the second pillar with the network.

**2 Kings 25:18**

And the chief guard took Seraiah the first priest and Zephaniah of the second order and the three keeping the threshold.

**2 Kings 25:19**

And from the city he took one eunuch who was overseer over the men of war and five men of those seeing the king's face who were found in the city and the scribe of the ruler of the force, the one mustering the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land found in the city.

**2 Kings 25:20**

And Nebuzaradan the chief guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

**2 Kings 25:21**

And the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath, and Judah was deported from its land.

**2 Kings 25:22**

And the people left in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left, over them he appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.

**2 Kings 25:23**

And all the commanders of the force, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon appointed Gedaliah, and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, even Ishmael son of Nethaniah and Johanan son of Careah and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite and Iezonias son of the Maachathite, they and their men.

**2 Kings 25:24**

And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men and said to them, Do not fear the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well for you.

**2 Kings 25:25**

And it came to be in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama from the seed of the kings, and ten men with him, came and struck Gedaliah, and he died, and also the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

**2 Kings 25:26**

And all the people rose, from small to great, and the commanders of the forces, and they entered into Egypt, because they feared from before the Chaldeans.

**2 Kings 25:27**

And it came to be in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Joakim king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign, lifted up the head of Joakim king of Judah from prison.

**2 Kings 25:28**

And he spoke good things with him and gave his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.

**2 Kings 25:29**

And he changed the garments of his prison, and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.

**2 Kings 25:30**

And his allowance, a continual allowance, was given to him from the king's house, a day's portion on its day, all the days of his life.

### 1 Chronicles

#### Chapter 1

**1 Chronicles 1:1**

Adam, Seth, Enos,

**1 Chronicles 1:2**

Kenan, Mahalaleel, Jared,

**1 Chronicles 1:3**

Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,

**1 Chronicles 1:4**

Noah. Sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, Japheth.

**1 Chronicles 1:5**

Sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Elishah, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

**1 Chronicles 1:6**

Sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

**1 Chronicles 1:7**

Sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rhodioi.

**1 Chronicles 1:8**

Sons of Ham: Cush, Mestraim, Phut, and Canaan.

**1 Chronicles 1:9**

Sons of Cush: Sheba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sebekatha. Sons of Raamah: Sheba and Oudadan.

**1 Chronicles 1:10**

And Cush begot Nimrod. This one began to be a giant hunter upon the earth.

**1 Chronicles 1:17**

Sons of Shem: Elam and Asshur and Arphaxad.

**1 Chronicles 1:24**

Shelah.

**1 Chronicles 1:25**

Eber, Peleg, Reu,

**1 Chronicles 1:26**

Serug, Nahor, Terah,

**1 Chronicles 1:27**

Abraham.

**1 Chronicles 1:28**

And sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.

**1 Chronicles 1:29**

And these are their generations: Nebajoth the firstborn of Ishmael, and Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

**1 Chronicles 1:30**

Massa, Idouma, Massa, Hadad, Teman,

**1 Chronicles 1:31**

Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are sons of Ishmael.

**1 Chronicles 1:32**

And sons of Keturah, concubine of Abraham, and she bore to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Soe. And sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.

**1 Chronicles 1:33**

And sons of Midian: Ephah, Hepher, Enoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were sons of Keturah.

**1 Chronicles 1:34**

And Abraham begot Isaac. Sons of Isaac: Esau and Jacob.

**1 Chronicles 1:35**

Sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Ieoul, Ieglom, and Kore.

**1 Chronicles 1:36**

Sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, and from Timnah, Amalek.

**1 Chronicles 1:37**

And sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Some, and Mizzah.

**1 Chronicles 1:38**

Sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.

**1 Chronicles 1:39**

And sons of Lotan: Horites and Heman, and Elath and Namna.

**1 Chronicles 1:40**

Sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. And sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.

**1 Chronicles 1:41**

Sons of Anah: Dishan. Sons of Dishan: Emeron, Eshban, Ithran, and Haran.

**1 Chronicles 1:42**

And sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zoukan, and Jakan. Sons of Dishan also: Os and Haran.

**1 Chronicles 1:43**

And these were their kings: Balak son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

**1 Chronicles 1:44**

And Balak died, and Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:45**

And Jobab died, and Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:46**

And Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the plain of Moab, reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Gittaim.

**1 Chronicles 1:47**

And Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:48**

And Samlah died, and Saul from Rehoboth by the river reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:49**

And Saul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.

**1 Chronicles 1:50**

And Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, and Hadad son of Bedad reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Peor.

**1 Chronicles 1:51**

And Hadad died, and the chiefs of Edom were: chief Timnah, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,

**1 Chronicles 1:52**

chief Elibamas, chief Elas, chief Pinon,

**1 Chronicles 1:53**

chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mabsar,

**1 Chronicles 1:54**

chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These were chiefs of Edom.

#### Chapter 2

**1 Chronicles 2:1**

These are names of the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,

**1 Chronicles 2:2**

Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, Asher.

**1 Chronicles 2:3**

Sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shallum. These three were born to him from the daughter of Shua the Canaanite. And Er, firstborn of Judah, was evil before the Lord, and he put him to death.

**1 Chronicles 2:4**

And Tamar his bride bore to him Perez and Zerah. All sons of Judah were five.

**1 Chronicles 2:5**

Sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.

**1 Chronicles 2:6**

And sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara, all five.

**1 Chronicles 2:7**

And sons of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who transgressed in the devoted thing.

**1 Chronicles 2:8**

And sons of Ethan: Azariah.

**1 Chronicles 2:9**

And sons of Hezron, who were born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram, Caleb, and Aram.

**1 Chronicles 2:10**

And Aram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Nahshon, ruler of the house of Judah.

**1 Chronicles 2:11**

And Nahshon begot Salmon, and Salmon begot Boaz.

**1 Chronicles 2:12**

And Boaz begot Obed, and Obed begot Jesse.

**1 Chronicles 2:13**

And Jesse begot his firstborn Eliab, Amminadab the second, Shimma the third,

**1 Chronicles 2:14**

Nathanael the fourth, Raddai the fifth,

**1 Chronicles 2:15**

Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.

**1 Chronicles 2:16**

And their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. And sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three.

**1 Chronicles 2:17**

And Abigail begot Amasa, and father of Amasa was Jether the Ismaelite.

**1 Chronicles 2:18**

And Caleb son of Hezron begot with Azubah his wife and Jerioth. And these were her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Araunah.

**1 Chronicles 2:19**

And Azubah died, and Caleb took to himself Ephrath, and she bore to him Or.

**1 Chronicles 2:20**

And Or begot Huri, and Huri begot Beseleel.

**1 Chronicles 2:21**

And after this Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir father of Gilead, and he took her, and he was sixty years old, and she bore to him Segub.

**1 Chronicles 2:22**

And Segub begot Jair, and he had twenty-three cities in Gilead.

**1 Chronicles 2:23**

And Geshur and Aram took the villages of Jair from them, even Kanath and its villages, sixty cities. All these were sons of Machir father of Gilead.

**1 Chronicles 2:24**

And after Hezron died, Caleb came to Ephrathah, and Abijah wife of Hezron bore to him Ashur father of Tekoa.

**1 Chronicles 2:25**

And sons of Jerahmeel firstborn of Hezron were Ram the firstborn, and Baana, and Aran, and Ozem his brother.

**1 Chronicles 2:26**

And Jerahmeel had another wife, and her name was Atarah. She is the mother of Onam.

**1 Chronicles 2:27**

And sons of Ram firstborn of Jerahmeel were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.

**1 Chronicles 2:28**

And sons of Onam were Shammai and Jedaiah. And sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.

**1 Chronicles 2:29**

And the name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail, and she bore to him Achabar and Molid.

**1 Chronicles 2:30**

Sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim. And Seled died having no children.

**1 Chronicles 2:31**

And sons of Appaim: Ishi. And sons of Ishi: Sheshan. And sons of Sheshan: Ahlai.

**1 Chronicles 2:32**

And sons of Jedaiah: Shammai, Jether, and Jonathan. And Jether died having no children.

**1 Chronicles 2:33**

And sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were sons of Jerahmeel.

**1 Chronicles 2:34**

And Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. And Sheshan had an Egyptian servant, and his name was Jekuthiel.

**1 Chronicles 2:35**

And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jekuthiel his servant for a wife, and she bore to him Attai.

**1 Chronicles 2:36**

And Attai begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabad.

**1 Chronicles 2:37**

And Zabad begot Ephlal, and Ephlal begot Obed.

**1 Chronicles 2:38**

And Obed begot Jehu, and Jehu begot Azariah.

**1 Chronicles 2:39**

And Azariah begot Helez, and Helez begot Eleasah.

**1 Chronicles 2:40**

And Eleasah begot Sisamai, and Sisamai begot Shallum.

**1 Chronicles 2:41**

And Shallum begot Iechemian, and Iechemias begot Elishama.

**1 Chronicles 2:42**

And sons of Caleb brother of Jerahmeel: Mareshah his firstborn. This one was the father of Ziph, and sons of Mareshah father of Hebron.

**1 Chronicles 2:43**

And sons of Hebron: Kore, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.

**1 Chronicles 2:44**

And Shema begot Raem father of Jorkeam, and Jorkeam begot Shammai.

**1 Chronicles 2:45**

And his son was Maon, and Maon was the father of Bethzur.

**1 Chronicles 2:46**

And Ephah, concubine of Caleb, bore Haran and Mesha and Gazez, and Haran begot Gazez.

**1 Chronicles 2:47**

And sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jotham, Gershon, Phalet, Ephah, and Shaaph.

**1 Chronicles 2:48**

And concubine of Caleb, Maachah, bore Sheber and Tharchna.

**1 Chronicles 2:49**

And Shaaph begot father of Madmannah and Saou father of Machbenah and father of Gaibaa. And daughter of Caleb was Achsah.

**1 Chronicles 2:50**

These were sons of Caleb, sons of Or firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal father of Kirjathjearim,

**1 Chronicles 2:51**

Solomon father of Bethlehem, Hareph father of Bethgader.

**1 Chronicles 2:52**

And sons of Shobal father of Kirjathjearim were Haroeh and half of the Manahethites.

**1 Chronicles 2:53**

And the families of Kirjathjearim were the Ithrites, Puhites, Shumathites, and Mishraites; from these came out the Zareathites and Eshtaulites.

**1 Chronicles 2:54**

Sons of Solomon: Bethlehem, Netophathites, Ataroth, house of Joab, and half of the Manahethites, Esarei.

**1 Chronicles 2:55**

Families of scribes dwelling in Iabes: Thargathiim, Samathiim, Sookathiim. These are the Kinaioi who came from Mesema, father of the house of Rechab.

#### Chapter 3

**1 Chronicles 3:1**

And these were sons of David born to him in Hebron: the firstborn Amnon by Ahinoam the Jezreelite, the second Daniel by Abigail the Carmelite,

**1 Chronicles 3:2**

the third Absalom son of Maachah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, the fourth Adonijah son of Haggith,

**1 Chronicles 3:3**

the fifth Shephatiah by Abital, the sixth Ithream by Eglah his wife.

**1 Chronicles 3:4**

Six were born to him in Hebron, and he reigned there seven years and six months, and thirty-three years he reigned in Jerusalem.

**1 Chronicles 3:5**

And these were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, four, by Beersheba daughter of Ammiel,

**1 Chronicles 3:6**

and Ibhar and Elishama and Eliphelet,

**1 Chronicles 3:7**

and Nogah and Nepheg and Ianoue,

**1 Chronicles 3:8**

and Elishama and Eliada and Eliphelet, nine.

**1 Chronicles 3:9**

All were sons of David, besides sons of the concubines, and Tamar their sister.

**1 Chronicles 3:10**

Sons of Solomon: Rehoboam, Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,

**1 Chronicles 3:11**

Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,

**1 Chronicles 3:12**

Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,

**1 Chronicles 3:13**

Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,

**1 Chronicles 3:14**

Amon his son, Josiah his son.

**1 Chronicles 3:15**

And sons of Josiah: firstborn Johanan, second Joakim, third Zedekiah, fourth Shallum.

**1 Chronicles 3:16**

And sons of Joakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.

**1 Chronicles 3:17**

And sons of Iechonia-asir: Shealtiel his son,

**1 Chronicles 3:18**

Melchiram and Pedaiah and Shenazar and Jecamiah and Hoshama and Denethi.

**1 Chronicles 3:19**

And sons of Shealtiel: Zerubbabel and Shimei. And sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister,

**1 Chronicles 3:20**

and Hashubah and Ohel and Berechiah and Hasadiah and Jushabhesed, five.

#### Chapter 10

**1 Chronicles 10:1**

And Philistines fought against Israel, and Israel fled from before Philistines, and wounded men fell on Mount Gilboa.

**1 Chronicles 10:2**

And Philistines pursued after Saul and after his sons, and Philistines struck Jonathan and Amminadab and Melchishua, sons of Saul.

**1 Chronicles 10:3**

And battle grew heavy against Saul, and archers found him with bows, and he was pained from arrows.

**1 Chronicles 10:4**

And Saul said to one carrying his weapons, Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised come and mock me. But one carrying his weapons would not, because he feared greatly. And Saul took sword and fell upon it.

**1 Chronicles 10:5**

And one carrying his weapons saw that Saul had died, and he too fell upon his sword and died.

**1 Chronicles 10:6**

And Saul died, and his three sons died on that day, and all his house died together.

**1 Chronicles 10:7**

And every man of Israel in valley saw that Israel fled and that Saul and his sons had died, and they left their cities and fled, and Philistines came and lived in them.

**1 Chronicles 10:8**

And it came to pass on next day, and Philistines came to strip slain men, and they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

**1 Chronicles 10:9**

And they stripped him and took his head and his weapons, and sent into the land of Philistines all around to proclaim good news to their idols and to people.

**1 Chronicles 10:10**

And they put his weapons in the house of their god, and they put his head in the house of Dagon.

**1 Chronicles 10:11**

And all dwelling in Gilead heard all that Philistines had done to Saul and to Israel.

**1 Chronicles 10:12**

And every mighty man from Gilead rose and took body of Saul and bodies of his sons and brought them to Jabesh, and they buried their bones under oak in Jabesh and fasted seven days.

**1 Chronicles 10:13**

And Saul died in his lawless deeds which he committed lawlessly against the Lord, against the word of the Lord, because he did not keep it, because Saul inquired through ventriloquist to seek, and Samuel prophet answered him.

**1 Chronicles 10:14**

And he did not seek the Lord, and he put him to death and turned kingdom to David son of Jesse.

#### Chapter 11

**1 Chronicles 11:1**

And all Israel came to David in Hebron, saying, Behold, we are your bones and your flesh.

**1 Chronicles 11:2**

Even yesterday and third day, when Saul was king, you were one bringing Israel out and bringing it in, and the Lord your God said to you, You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.

**1 Chronicles 11:3**

And all the elders of Israel came to the king in Hebron, and King David made covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord, and they anointed David king over Israel according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Samuel.

**1 Chronicles 11:4**

And the king and men of Israel went to Jerusalem, this is Jebus, and there were Jebusites dwelling in the land.

**1 Chronicles 11:5**

And those dwelling in Jebus said to David, You shall not enter here. But he captured stronghold of Zion; this is the City of David.

**1 Chronicles 11:6**

And David said, Whoever strikes Jebusite first shall become ruler and commander. And Joab son of Zeruiah went up first and became ruler.

**1 Chronicles 11:7**

**1 Chronicles 11:8**

**1 Chronicles 11:9**

**1 Chronicles 11:10**

**1 Chronicles 11:11**

**1 Chronicles 11:12**

**1 Chronicles 11:13**

**1 Chronicles 11:14**

**1 Chronicles 11:15**

And three from thirty chiefs went down to rock, to David, into the cave of Adullam, and the camp of the Philistines had camped in the valley of giants.

**1 Chronicles 11:16**

**1 Chronicles 11:17**

And David desired and said, Who will give me water to drink from cistern of Bethlehem, one by gate?

**1 Chronicles 11:18**

**1 Chronicles 11:19**

And he said, God be merciful to me from doing this thing. Shall I drink blood of these men with their lives? For with their lives they brought it. And he would not drink it. These things three mighty men did.

**1 Chronicles 11:20**

And Abishai brother of Joab, he was chief of the three. He drew his sword against three hundred wounded men at one time, and he was named among three.

**1 Chronicles 11:21**

**1 Chronicles 11:22**

**1 Chronicles 11:23**

**1 Chronicles 11:24**

These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and to him was name among three mighty men.

**1 Chronicles 11:25**

**1 Chronicles 12:1**

Azer chief, Obadiah second, Eliab third,

**1 Chronicles 12:11**

Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth,

**1 Chronicles 12:16**

**1 Chronicles 12:17**

And some from the sons of Benjamin and Judah came for help to David.

**1 Chronicles 12:18**

And David went out to meet them and said to them, If you have come to me in peace, let my heart be united with you; but if to betray me to my enemies, though no truth of hand is against me, may God of our fathers see and rebuke.

**1 Chronicles 12:19**

And spirit clothed Amasai, chief of thirty, and he said, Go, and your people, David son of Jesse. Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers, because your God has helped you. And David received them and set them as chiefs of forces.

**1 Chronicles 12:20**

And from Manasseh some joined David when Philistines came against Saul for battle, and he did not help them, because by counsel commanders of Philistines sent him away, saying, At cost of heads of those men he will return to his lord Saul.

**1 Chronicles 12:21**

When he went to Ziklag, there joined him from Manasseh: Edna and Iozabath and Jediael and Michael and Iosabeth and Elimouth and Selathi, heads of thousands of Manasseh.

**1 Chronicles 12:22**

And they fought alongside David against raiding band, because all were mighty of strength, and they became leaders in army, in force.

**1 Chronicles 12:23**

**1 Chronicles 12:24**

And these were names of chiefs of army who came to David in Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul to him according to the word of the Lord.

**1 Chronicles 12:25**

Sons of Judah, shield-bearers and spear-bearers, six thousand eight hundred, mighty for battle line.

**1 Chronicles 12:26**

From the sons of Simeon, mighty in strength for battle line, seven thousand one hundred.

**1 Chronicles 12:27**

From the sons of Levi, four thousand six hundred.

**1 Chronicles 12:28**

And Joadas leader for Aaron, and with him three thousand seven hundred.

**1 Chronicles 12:29**

And Zadok, young man mighty in strength, and from his father’s house, twenty-two chiefs.

**1 Chronicles 12:30**

And from the sons of Benjamin, brothers of Saul, three thousand, and still most of them were keeping watch of the house of Saul.

**1 Chronicles 12:31**

And from the sons of Ephraim, twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty in strength, men of name by the houses of their fathers.

**1 Chronicles 12:32**

And from the half tribe of Manasseh, eighteen thousand who were named by name to come make David king.

**1 Chronicles 12:33**

And from the sons of Issachar, knowing understanding for times, knowing what Israel should do, their chiefs were two hundred, and all their brothers with them.

**1 Chronicles 12:34**

And from Zebulun, going out for battle line with every weapon of war, fifty thousand to help David, not double-hearted.

**1 Chronicles 12:35**

And from Naphtali, one thousand chiefs, and with them with shields and spears, thirty-seven thousand.

**1 Chronicles 12:36**

And from Danites, drawing up for battle, twenty-eight thousand eight hundred.

**1 Chronicles 12:37**

And from Asher, going out to help in war, forty thousand.

**1 Chronicles 12:38**

And from beyond Jordan, from Reuben and Gad and from the half tribe of Manasseh, with every weapon of war, one hundred twenty thousand.

**1 Chronicles 12:39**

All these were men of war, drawing up battle line with peaceful soul, and they came to Hebron to make David king over all Israel, and the remnant of Israel were one soul to make David king.

**1 Chronicles 12:40**

And they were there three days, eating and drinking, because their brothers had prepared for them.

**1 Chronicles 12:41**

And those bordering them, even as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, were bringing to them on camels and donkeys and mules and on calves provisions, meal, fig cakes, raisins, wine and oil, calves and sheep in abundance, because gladness was in Israel.

#### Chapter 13

**1 Chronicles 13:1**

And David took counsel with commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.

**1 Chronicles 13:2**

And David said to all the assembly of Israel, If this seems good to you, and if it has been prospered from the Lord our God, let us send to our brothers left behind in all the land of Israel, and with them to priests and Levites in the cities of their possession, and let them gather to us.

**1 Chronicles 13:3**

And let us bring the ark of our God to us, because from the days of Saul they did not seek it.

**1 Chronicles 13:4**

And all the assembly said to do so, because word was upright in the eyes of all the people.

**1 Chronicles 13:5**

And David assembled all Israel from the borders of Egypt and as far as entrance of Hamath, to bring the ark of God from the city of Kirjathjearim.

**1 Chronicles 13:6**

And David brought it up, and all Israel went up to the City of David, which belonged to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the Lord seated upon cheroubim, where his name was called upon it.

**1 Chronicles 13:7**

And they placed the ark of God on new wagon from the house of Amminadab, and Uzza and his brothers were leading wagon.

**1 Chronicles 13:8**

And David and all Israel were playing before God with all their strength, and with songs and lyres and harps and tambourines and cymbals and trumpets.

**1 Chronicles 13:9**

And they came as far as threshing floor, and Uzza stretched out his hand to grasp ark, because calf turned it aside.

**1 Chronicles 13:10**

And the Lord’s anger grew hot against Uzza, and he struck him there because he stretched out his hand upon ark, and he died there before God.

**1 Chronicles 13:11**

And David was troubled because the Lord had broken out with breach against Uzza, and he called that place Breach-of-Uzza until this day.

**1 Chronicles 13:12**

And David feared God on that day, saying, How shall I bring the ark of God to myself?

**1 Chronicles 13:13**

And David did not bring back ark to himself into the City of David, but turned it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite.

**1 Chronicles 13:14**

And the ark of God stayed in the house of Obededom three months, and God blessed Abeddaram and all his things.

#### Chapter 14

**1 Chronicles 14:1**

And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar woods and builders of walls and carpenters of wood to build him house.

**1 Chronicles 14:2**

And David knew that the Lord had established him over Israel, because his kingdom was exalted on high for the sake of his people Israel.

**1 Chronicles 14:3**

And David took yet more wives in Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to David.

**1 Chronicles 14:4**

And these were names of children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

**1 Chronicles 14:5**

and Ibhar and Elishua and Elpalet,

**1 Chronicles 14:6**

and Nogah and Nepheg and Ianouou,

**1 Chronicles 14:7**

and Elishama and Beeliada and Elpalet.

**1 Chronicles 14:8**

And Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, and all Philistines went up to seek David, and David heard and went out to meet them.

**1 Chronicles 14:9**

And Philistines came and fell upon the valley of giants.

**1 Chronicles 14:10**

And David inquired through God, saying, Shall I go up against Philistines, and will you give them into my hands? And the Lord said to him, Go up, and I will give them into your hands.

**1 Chronicles 14:11**

And he went up to Baalpharasin, and David struck them there. And David said, God broke through my enemies by my hand like the breaking of waters. Therefore name of that place was called Breach-of-Pharasin.

**1 Chronicles 14:12**

And they left their gods there, and David said to burn them with fire.

**1 Chronicles 14:13**

And Philistines added yet again and again fell upon the valley of giants.

**1 Chronicles 14:14**

And David again inquired of God, and God said to him, You shall not go after them; turn away from them and come upon them near pear trees.

**1 Chronicles 14:15**

And when you hear the sound of shaking in tops of pear trees, then you shall go out into battle, because God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines.

**1 Chronicles 14:16**

And he did as God commanded him, and he struck the camp of the Philistines from Gibeon as far as Gezer.

**1 Chronicles 14:17**

And the name of David became in all the land, and the Lord put his fear upon all nations.

#### Chapter 15

**1 Chronicles 15:1**

And he made houses for himself in the City of David, and he prepared place for the ark of God and made tent for it.

**1 Chronicles 15:2**

Then David said, It is not for any to carry the ark of God except Levites, because the Lord chose them to carry the ark of the Lord and to minister to him forever.

**1 Chronicles 15:3**

And David assembled all Israel in Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the Lord to place which he prepared for it.

**1 Chronicles 15:4**

And David gathered sons of Aaron and Levites:

**1 Chronicles 15:5**

from the sons of Kohath, Uriel chief, and his brothers, one hundred twenty;

**1 Chronicles 15:6**

from the sons of Merari, Asaiah chief, and his brothers, two hundred fifty;

**1 Chronicles 15:7**

from the sons of Gershom, Joel chief, and his brothers, one hundred fifty;

**1 Chronicles 15:8**

from the sons of Elzaphan, Shemaiah chief, and his brothers, two hundred;

**1 Chronicles 15:9**

from the sons of Hebron, Eliel chief, and his brothers, eighty;

**1 Chronicles 15:10**

from the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab chief, and his brothers, one hundred twelve.

**1 Chronicles 15:11**

**1 Chronicles 15:12**

**1 Chronicles 15:13**

**1 Chronicles 15:14**

**1 Chronicles 15:15**

**1 Chronicles 15:16**

**1 Chronicles 15:18**

and with them their brothers of second rank: Zechariah and Uzziel and Shemiramoth and Jehiel and Unni and Eliab and Benaiah and Maaseiah and Maaseiah and Eliphalia and Makenia and Obededom and Jeiel and Uzziah, gatekeepers.

**1 Chronicles 15:19**

And singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan had bronze cymbals to make sound heard.

**1 Chronicles 15:20**

Zechariah and Uzziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Masaias, Benaiah, with harps on alamoth.

**1 Chronicles 15:21**

And Mattathias and Eliphalias and Makenias and Obededom and Jeiel and Uzziah with lyres on the eighth, to lead strongly.

**1 Chronicles 15:22**

**1 Chronicles 15:23**

**1 Chronicles 15:24**

**1 Chronicles 15:25**

And David and elders of Israel and commanders of thousands were going to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the house of Obededom with gladness.

**1 Chronicles 15:26**

**1 Chronicles 15:27**

**1 Chronicles 15:28**

**1 Chronicles 15:29**

**1 Chronicles 16:1**

**1 Chronicles 16:6**

and Benaiah and Uzziel the priests with trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.

**1 Chronicles 16:7**

**1 Chronicles 16:8**

**1 Chronicles 16:9**

**1 Chronicles 16:10**

**1 Chronicles 16:11**

**1 Chronicles 16:12**

**1 Chronicles 16:13**

seed of Israel, his servants, sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.

**1 Chronicles 16:14**

**1 Chronicles 16:15**

**1 Chronicles 16:16**

**1 Chronicles 16:17**

**1 Chronicles 16:18**

**1 Chronicles 16:25**

**1 Chronicles 16:26**

**1 Chronicles 16:27**

**1 Chronicles 16:28**

**1 Chronicles 16:29**

**1 Chronicles 16:34**

**1 Chronicles 16:35**

**1 Chronicles 16:36**

**1 Chronicles 16:37**

**1 Chronicles 16:39**

**1 Chronicles 16:41**

and with him Heman and Jeduthun and rest of chosen ones named by name to praise the Lord, because his mercy is forever,
