to Harim, Adna; to Meraioth, Helkai;

**Nehemiah 12:16**

to Addai, Zechariah; to Ginnethon, Meshullam;

**Nehemiah 12:17**

to Abijah, Zichri; to Benjamin, in times; to Piltai,

**Nehemiah 12:18**

to Bilgah, Shammua; to Shemaiah, Jonathan;

**Nehemiah 12:19**

to Joiarib, Mattenai; to Jedaiah, Uzzi;

**Nehemiah 12:20**

to Sallai, Kallai; to Amok, Ebed;

**Nehemiah 12:21**

to Hilkiah, Hashabiah; to Iedeiou, Nathanael.

**Nehemiah 12:22**

The Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua were written as heads of fathers, and the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian.

**Nehemiah 12:23**

Sons of Levi, heads of fathers, were written in the book of words of the days until days of Johanan son of Eliashib.

**Nehemiah 12:24**

And leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah and Sherebiah and Jeshua and sons of Kadmiel, and their brothers opposite them, to hymn and praise by the command of David man of God, course by course.

**Nehemiah 12:25**

When I was gathering the gatekeepers.

**Nehemiah 12:26**

In the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah and Ezra the priest, the scribe.

**Nehemiah 12:27**

And at the dedication of wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in their places, to bring them into Jerusalem to make dedication and rejoicing, in thanksgiving and in songs, with cymbals and stringed instruments and lyres.

**Nehemiah 12:28**

And the sons of the singers were gathered both from the district round about into Jerusalem and from the farmsteads,

**Nehemiah 12:29**

and from the fields, because the singers built farmsteads for themselves in Jerusalem.

**Nehemiah 12:30**

And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gatekeepers and the wall.

**Nehemiah 12:31**

And I brought up rulers of Judah upon the wall and set two great thanksgiving choirs, and they went to the right upon the wall by the Dung Gate.

**Nehemiah 12:32**

And after them went Hoshaiah and half of rulers of Judah,

**Nehemiah 12:33**

and Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,

**Nehemiah 12:34**

Judah and Benjamin and Shemaiah and Jeremiah,

**Nehemiah 12:35**

and from the sons of the priests with trumpets, Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,

**Nehemiah 12:36**

and his brothers, Shemaiah and Uzziel, praising in songs of David man of God, and Ezra the scribe before them,

**Nehemiah 12:37**

at Gate of Ain opposite them. They went up on steps of the city of David, on the ascent of the wall above the house of David and as far as Water Gate eastward.

**Nehemiah 12:38**

And the second thanksgiving choir was going to meet them, and I after it, and half of the people upon the wall above Tower of Ovens and as far as Broad Wall,

**Nehemiah 12:39**

and above the Gate of Ephraim and to the Old Gate and to Fish Gate and Tower of Hananeel and as far as Sheep Gate, and they stood in Gate of the Guard.

**Nehemiah 12:40**

And the two choirs stood in the house of God, and I and half of the generals with me,

**Nehemiah 12:41**

and the priests, Eliakim, Maaseiah, Benjamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, Ananias, with trumpets,

**Nehemiah 12:42**

and Maaseiah and Shemaiah and Eleazar and Uzzi and Jehohanan and Malchiah and Elam and Ezour. And the singers were heard, and they were appointed.

**Nehemiah 12:43**

And they sacrificed on that day great sacrifices and rejoiced, because God gladdened them greatly, and their wives and their children rejoiced, and rejoicing in Jerusalem was heard from far away.

**Nehemiah 12:44**

And on that day men were appointed over the treasury-rooms, for the treasures, the firstfruits, the tithes, and the things gathered in them by rulers of the cities, portions for the priests and for the Levites, because rejoicing was in Judah over the priests and over the Levites who stood.

**Nehemiah 12:45**

And they kept charges of their God and charges of the purification and the singers and the gatekeepers, as commands of David and Solomon his son.

**Nehemiah 12:46**

For in the days of David, Asaph from the beginning was the chief of the singers, and there was hymn and praise to God.

**Nehemiah 12:47**

And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel were giving portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, matter of each day on its day, and sanctifying for the Levites, and the Levites sanctifying for the sons of Aaron.

#### Chapter 13

**Nehemiah 13:1**

On that day it was read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people, and it was found written in it that Ammonites and Moabites should not enter into assembly of God forever,

**Nehemiah 13:2**

because they did not meet sons of Israel with bread and water, and they hired Balaam against him to curse him, and our God turned the curse into blessing.

**Nehemiah 13:3**

And it came to be when they heard the law, they separated every mixed group in Israel.

**Nehemiah 13:4**

And before this, Eliashib the priest was dwelling in treasury-room of the house of our God, being near to Tobiah,

**Nehemiah 13:5**

and he made for him a great treasury-room, and there they formerly gave the manna and the frankincense and the vessels and the tithe of grain and wine and oil, the command for the Levites and the singers and the gatekeepers, and firstfruits of the priests.

**Nehemiah 13:6**

And in all this I was not in Jerusalem, because in thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I came to the king, and after the end of days I asked leave from the king.

**Nehemiah 13:7**

And I came to Jerusalem and understood the evil which Eliashib did for Tobiah, making for him a treasury-room in the court of the house of God.

**Nehemiah 13:8**

And it seemed very evil to me, and I threw all vessels of the house of Tobiah outside the treasury-room.

**Nehemiah 13:9**

And I said, and they purified the treasury-rooms, and I restored there vessels of the house of God, the manna, and the frankincense.

**Nehemiah 13:10**

And I knew that portions of the Levites had not been given, and the Levites and the singers doing the work fled, each man to his own field.

**Nehemiah 13:11**

And I contended with the generals and said, Why was the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them and set them in their standing.

**Nehemiah 13:12**

And all Judah brought tithe of the grain and the wine and the oil into the treasuries.

**Nehemiah 13:13**

Over the hand of Shelemiah the priest and Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah from the Levites, and over their hand Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah, because they were reckoned faithful to divide to their brothers.

**Nehemiah 13:14**

Remember me, O God, in this, and let not my mercy be wiped out, which I did in the house of the Lord God.

**Nehemiah 13:15**

In those days I saw in Judah men treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing sheaves and loading them on the donkeys, and wine and grapes and figs and every burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on Sabbath day, and I testified on the day of their selling.

**Nehemiah 13:16**

And they were dwelling in it, bringing fish and every kind of merchandise, selling on the Sabbath to the sons of Judah and in Jerusalem.

**Nehemiah 13:17**

And I contended with the sons of Judah, the free men, and said to them, What is this evil thing you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day?

**Nehemiah 13:18**

Did not your fathers do thus, and our God brought all these evils upon them and upon us and upon this city? And you add wrath upon Israel by profaning the Sabbath.

**Nehemiah 13:19**

And it came to be when the gates of Jerusalem were set before the Sabbath, I gave word and they shut the gates, and I said that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And from my servants I set some over the gates, so that no burden be brought in on Sabbath day.

**Nehemiah 13:20**

And all the traders and sellers of merchandise lodged outside Jerusalem once and twice.

**Nehemiah 13:21**

And I testified among them and said to them, Why do you lodge opposite the wall? If you do this a second time, I will stretch out my hand against you. From that time they did not come on the Sabbath.

**Nehemiah 13:22**

And I told the Levites, those being purified and coming to guard the gates, to sanctify the Sabbath day. Concerning these things remember me, O God, and spare me according to the abundance of your mercy.

**Nehemiah 13:23**

And in those days I saw the Jews who had seated Ashdodite, Ammonite, and Moabite women.

**Nehemiah 13:24**

And half of their sons were speaking Ashdodite and were not recognizing how to speak Ioudaian.

**Nehemiah 13:25**

And I contended with them and cursed them and struck men among them and made them bald, and made them swear by God that you will not give your daughters to their sons and will not take from their daughters for your sons.

**Nehemiah 13:26**

Did not Solomon king of Israel sin thus? And among many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by God, and God gave him as king over all Israel, yet foreign women turned even him aside.

**Nehemiah 13:27**

And shall we listen to you to do all this evil, to act faithlessly toward our God, seating foreign women?

**Nehemiah 13:28**

And from the sons of Joiada, of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, and I drove him out from me.

**Nehemiah 13:29**

Remember them, O God, for kinship with the priesthood and covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.

**Nehemiah 13:30**

And I purified them from every foreign thing and set courses for the priests and for the Levites, each man as his work,

**Nehemiah 13:31**

and the gift of the wood-bearers at appointed times, year by year, and in the firstfruits. Remember me, O our God, for goodness.

### Esther

#### Chapter 1

**Esther 1:1**

And it came to be after these words, in the days of Artaxerxes, this Artaxerxes ruled from India over one hundred twenty-seven provinces.

**Esther 1:2**

In those days, when King Artaxerxes was enthroned in Shushan the city,

**Esther 1:3**

in the third year of his reign he made a feast for his friends and the rest of the nations and the nobles of Persia and Media and rulers of the satrapies,

**Esther 1:4**

and after this, after showing them wealth of his kingdom and glory of joy of his riches for one hundred eighty days,

**Esther 1:5**

when days of the marriage were fulfilled, the king made a drinking-feast for the nations found in the city for six days, in the court of the house of the king,

**Esther 1:6**

adorned with linen and carbasus stretched on linen and purple cords, on rings of gold and silver, on marble pillars, and couches of gold and silver on pavement of emerald stone and pearl and marble stone, and coverings transparent and variously flowered, with roses scattered around.

**Esther 1:7**

And golden and silver cups, and a carbuncle cup set forth worth thirty thousand talents. Wine was much and sweet, which the king himself drank.

**Esther 1:8**

And this drinking was not according to fixed law, for thus the king willed, and he ordered the stewards to do his pleasure and that of the men.

**Esther 1:9**

And Vashti the queen made a drinking-feast for the women in the royal house where King Artaxerxes was.

**Esther 1:10**

And on the seventh day, when the king became merry, he said to Aman and Bazan and Tharra and Bigtha and Abagtha and Abataza and Tharaba, the seven eunuchs serving King Artaxerxes,

**Esther 1:11**

to bring in the queen to him, to crown her and put the diadem on her and show her beauty to all the rulers and the nations, because she was beautiful.

**Esther 1:12**

And Vashti the queen would not listen to come with the eunuchs, and the king was grieved and enraged.

**Esther 1:13**

And he said to his friends, Thus Vashti has spoken. So make law and judgment concerning this.

**Esther 1:14**

And Arkesaios and Sarsathaios and Marsena approached him, rulers of Persians and Medes, those near the king, first seated beside the king,

**Esther 1:15**

and they reported to him according to the laws what ought to be done to Vashti the queen, because she did not do what was commanded by the king through the eunuchs.

**Esther 1:16**

And Memucan said to the king and the rulers, Not against the king only did Vashti the queen do wrong, but also against all the rulers and leaders of the king.

**Esther 1:17**

For he recounted to them words of the queen and how she contradicted the king, even as she contradicted King Artaxerxes.

**Esther 1:18**

Thus today the remaining princesses of rulers of Persia and Media, hearing what she said to the king, will likewise dare to dishonor their husbands.

**Esther 1:19**

If then it seems good to the king, let him issue a royal command and let it be written among laws of Medes and Persians and not otherwise used, that the queen enter to him no more, and let the king give her royal place to a woman better than she.

**Esther 1:20**

And let the law which the king makes be heard in his kingdom, and thus all women will give honor to their husbands, from poor to rich.

**Esther 1:21**

And the word pleased the king and the rulers, and the king did as Memucan spoke.

**Esther 1:22**

And he sent into all the kingdom, province by province in their own language, so that there might be fear in their houses.

#### Chapter 2

**Esther 2:1**

And after these words the king ceased from wrath and no longer remembered Vashti, remembering what she said and how he condemned her.

**Esther 2:2**

And the servants of the king said, Let incorrupt young girls, beautiful in appearance, be sought for the king.

**Esther 2:3**

And let the king appoint local rulers in all provinces of his kingdom, and let them choose virgin girls, beautiful in appearance, into Shushan the city, into the women's house, and let them be delivered to eunuch of the king, keeper of the women, and let cosmetics and the rest of care be given.

**Esther 2:4**

And the woman who pleases the king shall reign instead of Vashti. And the matter pleased the king, and he did thus.

**Esther 2:5**

And there was a Jewish man in Shushan the city, and his name was Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin,

**Esther 2:6**

who was a captive from Jerusalem, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon carried away captive.

**Esther 2:7**

And he had a foster-child, daughter of Amminadab his father's brother, and her name was Esther. And after her parents died he trained her for himself as a wife, and the girl was beautiful in appearance.

**Esther 2:8**

And when command of the king was heard, many girls were gathered into Shushan the city under the hand of Hegai, and Esther was led to Hegai, keeper of the women.

**Esther 2:9**

And the girl pleased him and found favor before him, and he hurried to give her the cosmetics and the portion and the seven girls appointed to her from the royal house, and he treated her and her maidservants well in the women's house.

**Esther 2:10**

And Esther did not reveal her race or her homeland, for Mordecai commanded her not to report it.

**Esther 2:11**

And every day Mordecai walked around the women's court, looking to see what would happen to Esther.

**Esther 2:12**

And this was the time for a girl to go in to the king, when she completed twelve months, for thus the days of treatment are completed: six months being anointed with the oil of myrrh and six months with spices and with the women's cosmetics.

**Esther 2:13**

And then she goes in to the king, and whatever she says will be given to her to go in with her from the women's house as far as the royal rooms.

**Esther 2:14**

In evening she goes in, and by day she returns to the second women's house, where Shaashgaz the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, is, and she no longer goes in to the king unless called by name.

**Esther 2:15**

And when time of Esther, daughter of Amminadab the father's brother of Mordecai, was fulfilled to go in to the king, she rejected nothing of what Hegai the eunuch, keeper of the women, commanded her. For Esther was finding favor from all seeing her.

**Esther 2:16**

And Esther went in to Artaxerxes the king in the twelfth month, which is Adar, in the seventh year of his reign.

**Esther 2:17**

And the king loved Esther, and she found favor beyond all the virgins, and he put upon her the woman's diadem.

**Esther 2:18**

And the king made a feast for all his friends and the forces for seven days, and exalted wedding of Esther and made a remission for those under his kingdom.

**Esther 2:19**

And Mordecai was serving in the court.

**Esther 2:20**

And Esther did not reveal her homeland, for thus Mordecai commanded her to fear God and do his commandments, just as when she was with him, and Esther did not change her conduct.

**Esther 2:21**

And the two eunuchs of the king, chief bodyguards, were grieved because Mordecai had been promoted, and they sought to kill Artaxerxes the king.

**Esther 2:22**

And the matter became known to Mordecai, and he signaled it to Esther, and she made known to the king the details of the plot.

**Esther 2:23**

And the king examined the two eunuchs and hanged them, and the king ordered it to be recorded for remembrance in the royal library concerning the favor of Mordecai, with praise.

#### Chapter 3

**Esther 3:1**

And after these things King Artaxerxes honored Aman son of Hammedatha the Agagite and exalted him and gave him first rank beyond all his friends.

**Esther 3:2**

And all in the court were bowing to him, for thus the king commanded it to be done, but Mordecai was not bowing to him.

**Esther 3:3**

And those in the court of the king said to Mordecai, Mordecai, why do you disregard things spoken by the king?

**Esther 3:4**

Every day they spoke to him, and he was not listening to them, and they reported Mordecai to Aman, as one opposing words of the king, and Mordecai showed them that he is a Jew.

**Esther 3:5**

And Aman, perceiving that Mordecai was not bowing to him, was enraged greatly.

**Esther 3:6**

And he planned to destroy all the Jews under kingdom of Artaxerxes.

**Esther 3:7**

And he made a decree in the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes and cast lots, day by day and month by month, so as to destroy the race of Mordecai in one day, and the lot fell on the fourteenth of the month, which is Adar.

**Esther 3:8**

And he spoke to King Artaxerxes, saying, There is a nation scattered among the nations in all your kingdom, and their laws differ from all nations, and they disregard laws of the king, and it is not advantageous for the king to let them remain.

**Esther 3:9**

If it seems good to the king, let it be decreed to destroy them, and I will write ten thousand talents of silver into the treasury of the king.

**Esther 3:10**

And the king removed the ring and gave it into the hand of Aman to seal against the writings against the Jews.

**Esther 3:11**

And the king said to Aman, Keep the silver, and use the nation as you wish.

**Esther 3:12**

And scribes of the king were called on the thirteenth of the first month, and they wrote as Aman commanded to the generals and the rulers over every province, from India to Ethiopia, to the one hundred twenty-seven provinces, and to the rulers of the nations in their own language, by Artaxerxes the king.

**Esther 3:13**

And it was sent by book-carriers into the kingdom of Artaxerxes to destroy the race of the Jews in one day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their goods.

**Esther 3:14**

Copies of the letters were posted province by province, and command was given to all the nations to be ready for this day.

**Esther 3:15**

And the matter was hurried, even in Shushan. But the king and Aman were drinking, while the city was troubled.

#### Chapter 4

**Esther 4:1**

And Mordecai, perceiving what was being carried out, tore his garments and put on sackcloth and sprinkled himself with ashes, and leaping through the broad place of the city he cried with a loud voice, A nation that did no wrong is being taken away.

**Esther 4:2**

And he came as far as the king's gate and stood, for it was not lawful for him to enter the court wearing sackcloth and ashes.

**Esther 4:3**

And in every province where the letters were posted, there was cry and beating and great mourning for the Jews. They spread sackcloth and ashes for themselves.

**Esther 4:4**

And maidservants and eunuchs of the queen came in and reported to her, and hearing what happened she was troubled, and she sent to clothe Mordecai and take away the sackcloth from him, but he was not persuaded.

**Esther 4:5**

And Esther called Hathach her eunuch, who stood by her, and sent to learn from Mordecai the exact truth.

**Esther 4:7**

And Mordecai showed him what had happened and the promise which Aman promised to the king, ten thousand talents to the treasury, so as to destroy the Jews.

**Esther 4:8**

And he gave him copy of the notice posted in Shushan for their destruction, to show Esther, and he told him to command her, after going in, to plead with the king and urge him for the people, remembering days of your humiliation, how you were nourished in my hand, because Aman, the second to the kingdom, has spoken against us for death. Call upon the Lord and speak to the king concerning us and rescue us from death.

**Esther 4:9**

And Hathach went in and spoke to her all these words.

**Esther 4:10**

And Esther said to Hathach, Go to Mordecai and say that

**Esther 4:11**

all nations of the kingdom know that every man or woman who enters to the king in the inner court uncalled has no salvation, except the one to whom the king stretches out the golden scepter, that one will be saved. And I have not been called to go in to the king these thirty days.

**Esther 4:12**

And Hathach reported to Mordecai all words of Esther.

**Esther 4:13**

And Mordecai said to Hathach, Go and tell Esther, Do not say to yourself that you alone in the kingdom will be saved beyond all the Jews.

**Esther 4:14**

For if you disregard in this time, help and shelter will be for the Jews from another place, but you and house of your father will perish. And who knows whether for this very time you came to reign?

**Esther 4:15**

And Esther sent back the one who came to her, to Mordecai, saying,

**Esther 4:16**

Go, gather the Jews in Shushan and fast for me, and do not eat or drink for three days, night and day. And I and my maidservants will likewise go without food, and then I will go in to the king contrary to the law. If then I must perish, I will perish.

**Esther 4:17**

And Mordecai went and did all that Esther commanded him.

#### Chapter 5

**Esther 5:1**

And it happened on the third day, when she ceased praying, she took off garments of service and put on her glory.

**Esther 5:2**

And after lifting the golden scepter she placed it on her neck and kissed it and said, Speak to me.

**Esther 5:3**

And the king said, What do you want, Esther, and what is your request? Even to half of my kingdom, it shall be yours.

**Esther 5:4**

And Esther said, My marked day is today. If then it seems good to the king, let him and Aman come to the feast which I will make today.

**Esther 5:5**

And the king said, Hasten Aman, so that we may do word of Esther. And both came to the feast which Esther spoke of.

**Esther 5:6**

And during the drinking the king said to Esther, What is it, Queen Esther? It shall be yours, whatever you ask.

**Esther 5:7**

And she said, My petition and my request are this:

**Esther 5:8**

If I found favor before the king, let the king and Aman come tomorrow to the feast which I will make for them, and tomorrow I will do the same things.

**Esther 5:9**

And Aman went out from the king overjoyed and rejoicing. But when Aman saw Mordecai the Jew in the court, he was enraged greatly.

**Esther 5:10**

And after entering his own house he called his friends and Zeresh his wife.

**Esther 5:11**

And he showed them his wealth and the honor which the king placed on him and how he made him hold first place and lead the kingdom.

**Esther 5:12**

And Aman said, The queen called no one to the feast with the king except me, and for tomorrow I have been called.

**Esther 5:13**

And these things do not please me whenever I see Mordecai the Jew in the court.

**Esther 5:14**

And Zeresh his wife and the friends said to him, Let a timber of fifty cubits be cut for you, and in the morning speak to the king, and let Mordecai be hanged on the timber. But you go into the feast with the king and rejoice. And the word pleased Aman, and the timber was prepared.

#### Chapter 6

**Esther 6:1**

But the Lord drove sleep away from the king in that night, and he told his teacher to bring in memorial records of the days, to read to him.

**Esther 6:2**

And he found the writings written concerning Mordecai, how he reported to the king about the two eunuchs of the king while they were guarding him and seeking to lay hands on Artaxerxes.

**Esther 6:3**

And the king said, What honor or favor have we done for Mordecai? And the servants of the king said, You did nothing for him.

**Esther 6:4**

And as the king was inquiring concerning the favor of Mordecai, behold Aman was in the court. And the king said, Who is in the court? And Aman came in to speak to the king to hang Mordecai on the timber which he prepared.

**Esther 6:5**

And the servants of the king said, Behold, Aman stands in the court. And the king said, Call him.

**Esther 6:6**

And the king said to Aman, What shall I do for the man whom I wish to honor? And Aman said in himself, Whom does the king wish to honor except me?

**Esther 6:7**

And he said to the king, For the man whom the king wishes to honor,

**Esther 6:8**

let servants of the king bring linen robe which the king wears and horse on which the king rides,

**Esther 6:9**

and let one of the king's glorious friends give it, and let him robe the man whom the king loves and lift him upon the horse and proclaim through the broad place of the city, saying, Thus it shall be to every man whom the king honors.

**Esther 6:10**

And the king said to Aman, As you spoke, so do to Mordecai the Jew, who serves in the court, and let not one word of what you spoke fall away.

**Esther 6:11**

And Aman took the robe and the horse and robed Mordecai and lifted him upon the horse and went through the broad place of the city and proclaimed, saying, Thus it shall be to every man whom the king wishes to honor.

**Esther 6:12**

And Mordecai returned to the court, but Aman returned to his own house grieving, with head covered.

**Esther 6:13**

And Aman recounted to Zeresh his wife and to the friends what happened to him, and the friends and the wife said to him, If Mordecai is from race of Jews, you began to be humbled before him, and falling you will fall; you will never be able to resist him, because living God is with him.

**Esther 6:14**

While they were still speaking, the eunuchs arrived, hurrying Aman to the drinking-feast which Esther prepared.

#### Chapter 7

**Esther 7:1**

And the king and Aman went in to drink with the queen.

**Esther 7:2**

And on the second day during the drinking the king said, What is it, Queen Esther, and what is your petition and what is your request? Even to half of my kingdom, let it be yours.

**Esther 7:3**

And she answered and said, If I found favor before the king, let my life be given for my petition and my people for my request.

**Esther 7:4**

For I and my people were sold for destruction and plundering and slavery, we and our children, for boy-servants and girl-servants. And I kept silent, for the accuser is not worthy of the king's court.

**Esther 7:5**

And the king said, Who is this one who dared to do this thing?

**Esther 7:6**

And Esther said, An enemy, Aman, this evil one. And Aman was thrown into turmoil before the king and the queen.

**Esther 7:7**

And the king rose from the banquet into the garden, but Aman was begging the queen, for he saw himself in evils.

**Esther 7:8**

And the king returned from the garden. Aman had fallen on the couch, begging the queen. And the king said, So then will he even force the woman in my own house? And Aman, hearing, was struck in the face.

**Esther 7:9**

And Bouthathan, one of the eunuchs, said to the king, Behold, Aman also prepared a timber for Mordecai, the one who spoke for the king, and it stands in Aman's house, fifty cubits. And the king said, Let him be impaled on it.

**Esther 7:10**

And Aman was hanged on the timber which he prepared for Mordecai, and then the king ceased from wrath.

#### Chapter 8

**Esther 8:1**

And on that day King Artaxerxes gave to Esther all things that belonged to Aman the accuser, and Mordecai was called by the king, for Esther showed that he was related to her.

**Esther 8:2**

And the king took the ring which he removed from Aman and gave it to Mordecai, and Esther appointed Mordecai over all things of Aman.

**Esther 8:3**

And Esther added and spoke to the king and fell at his feet and asked him to remove evil of Aman and all he did against the Jews.

**Esther 8:4**

And the king stretched out to Esther the golden scepter. And Esther rose to stand by the king.

**Esther 8:5**

And Esther said, If it seems good to you and I found favor, let the letters sent by Aman be turned back, the ones written to destroy the Jews who are in your kingdom.

**Esther 8:6**

For how shall I be able to see mistreatment of my people? And how shall I be saved amid destruction of my homeland?

**Esther 8:7**

And the king said to Esther, If all things of Aman I gave and granted to you, and him I hanged on timber because he laid hands on the Jews, what do you still seek?

**Esther 8:8**

Write also yourselves in my name as seems good to you, and seal it with my ring. For whatever is written when the king commands and sealed with my ring, there is no contradicting it.

**Esther 8:9**

And the scribes were called in the first month, which is Nisan, on the twenty-third of that year, and it was written for the Jews what he commanded to the administrators and rulers of the satrapies, from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven satrapies, province by province in its own language.

**Esther 8:10**

And it was written through the king and sealed with his ring, and they sent the letters through book-carriers,

**Esther 8:11**

just as he commanded them to use their laws in every city, to help themselves and deal with their adversaries and those opposing them as they wish,

**Esther 8:12**

on one day in all kingdom of Artaxerxes, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, which is Adar.

**Esther 8:13**

And let copies be publicly posted in all the kingdom, and let all the Jews be ready for this day to fight those set against them.

**Esther 8:14**

So the riders went out hurrying to fulfill what the king spoke, and the decree was also posted in Shushan.

**Esther 8:15**

And Mordecai went out clothed in royal robe and wearing golden crown and linen purple diadem, and those in Shushan, seeing, rejoiced.

**Esther 8:16**

And for the Jews there came light and gladness,

**Esther 8:17**

in each city and province wherever the decree and notice were posted, joy and gladness came for the Jews, a feast and rejoicing, and many of the nations were circumcised and became Ioudaizing because of fear of the Jews.

#### Chapter 9

**Esther 9:1**

For in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth of the month, which is Adar, the letters written by the king were at hand.

**Esther 9:2**

On that day those opposing the Jews were destroyed, for no one stood against them, fearing them.

**Esther 9:3**

For rulers of the satrapies and the tyrants and the king's scribes were honoring the Jews, for fear of Mordecai was pressing upon them.

**Esther 9:4**

For decree of the king had fallen that his name be spoken in all the kingdom.

**Esther 9:6**

And in Shushan the city the Jews killed five hundred men,

**Esther 9:7**

both Parshandatha and Dalphon and Pisgah,

**Esther 9:8**

and Poratha and Adalia and Sarbacha,

**Esther 9:9**

and Parmashta and Arisai and Aridai and Vaizatha,

**Esther 9:10**

the ten sons of Aman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, enemy of the Jews, and they plundered.

**Esther 9:11**

On that day the number of the slain in Shushan was reported to the king.

**Esther 9:12**

And the king said to Esther, The Jews destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the city, and in the district how do you think they acted? What more do you request? And it shall be yours.

**Esther 9:13**

And Esther said to the king, Let it be given to the Jews to act likewise tomorrow, and to hang the ten sons of Aman.

**Esther 9:14**

And he permitted it to happen thus and ordered bodies of Aman's sons to be hung for the Jews of the city.

**Esther 9:15**

And the Jews were gathered in Shushan on the fourteenth of Adar and killed three hundred men, and they plundered nothing.

**Esther 9:16**

And the rest of the Jews in the kingdom gathered and were helping themselves, and they rested from the war. For they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth of Adar and plundered nothing.

**Esther 9:17**

And they rested on the fourteenth of the same month and kept it as day of rest with joy and gladness.

**Esther 9:18**

But the Jews in Shushan the city were gathered on the fourteenth and did not rest, but kept the fifteenth with joy and gladness.

**Esther 9:19**

Therefore the Jews scattered in every country outside keep the fourteenth of Adar as a good day with joy, sending portions each to his neighbor, and those dwelling in the capitals keep also the fifteenth of Adar as a good day of rejoicing, sending portions to neighbors.

**Esther 9:20**

And Mordecai wrote these words into a book and sent to the Jews, as many as were in the kingdom of Artaxerxes, both near and far,

**Esther 9:21**

to establish these good days, to keep both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,

**Esther 9:22**

for in these days the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month in which, being Adar, it was turned for them from mourning into joy and from grief into a good day, to keep all as good days of marriages and rejoicing, sending portions to friends and to the poor.

**Esther 9:23**

And the Jews accepted it, just as Mordecai wrote to them,

**Esther 9:24**

how Aman son of Hammedatha the Macedonian warred against them, as he made decree and lot to destroy them,

**Esther 9:25**

and how he entered to the king, saying to hang Mordecai. But the evils which he attempted to bring upon the Jews came upon him, and he and his children were hanged.

**Esther 9:26**

Therefore these days were called Purim because of the lots, for in their language they call them Purim, because of words of this letter and what they suffered because of these things and what happened to them.

**Esther 9:27**

And the Jews established and accepted it upon themselves and upon their seed and upon those added to them, and they will use no other way, but these days will be a memorial kept generation by generation and city and father-house and province.

**Esther 9:28**

And these days of Purim will be kept for all time, and their memorial shall never fail from the generations.

**Esther 9:29**

And Esther the queen, daughter of Amminadab, and Mordecai the Jew wrote all that they did, even the confirming of the letter of Purim.

**Esther 9:31**

And Mordecai and Esther the queen established for themselves by themselves, and then after establishing according to their safety and their counsel,

**Esther 9:32**

Esther established by word forever, and it was written for remembrance.

#### Chapter 10

**Esther 10:1**

And the king wrote taxes upon the kingdom of both land and sea.

**Esther 10:2**

And his strength and bravery and the wealth and glory of his kingdom, behold, these are written in the book of kings of Persia and Media for remembrance.

**Esther 10:3**

And Mordecai succeeded King Artaxerxes and was great in the kingdom and glorified by the Jews and loved, recounting the way of life to all his nation.

### Job

#### Chapter 1

**Job 1:1**

There was a certain man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job, and that man was true, blameless, righteous, god-fearing, turning away from every evil thing.

**Job 1:2**

And there came to him seven sons and three daughters.

**Job 1:3**

And his livestock was seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred grazing she-donkeys, and very much service, and great works were his upon the land. And that man was noblest of those from sunrise.

**Job 1:4**

And his sons, going to one another, were making a feast each day, bringing along also their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

**Job 1:5**

And when days of the feast were completed, Job sent and purified them. Rising early, he offered sacrifices for them according to their number, and one calf for sin concerning their souls. For Job said, Lest my sons thought evil things in their mind toward God. Thus Job was doing all the days.

**Job 1:6**

And when this day came, behold, angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the slanderer came with them.

**Job 1:7**

And the Lord said to the slanderer, From where are you here? And answering, the slanderer said to the Lord, After going around the earth and walking about under heaven, I am here.

**Job 1:8**

And the Lord said to him, Did you set your mind against my servant Job, because there is no man like him on the earth, blameless, true, god-fearing, turning away from every evil thing?

**Job 1:9**

And the slanderer answered and said before the Lord, Does Job fear God for nothing?

**Job 1:10**

Did you not fence in things outside him and inside his house and outside all that belongs to him round about? The works of his hands you blessed, and his cattle you made many upon the earth.

**Job 1:11**

But stretch out your hand and touch all that he has, and surely he will bless you to your face.

**Job 1:12**

Then the Lord said to the slanderer, Behold, all things that are his I give into your hand, only do not touch him. And the slanderer went out from the Lord.

**Job 1:13**

And it happened on a day when Job's sons and daughters were drinking wine in the house of their elder brother,

**Job 1:14**

and behold, a messenger came to Job and said to him, The yoke of oxen were plowing, and the she-donkeys were grazing beside them,

**Job 1:15**

and the raiders came and took them captive, and the servants they killed with swords. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

**Job 1:16**

While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and devoured the shepherds likewise. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

**Job 1:17**

While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, The horsemen made against us three heads, and they surrounded the camels and took them captive, and the servants they killed with swords. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

**Job 1:18**

While this one was still speaking, another messenger came, saying to Job, Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking at their elder brother's house,

**Job 1:19**

and suddenly a great wind came from the wilderness and touched the four corners of the house, and the house fell on your children, and they died. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

**Job 1:20**

So Job rose, tore his garments, shaved hair of his head, and falling to the ground worshiped and said,

**Job 1:21**

Naked I came out from the womb of my mother, naked also I will go away there. The Lord gave, the Lord took away. As it seemed good to the Lord, so also it came to pass. Let the name of the Lord be blessed.

**Job 1:22**

In all these things that happened to him, Job sinned in nothing before the Lord and gave no folly to God.

#### Chapter 2

**Job 2:1**

And it came to be on this day also that angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the slanderer came among them to stand before the Lord.

**Job 2:2**

And the Lord said to the slanderer, From where do you come? Then the slanderer said before the Lord, After passing through what is under heaven and walking all around, I am here.

**Job 2:3**

And the Lord said to the slanderer, Did you then give attention to my servant Job, because there is no man like him on the earth, innocent, true, blameless, god-fearing, turning away from every evil, and he still holds fast his innocence? Yet you spoke against his possessions to destroy them for nothing.

**Job 2:4**

And taking up the matter, the slanderer said to the Lord, Skin for skin, all things a man has he will pay for his life.

**Job 2:5**

But stretch out your hand and touch his bones and his flesh, and surely he will bless you to your face.

**Job 2:6**

And the Lord said to the slanderer, Behold, I hand him over to you; only preserve his life.

**Job 2:7**

And the slanderer went out from the Lord and struck Job with a grievous sore from feet to head.

**Job 2:8**

And he took a potsherd to scrape the discharge, and he sat upon the dung-heap outside the city.

**Job 2:9**

And when much time had passed, his wife said to him, How long will you endure, saying, Behold, I wait yet a little time, expecting hope of my deliverance? For behold, your memorial has vanished from the earth, sons and daughters of my womb, pangs and labors which I toiled for in vain with hardships. And you yourself sit in decay of worms, passing the night in the open air. And I am a wanderer and servant, going from place to place and house to house, waiting for sun to set so that I may rest from labors and pains that now hold me fast. But speak some word to the Lord and die.

**Job 2:10**

And looking at her, he said to her, You spoke like one of the foolish women. If we accepted good things from the hand of the Lord, shall we not bear evil things? In all these things that happened to him, Job sinned in nothing with his lips before God.

**Job 2:11**

And hearing all the evils that came upon him, his three friends came, each from his own country, to him: Eliphaz the Temanite king, Bildad the Sauchaian tyrant, and Zophar the Naamathite king. And they came to him with one purpose, to encourage and visit him.

**Job 2:12**

And seeing him from far off, they did not recognize him, and crying with a loud voice they wept, each tearing his own robe and scattering dust.

**Job 2:13**

They sat with him seven days and seven nights, and none of them spoke, for they saw that the blow was dreadful and very great.

#### Chapter 3

**Job 3:1**

After this Job opened his mouth

**Job 3:2**

and cursed his day, saying,

**Job 3:3**

Let the day perish in which I was born, and the night in which they said, Behold, a male.

**Job 3:4**

Let that day be darkness, and let not the Lord seek it from above, nor let light come upon it.

**Job 3:5**

Let darkness and the shadow of death take it. Let gloom come upon it.

**Job 3:6**

Let the day and that night be cursed. Let darkness take it away. Let it not be among days of the year, nor counted among days of months.

**Job 3:7**

But let that night be pain, and let no gladness come upon it, nor joy.

**Job 3:8**

But let the one cursing that day curse it, the one preparing to master the great sea-beast.

**Job 3:9**

Let stars of that night be darkened. Let it wait and not come into light, nor see morning-star rising,

**Job 3:10**

because it did not shut gates of my mother's womb, for then it would have removed pain from my eyes.

**Job 3:11**

For why did I not die in the belly? And coming out from the womb, why did I not immediately perish?

**Job 3:12**

Why then did knees meet me? And why breasts, that I sucked?

**Job 3:13**

Now, having lain down, I would have been quiet. Having slept, I would have rested

**Job 3:14**

with kings, counselors of earth, who gloried themselves over swords,

**Job 3:15**

or with rulers whose gold was much, who filled their houses with silver,

**Job 3:16**

or like miscarriage coming out from the womb of a mother, or like infants who never saw light.

**Job 3:17**

There the ungodly burned out rage of wrath. There the weary in body rested.

**Job 3:18**

And there the eternal ones together did not hear the voice of tax-collector.

**Job 3:19**

Small and great are there, and servant not fearing his lord.

**Job 3:20**

Why then is light given to those in bitterness, and life to souls in pains,

**Job 3:21**

who long for death and do not obtain it, digging for it as for treasures,

**Job 3:22**

who become overjoyed if they should attain it?

**Job 3:23**

Death is rest for a man, for God shut in against him.

**Job 3:24**

For before my food, groaning comes to me, and I weep, being held fast by fear.

**Job 3:25**

For fear which I pondered came upon me, and what I dreaded met me.

**Job 3:26**

I neither had peace nor was quiet nor rested, but wrath came to me.

#### Chapter 4

**Job 4:1**

And taking up the matter, Eliphaz the Temanite says,

**Job 4:2**

Were many times spoken to you in distress? But strength of your words, who will bear?

**Job 4:3**

For you instructed many and encouraged weak hands.

**Job 4:4**

And those failing you raised up by words, and upon knees without strength you put courage.

**Job 4:5**

But now pain comes upon you and touches you, and you were hasty.

**Job 4:6**

Is not your fear foolishness, and your hope, and innocence of your way?

**Job 4:7**

Remember then, who being pure perished? Or when did true men perish root and all?

**Job 4:8**

In the way I saw, those plowing improper things and those sowing them will reap pains for themselves.

**Job 4:9**

By the command of the Lord they will perish, and by breath of his wrath they will be wiped out.

**Job 4:10**

The strength of a lion, the voice of a lioness, and boast of dragons were quenched.

**Job 4:11**

Ant-lion perished for not having food, and lion cubs abandoned one another.

**Job 4:12**

But if any true word happened in your sayings, none of these evils would ever have met you. Will not my ear receive strange things from him?

**Job 4:13**

But fears and the sound of night, fear falling on men,

**Job 4:14**

dread met me and trembling, and greatly my bones shook together.

**Job 4:15**

And a spirit came upon my face, and my hairs and flesh shuddered.

**Job 4:16**

I stood up and did not recognize; I looked, and there was no form before my eyes, but only a breeze, and I was hearing a voice:

**Job 4:17**

What then? Shall mortal be pure before the Lord, or shall a man be blameless by his works?

**Job 4:18**

If he does not trust in his servants, and against his angels he devised something crooked,

**Job 4:19**

then those dwelling in the houses of clay, from which we also are from the same clay, he struck like a moth.

**Job 4:20**

And from morning until evening they no longer exist, because they were not able to help themselves. They perished.

**Job 4:21**

For he breathed on them and they dried up. They perished for not having wisdom.

#### Chapter 5

**Job 5:1**

But call, if anyone will hear you, or if you will see any of the holy angels.

**Job 5:2**

For anger kills the fool, and jealousy kills the wandering one.

**Job 5:3**

But I saw fools throwing down root, yet immediately their way of life was eaten up.

**Job 5:4**

Let their sons be far from deliverance, and let them be beaten at the doors of inferiors, and there will be no one rescuing.

**Job 5:5**

For what they gathered, righteous men will eat, but they themselves will not be delivered from evils. Let their strength be drained away.

**Job 5:6**

For toil will not come out from the earth, nor will pain sprout up from the mountains.

**Job 5:7**

But man is born for toil, and young vultures fly to the heights.

**Job 5:8**

Yet I will petition the Lord, and I will call on the Master of all.

**Job 5:9**

He does great and unsearchable things, glorious and extraordinary things beyond number,

**Job 5:10**

giving rain upon the earth, sending water upon what is under heaven,

**Job 5:11**

making lowly ones into height, raising up those who were lost,

**Job 5:12**

turning aside counsels of the crafty, and their hands will never do what is true,

**Job 5:13**

the one catching wise men in their cunning, and overthrowing counsel of the twisted,

**Job 5:14**

in daytime darkness will meet them, and at noon they will grope as in night.

**Job 5:15**

But let the weak perish in war, and let the powerless come out from the hand of the mighty.

**Job 5:16**

And let there be hope for the powerless, but mouth of the unrighteous be stopped.

**Job 5:17**

But blessed is man whom the Lord corrected; do not reject discipline of the Almighty.

**Job 5:18**

For he causes pain and again restores. He struck, and his hands healed.

**Job 5:19**

Six times from necessities he will deliver you, and in the seventh evil will not touch you.

**Job 5:20**

In famine he will rescue you from death, and in war he will free you from the hand of iron.

**Job 5:21**

From scourge of the tongue he will hide you, and you will not fear evils coming.

**Job 5:22**

You will laugh at unjust and lawless men, and you will not fear from wild beasts,

**Job 5:23**

for wild beasts will be at peace with you.

**Job 5:24**

Then you will know that your house will be at peace, and dwelling of your tent will never go wrong.

**Job 5:25**

And you will know that your seed is many, and your children will be like all-herbage of the field.

**Job 5:26**

And you will come to the grave like ripe grain harvested in its season, or like a heap of threshing floor gathered at its time.

**Job 5:27**

Behold, these things we searched out. These are what we heard. But you, know for yourself if you did anything.

#### Chapter 6

**Job 6:1**

And taking up the matter, Job says,

**Job 6:2**

If only someone might weigh my anger, and lift my pains together in balance.

**Job 6:3**

For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seashore; but, as it seems, my words are worthless.

**Job 6:4**

For arrows of the Lord are in my body, whose fury drinks up my blood; whenever I begin to speak, they stab me.

**Job 6:5**

For surely wild donkey does not cry for nothing, unless seeking grain; nor will ox bellow at manger while having fodder.

**Job 6:6**

Will bread be eaten without salt? Or is there taste in empty words?

**Job 6:7**

For my soul cannot cease, for I see my foods as stench, like smell of lion.

**Job 6:8**

If only my request might come, and the Lord might give my hope.

**Job 6:9**

Let the Lord begin and wound me; but in end let him not destroy me.

**Job 6:10**

Let my city be grave, upon whose walls I leaped; upon it I will by no means spare myself, for I did not lie about words of holy God.

**Job 6:11**

For what strength have I, that I keep enduring? Or what time remains for me, that my soul keeps bearing?

**Job 6:12**

Is my strength the strength of stones, or is my flesh bronze?

**Job 6:13**

Or was I not trusting in him? But help has gone far from me.

**Job 6:14**

Mercy renounced me, and visitation of the Lord overlooked me.

**Job 6:15**

My near ones did not regard me; like failing torrents, or like a wave they passed me by.

**Job 6:16**

Those who feared me before have now fallen upon me, like snow or frozen ice.

**Job 6:17**

As things melted when heat came, what they were was not recognized.

**Job 6:18**

Thus I too was abandoned by all; I perished and became homeless.

**Job 6:19**

Look at ways of Tema, paths of Sheba, those who look intently.

**Job 6:20**

They will owe shame, those trusting in cities and riches.

**Job 6:21**

But now you too fell upon me without mercy, so that seeing my wound you were afraid.

**Job 6:22**

For what? Did I ask anything from you, or do I need some of your strength?

**Job 6:23**

So as to save me from enemies, or rescue me from the hand of rulers?

**Job 6:24**

Teach me, and I will be silent; if I have gone astray, show me.

**Job 6:25**

As it seems, the words of truth are worthless, for I do not ask strength from you.

**Job 6:26**

Nor will your reproof stop me with words, for neither will I endure the sound of your speech.

**Job 6:27**

Only because you fall upon orphan, and spring against your friend.

**Job 6:28**

But now, looking into your faces, I will not lie.

**Job 6:29**

Sit down then, and let there not be injustice; and again come together with righteous judgment.

**Job 6:30**

For there is no injustice on my tongue; does not my throat ponder understanding?

#### Chapter 7

**Job 7:1**

Is not life of man on earth a trial, and his life like that of day-laborer?

**Job 7:2**

Like servant fearing his master and having attained shade, like a hired man waiting for his wage,

**Job 7:3**

so I too inherited empty months, and nights of pains were given me.

**Job 7:4**

If I lie down, I say, When day? and when I rise again, When evening? And I am full of pains from evening until morning.

**Job 7:5**

My body is mixed with rottenness of worms; I melt clods of earth, scraping off the discharge.

**Job 7:6**

My life is lighter than speech, and has perished in empty hope.

**Job 7:7**

Remember then that my life is breath, and my eye will no longer return to see good.

**Job 7:8**

Eye of one seeing me will not look on me; your eyes are on me, and I am no longer.

**Job 7:9**

Like cloud cleansed away from heaven, if man goes down to Hades, he will certainly not come up again.

**Job 7:10**

Nor will he ever return again to his own house, nor will his place know him anymore.

**Job 7:11**

But therefore neither will I spare my mouth; I will speak in distress, opening bitterness of my soul while hard pressed.

**Job 7:12**

Am I sea or dragon, that you set a guard over me?

**Job 7:13**

If I say, My bed will comfort me, and my couch will bear my complaint for me,

**Job 7:14**

then you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions.

**Job 7:15**

You will free my soul from breath, and my bones from death.

**Job 7:16**

For I will not live forever, that I should be patient. Depart from me, for my life is empty.

**Job 7:17**

What is man, that you magnified him, or that you set your mind on him,

**Job 7:18**

or make visitation of him until morning, and judge him for rest?

**Job 7:19**

Until when will you not let me be, nor release me until I swallow my spittle in pain?

**Job 7:20**

If I sinned, what can I do to you, knower of minds of men? Why did you set me as your accuser? And I have become burden to you.

**Job 7:21**

And why did you not make forgetfulness of my lawlessness and cleansing of my sin? For now I will depart into earth, and seeking me early, I am no more.

#### Chapter 8

**Job 8:1**

And taking up the matter, Bildad the Shuhite says,

**Job 8:2**

How long will you speak these things, wind of many words from your mouth?

**Job 8:3**

Will the Lord do injustice in judging, or will maker of all disturb what is right?

**Job 8:4**

If your sons sinned before him, he sent them away in the hand of their lawlessness.

**Job 8:5**

But you, rise early toward the Lord, begging Almighty.

**Job 8:6**

If you are pure and true, he will hear your petition and restore to you dwelling of righteousness.

**Job 8:7**

Then your first things will be few, but your last things beyond counting.

**Job 8:8**

Ask indeed former generation, and search out race of fathers.

**Job 8:9**

For we are of yesterday and do not know; for our life on earth is shadow.

**Job 8:10**

Will not these teach you and tell you, and bring out words from their heart?

**Job 8:11**

Does papyrus flourish without water, or will reed rise high without drink?

**Job 8:12**

While still on its root and not yet cut, before any herb drinks, does it not dry up?

**Job 8:13**

So then will be the end of all who forget the Lord, for the hope of the ungodly will perish.

**Job 8:14**

For his house will be uninhabited, and his tent will turn out to be spider's web.

**Job 8:15**

If he lean on his house, it will not stand; if he take hold of it, it will not endure.

**Job 8:16**

For it is moist under the sun, and from its decay its shoot will come out.

**Job 8:17**

It sleeps upon gathering of stones, and in the midst of pebbles it will live.

**Job 8:18**

If place swallow it up, it will deny it: You have not seen such things.

**Job 8:19**

For such is overthrow of the ungodly, and from earth another will sprout.

**Job 8:20**

**Job 8:21**

**Job 8:22**

But their enemies will clothe themselves with shame, and the dwelling of the ungodly will not be.

#### Chapter 9

**Job 9:1**

And taking up the matter, Job says,

**Job 9:2**

In truth I know that it is so; for how will a mortal be righteous before the Lord?

**Job 9:3**

**Job 9:4**

**Job 9:5**

**Job 9:6**

He who shakes what is under heaven from foundations, and its pillars totter.

**Job 9:7**

**Job 9:8**

**Job 9:9**

**Job 9:10**

**Job 9:11**

**Job 9:12**

**Job 9:13**

**Job 9:14**

**Job 9:15**

**Job 9:16**

**Job 9:17**

**Job 9:18**

**Job 9:19**

**Job 9:20**

Even if I am righteous, my mouth will act ungodly; if I am blameless, I will turn crooked.

**Job 9:21**

**Job 9:22**

**Job 9:23**

**Job 9:24**

**Job 9:25**

**Job 9:26**

**Job 9:27**

**Job 9:28**

**Job 9:29**

**Job 9:30**

**Job 9:31**

**Job 9:32**

**Job 9:33**

**Job 9:34**

Let him take his rod away from me, and let his fear not whirl me about.

**Job 9:35**

Then I would not fear, but speak, for I do not know myself so.

#### Chapter 10

**Job 10:1**

Weary in my soul, groaning, I will let my words go upon him; I will speak bitterness of my soul while hard pressed.

**Job 10:2**

And I will say to the Lord, Do not treat me as ungodly; teach me why you judged me thus.

**Job 10:3**

Is it good to you if I act unjustly, that you reject works of your hands, but give heed to the counsel of the ungodly?

**Job 10:4**

Do you look as mortal looks, or see as man sees?

**Job 10:5**

Is your life human, or your years those of man,

**Job 10:6**

that you searched out my lawlessness and tracked down my sins?

**Job 10:7**

For you know that I did not act ungodly, but there is none rescuing from your hands.

**Job 10:8**

**Job 10:9**

**Job 10:10**

Did you not milk me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?

**Job 10:11**

With skin and flesh you clothed me, and with bones and sinews you wove me.

**Job 10:12**

**Job 10:13**

Holding these things within yourself, I know that you can do all things, and nothing is impossible to you.

**Job 10:14**

If I sin, you watch me, and from lawlessness you did not make me innocent.

**Job 10:15**

If I am ungodly, woe to me; if I am righteous, I cannot lift myself up, for I am full of dishonor.

**Job 10:16**

**Job 10:17**

Renewing my examination against me, you used great wrath toward me and brought trials upon me.

**Job 10:18**

**Job 10:19**

**Job 10:20**

Is not time of my life small? Let me be, that I may rest a little,

**Job 10:21**

**Job 10:22**

into the land of eternal darkness, where there is no light, nor seeing of life among mortals.

#### Chapter 11

**Job 11:1**

And taking up the matter, Zophar the Naamathite says,

**Job 11:2**

**Job 11:3**

**Job 11:4**

**Job 11:5**

**Job 11:6**

**Job 11:7**

**Job 11:8**

**Job 11:9**

**Job 11:10**

**Job 11:11**

**Job 11:12**

**Job 11:13**

**Job 11:14**

**Job 11:15**

**Job 11:16**

And you will forget toil, like a wave that passed by, and you will not be alarmed.

**Job 11:17**

And your prayer will be like a morning star, and life will rise for you from midday.

**Job 11:18**

And you will be confident because there is hope for you; and out of care and anxiety peace will appear for you.

**Job 11:19**

**Job 11:20**

But salvation will fail them, for their hope is destruction, and the eyes of the ungodly will melt.

#### Chapter 12

**Job 12:1**

And taking up the matter, Job says,

**Job 12:2**

Then you are men indeed, and wisdom will die with you?

**Job 12:3**

But I too have heart like you.

**Job 12:4**

For a righteous and blameless man became an object of mockery.

**Job 12:5**

**Job 12:6**

**Job 12:7**

**Job 12:8**

**Job 12:9**

**Job 12:10**

**Job 12:11**

**Job 12:12**

**Job 12:13**

**Job 12:14**

**Job 12:15**

**Job 12:16**

With him are might and strength; with him knowledge and understanding.

**Job 12:17**

Leading counselors away captive, he drove judges of earth mad.

**Job 12:18**

**Job 12:19**

Sending priests away captive, he overthrew rulers of the earth.

**Job 12:20**

Changing lips of faithful men, he takes away understanding of elders.

**Job 12:21**

**Job 12:22**

**Job 12:23**

**Job 12:24**

**Job 12:25**

#### Chapter 13

**Job 13:1**

Behold, my eye has seen these things, and my ear heard them.

**Job 13:2**

What you know, I also know; I am not less understanding than you.

**Job 13:3**

But indeed I will speak to the Lord, and if he wishes I will reason before him.

**Job 13:4**

**Job 13:5**

**Job 13:6**

**Job 13:7**

**Job 13:8**

**Job 13:9**

**Job 13:10**

**Job 13:11**

**Job 13:12**

**Job 13:13**

**Job 13:14**

**Job 13:15**

**Job 13:16**

**Job 13:17**

**Job 13:18**

**Job 13:19**

**Job 13:20**

**Job 13:21**

**Job 13:22**

**Job 13:23**

**Job 13:24**

**Job 13:25**

**Job 13:26**

**Job 13:27**

**Job 13:28**

#### Chapter 14

**Job 14:1**

**Job 14:2**

**Job 14:3**

**Job 14:4**

**Job 14:5**

**Job 14:6**

**Job 14:7**

**Job 14:8**

**Job 14:9**

**Job 14:10**

**Job 14:11**

**Job 14:12**

**Job 14:13**

**Job 14:14**

**Job 14:15**

**Job 14:16**

**Job 14:17**

**Job 14:18**

**Job 14:19**

**Job 14:20**

**Job 14:21**

**Job 14:22**

#### Chapter 15

**Job 15:1**

And taking up the matter, Eliphaz the Temanite says,

**Job 15:2**

**Job 15:3**

**Job 15:4**

**Job 15:5**

**Job 15:6**

**Job 15:7**

**Job 15:8**

**Job 15:9**

**Job 15:10**

**Job 15:11**

**Job 15:12**

**Job 15:13**

**Job 15:14**

**Job 15:15**

**Job 15:16**

**Job 15:17**

**Job 15:18**

**Job 15:19**

**Job 15:20**

**Job 15:21**

**Job 15:22**

**Job 15:23**

**Job 15:24**

**Job 15:25**

**Job 15:26**

**Job 15:27**

**Job 15:28**

**Job 15:29**

**Job 15:30**

**Job 15:31**

**Job 15:32**

**Job 15:33**

**Job 15:34**

**Job 15:35**

#### Chapter 16

**Job 16:1**

And taking up the matter, Job says,

**Job 16:2**

I heard many such things, all of you comforters of evils.

**Job 16:3**

For is there not order to windy words? Or what troubles you that you answer?

**Job 16:4**

I too would speak like you, if only your soul lay in place of mine; then I would exult over you with words and shake head against you.

**Job 16:5**

But let there be strength in my mouth; I will not spare movement of my lips.

**Job 16:6**

**Job 16:7**

**Job 16:8**

**Job 16:9**

**Job 16:10**

**Job 16:11**

**Job 16:12**

**Job 16:13**

**Job 16:14**

**Job 16:15**

**Job 16:16**

**Job 16:17**

**Job 16:18**

**Job 16:19**

**Job 16:20**

**Job 16:21**

**Job 16:22**

#### Chapter 17

**Job 17:1**

**Job 17:2**

**Job 17:3**

**Job 17:4**

**Job 17:5**

**Job 17:6**

**Job 17:7**

**Job 17:8**

**Job 17:9**

**Job 17:10**

**Job 17:11**

**Job 17:12**

**Job 17:13**

**Job 17:14**

**Job 17:15**

**Job 17:16**

#### Chapter 18

**Job 18:1**

And taking up the matter, Bildad the Shuhite says,

**Job 18:2**

How long will you not stop? Hold back, so we also may speak.

**Job 18:3**

**Job 18:4**

**Job 18:5**

**Job 18:6**

**Job 18:7**

**Job 18:8**

**Job 18:9**

**Job 18:10**

**Job 18:11**

**Job 18:12**

**Job 18:13**

**Job 18:14**

**Job 18:15**

**Job 18:16**

**Job 18:17**

**Job 18:18**

**Job 18:19**

**Job 18:20**

**Job 18:21**

#### Chapter 19

**Job 19:1**

And taking up the matter, Job says,

**Job 19:2**

**Job 19:3**

**Job 19:4**

**Job 19:5**

**Job 19:6**

**Job 19:7**

**Job 19:9**

**Job 19:10**

**Job 19:11**

**Job 19:12**

**Job 19:13**

**Job 19:14**

**Job 19:15**

**Job 19:16**

**Job 19:17**

**Job 19:18**

**Job 19:20**

**Job 19:21**

**Job 19:22**

**Job 19:23**

**Job 19:24**

**Job 19:25**

**Job 19:26**

he will raise up my skin enduring these things, for from the Lord these things were accomplished for me.

**Job 19:27**

**Job 19:28**

#### Chapter 20

**Job 20:1**

And taking up the matter, Zophar the Naamathite says,

**Job 20:2**

**Job 20:3**

**Job 20:4**

Do you not know these things from long ago, from when man was placed upon earth,

**Job 20:5**

**Job 20:6**

**Job 20:7**

**Job 20:8**

**Job 20:9**

**Job 20:10**

**Job 20:11**

**Job 20:12**

If evil be sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue.

**Job 20:13**

**Job 20:14**

**Job 20:15**

**Job 20:16**

**Job 20:17**

**Job 20:18**

**Job 20:19**

**Job 20:20**

**Job 20:21**

**Job 20:22**

**Job 20:23**

**Job 20:24**

**Job 20:25**

**Job 20:26**

**Job 20:27**

**Job 20:28**

**Job 20:29**

#### Chapter 21

**Job 21:1**

And taking up the matter, Job says,

**Job 21:2**

**Job 21:3**

Bear with me, and I will speak; then afterward laugh at me.

**Job 21:4**

**Job 21:5**

**Job 21:6**

**Job 21:7**

**Job 21:8**

**Job 21:9**

**Job 21:10**

**Job 21:11**

**Job 21:12**

**Job 21:13**

**Job 21:14**

**Job 21:15**

**Job 21:16**

**Job 21:18**

**Job 21:22**

**Job 21:23**

**Job 21:24**

**Job 21:25**

**Job 21:26**

**Job 21:27**

**Job 21:28**

**Job 21:29**

**Job 21:30**

**Job 21:31**

**Job 21:32**

**Job 21:33**

#### Chapter 22

**Job 22:1**

**Job 22:2**

**Job 22:3**

**Job 22:5**

**Job 22:7**

**Job 22:8**

**Job 22:9**

**Job 22:10**

**Job 22:11**

**Job 22:12**

**Job 22:13**

**Job 22:15**

**Job 22:16**

**Job 22:17**

**Job 22:18**

**Job 22:19**

**Job 22:20**

**Job 22:21**

**Job 22:22**

**Job 22:23**

**Job 22:24**

**Job 22:25**

**Job 22:26**

**Job 22:27**

**Job 22:28**

**Job 22:29**

**Job 22:30**

#### Chapter 23

**Job 23:1**

And taking up the matter, Job says,

**Job 23:2**

**Job 23:5**

**Job 23:7**

**Job 23:8**

**Job 23:11**

**Job 23:17**

#### Chapter 24

**Job 24:1**

**Job 25:1**

And taking up the matter, Bildad the Shuhite says,

**Job 26:1**

**Job 26:13**

**Job 27:1**

**Job 27:21**

**Job 28:1**

**Job 29:1**

#### Chapter 30

**Job 30:1**

**Job 31:1**

**Job 31:34**

**Job 31:35**

**Job 31:36**

**Job 31:37**

**Job 31:38**

**Job 31:39**

#### Chapter 32

**Job 32:1**

**Job 32:4**

**Job 32:5**

**Job 32:7**

**Job 32:8**

**Job 32:9**

**Job 32:10**

**Job 32:13**

**Job 32:15**

**Job 32:16**

**Job 32:17**

**Job 32:18**

**Job 32:19**

**Job 32:21**

**Job 33:1**

**Job 33:28**

**Job 33:29**

**Job 33:30**

**Job 33:31**

**Job 33:32**

**Job 34:1**

#### Chapter 41

Who will uncover the face of its clothing? And who would enter fold of its breastplate?

**Job 41:6**

Who will open gates of its face? Around its teeth is fear.

**Job 41:7**

Its inward parts are bronze shields, and its binding like emery stone.

**Job 41:8**

One cleaving to another, and breath will by no means pass through it.

**Job 41:9**

A man to his brother will be glued; they hold together and will by no means be torn apart.

**Job 41:10**

At its sneezing light shines, and its eyes like form of morning star.

**Job 41:11**

From its mouth go out burning lamps, and hearths of fire are scattered abroad.

**Job 41:12**

From its nostrils comes out smoke of furnace burning with coals of fire.

**Job 41:13**

Its soul is coals, and flame goes out from its mouth.

**Job 41:14**

And in its neck strength lodges; destruction runs before it.

**Job 41:15**

Fleshes of its body are joined together; he will pour upon it, and it will not be shaken.

**Job 41:16**

Its heart is fixed like stone, standing like unhammersmitten anvil.

**Job 41:17**

When it turns, there is fear to beasts, to quadrupeds on earth leaping.

**Job 41:18**

If spears meet it, they will do nothing, nor raised spear and breastplate.

**Job 41:19**

For it counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.

**Job 41:20**

Bronze bow will by no means wound it; it counts stone-slinger as grass.

**Job 41:21**

Hammers were counted as reed, and it laughs at shaking of fire-bearer.

**Job 41:22**

Its bed is sharp spits, and all gold of sea under it like immeasurable clay.

**Job 41:23**

It makes deep boil like a bronze pot, and counts sea like a perfume-vessel.

**Job 41:24**

And Tartarus of deep it counted like captive, and deep for its walking.

**Job 41:25**

There is nothing upon earth like it, made to be mocked by my angels.

**Job 41:26**

It sees every high thing; and it is the king of all things in waters.

#### Chapter 42

**Job 42:1**

And taking up the matter, Job says to the Lord,

**Job 42:2**

I know that you can do all things, and nothing is impossible for you.

**Job 42:3**

For who is one hiding counsel from you, sparing words, and thinking to hide you? And who will tell me things I did not know, great and wonderful things which I did not understand?

**Job 42:4**

Hear me, Lord, that I too may speak; I will ask you, and you teach me.

**Job 42:5**

By hearing of ear I formerly heard you, but now my eye has seen you.

**Job 42:6**

Therefore I despised myself and melted away, and I count myself earth and ashes.

**Job 42:7**

And it happened after the Lord spoke all these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, You and your two friends sinned, for you spoke nothing true before me, as my servant Job did.

**Job 42:8**

Now then take seven calves and seven rams and go to my servant Job, and he will make fruit-offering concerning you. And my servant Job will pray concerning you, because unless I receive his face, for his sake I would have destroyed you, for you did not speak truth concerning my servant Job.

**Job 42:9**

And Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Lord instructed them, and through Job he loosed their sin.

**Job 42:10**

And the Lord increased Job. And when he prayed also concerning his friends, he forgave them their sin. And the Lord gave double whatever had been before Job, for doubling.

**Job 42:11**

And all his brothers and sisters heard all things that happened to him, and they came to him, and all who had known him from first. And eating and drinking with him, they comforted him and marveled over all that the Lord brought upon him. And each gave him one lamb and a gold four-drachma piece unstamped.

**Job 42:12**

And the Lord blessed last things of Job more than former things. And his livestock was fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female grazing donkeys.

**Job 42:13**

And seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

**Job 42:14**

And he called first Day, second Cassia, and third Horn of Amaltheia.

**Job 42:15**

And no women under heaven were found better than daughters of Job, and father gave them inheritance among their brothers.

**Job 42:16**

And Job lived after the blow one hundred seventy years; altogether he lived two hundred forty-eight years, and Job saw his sons and sons of his sons, fourth generation.

**Job 42:17**

And Job died old and full of days. And it is written that he will rise again with those whom the Lord raises up. This man, interpreted from the Syriac book, dwelt in the land of Uz on the borders of Idumaia and Arabia, and his former name was Jobab. Taking an Arabian wife, he fathered a son whose name was Ennon. And he himself was the son of Zerah, one of the sons of Esau, from his mother Bozrah, so as to be fifth from Abraham. And these were kings who reigned in Edom, over which he also first ruled: Balak son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah; after Balak, Jobab called Job; after him Husham, ruler from the country of Temanite; after him Hadad son of Bedad, who cut down Midian in the plain of Moab, and the name of his city was Gittaim. And friends coming to him were Eliphaz king of the sons of Esau from the Temanites, Bildad tyrant of the Sauchites, and Zophar king of the Naamathites.

### Psalms

#### Chapter 1

**Psalms 1:1**

Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of ungodly men, and did not stand in the way of sinners, and did not sit upon the seat of pestilent men,

**Psalms 1:2**

but his delight is in the law of the Lord, and in his law he will meditate day and night.

**Psalms 1:3**

And he will be like a tree planted by outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not wither, and all things whatever he does will prosper.

**Psalms 1:4**

Not so ungodly men, not so, but like chaff which wind throws from the face of the earth.

**Psalms 1:5**

Because of this ungodly men will not stand in judgment, nor sinners in the counsel of righteous men.

**Psalms 1:6**

For the Lord knows the way of righteous men, but the way of ungodly men will perish.

#### Chapter 2

**Psalms 2:1**

Why did nations rage, and peoples meditate empty things?

**Psalms 2:2**

The kings of the earth stood by, and rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Anointed. Interlude.

**Psalms 2:3**

Let us tear their bonds apart and cast their yoke from us.

**Psalms 2:4**

One dwelling in heavens will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them.

**Psalms 2:5**

Then he will speak to them in his wrath and trouble them in his anger.

**Psalms 2:6**

But I was set as king by him upon Zion, his holy mountain,

**Psalms 2:7**

declaring decree of the Lord. The Lord said to me, You are my son; today I have begotten you.

**Psalms 2:8**

Ask from me, and I will give nations as your inheritance and ends of the earth as your possession.

**Psalms 2:9**

You will shepherd them with iron rod; like potter's vessel you will shatter them.

**Psalms 2:10**

And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all judging earth.

**Psalms 2:11**

Serve the Lord in fear and rejoice in him with trembling.

**Psalms 2:12**

Take hold of instruction lest the Lord be angered and you perish from a righteous way when his wrath is quickly kindled. Blessed are all who trust in him.

#### Chapter 3

**Psalms 3:1**

Psalm of David, when he fled from the face of Absalom his son.

**Psalms 3:2**

Lord, why were those afflicting me multiplied? Many rise up against me.

**Psalms 3:3**

Many say to my soul, There is no salvation for him in his God. Interlude.

**Psalms 3:4**

But you, Lord, are my defender, my glory, and one lifting my head.

**Psalms 3:5**

With my voice I cried to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain. Interlude.

**Psalms 3:6**

I lay down and slept; I awoke, because the Lord will help me.

**Psalms 3:7**

I will not fear from myriads of the people those surrounding and attacking me.

**Psalms 3:8**

Rise up, Lord; save me, my God, because you struck all who hate me for nothing; the teeth of sinners you shattered.

**Psalms 3:9**

Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing upon your people.

#### Chapter 4

**Psalms 4:1**

For end. In psalms. Song of David.

**Psalms 4:2**

When I call, God of my righteousness heard me; in affliction you widened space for me. Have pity on me and hear my prayer.

**Psalms 4:3**

Sons of men, until when heavy-hearted? Why do you love vanity and seek lie? Interlude.

**Psalms 4:4**

And know that the Lord made his holy one wondrous; The Lord will hear me when I cry to him.

**Psalms 4:5**

Be angry and do not sin; say within your hearts, and upon your beds be pierced through. Interlude.

**Psalms 4:6**

Offer a sacrifice of righteousness and hope upon the Lord.

**Psalms 4:7**

Many say, Who will show us good things? Light of your face, Lord, was marked upon us.

**Psalms 4:8**

You gave gladness into my heart, from season when their grain and wine and oil were multiplied.

**Psalms 4:9**

In peace, at same time, I will lie down and sleep, because you, Lord, alone settled me in hope.

#### Chapter 5

**Psalms 5:1**

For end. Concerning her who inherits. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 5:2**

Give ear to my words, Lord; understand my cry.

**Psalms 5:3**

Attend to the voice of my petition, my King and my God, because to you I will pray, Lord.

**Psalms 5:4**

In morning you will hear my voice; in morning I will stand before you and keep watch.

**Psalms 5:5**

For you are not God willing lawlessness, nor will one doing evil dwell with you.

**Psalms 5:6**

Lawless men will not remain before your eyes; you hated all working lawlessness.

**Psalms 5:7**

You will destroy all speaking lie; man of bloods and deceit the Lord abhors.

**Psalms 5:8**

But I, in the multitude of your mercy, will enter into your house; I will worship toward your holy temple in your fear.

**Psalms 5:9**

Lord, lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies; make your way straight before me.

**Psalms 5:10**

Because there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain; their throat open grave; with their tongues they dealt deceitfully.

**Psalms 5:11**

Judge them, God; let them fall from their counsels. According to the multitude of their ungodliness cast them out, because they embittered you, Lord.

**Psalms 5:12**

And let all hoping in you be glad; into age they will rejoice, and you will dwell among them; and all loving your name will boast in you.

**Psalms 5:13**

Because you will bless a righteous man, Lord; as with a weapon of favor you crowned us.

#### Chapter 6

**Psalms 6:1**

For end. In hymns. Concerning eighth. Psalm of David.

**Psalms 6:2**

Lord, do not reprove me in your fury, nor discipline me in your anger.

**Psalms 6:3**

Have mercy on me, Lord, because I am weak. Heal me, Lord, because my bones were troubled.

**Psalms 6:4**

And my soul was greatly troubled. And you, Lord, until when?

**Psalms 6:5**

Turn back, Lord; rescue my soul. Save me because of your mercy.

**Psalms 6:6**

Because in death there is none remembering you; and in Hades who will confess to you?

**Psalms 6:7**

I toiled in my groaning; every night I will wash my bed, with my tears I will soak my couch.

**Psalms 6:8**

My eye was troubled from anger; I grew old among all my enemies.

**Psalms 6:9**

Depart from me, all working lawlessness, because the Lord heard the voice of my weeping.

**Psalms 6:10**

The Lord heard my petition; The Lord received my prayer.

**Psalms 6:11**

Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled; let them turn back and be greatly ashamed very quickly.

#### Chapter 7

**Psalms 7:1**

Psalm of David, which he sang to the Lord concerning the words of Cushi son of Iemeni.

**Psalms 7:2**

Lord my God, upon you I hoped; save me from all pursuing me and rescue me,

**Psalms 7:3**

lest he seize my soul like a lion, while there is none redeeming and none saving.

**Psalms 7:4**

Lord my God, if I did this, if there is injustice in my hands,

**Psalms 7:5**

if I repaid evil to those repaying me, then let me fall away from my enemies empty.

**Psalms 7:6**

Then let enemy pursue my soul and seize it, and trample my life into earth, and settle my glory in dust. Interlude.

**Psalms 7:7**

Rise up, Lord, in your anger; be lifted up at ends of my enemies. Wake up, Lord my God, in command which you enjoined.

**Psalms 7:8**

And a gathering of peoples will encircle you, and over this return on high.

**Psalms 7:9**

The Lord judges peoples. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness and according to my innocence upon me.

**Psalms 7:10**

Let the evil of sinners come to an end, and you will set a righteous man straight, examining hearts and kidneys, O God.

**Psalms 7:11**

My help is righteous from God, the one saving upright ones in heart.

**Psalms 7:12**

God is righteous judge, strong and patient, not bringing on anger each day.

**Psalms 7:13**
